title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰學而時習之不亦說乎
楊應兆
同考試官學正梁批典雅冲淡理意渾然蓋有心
得者允宜首錄
考試官敎諭劉批不落塵筌詞藻自麗
考試官敎諭蔣批鎔意鑄詞極爲密緻
聖人首著心得之學亦在乎熟之而已矣夫學
===
求有得於心也所學者熟而心有不自得哉此
萬世道學之原也夫子揭以示人若曰人心通
乎太虛未有不說於道者也惟不學則不知道
而學之未熟則苦難而弗說矣誠知人不可以
不學也而仰法前脩以爲進趨之準知學之不
可以已也而遜志時敏以勤服習之功習其所
知而明善之學時亹亹焉將求通於性命而瞬
息之無間也習其所行而誠身之學時汲汲焉
將求進於聖神而動息之有養也夫向往旣專
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子曰：「學而時習之，不亦說乎？」
楊應兆
同考試官學正梁批：典雅冲淡，理意渾然，蓋有心得者，允宜首錄。
考試官敎諭劉批：不落塵筌，詞藻自麗。
考試官敎諭蔣批：鎔意鑄詞，極爲密緻。

聖人首著心得之學，亦在乎熟之而已矣。夫學，求有得於心也；所學者熟，而心有不自得哉？此萬世道學之原也，夫子揭以示人，若曰：人心通乎太虛，未有不說於道者也。惟不學則不知道，而學之未熟，則苦難而弗說矣。誠知人不可以不學也，而仰法前脩，以爲進趨之準；知學之不可以已也，而遜志時敏，以勤服習之功。習其所知，而明善之學時亹亹焉，將求通於性命，而瞬息之無間也；習其所行，而誠身之學時汲汲焉，將求進於聖神，而動息之有養也。夫向往旣專，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: "To learn and in due time to practice what one has learned—is this not also a pleasure?"

Yang Yingzhao 楊應兆

Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Liang 梁: "Classic and elegant, calm and understated, its principles and meaning form a seamless whole. Clearly written by someone who has attained genuine personal insight, it truly deserves to be recorded in first place."
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Liu 劉: "It does not fall into mundane clichés; its diction and style are naturally graceful."
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Jiang 蔣: "It fuses meaning and casts words with the utmost precision and care."

When the Sage first sets forth the learning that brings personal realization in the mind, it lies simply in bringing it to maturity through familiarity. Now, learning seeks to attain something within the mind; when what one learns has become thoroughly familiar, how could the mind fail to find satisfaction in itself? This is the source of the Learning of the Way for ten thousand generations. The Master held it up to show to people, as if to say: The human mind communicates with the Great Vacuity; there is no one who does not take pleasure in the Way. Only when one does not learn does one not know the Way, and when one's learning is not yet thoroughly familiar, one suffers from its difficulty and feels no pleasure. If one truly knows that a person cannot do without learning, and looks up to emulate the worthy exemplars of the past as the standard for one's own advancement and pursuit; and if one knows that learning cannot be broken off, and keeps a humble will while striving constantly, so as to be diligent in the work of practice and application—then one practices what one knows, and the learning of illuminating goodness goes on tirelessly at all times, seeking to penetrate human nature and Heaven's mandate without a single moment's interruption; and one practices what one does, and the learning of making the self sincere proceeds eagerly at all times, seeking to advance toward the realm of the sagely and spirit-like, while maintaining cultivation in both movement and rest. Now, once one's aspiration is focused…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
則精神自聚而喜意爲之潛滋積習有常則旨
趣自通而天機爲之渙發知以涵泳而熟焉性
命一源不苦於扞格也愈精明則愈融液固獨
覺其妙而不能言者乎行以敦篤而熟焉神聖
一心不苦於矜持也愈進脩則愈浹洽固自得
其趣而不能已者乎是學非外於心也所以還
吾順適之眞也說非離於學也所以要吾敏學
之趣也以之錫類而所說不孤以之貞遇而所
說不改斯其爲天下之全學也豈或作或輟者
===
可與幾哉彼耳順從心吾夫子蓋得乎說之妙
者而其敏求發憤必至於七十而始化焉是聖
人固自志學以至終身而始要其成矣天縱生
知其功如此則說心之妙豈易言哉噫竭才立
卓顏其幾矣而願息之請亦爲聖人之徒焉此
時習之學夫子所以首垂訓也
三者天下之達德也所以行之者一也
楊同春
同考試官敎諭徐 批 只用本色語而旨趣雋永可
punctuated:
則精神自聚，而喜意爲之潛滋；積習有常，則旨趣自通，而天機爲之渙發。知以涵泳而熟焉，性命一源，不苦於扞格也；愈精明則愈融液，固獨覺其妙而不能言者乎？行以敦篤而熟焉，神聖一心，不苦於矜持也；愈進脩則愈浹洽，固自得其趣而不能已者乎？是學非外於心也，所以還吾順適之眞也；說非離於學也，所以要吾敏學之趣也。以之錫類，而所說不孤；以之貞遇，而所說不改。斯其爲天下之全學也，豈或作或輟者可與幾哉？彼耳順、從心，吾夫子蓋得乎說之妙者，而其敏求、發憤，必至於七十而始化焉，是聖人固自志學以至終身而始要其成矣。天縱生知，其功如此，則說心之妙，豈易言哉？噫！竭才、立卓，顏其幾矣，而願息之請，亦爲聖人之徒焉。此時習之學，夫子所以首垂訓也。

「三者天下之達德也，所以行之者一也。」
楊同春
同考試官敎諭徐批：只用本色語，而旨趣雋永可愛，佳士也，錄之。
translation_en:
… then one's vital spirit naturally concentrates, and a sense of joy quietly grows within; when accumulated practice is constant, the underlying meaning naturally becomes clear, and the heavenly mechanism radiates forth. When knowledge becomes mature through immersive contemplation, human nature and Heaven's mandate share a single source, and one no longer suffers from obstruction; the more lucid it becomes, the more thoroughly it blends and dissolves—is it not something whose subtlety one feels alone without being able to put into words? When action becomes mature through earnest devotion, the divine and the sagely are of one mind, and one no longer suffers from strained restraint; the more one advances in self-cultivation, the more deeply imbued one becomes—is it not something whose savor one attains for oneself without being able to stop? Thus learning is not external to the mind; it is the means by which we restore the true state of our natural ease. Joy is not separate from learning; it is the means by which we consummate the relish of our diligent study. Extending it to kindred spirits, what one delights in is not solitary; holding fast to it amid adversity, what one delights in does not change. This is what constitutes the complete learning of the world—how could those who work by fits and starts ever hope to approach it? As for having an obedient ear at sixty and following the heart's desires at seventy, our Master indeed attained the subtlety of such joy; yet in his diligent seeking and eager striving, it was only upon reaching seventy that he achieved complete transformation. Thus even the Sage had to go from setting his heart on learning at fifteen all the way to the end of his life before bringing it to completion. If one whom Heaven endowed with innate knowledge required such effort, how could the subtlety of a joyful heart be easily spoken of? Alas! In exhausting his talents until the Master's way stood towering before him, Yan Yuan came close to it; and even he who requested to rest in death was still a disciple of the Sage. This learning through constant practice is why the Master handed down this teaching first of all.

"These three are the universal virtues of the world, and the means by which they are practiced is one."
Yang Tongchun 楊同春
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xu 徐: He uses only natural, unadorned language, yet the meaning and flavor are lastingly evocative and delightful… [continued on next page]

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
愛佳士也錄之
考試官教諭劉批認理精深一洗俗調
考試官教諭蔣批大雅之文可式多士
中庸指德之爲達而約之於誠焉夫誠者德之
精也德通天下而非誠其何以行之哉夫子以
此進魯君若曰治固貴乎敦本道必先於存誠
明於道德之原而脩身立政者裕如矣彼達道
有五而三德行之智仁勇是也之三者賦出維
皇而明通公溥皆其本然之懿善緣民秉而剛
===
健貞固乃其各足之良達之一世之天下此心
同則此德同蓋自真精妙合之初不以聖愚爲
厚薄也達之萬世之天下均是性則均是德蓋
自理氣凝成之後不以古今爲異同也夫是之
謂達德也以此三者行此五者其惟一誠乎蓋
至理惟一則不虛而貫徹乎綱常者本無僞妄
之間人心惟一則不雜而經綸乎物則者自妙
推行之通統三德於一誠則心精之內裕固粹
然其無疵焉心爲實心道有所據而自凝矣其
punctuated:
愛，佳士也，錄之。
考試官教諭劉批：認理精深，一洗俗調。
考試官教諭蔣批：大雅之文，可式多士。

《中庸》指德之爲達，而約之於誠焉。夫誠者，德之精也；德通天下，而非誠其何以行之哉？夫子以此進魯君，若曰：治固貴乎敦本，道必先於存誠，明於道德之原，而脩身立政者裕如矣。彼達道有五，而三德行之，智、仁、勇是也。之三者，賦出維皇，而明通公溥，皆其本然之懿；善緣民秉，而剛健貞固，乃其各足之良。達之一世之天下，此心同則此德同，蓋自真精妙合之初，不以聖愚爲厚薄也；達之萬世之天下，均是性則均是德，蓋自理氣凝成之後，不以古今爲異同也。夫是之謂達德也。以此三者行此五者，其惟一誠乎！蓋至理惟一則不虛，而貫徹乎綱常者，本無僞妄之間；人心惟一則不雜，而經綸乎物則者，自妙推行之通。統三德於一誠，則心精之內裕，固粹然其無疵焉。心爲實心，道有所據而自凝矣，其
translation_en:
…lovable. He is a fine scholar; let this be recorded for publication.
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: His grasp of principle is refined and profound, completely washing away vulgar conventions.
Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: Writing of great elegance, worthy to serve as a model for the multitude of scholars.

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) points out how the virtues are universal, and reduces their practice to a single sincerity. Now sincerity is the essence of virtue; though the virtues extend throughout the world, without sincerity how could they be practiced? The Master presented this to the ruler of Lu, as if to say: Governance indeed values strengthening the root, and the Way must begin with preserving sincerity; once one is clear about the source of the Way and of virtue, cultivating the person and establishing governance will proceed with effortless abundance. Those universal Ways are five, and three virtues put them into practice: wisdom, humanity, and courage. These three are endowed by Heaven above, so that clarity of understanding and impartial breadth are all their inherent excellence; goodness follows from what the people hold fast as their moral nature, so that vigorous strength and firm constancy are the innate good sufficient in each person. Extended throughout the world of a single age, since this mind is the same, this virtue is the same—for from the very beginning when the true and subtle essences wondrously combined, it is not made thicker or thinner according to whether one is a sage or a fool. Extended throughout the world of ten thousand generations, since the nature is shared equally, the virtue is shared equally—for once principle and vital force have coalesced into form, it does not vary between antiquity and the present. This is what is meant by the universal virtues. To practice those five by means of these three—does it not lie in a single sincerity alone? For when supreme principle is unitary, it is not empty, and what pervades the cardinal human bonds is fundamentally without any intrusion of falsehood or deceit; when the human mind is unitary, it is not mixed, and what orders the norms of things naturally achieves the wondrous unobstructedness of putting them into practice. If one unites the three virtues in a single sincerity, then the inner abundance of the mind's essence is indeed pure and without blemish. When the mind is a real mind, the Way has something to rest upon and naturally coalesces; is this not…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天秩之所以敘乎運一誠於三德則性真之流
行固渾然其無累焉行為實行理有所依而自
立矣其人紀之所以脩乎是一以函三則心極
純而德備三以行五則身極建而道脩文武之
止信惇信以立人極者胥此耳公其勉之哉雖
然誠者天德之精非徒真妄錯雜不足以立德
而擇善固執之際少有意念之牿焉亦非聖人
純懿之學矣況魯公之實不足成者而能慰夫
子東周之望乎彼外施仁義固不足效唐虞而
===
執實御虛則亦術數之學耳而又何責於公也
噫王道本於誠意信哉
堯以不得舜為己憂舜以不得禹皐陶為
己憂夫以百畝之不易為己憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠教人以善謂之忠
為天下得人者謂之仁
傅爾珍
同考試官教諭毛批此題頭緒頗多作之獨無痕
跡且氣鬯詞雅足覘邃學允宜高薦
punctuated:
天秩之所以敘乎！運一誠於三德，則性真之流行固渾然其無累焉；行為實行，理有所依而自立矣，其人紀之所以脩乎！是一以函三，則心極純而德備；三以行五，則身極建而道脩。文、武之止信、惇信以立人極者，胥此耳，公其勉之哉！雖然，誠者，天德之精，非徒真妄錯雜不足以立德，而擇善固執之際，少有意念之牿焉，亦非聖人純懿之學矣。況魯公之實不足成者，而能慰夫子東周之望乎？彼外施仁義，固不足效唐、虞；而執實御虛，則亦術數之學耳，而又何責於公也？噫！王道本於誠意，信哉！

堯以不得舜為己憂，舜以不得禹、皐陶為己憂。夫以百畝之不易為己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠，為天下得人者謂之仁。
傅爾珍
同考試官教諭毛批：此題頭緒頗多，作之獨無痕跡，且氣鬯詞雅，足覘邃學，允宜高薦。
translation_en:
…whereby the heavenly order is set in array! When one operates with a single sincerity through the three virtues, the flow of the true nature is indeed seamless and untrammeled; one's conduct becomes genuine conduct, principle has something to rely upon and stands on its own—is this not whereby the human relationships are cultivated! Thus, when the one encompasses the three, the supreme standard of the mind is pure and virtue is complete; when the three are used to practice the five, the supreme standard of the person is established and the Way is cultivated. That whereby Kings Wen and Wu abided in trustworthiness and esteemed trustworthiness to establish the supreme standard for humanity was nothing other than this. May the Duke strive at it! Even so, sincerity is the essence of heavenly virtue. Not only is a mixture of truth and falsehood insufficient to establish virtue, but even in choosing the good and holding fast to it, if there is the slightest fettering of deliberate intent, it is no longer the pure and admirable learning of the sage. How much less could the Duke of Lu, whose reality was insufficient for achievement, fulfill the Master's hope for an Eastern Zhou? Those who outwardly display benevolence and righteousness are certainly inadequate to emulate Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun]; and as for grasping the substantial to control the empty, that too is merely the learning of statecraft and manipulation—what more then could be demanded of the Duke? Alas! That the Kingly Way is rooted in making the intentions sincere—how true indeed!

"Yao made not getting Shun his own anxiety; Shun made not getting Yu and Gao Yao his own anxiety. Now he who makes the failure to till his hundred mu of land his own anxiety is a farmer. Sharing wealth with others is called kindness; teaching others to be good is called loyalty; finding the right men for the Empire is called benevolence."
Fu Erzhen 傅爾珍
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Mao: This topic has quite a few threads, yet this composition alone shows no trace of artificial seams. Moreover, its vital breath flows smoothly and its diction is elegant, which is sufficient to reveal profound learning. It truly deserves to be highly recommended.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭劉批精粹老練迥異諸作
考試官敎諭蔣批意高詞古一結尤精
觀聖君憂在得賢而其仁天下者大矣夫賢者
人君之所寄以仁天下者也聖君之憂所以必
先其大乎且夫帝王以身任君師之責其心於
天下者無窮也然有不能必爲之勢焉惟得人
以寄其心而已彼堯欲仁有唐之天下其可憂
者多矣然而堯不憂也憂不得舜而已惟得舜
而其心始慰焉舜欲仁有虞之天下其可憂者
===
多矣然而舜不憂也憂不得禹臯陶而已惟得
禹臯陶而其心始慰焉若夫百畝不易農夫之
憂耳而豈堯舜之所以爲憂乎夫聖人所憂之
大若此而不可以知其仁天下之大者哉蓋財
爲民命自我分之惠矣而不足以盡利也善爲
民性自我敎之忠矣而不足以盡神也惟夫爲
天下得人者以司導利之寄則養賢及民輔吾
力之不及天下被容保之仁而不知其爲惠也
豈若小惠之未遍哉以托綏猷之任則得賢弘
punctuated:
考試官敎諭劉批：精粹老練，迥異諸作。
考試官敎諭蔣批：意高詞古，一結尤精。
觀聖君憂在得賢，而其仁天下者大矣。夫賢者，人君之所寄以仁天下者也，聖君之憂，所以必先其大乎！且夫帝王以身任君師之責，其心於天下者無窮也；然有不能必爲之勢焉，惟得人以寄其心而已。彼堯欲仁有唐之天下，其可憂者多矣，然而堯不憂也，憂不得舜而已，惟得舜而其心始慰焉；舜欲仁有虞之天下，其可憂者多矣，然而舜不憂也，憂不得禹、臯陶而已，惟得禹、臯陶而其心始慰焉。若夫百畝不易，農夫之憂耳，而豈堯、舜之所以爲憂乎？夫聖人所憂之大若此，而不可以知其仁天下之大者哉？蓋財爲民命，自我分之，惠矣，而不足以盡利也；善爲民性，自我敎之，忠矣，而不足以盡神也。惟夫爲天下得人者，以司導利之寄，則養賢及民，輔吾力之不及，天下被容保之仁而不知其爲惠也，豈若小惠之未遍哉？以托綏猷之任，則得賢弘…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: Refined and seasoned, vastly superior to the other compositions.
Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: Elevated in meaning and archaic in diction; the concluding passage is especially fine.
When we observe that the sage ruler’s concern lies in obtaining worthy men, we see how great is his benevolence toward the world! For worthy men are those to whom the ruler entrusts the task of extending benevolence to the world; is this not why the sage ruler’s concern must first address what is great? Moreover, when emperors and kings personally assume the responsibilities of both ruler and teacher, their concern for the world is boundless. Yet by the nature of their position they cannot do everything themselves; they can only obtain the right men to whom to entrust their intentions. When Yao wished to extend benevolence to the world of Tang, there were many things to be concerned about. Yet Yao did not worry about them; his only concern was not obtaining Shun, and only when he obtained Shun was his mind set at ease. When Shun wished to extend benevolence to the world of Yu, there were many things to be concerned about. Yet Shun did not worry about them; his only concern was not obtaining Yu and Gao Yao, and only when he obtained Yu and Gao Yao was his mind set at ease. As for a hundred mu of land not being properly cultivated, that is merely the concern of a farmer—how could it be what Yao and Shun made their concern? Since what the sages worried about was as great as this, can we not know from it the greatness of their benevolence toward the world? For wealth is the lifeblood of the people; if I distribute it myself, that is kindness, yet it is insufficient to exhaust all benefit. Goodness is the nature of the people; if I teach it myself, that is loyalty, yet it is insufficient to exhaust all miraculous transformative power. Only one who obtains the right men for the world—entrusting them with the charge of guiding material benefit, so that nourishing the worthy extends to the people and supplements what my own strength cannot reach, causing the world to receive the benevolence of tolerant protection without even realizing it is a kindness—how could that be like petty kindnesses that fail to reach everyone? And entrusting them with the duty of tranquilizing plans, so that obtaining the worthy broadens…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
化濟吾道之所同天下被錫類之仁而忘其所
以敎也豈若徒忠之未孚哉故禹臯之仁即舜
之仁也舜之仁即堯之仁也惟其仁之大是以
憂之急而又何容於耕乎吁充竝耕之說不過
分財敎善之意而其術且窮矣雖然聖人憂在
得賢則岳牧羣工皆其所急而獨憂不得舜禹
臯者爲重端揆之任也蓋端揆得人則衆職咸
舉玄德升聞而元愷彙進其機之類應固如此
噫親賢之中有先務焉仁天下者法堯舜而已
===
易
元者善之長也
傅爾珍
同考試官敎諭毛批〔通篇發揮元德不著色相而〕
〔理意充然可掬蓋大手筆也〕
考試官敎諭劉批〔筆力遒勁文采爛然〕
考試官敎諭蔣批〔意正詞腴可以式矣〕
文言於乾德之元而著其統天下之善焉夫元
固天德之大始也自人具之而天下之善不統
punctuated:
化，濟吾道之所同，天下被錫類之仁，而忘其所以敎也，豈若徒忠之未孚哉？故禹、臯之仁，即舜之仁也；舜之仁，即堯之仁也。惟其仁之大，是以憂之急，而又何容於耕乎？吁！充竝耕之說，不過分財、敎善之意，而其術且窮矣。雖然，聖人憂在得賢，則岳、牧、羣工皆其所急，而獨憂不得舜、禹、臯者，爲重端揆之任也。蓋端揆得人，則衆職咸舉，玄德升聞，而元、愷彙進，其機之類應固如此。噫！親賢之中有先務焉，仁天下者，法堯、舜而已。
《易》
「元者，善之長也。」
傅爾珍
同考試官敎諭毛批：〔通篇發揮元德，不著色相，而理意充然可掬，蓋大手筆也。〕
考試官敎諭劉批：〔筆力遒勁，文采爛然。〕
考試官敎諭蔣批：〔意正詞腴，可以式矣。〕
《文言》於乾德之元，而著其統天下之善焉。夫元固天德之大始也，自人具之，而天下之善不統
translation_en:
…transformation, thereby aiding what our Way holds in common, then the world receives the benevolence that bestows blessings on one's kind and forgets the means by which it was taught. How could this be like mere loyalty that fails to inspire trust? Therefore, the benevolence of Yu 禹 and Gao Yao 臯陶 is none other than the benevolence of Shun 舜; the benevolence of Shun is none other than the benevolence of Yao 堯. Because their benevolence was so great, their anxiety was so urgent—what room, then, could they have had for plowing the fields? Alas! Even if one carries the doctrine of rulers plowing alongside the people to its utmost, it amounts to no more than the idea of distributing wealth and teaching goodness, and even that technique would soon be exhausted. Even so, since the sage's anxiety lies in obtaining worthy men, the Four Peaks (Yue 岳), the Twelve Pastors (Mu 牧), and the multitude of officials are all his urgent concern; yet his sole anxiety was failing to find Shun, Yu, and Gao Yao, because he attached paramount importance to the responsibility of the chief minister. For when the right person is found as chief minister, all offices are well managed: as Shun's mysterious virtue rose to be heard on high, the Eight Worthies (Bakai 八愷) and Eight 元 (Bayuan 八元) advanced together by category—such is naturally the responsive mechanism by which like attracts like. Ah! Even within showing affection for the worthy, there is a foremost priority; he who would bring benevolence to the world need only model himself on Yao and Shun.

The Book of Changes (Yi 易)
"Origination is the chief of all goodness."
Fu Erzhen 傅爾珍
Associate Examiner and Instructor (Jiaoyu 敎諭) Mao 毛 comments: 〔Throughout the piece, he expounds on the virtue of Origination without clinging to superficial appearances, yet its principle and meaning are so full that they could be scooped up in the hands—truly the work of a master hand.〕
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: 〔The brushwork is vigorous and strong, and the literary brilliance is dazzling.〕
Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: 〔The ideas are upright and the diction rich; it can serve as a model.〕

The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan 文言), regarding Origination among the virtues of the Creative (Qian 乾), makes manifest how it encompasses all goodness in the world. Now, Origination is indeed the great beginning of Heaven's virtue; once human beings are endowed with it, is not all the goodness in the world encompassed…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
於是乎昔文言之意若曰天之有元也造化由
之以綱維羣生由之以立命夫固爲天德之首
矣而其在人也何如蓋天生萬物而元始之則
吾人得之於賦予者惟此理爲最先天有四德
而元統之則吾人受之爲秉彝者惟此善爲至
大故繼善之後萬理咸備而一元之根於太始
者實有以開萬理之原成性之中衆善悉有而
一元之通乎太極者實有以主衆善之妙秩之
爲五常善固各有定體也而肫肫懇至之意聯
===
貫於其中者爲能兼總而不遺焉維皇降衷之
懿玆其莫之與京者矣散之爲百行善固不可
勝用也而生生不息之理渾融於其内者爲能
宰制而無外焉上帝賦畀之良玆其莫之與竝
者矣要之未有物先則是元爲天地莫先之德
既有物後則是元爲人心統體之全天下固未
有一善而不統於元亦未有外元而可以爲善
者也不謂善之長而何哉吁元之在人其大若
此故聖人得之爲首出庶物之資體之爲克長
punctuated: 於是乎？昔《文言》之意若曰：天之有元也，造化由之以綱維，羣生由之以立命，夫固爲天德之首矣；而其在人也何如？蓋天生萬物而元始之，則吾人得之於賦予者，惟此理爲最先；天有四德而元統之，則吾人受之爲秉彝者，惟此善爲至大。故繼善之後，萬理咸備，而一元之根於太始者，實有以開萬理之原；成性之中，衆善悉有，而一元之通乎太極者，實有以主衆善之妙。秩之爲五常，善固各有定體也，而肫肫懇至之意聯貫於其中者，爲能兼總而不遺焉，維皇降衷之懿，玆其莫之與京者矣；散之爲百行，善固不可勝用也，而生生不息之理渾融於其内者，爲能宰制而無外焉，上帝賦畀之良，玆其莫之與竝者矣。要之，未有物先，則是元爲天地莫先之德；既有物後，則是元爲人心統體之全。天下固未有一善而不統於元，亦未有外元而可以爲善者也。不謂善之長而何哉？吁！元之在人，其大若此。故聖人得之爲首出庶物之資，體之爲克長…
translation_en: … under it? Formerly, the meaning of the "Commentary on the Words of the Text" (Wenyan) was as if to say: In Heaven's possession of origination (yuan), the creative transformation relies on it for its guiding framework, and the multitude of living things rely on it to establish their destinies; it is indeed the head of the heavenly virtues. Yet how does it manifest in humanity? For Heaven gives birth to the myriad things and origination initiates them; thus, in what we humans obtain from this endowment, this principle alone comes first. Heaven possesses four virtues and origination encompasses them; thus, in what we humans receive as our constant nature, this goodness alone is the greatest. Therefore, after continuing this goodness, the myriad principles are all complete, and the single origination rooted in the Great Beginning truly serves to open the source of the myriad principles. Within the completed nature, all forms of goodness are fully present, and the single origination communicating with the Supreme Ultimate truly serves to preside over the subtlety of all forms of goodness. Ordered into the Five Constant Virtues, each goodness indeed has its definite substance, yet the earnest and sincere intent threading through them is able to comprehensively unite them without omission—among the beauties of the August Heaven's bestowed moral sense, nothing can rival this! Dispersed into the hundred conducts, goodness is indeed inexhaustible in its application, yet the principle of ceaseless generation blended within them is able to govern them with nothing left outside—among the innate goodness endowed by the Supreme Lord, nothing can stand as its equal! In sum, before anything exists, this origination is the foremost virtue of Heaven and Earth; after things come into existence, this origination is the overarching totality of the human mind. In all the world, there has never been a single goodness not encompassed by origination, nor has there ever been anything outside of origination that can be considered good. If we do not call it the chief of all goodness, what then should we call it? Ah! Such is the greatness of origination as it exists in humanity. Therefore, the sage obtains it as the endowment by which he rises preeminent above the multitude of things, and embodies it as the Way of being able to serve as chief and…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
克君之道者亦惟一元而已乾元之大至是其
無餘蘊乎雖然人君法天致治體元爲先而所
以會乎元德之精者惟學而已蓋天以元運而
神功昭心以學純而天德粹故如天好生萬古
稱元良焉其精一之學可想也噫體元者當懋
於學而調元者其亦加之意乎
有大而能謙必豫故受之以豫
劉師周
同考試官教諭毛批保泰之旨發明殆盡且格調
===
不凡易義之絕唱者
考試官教諭劉批理精詞典深於易者
考試官教諭蔣批善發序卦之旨
觀持盈者之致豫而易卦相承之義昭矣甚矣
有之不可恃也能謙而天下之豫應之矣序卦
之旨深哉且夫治道以太和爲極隆而王者以
謙虛爲盛節大而易盈欲致天下之和也難矣
誠使撫盈成之運而懷抑畏之忱德欲其盛不
敢驕以亢也際亨大之期而存挹損之戒禮欲
punctuated:
克君之道者，亦惟一元而已。乾元之大，至是其無餘蘊乎！雖然，人君法天致治，體元爲先，而所以會乎元德之精者，惟學而已。蓋天以元運而神功昭，心以學純而天德粹，故如天好生，萬古稱元良焉，其精一之學可想也。噫！體元者當懋於學，而調元者其亦加之意乎！

有大而能謙必豫故受之以豫
劉師周
同考試官教諭毛批：保泰之旨，發明殆盡，且格調不凡，易義之絕唱者。
考試官教諭劉批：理精詞典，深於《易》者。
考試官教諭蔣批：善發《序卦》之旨。

觀持盈者之致豫，而《易》卦相承之義昭矣。甚矣，「有」之不可恃也！能謙而天下之豫應之矣，《序卦》之旨深哉！且夫治道以太和爲極隆，而王者以謙虛爲盛節。大而易盈，欲致天下之和也，難矣！誠使撫盈成之運，而懷抑畏之忱，德欲其盛，不敢驕以亢也；際亨大之期，而存挹損之戒，禮欲…
translation_en:
… a true ruler, lies solely in the single Principle of Origination (yuan). The greatness of the Origination of Qian (the Creative) is at this point expressed without holding anything back! Even so, when a ruler models himself on Heaven to bring about order, embodying Origination comes first; yet that by which he grasps the essence of the virtue of Origination is learning alone. For Heaven revolves through Origination and its marvellous achievements are made manifest; the mind is purified through learning and its heavenly virtue becomes unalloyed. Thus, loving life as Heaven does, he is praised for ten thousand ages as supreme in goodness—one may well imagine his learning of pureness and oneness! Alas! He who embodies Origination ought to exert himself in learning, and should not those who harmonize the vital forces of Origination also give heed to this?

"Possessing what is great and yet being able to be modest, there will certainly be harmony and satisfaction (Yu); hence it is followed by the hexagram Yu."
By Liu Shizhou 劉師周.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Mao 毛 comments: The purport of preserving great prosperity is expounded almost exhaustively; moreover, its style is extraordinary—an unmatched masterpiece among essays on the meaning of the Book of Changes (Yi).
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: Precise in principle and classical in diction; one who is profound in the Book of Changes.
Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: Skilfully brings out the purport of the Sequence of the Hexagrams (Xugua).

When we observe how one who maintains fullness brings about harmony and satisfaction (Yu), the meaning of the succession of hexagrams in the Book of Changes becomes clear. Extreme indeed is the fact that "great possession" (Dayou) cannot be presumed upon! When one is able to be modest, the harmony and satisfaction of the whole world respond to him—how profound is the purport of the Sequence of the Hexagrams! Moreover, the Way of governance takes supreme harmony as its highest flourishing, and a true king takes modesty and open-mindedness as his crowning virtue. When things are great, they easily become full to overflowing; to wish then to bring about the harmony of the world is difficult indeed! If indeed, while presiding over a destiny of fullness and completion, one cherishes a sincere feeling of self-restraint and reverence, wishing one's virtue to be abundant and not daring to be arrogant or overbearing; and while encountering an era of great success, one preserves the warning of modesty and self-diminution, wishing one's deportment in ritual to be…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其恭不敢矜以肆也則滿而不溢吾心有至和
焉而協應者成不言之孚上而能下吾身以順
動焉而從欲者妙無心之應撝謙崇於一人而
禮讓刑於百辟以庶官則和於朝焉喜起之風
可想也温恭隆於五位而雍穆達於萬邦以兆
民則和於野焉熈皡之治可繼也蓋謙不期豫
而有必豫之理矣故序卦者於謙而受之以豫
非有所強也先天下而憂者後天下而樂機之
相因則然也受豫而先之以謙非無所為也知
===
===
無疆之恤者享無疆之休道之相通則然也謙
豫相承之義謂不有取於是哉是則豫所以保
天下之有而謙所以和天下之心聖王之治夫
固考之易理而不悖者矣有大者其可以盈乎
噫世之德色於治平者可鑑矣雖然君道盡於
乾而不欲其亢皆謙之意也顧謙主於巽而易
於不振焉故泰之包荒必曰馮河而威如之吉
可以孚交是又以健制謙之道也若後之謙而
未遑寬而無制其亦沉潛而不能剛克者歟故
punctuated: 其恭，不敢矜以肆也。則滿而不溢，吾心有至和焉，而協應者成不言之孚；上而能下，吾身以順動焉，而從欲者妙無心之應。撝謙崇於一人，而禮讓刑於百辟，以庶官則和於朝焉，喜起之風可想也；温恭隆於五位，而雍穆達於萬邦，以兆民則和於野焉，熈皡之治可繼也。蓋謙不期豫，而有必豫之理矣。故《序卦》者於《謙》而受之以《豫》，非有所強也，先天下而憂者，後天下而樂，機之相因則然也；受《豫》而先之以《謙》，非無所為也，知無疆之恤者，享無疆之休，道之相通則然也。《謙》、《豫》相承之義，謂不有取於是哉？是則《豫》所以保天下之有，而《謙》所以和天下之心，聖王之治，夫固考之《易》理而不悖者矣。有大者其可以盈乎？噫！世之德色於治平者，可鑑矣。雖然，君道盡於《乾》，而不欲其亢，皆謙之意也。顧謙主於巽，而易於不振焉。故《泰》之「包荒」，必曰「馮河」，而「威如」之吉，可以「孚交」，是又以健制謙之道也。若後之謙而未遑，寬而無制，其亦沉潛而不能剛克者歟！故
translation_en:
…[he desires that rites] be respectful, not daring to be boastful or unrestrained. Thus, being full yet not overflowing, within one's own heart there is supreme harmony, and those who respond in accord achieve an unspoken trust; being on high yet able to humble oneself, one's person moves in compliance, and those who follow their desires manifest the marvelous response of an uncontrived mind. When unassuming modesty is exalted in the One Man, and courteous deference serves as a model for the hundred lords, then as for the multitude of officials, there is harmony at court, and the spirit of joyful encouragement can be envisioned; when warm reverence flourishes on the fifth-place throne, and harmonious concord reaches the myriad states, then as for the millions of people, there is harmony in the countryside, and the governance of bright tranquility can be continued. Indeed, modesty does not aim at contentment, yet it possesses the principle that inevitably leads to contentment.

Therefore, that the "Sequence of the Hexagrams" (Xugua) follows Modesty (Qian) with Contentment (Yu) is not anything forced: he who worries before the world rejoices after the world, for the mutual causation of pivotal tendencies is naturally so. That in receiving Contentment it precedes it with Modesty is not without purpose: he who knows boundlesssolicitude enjoys boundless blessings, for the mutual penetration of principles is naturally so. Can the meaning of Modesty and Contentment succeeding one another not be drawn from this? Thus Contentment is that whereby one preserves the possessions of the world, and Modesty is that whereby one harmonizes the hearts of the world. The governance of the sage-kings, when examined against the principles of the Changes (Yi), is indeed never in contradiction with them. Can one who possesses greatness afford to be self-satisfied? Alas! Those in the world who put on a self-congratulatory air in times of peace and order should take this as a mirror.

Even so, the ruler's Way is fully realized in the Creative (Qian), and the desire that it not become overbearing is altogether the meaning of modesty. Yet modesty is governed by accommodation, and thus easily lapses into listlessness. Therefore, in Peace (Tai), "embracing the荒 [uncultivated]" must be paired with "fording the river without a boat," and the good fortune of "majestic dignity" (in Great Possession, Dayou) can follow upon "trusting and interacting"—this, again, is the Way of regulating modesty with strength. As for those in later times whose modesty leaves them with no leisure to act [?], and whose寬 (lenience) lacks regulation, are they not sunk in passivity and unable to prevail through firmness? Therefore…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
曰明剛柔之節而後可以言治也
書
后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏
德
阮和咸
同考試官教諭徐批作此多泥體裁致忽本旨結
構自然詞理精到僅見是文耳錄之
考試官教諭劉批認意精深措詞渾雅
考試官教諭蔣批精確有體脉絡尤明
===
大臣陳謨於君惟欲交儆以成化焉夫君臣萬
化之原也能交脩而政乂民善矣大臣陳謨及
此其願治無窮之心乎想其祗承于帝若曰天
下之治致之固不易保之亦甚難今之時雖平
成矣而乘時以保治者其敢不慎乎彼人君主
文命之治其道固惟艱也是必思天心難享而
惕若以凝其精治功難成而奮勵以鼓其志孜
孜然立政安民之憂蓋不敢以治安為幸而實
能圖其艱矣人臣輔文命之治其道亦甚艱也
punctuated:
曰：明剛柔之節，而後可以言治也。

書

「后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。」

阮和咸

同考試官教諭徐批：作此多泥體裁，致忽本旨。結構自然，詞理精到，僅見是文耳，錄之。
考試官教諭劉批：認意精深，措詞渾雅。
考試官教諭蔣批：精確有體，脉絡尤明。

大臣陳謨於君，惟欲交儆以成化焉。夫君臣，萬化之原也，能交脩而政乂民善矣。大臣陳謨及此，其願治無窮之心乎！想其祗承于帝，若曰：天下之治，致之固不易，保之亦甚難。今之時雖平成矣，而乘時以保治者，其敢不慎乎？彼人君主文命之治，其道固惟艱也。是必思天心難享，而惕若以凝其精；治功難成，而奮勵以鼓其志。孜孜然立政安民之憂，蓋不敢以治安為幸，而實能圖其艱矣。人臣輔文命之治，其道亦甚艱也。
translation_en:
… Thus it is said: Only after one understands the proper measure of firmness and gentleness can one speak of governance.

Book of Documents (Shu)

"If the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of being a sovereign, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of being a minister, government will be well-ordered, and the black-haired people will be quick to cultivate virtue."

Ruan Hexian 阮和咸

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Xu's comment: Those who write on this topic mostly cling rigidly to stylistic conventions and consequently neglect the fundamental meaning. Only in this essay does one see a natural structure and precise diction and reasoning; we record it for publication.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Liu's comment: Its grasp of the meaning is profound, and its phrasing is simple and elegant.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Jiang's comment: Precise and well-structured, with an especially clear thread of thought.

When the great minister set forth his counsels before his sovereign, he desired only that they mutually caution each other so as to bring about transformative rule. Now, sovereign and minister are the source of all transformations; when they are able to cultivate their duties together, governance becomes well-ordered and the people become good. For the great minister's counsels to reach this point—was it not out of a boundless desire for good governance! One may imagine him reverently addressing the Emperor [Shun], as if to say: Good order in the world is certainly not easy to bring about, and it is also exceedingly difficult to preserve. Although the present age has achieved peace and order, how could those who avail themselves of the times to preserve this order dare not be cautious? Now, for the sovereign who presides over the governance of civilizing instruction, his Way is indeed full of difficulty. He must reflect that the heart of Heaven is hard to satisfy, and thus remain vigilantly apprehensive so as to concentrate his spirit; and that the achievements of governance are hard to bring to completion, and thus rouse himself to stir up his resolve. Tirelessly concerned with establishing governance and bringing peace to the people, he dares not regard peace and stability as mere good fortune, and is truly able to attend to the difficulties of his position. For the minister who assists in the governance of civilizing instruction, his Way is also exceedingly difficult. …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
是必思身繫安危而愈勵乎精白之念力勝艱
大而益操乎敬事之忱汲汲然惟輔政保民之
圖蓋不敢以豫大爲慶而實克盡其難矣如是
而治化其容已乎吾知政以人而舉也惟上下
既協於同心則百揆乃底於時敘大綱舉焉萬
目張焉蓋業廣於勤而朝於是乎無廢政矣使
交脩之未至能必政之盡乂乎民以德而化也
惟表則既會於明良則兆民自底於從欲易其
惡焉至其中焉蓋民從所好而野於是乎無頑
===
俗矣使交儆之或怠能必民之盡化乎噫大禹
保治之心至矣夫兢業如帝無以復加而克艱
之說禹復惓惓若此豈好爲危言者哉蓋惟舜
有至虛之心故禹之責難不知其過若舜之命
禹而遂以四海困窮危之則其情益切矣豈非
以禹之不自滿假其心猶之己乎噫保治者其
求諸二聖之心可也
君子所其無逸
孫愈賢
punctuated:
是必思身繫安危，而愈勵乎精白之念；力勝艱大，而益操乎敬事之忱。汲汲然惟輔政保民之圖，蓋不敢以豫大爲慶，而實克盡其難矣。如是，而治化其容已乎？吾知政以人而舉也。惟上下既協於同心，則百揆乃底於時敘。大綱舉焉，萬目張焉，蓋業廣於勤，而朝於是乎無廢政矣。使交脩之未至，能必政之盡乂乎？民以德而化也。惟表則既會於明良，則兆民自底於從欲。易其惡焉，至其中焉，蓋民從所好，而野於是乎無頑俗矣。使交儆之或怠，能必民之盡化乎？噫！大禹保治之心至矣。夫兢業如帝，無以復加，而克艱之說，禹復惓惓若此，豈好爲危言者哉？蓋惟舜有至虛之心，故禹之責難不知其過；若舜之命禹，而遂以四海困窮危之，則其情益切矣。豈非以禹之不自滿假，其心猶之己乎？噫！保治者其求諸二聖之心可也。

君子所其無逸
孫愈賢
translation_en:
…He must reflect that his own person is bound up with security and danger, and thus ever more strongly encourage his pure and untainted thoughts; that his strength must bear up under what is difficult and great, and thus ever more firmly hold to his sincere devotion in attending to affairs. Tirelessly planning only to assist in governance and protect the people, he surely does not dare to rejoice in ease and grandeur, but truly is able to exhaust the difficulties of his task. Being thus, how could transformative governance possibly cease? I know that governance is raised up through men. Only when sovereign and minister are already united in being of one mind are all the general affairs brought to timely order. The great guiding principles are raised up, and the myriad details are spread open; for achievements are broadened through diligence, and thus in the court there are no neglected policies. If mutual cultivation had not reached the utmost, could one be certain that governance would be completely ordered? The people are transformed through virtue. Only when the standards set at the top already converge in an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers do the millions of the people naturally come to follow what is desired of them. Changing their wickedness, they arrive at the mean; for the people follow what their superiors love, and thus in the countryside there are no obstinate customs. If mutual admonition were ever negligent, could one be certain that the people would be completely transformed? Ah! Great Yu’s heart in preserving good governance reached the utmost! Now, in being cautious andreverent like the Emperor [Shun], nothing more could be added; yet in his doctrine of overcoming difficulties, Yu was again so earnestly insistent as this—was he merely fond of uttering alarming words? It was surely because Shun possessed a supremely receptive mind that Yu, in urging difficult duties upon him, did not consider it excessive. And when Shun charged Yu, and thereupon warned him with the danger of the Four Seas falling into distress and poverty, his feelings were even more urgent. Was it not because Yu was free of self-satisfaction and arrogance, his mind being just like Shun’s own? Ah! Those who would preserve good governance may well seek it in the minds of these two sages.

"The noble man makes 'without-idleness' his dwelling-place" (Junzi suo qi wu yi) [Book of Documents, "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wu yi)]
By Sun Yuxian

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭徐批周公忠愛勤懇子能言之且
不費詞擅場之作也
考試官敎諭劉批語意懇到得忠告體
考試官敎諭蔣批理明詞達義之隹者
大臣表君子之居勤忠告之意至矣夫天下之
治成於勤也以勤作所其君子之所以致治乎
周公因成王初政而欲防其漸也故儆之若曰
王業難於持盈君心貴於慎始嗣王新服厥命
尚其仰法於君子乎蓋君子一身天下之安危
===
係焉居已於逸而欲貽天下之安者難矣故以
崇高非得肆之地也而天行為健隨在皆兢業
之圖以盈成非可恃之業也而日强為敬無往
非勵精之念自昧爽以至日昃時雖屢遷而居
之愈微則防之愈切將以為居身之珎而夙夜
罔不勤焉自臨御以至宴息居雖不齊而所處
益密則所操益慎將以為宅身之要而出入罔
不欽焉上而祈天則精明之念與於穆相為感
孚而兢兢然對越之不違蓋不待承之祭祀而
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭徐批：周公忠愛勤懇，子能言之，且不費詞，擅場之作也。
考試官敎諭劉批：語意懇到，得忠告體。
考試官敎諭蔣批：理明詞達，義之隹者。

大臣表君子之居勤，忠告之意至矣。夫天下之治，成於勤也；以勤作所，其君子之所以致治乎！周公因成王初政，而欲防其漸也，故儆之若曰：王業難於持盈，君心貴於慎始。嗣王新服厥命，尚其仰法於君子乎！蓋君子一身，天下之安危係焉；居已於逸，而欲貽天下之安者，難矣。故以崇高非得肆之地也，而天行為健，隨在皆兢業之圖；以盈成非可恃之業也，而日强為敬，無往非勵精之念。自昧爽以至日昃，時雖屢遷，而居之愈微，則防之愈切，將以為居身之珎，而夙夜罔不勤焉；自臨御以至宴息，居雖不齊，而所處益密，則所操益慎，將以為宅身之要，而出入罔不欽焉。上而祈天，則精明之念與於穆相為感孚，而兢兢然對越之不違，蓋不待承之祭祀，而
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Instructor Xu, comments: "You are able to articulate the Duke of Zhou's loyalty, affection, and earnestness, and without wasting words—a masterwork of the examination hall."
Examiner, Instructor Liu, comments: "The words and meaning are earnest and thorough, capturing the proper style of loyal admonition."
Examiner, Instructor Jiang, comments: "The principles are clear and the expression is fluent; a fine piece of exposition."

When the great minister sets forth how the noble man abides in diligence, his intention of offering loyal admonition reaches the utmost. Now, the governance of the world is achieved through diligence; taking diligence as one's dwelling place—is this not how the noble man brings about order! Because King Cheng was just beginning his personal rule, the Duke of Zhou wished to guard against nascent laxity, and so he cautioned him as if to say: "In the royal enterprise, it is hard to preserve fullness; in the ruler's mind, what is珍貴 [valued] is prudence at the outset. Now that the successor king has newly taken up his mandate, may he look up and model himself upon the noble man!" For upon the single person of the noble man hangs the security or peril of the world; to place oneself in ease and yet wish to bequeath security to the world is difficult indeed. Therefore, he regards exalted height not as a place where one may indulge oneself, and taking the movement of Heaven as his model of vigor, everywhere he engages in cautious and fearful planning; he regards accomplished fullness not as a patrimony to be relied upon, and taking daily self-strengthening as his reverence, in every instance he harbors thoughts of rousing his spirit. From dawn until the sun inclines westward, though the hours repeatedly shift, the more subtly he abides in it, the more earnestly he guards himself; he would take it as the treasure in which his person abides, and morning and night there is nothing in which he is not diligent. From presiding at court to retiring for rest, though his situations vary, the more closely he examines his circumstances, the more prudently he maintains his resolve; he would take it as the essential principle for settling his person, and in going out and coming in there is nothing in which he is not reverent. Above, in praying to Heaven, his pure and bright thoughts mutually resonate and accord with the profound and august unseen, and cautiously and fearfully he responds to its presence without departing from it; indeed, he does not wait until he presents sacrifices, for…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
莫非上帝攸臨之所矣其斯以熙鴻號於無窮
乎下而保民則憂勤之衷與衆志相爲聯屬而
皇皇然保乂之不懈蓋不必措諸設施而莫非
顧畏民畧之所矣其斯以基鴻業於弗替乎要
之開泰者垂懿恭之範保泰者紹緝熙之傳無
逸乃逸而天下萬世享其安矣吾王其懋之哉
雖然害治之弊非一端而周公獨以無逸爲戒
何哉蓋人情勞則思善逸則思淫縱欲敗度皆
自逸之一念啓之也故創業之君常恐佚豫之
不足以貽謀而繼體者敢不慎哉噫成王幼冲
之年逸欲未萌而周公豫防之此其忠之所以
爲大也
詩
大人占之衆維魚矣實維豐年旐維旟矣
室家溱溱
錫應兆
同考試官學正梁批中興氣象模寫燦然而末歸
保終意尤覺深邃宜錄以式
punctuated:
莫非上帝攸臨之所矣，其斯以熙鴻號於無窮乎！下而保民，則憂勤之衷與衆志相爲聯屬，而皇皇然保乂之不懈，蓋不必措諸設施，而莫非顧畏民畧之所矣，其斯以基鴻業於弗替乎！要之，開泰者垂懿恭之範，保泰者紹緝熙之傳；無逸乃逸，而天下萬世享其安矣。吾王其懋之哉！雖然，害治之弊非一端，而周公獨以「無逸」爲戒，何哉？蓋人情勞則思善，逸則思淫，縱欲敗度，皆自逸之一念啓之也。故創業之君，常恐佚豫之不足以貽謀，而繼體者敢不慎哉！噫！成王幼冲之年，逸欲未萌，而周公豫防之，此其忠之所以爲大也。
詩
「大人占之，衆維魚矣，實維豐年；旐維旟矣，室家溱溱。」
錫應兆
同考試官學正梁批：中興氣象，模寫燦然，而末歸保終，意尤覺深邃，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…there is nowhere that is not a place where the Lord on High draws near. Is it not by this means that one expands the great title endlessly? Below, in protecting the people, one's anxious and diligent heart is joined with the will of the multitude, and one urgently protects and governs them without slackening; indeed, one need not wait to put this into concrete measures before there is nowhere that is not a place of heeding and fearing the perils of the common people [reading 畧 as 碞]. Is it not by this means that one lays the foundation of the great enterprise so that it never declines? In sum, he who inaugurates an era of peace hands down a model of admirable reverence, and he who preserves an era of peace continues the tradition of radiant continuity. By taking no ease, one achieves true ease, and the realm for ten thousand generations enjoys its tranquility. May my King strive at this!

Even so, the abuses that harm governance are not of a single kind; why then did the Duke of Zhou warn solely against "taking ease"? It is because in human nature, toil makes one think of goodness, whereas ease makes one think of licentiousness; indulging desires and ruining the standards of conduct are all set in motion by a single thought of ease. Therefore, a ruler who founds a dynasty always fears that idleness and pleasure will fail to leave a good plan for his descendants—how then could a successor to the throne dare not be cautious? Alas! During King Cheng's tender years, desires for ease had not yet sprouted, yet the Duke of Zhou guarded against them in advance: this is why his loyalty was so great.

Classic of Poetry (Shi)

"The grand diviner interprets it: 'Locusts becoming fish—truly it is a year of abundance; tortoise-and-snake banners becoming falcon banners—households will be teeming.'"

By Xi Yingzhao 錫應兆.

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Liang comments: The atmosphere of dynastic revival is brilliantly depicted, and at the end it returns to the theme of preserving the achievement to the finish, making the meaning feel especially profound. It is fitting to record this as a model.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉批春融典麗結意獨精
考試官教諭蔣批鋪張盛治意到詞足
詩人於牧人之夢而決其富庶之徵焉夫國家
以富庶爲祥也而占於牧人之夢焉不可以觀
中興之氣象乎詩詠無羊以志治者若曰國家
之興也固必有鬼神以司其柄亦必有禎祥以
顯其機眾維魚而旐維旟牧人之夢誠異矣大
人者司占而決疑者也其將謂之何哉蓋我周
以農事開國而豐年綏於萬邦維昔之富不可
===
===
及矣今夢眾而魚固以少致多者也其必天祐
斯民而歲月無易貽之以順成之休帝昭明賜
而稼穡用登溥之以豐穰之慶以足民食則三
農不匱也以厚邦儲則九賦可繼也蓋吾王憂
旱之志固足以兆康而茲特洩其秘耳其它自
古有年之盛不重光乎我周以聚民立國而庶
繁徵於奕世維昔之庶不可及矣今夢旐而旟
固以寡致眾者也其必太和洋溢而生齒日繁
相安於樂利之境順治鼓舞而歸附日眾益顯
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉批：春融典麗，結意獨精。
考試官教諭蔣批：鋪張盛治，意到詞足。

詩人於牧人之夢，而決其富庶之徵焉。夫國家以富庶爲祥也，而占於牧人之夢焉，不可以觀中興之氣象乎？《詩》詠《無羊》以志治者，若曰：國家之興也，固必有鬼神以司其柄，亦必有禎祥以顯其機。眾維魚而旐維旟，牧人之夢誠異矣。大人者，司占而決疑者也，其將謂之何哉？蓋我周以農事開國，而豐年綏於萬邦，維昔之富不可及矣。今夢眾而魚，固以少致多者也。其必天祐斯民，而歲月無易，貽之以順成之休；帝昭明賜，而稼穡用登，溥之以豐穰之慶。以足民食，則三農不匱也；以厚邦儲，則九賦可繼也。蓋吾王憂旱之志，固足以兆康，而茲特洩其秘耳。其它自古有年之盛，不重光乎？我周以聚民立國，而庶繁徵於奕世，維昔之庶不可及矣。今夢旐而旟，固以寡致眾者也。其必太和洋溢，而生齒日繁，相安於樂利之境；順治鼓舞，而歸附日眾，益顯
translation_en:
Examiner Instructor Liu comments: Warm as spring, classical and elegant; the concluding idea is uniquely refined.
Examiner Instructor Jiang comments: It elaborates grandly on a flourishing rule; the meaning hits the mark and the diction is ample.

From the herdsman's dream, the poet determines the portents of wealth and populousness. Now, the state regards wealth and populousness as auspicious signs; when these are divined from the dream of a herdsman, can one not observe therein the spirit of a dynastic restoration? The Book of Odes (Shijing) sings "Wu yang" (No Sheep) to record good governance, as if to say: When a state rises, there must surely be spirits and gods to hold the handle of its destiny, and there must also be auspicious portents to manifest its subtle workings. "Locusts—no, fish; tortoise-and-snake banners—no, falcon banners": the herdsman's dream was truly extraordinary. The grand diviner is the one who presides over divination and resolves doubts; what then will he pronounce of it? Indeed, our Zhou dynasty founded the state upon agriculture, and years of abundance brought peace to the myriad domains; the wealth of former times could seemed beyond reach. Now, to dream of locusts becoming fish is surely a sign of the few giving rise to the many. It must be that Heaven blesses these people, and the seasons and months suffer no irregularity, bequeathing to them the blessing of smooth harvests; the Supreme Lord displays His bright gift, and the sown and reaped grain ascends to ripeness, spreading universally the joy of abundant crops. By making the people's food sufficient, the three classes of farmers suffer no want; by enriching the state's reserves, the nine revenues can be sustained. Indeed, our King's anxious concern over drought was already sufficient to presage prosperity, and this dream merely discloses that secret. Compared to the flourishing of "good years since antiquity" [?], does it not shine anew? Our Zhou dynasty established the state by gathering the people, and a thriving populace was evidenced through successive generations; the populousness of former times seemed beyond reach. Now, to dream of tortoise-and-snake banners becoming falcon banners is surely a sign of the sparse giving rise to the multitude. It must be that supreme harmony overflows and the registered population grows daily more numerous, dwelling together in peace within a realm of joy and benefit; harmonious rule inspires them, and those who turn in allegiance grow daily more numerous, increasingly manifesting…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
乎明昌之運列之邦畿無怨曠也布之甸服無
仳離也蓋吾王還定之仁固足以得衆而兹特
示其端耳其視咸和萬民之盛不再見乎吁民
富則君不患貧矣民庶則君不患寡矣以極治
之象而兆於牧人之微詩人之頌亦婉矣哉蓋
宣王側身脩行回天保民富庶之祥乃其自致
而時方懼其鮮終焉故托之夢兆而歆其無忘
厥初耳惜千畝不藉料民太原而無羊之響息
矣憂國者其慎諸
===
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸墍
李維美
同考試官學正梁批致願嫡嗣用答君福詩人意也
此作得之宜錄
考試官教諭劉批發明保治安民詞理具備
考試官教諭蔣批溫厚懇切得詩人旨
詩人願臣之愛君而切於保泰之慮焉夫君心
係天下之安危也政勤而民安焉非忠君者之
至願哉想其願君福而致望於嫡嗣者有曰君
punctuated:
乎明昌之運。列之邦畿，無怨曠也；布之甸服，無仳離也。蓋吾王還定之仁，固足以得衆，而兹特示其端耳。其視咸和萬民之盛，不再見乎？吁！民富則君不患貧矣，民庶則君不患寡矣。以極治之象，而兆於牧人之微，詩人之頌亦婉矣哉！蓋宣王側身脩行，回天保民，富庶之祥，乃其自致；而時方懼其鮮終焉，故托之夢兆，而歆其無忘厥初耳。惜千畝不藉，料民太原，而《無羊》之響息矣。憂國者其慎諸！
百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸墍。
李維美
同考試官學正梁批：致願嫡嗣，用答君福，詩人意也。此作得之，宜錄。
考試官教諭劉批：發明保治安民，詞理具備。
考試官教諭蔣批：溫厚懇切，得詩人旨。
詩人願臣之愛君，而切於保泰之慮焉。夫君心係天下之安危也，政勤而民安焉，非忠君者之至願哉？想其願君福而致望於嫡嗣者，有曰：君
translation_en:
… [even more manifest] in an era of bright prosperity. Arrayed across the royal domain, there will be none who are resentful or left unmarried; spread throughout the royal dependencies, there will be none who are separated or scattered. Indeed, our king's benevolence in restoring and settling the people is inherently sufficient to win the multitude, and this dream merely reveals the beginning of it. Compared to the flourishing age when harmony prevailed among all the myriad people, shall we not see it once again? Ah! When the people are wealthy, the ruler need not worry about poverty; when the people are numerous, the ruler need not worry about scarcity. To take the image of utmost good governance and foreshadow it through the humble figure of a herdsman—how subtle indeed is the poet's eulogy! For King Xuan humbled himself and cultivated his conduct, turning back Heaven's wrath and protecting the people. The auspicious signs of wealth and population were thus brought about by himself. Yet the men of the time feared that he might rarely carry things through to the end; therefore they entrusted their message to dream omens, inspiring him not to forget his initial resolve. Alas, when he later failed to plow the thousand-mu sacred field and numbered the people at Taiyuan, the echoes of the ode "Wu yang" (No Sheep) died away. Let those who worry for the state take heed of this!

"The hundred lords and minister-officials hold dear the Son of Heaven; / Unremitting in their positions, / Thereby the people find rest." (Book of Odes, "Jia le")

By Li Weimei 李維美.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Liang 梁: Expressing wishes for the legitimate heir as a way to respond to the ruler's blessings is the poet's intent. This composition grasps it and ought to be selected.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu 劉: It elucidates the preservation of order and the pacification of the people; both diction and reasoning are complete.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣: Gentle, generous, and earnest, it captures the poet's purport.

The poet wishes for the ministers to love their ruler, and is earnest in his concern for preserving great peace. Now, the ruler's mind determines the security or peril of the realm; that governance be diligent and the people at peace—is this not the supreme wish of those loyal to their ruler? Imagine how, in wishing blessings upon the ruler and placing his hopes in the legitimate heir, he says: When ruler…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
臣相遇以喜起爲情以交儆爲益者也王嗣立
綱紀以燕及其臣矣乃諸臣之心何如哉彼百
辟屏翰於外願治爲甚殷也仰明聖之度自切
翼戴之忱而元首股肱其情油然不容已焉卿
士輔相於內分義爲愈厚也幸際遇之隆益懷
圖報之念而手足腹心其情藹然不能釋焉然
豈敢以治安爲獻而不爲國家深長之慮者乎
蓋謹始而慮終者人君之所以保其泰也憂治
而危明者忠臣之所以防其漸也故惟明於治
===
忽之理而迪德凝命遠紹乎無逸之風察於否
泰之機而慎位保民丕振乎永清之烈以總乾
綱雖盈成猶初服焉則上有恒心下有恒愛而
熙洽之運將怙冒於無疆也吾君宜民之治玆
其有寄乎以飭法紀雖厚終猶虔始焉則勞以
一人逸以天下而治安之澤固昭升於不替也
吾君保佑之命玆其益申乎此則諸臣之心而
君福之所以爲隆者也吁君以善治安其臣臣
以保治媚其君一頌禱而計切國家忠哉周臣
punctuated: 臣相遇，以喜起爲情，以交儆爲益者也。王嗣立綱紀，以燕及其臣矣，乃諸臣之心何如哉？彼百辟屏翰於外，願治爲甚殷也；仰明聖之度，自切翼戴之忱，而元首股肱，其情油然不容已焉。卿士輔相於內，分義爲愈厚也；幸際遇之隆，益懷圖報之念，而手足腹心，其情藹然不能釋焉。然豈敢以治安爲獻，而不爲國家深長之慮者乎？蓋謹始而慮終者，人君之所以保其泰也；憂治而危明者，忠臣之所以防其漸也。故惟明於治忽之理，而迪德凝命，遠紹乎無逸之風；察於否泰之機，而慎位保民，丕振乎永清之烈。以總乾綱，雖盈成猶初服焉，則上有恒心，下有恒愛，而熙洽之運，將怙冒於無疆也，吾君宜民之治，玆其有寄乎！以飭法紀，雖厚終猶虔始焉，則勞以一人，逸以天下，而治安之澤，固昭升於不替也，吾君保佑之命，玆其益申乎！此則諸臣之心，而君福之所以爲隆者也。吁！君以善治安其臣，臣以保治媚其君，一頌禱而計切國家，忠哉周臣
translation_en: … sovereign and ministers meet, they take delight and inspiration as their sentiment, and mutual admonition as their benefit. Now that the king's heir has established the overarching principles and regulations so as to bring comfort and peace to his ministers, what then are the hearts of the various ministers like? Those hundred lords who act as screens and bulwarks in the outer regions are most earnest in their desire for good governance; looking up to the magnanimity of the enlightened sage, they naturally feel a keen sincerity in supporting and upholding him, and like the head and limbs, their affection wells up irrepressibly. The noble ministers who assist and counsel within the court have an even deeper sense of duty and righteousness; fortunate in the splendor of their encounter with such a ruler, they cherish all the more the thought of repaying his grace, and like hands, feet, and heart, their genial affection cannot be set aside. Yet how could they dare merely to offer up praise of peace and order without taking deep and far-reaching thought for the state? For being cautious at the beginning and mindful of the end is how a ruler preserves his prosperity; worrying in times of order and feeling peril in times of enlightenment is how a loyal minister guards against incipient decline. Therefore, may he clearly understand the principles of order and neglect, walk in virtue and consolidate the Mandate, distantly continuing the legacy of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi); may he discern the pivotal moments of stagnation and prosperity, be cautious in his position and protect the people, grandly rousing the meritorious achievement of eternal peace. By gathering up the sovereign authority, even in the fullness of achievement he acts as though at the very beginning of his reign; then above there will be a constant mind, below there will be constant affection, and a destiny of bright harmony will shelter and cover the realm without bound—shall not our sovereign's governance that suits the people find its reliance in this! By rectifying the laws and disciplines, even in bringing things to a generous conclusion he remains as reverent as at the start; then through the toil of the One Man, ease is brought to all under Heaven, and the blessings of order and peace will surely rise brightly without cease—shall not our sovereign's Mandate of protection and aid be ever more extended through this! Such is the heart of the various ministers, and the reason why the sovereign's blessings are so abundant. Ah! The sovereign comforts his ministers through good governance, and the ministers show devotion to their sovereign by preserving that governance. In a single prayer of praise, their counsels are earnestly devoted to the state—how loyal indeed was the Zhou ministers' …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之愛君也蓋假樂之陳用答鳧鷖固未知其嫡
嗣爲何如而勤政之效婉然可即得非以王儲
爲國本無逸爲家法而謀及其子孫者亦以規
及其君耶噫作之者顯德宜人述之者勤政致
媚信乎天下之治必君臣交泰而成也
春秋
冬城向桓公十有六年齊師宋師曹師城
邢僖公元年
劉文徵
同考試官教諭陶批聖人慎用民力意在言外此
作以麗詞發至理而體裁峻潔非徒作者
考試官教諭劉批對待森然峻整可誦
考試官教諭蔣批詞意嚴整經世之見也
===
春秋兩紀役之合時義者欲人君之重民力也
甚矣仁君不盡民之力也此春秋於城向城邢
而竝書以示意乎且夫善爲國者先保其民善
保民者必愛其力嘗觀春秋城向城邢之書而
知之矣彼向圯其城魯於冬而城之孰不曰龍
punctuated:
之愛君也！蓋《假樂》之陳，用答《鳧鷖》，固未知其嫡嗣爲何如，而勤政之效婉然可即。得非以王儲爲國本，無逸爲家法，而謀及其子孫者，亦以規及其君耶？噫！作之者顯德宜人，述之者勤政致媚，信乎天下之治，必君臣交泰而成也。

春秋
「冬，城向。」〔桓公十有六年〕「齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。」〔僖公元年〕
劉文徵
同考試官教諭陶批：聖人慎用民力，意在言外。此作以麗詞發至理，而體裁峻潔，非徒作者。
考試官教諭劉批：對待森然，峻整可誦。
考試官教諭蔣批：詞意嚴整，經世之見也。

《春秋》兩紀役之合時義者，欲人君之重民力也。甚矣，仁君不盡民之力也！此《春秋》於城向、城邢而竝書以示意乎？且夫善爲國者，先保其民；善保民者，必愛其力。嘗觀《春秋》城向、城邢之書而知之矣。彼向圯其城，魯於冬而城之，孰不曰龍
translation_en:
… love their ruler! Indeed, the presentation of the ode "Glorious and Joyous" (Jia le), used in reply to "Wild Ducks and Widgeons" (Fu yi), certainly could not yet know what the legitimate heir would be like, yet the efficacy of diligent governance could be gently approached through it. Could it not be that taking the royal heir as the foundation of the state and "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wu yi) as the family law—thus taking counsel for his descendants—was also a way of extending admonition to the ruler himself? Ah! He who initiates it manifests virtue and does right by the people; he who continues it is diligent in governance and inspires devotion. Truly, the good order of the world is necessarily achieved through the harmonious communion of ruler and minister.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In winter, [they] walled Xiang." [Sixteenth year of Duke Huan] "The army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Cao walled Xing." [First year of Duke Xi]
By Liu Wenzheng 劉文徵.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Tao 陶 comments: The sage's caution in employing the people's labor lies beyond the literal words. This essay uses elegant diction to bring forth ultimate principle, while its structure is lofty and pure—not the work of a mere ordinary writer.
Examiner, Instructor Liu 劉 comments: The parallelisms are strictly arrayed, lofty and well-ordered, worthy of recitation.
Examiner, Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: The diction and meaning are rigorous and well-ordered, showing insight into statecraft.

When the Spring and Autumn Annals twice records corvée labor that accorded with Both season and righteousness, it desires that the ruler of men attach importance to the people's strength. Extreme indeed is the benevolent ruler's refusal to exhaust the strength of the people! Is it for this reason that the Spring and Autumn Annals writes down both the walling of Xiang and the walling of Xing to convey its meaning? Moreover, he who is skilled at governing a state first protects his people; he who is skilled at protecting the people necessarily cherishes their strength. I have observed the records of walling Xiang and walling Xing in the Spring and Autumn Annals and understood this. Now, Xiang had its walls fall into ruin, and Lu walled it in winter. Who would not say that when the Dragon [constellation] …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
見戒事火見致用時可以使民矣殊不知役可
以時而興勞不以時而免也耕穫甫畢於三時
而勤動未息於終歲將無苦於力作而興楊柳
雨雪之悲者乎使以時而略之則牛羊其人者
皆以時為辭而不恤其私矣君子謂時而不勞
乎民可無誌也時而不能不勞乎民寧不為之
動念哉此城向之所以書也邢遷於狄齊率眾
而城之孰不曰彌縫其闕匡救其災義可以役
民矣殊不知民可以義而役力不以義而弛也
===
===
干戈甫息於捍患而版築遂興於設防將無疲
於奔命而起束薪束蒲之嘆者乎使因義而削
之則秦越其民者皆以義為解而不體其情矣
君子謂義而不勞乎民可無紀也義而不能不
勞乎民能不為之致意哉此城邢之所以書也
吁合時猶慎而況於不時乎合義且謹而況於
不義乎知此而重民力則食足生遂化行俗美
胥有賴矣春秋之望於仁君者至哉雖然魯納
突而城向義未盡協也特視夏城中丘彼善於
punctuated: 見戒事、火見致用，時可以使民矣。殊不知役可以時而興，勞不以時而免也。耕穫甫畢於三時，而勤動未息於終歲，將無苦於力作而興「楊柳雨雪」之悲者乎？使以時而略之，則牛羊其人者，皆以時為辭，而不恤其私矣。君子謂時而不勞乎民，可無誌也；時而不能不勞乎民，寧不為之動念哉？此城向之所以書也。邢遷於狄，齊率眾而城之，孰不曰彌縫其闕、匡救其災，義可以役民矣。殊不知民可以義而役，力不以義而弛也。干戈甫息於捍患，而版築遂興於設防，將無疲於奔命而起「束薪束蒲」之嘆者乎？使因義而削之，則秦越其民者，皆以義為解，而不體其情矣。君子謂義而不勞乎民，可無紀也；義而不能不勞乎民，能不為之致意哉？此城邢之所以書也。吁！合時猶慎，而況於不時乎？合義且謹，而況於不義乎？知此而重民力，則食足生遂、化行俗美，胥有賴矣。《春秋》之望於仁君者至哉！雖然，魯納突而城向，義未盡協也，特視夏城中丘，彼善於
translation_en:
…appears, one prepares for labor, and when the Fire Star appears, one puts the materials to use—so the season was proper for employing the people. Yet they fail to realize that while corvée may be initiated in the proper season, the toil is not eliminated simply because it is seasonal. When plowing and harvesting have barely finished after the three agricultural seasons, and yet diligent toil does not cease at the end of the year, will the people not suffer from the hard labor and raise the lament of "the willows and the falling snow" [from the Book of Odes, "Caiwei"]? If the chronicler had omitted the entry simply because it was done in season, then rulers who treat their people like cattle and sheep would all use seasonal timing as an excuse and show no compassion for their private needs. The gentleman says that if an undertaking is seasonal and does not weary the people, it need not be recorded; but when it is seasonal and yet cannot avoid wearying the people, how could one not be moved to concern for them? This is why the walling of Xiang was recorded.

When Xing was forced to relocate because of the Di tribes, Qi led the allied multitude to wall its new settlement. Who would not say that in patching up what was breached and rescuing them from calamity, the cause was righteous enough to mobilize the people for corvée? Yet they fail to realize that while the people may be mobilized in the name of righteousness, their physical strength is not spared simply because the cause is righteous. When shields and spears have barely rested from warding off disaster, and rammed-earth construction is immediately begun to erect defenses, will the people not be exhausted from rushing about on orders and raise the sigh of "bundled firewood and bundled rushes" [from the Book of Odes, "Yang zhi shui"]? If Confucius had deleted the entry because the cause was righteous, then rulers who regard their people's suffering with the indifference of Qin toward Yue would all use righteousness as an excuse and fail to sympathize with their feelings. The gentleman says that if an undertaking is righteous and does not weary the people, it need not be chronicled; but when it is righteous and yet cannot avoid wearying the people, how could one not pay heed to their plight? This is why the walling of Xing was recorded.

Alas! If one must be cautious even when acting in the proper season, how much more so when out of season? If one must be circumspect even when acting in accordance with righteousness, how much more so when unrighteous? If a ruler understands this and values the people's strength, then sufficiency of food, fulfillment of livelihood, the spread of moral transformation, and the excellence of customs will all depend upon it. How profound is the Spring and Autumn Annals' expectation for a benevolent ruler! Even so, when Lu installed Duke Li [Tu] and walled Xiang, its righteousness was not entirely fitting; it was merely that compared to walling Zhongqiu in summer, the former was somewhat better than…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
此耳若邢被狄難一旅可却乃師次聶北俟其
遷而城之得無養亂以爲功乎噫薄德之譏桓
固有以來之也
齊小白入于齊莊公九年公會齊人宋人
救鄭莊公二十有八年齊人救邢閔公
元年秋八月諸侯盟于首止僖公五年
九月戊辰諸侯盟于葵丘僖公九年
彭商英
同考試官教諭陶批君臣分義勞効條析不遺而
議論正大深得屬詞之體宜録之以式明經者
考試官教諭劉批不牽文義獨暢本旨
考試官教諭蔣批是非定於聖人桓仲當爲心服
===
春秋明嗣君之當立因有取於其臣之功焉夫
桓之有齊分之正也即管仲功不廢于天下而
不益見其當立乎昔子糾爭立而小白入齊內
無所稟上無所承白亦猶之糾也而春秋獨繫
之齊者何哉君子曰少不先長分也位定於分
制也臨淄之地白所宜居而觀於管仲之功尤
punctuated:
此耳。若邢被狄難，一旅可却，乃師次聶北，俟其遷而城之，得無養亂以爲功乎？噫！薄德之譏，桓固有以來之也。

「齊小白入于齊〔莊公九年〕。公會齊人、宋人救鄭〔莊公二十有八年〕。齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕。秋，八月，諸侯盟于首止〔僖公五年〕。九月，戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕。」
彭商英
同考試官教諭陶批：君臣分義勞効，條析不遺，而議論正大，深得屬詞之體，宜録之以式明經者。
考試官教諭劉批：不牽文義，獨暢本旨。
考試官教諭蔣批：是非定於聖人，桓、仲當爲心服。

《春秋》明嗣君之當立，因有取於其臣之功焉。夫桓之有齊，分之正也；即管仲功不廢于天下，而不益見其當立乎？昔子糾爭立而小白入齊，內無所稟，上無所承，白亦猶之糾也，而《春秋》獨繫之齊者，何哉？君子曰：少不先長，分也；位定於分，制也。臨淄之地，白所宜居，而觀於管仲之功，尤
translation_en:
… this one. As for Xing suffering the calamity of the Di tribes, a single brigade could have repelled them; yet the army halted at Niebei, waiting until Xing relocated before walling its city—was this not fostering disorder so as to claim merit? Alas! The criticism of being thin in virtue was indeed something Duke Huan brought upon himself.

"Xiaobai of Qi entered Qi [ninth year of Duke Zhuang]. The Duke met with men of Qi and men of Song to rescue Zheng [twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang]. Men of Qi rescued Xing [first year of Duke Min]. In autumn, in the eighth month, the feudal lords made a covenant at Shouzhi [fifth year of Duke Xi]. In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu [ninth year of Duke Xi]."
Peng Shangying
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Tao: The duty and righteousness between ruler and minister, as well as their toils and achievements, are analyzed point by point without omission. The argument is upright and grand, deeply grasping the proper form of connecting the Annals' entries; it is fitting to record this as a model for those who explicate the Classics.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu: Not bogged down by literal phrasing, it uniquely and fluently brings out the fundamental purport.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jiang: Right and wrong are settled by the Sage; Duke Huan and Guan Zhong would surely submit in their hearts.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) clarifies that the succeeding ruler ought to be established, and consequently approves the merits of his minister. Now, Duke Huan's possession of Qi was proper according to his status; even looking at how Guan Zhong's merits were not neglected throughout the realm, does one not see all the more clearly that he ought to have been established? Formerly, when Prince Jiu contended for the succession and Xiaobai entered Qi, internally he had no mandate from within the state, and above he had noinvestiture from the King—Xiaobai was in the same position as Jiu. Why then did the Spring and Autumn Annals uniquely attach him to "Qi"? The gentleman says: That the younger does not precede the elder is proper status; that the throne is settled according to status is the institution. The territory of Linzi was where Xiaobai ought to dwell, and when one observes the merits of Guan Zhong, it is especially …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
足徵焉蓋君子能爲可用而不能必用故必事
君以自顯亦必得君而有成也若仲之事桓豈
苟且以赴功名之會者哉徙義致主既以其才
而成當時之富强長慮遠謀又以其身而係天
下之輕重故桓之時夷狄橫矣中國諸侯誰與
安之乃仲獨相桓而以其節制之師一救乎鄭
再救乎邢焉冠裳鱗介凜然其防而夷不敢以
干夏者非其廟筭之鎮定乎桓之時周道衰矣
中國諸侯誰其尊之乃仲獨相桓而以其秩序
===
之經一盟首止再盟葵丘焉國儲王禁昭然其
分而下不敢以僭上者非其偉略之運用乎故
功在當時則當時稱其仁功在後世則後世蒙
其賜萬世公論定於聖人而獨於仲亟許之信
乎仲之無可議也而仲之所事者復何議哉故
曰小白之當立也雖然夫子之許仲固謂其擇
君而成事也乃不能致桓於王道而伯業且未
竟焉則仲豈粹然無議者乎噫學術既定伯不
可以王矣若射鉤之戒仲固諄諄而桓自怠焉
punctuated: 足徵焉。蓋君子能爲可用，而不能必用，故必事君以自顯，亦必得君而有成也。若仲之事桓，豈苟且以赴功名之會者哉？徙義致主，既以其才而成當時之富强；長慮遠謀，又以其身而係天下之輕重。故桓之時，夷狄橫矣，中國諸侯誰與安之？乃仲獨相桓，而以其節制之師，一救乎鄭，再救乎邢焉。冠裳鱗介，凜然其防，而夷不敢以干夏者，非其廟筭之鎮定乎？桓之時，周道衰矣，中國諸侯誰其尊之？乃仲獨相桓，而以其秩序之經，一盟首止，再盟葵丘焉。國儲王禁，昭然其分，而下不敢以僭上者，非其偉略之運用乎？故功在當時，則當時稱其仁；功在後世，則後世蒙其賜。萬世公論定於聖人，而獨於仲亟許之，信乎仲之無可議也，而仲之所事者復何議哉？故曰小白之當立也。雖然，夫子之許仲，固謂其擇君而成事也。乃不能致桓於王道，而伯業且未竟焉，則仲豈粹然無議者乎？噫！學術既定，伯不可以王矣。若射鉤之戒，仲固諄諄，而桓自怠焉，
translation_en: … suffices to prove it. For a gentleman can make himself fit for employment, yet cannot guarantee that he will be employed; therefore he must serve a ruler in order to distinguish himself, and must also find the right ruler in order to achieve success. In the case of Guan Zhong's 管仲 serving Duke Huan 桓, how could he have been one who compromised his principles merely to seize an opportunity for merit and fame? Shifting toward righteousness and devoting himself to his lord, he at once used his talents to achieve the wealth and power of the day; with farsighted plans and deep counsel, he furthermore bore in his own person the weight of the entire world. Thus, in Duke Huan's time, the barbarian tribes ran rampant; among the feudal lords of the Central States, who was there to bring them peace? Yet Guan Zhong alone served as chief minister to Duke Huan, and with his disciplined armies rescued Zheng 鄭 once, and again rescued Xing 邢. Caps and robes [of the civilized] and scales and shells [of the barbarians] were kept strictly separated by an awe-inspiring barrier, and that the barbarians did not dare to encroach upon the Xia 夏 [Chinese states]—was this not the stabilizing effect of his court strategy? In Duke Huan's time, the Way of Zhou 周 had declined; among the feudal lords of the Central States, who was there to honor it? Yet Guan Zhong alone served as chief minister to Duke Huan, and through his constant principles of order and hierarchy convened a covenant first at Shouzhi 首止, and a second covenant at Kuiqiu 葵丘. The royal heir-apparent and the king's prohibitions had their distinctions clearly manifested, and that inferiors did not dare to usurp the prerogatives of superiors—was this not the operation of his grand strategy? Therefore, as his achievements were in his own time, his own time praised his benevolence; as his achievements reached later generations, later generations enjoyed his benefaction. The impartial judgment of ten thousand generations is settled by the Sage [Confucius], and since he repeatedly commended Guan Zhong alone, truly Guan Zhong is beyond reproach! And how could there be any reproach against the one whom Guan Zhong served? Therefore it is said that Xiaobai 小白 [Duke Huan] ought to have been enthroned. Even so, when the Master commended Guan Zhong, he certainly meant that he chose his ruler and accomplished his enterprise. Yet he was unable to lead Duke Huan to the Kingly Way, and even the achievement of hegemony was not brought to full completion—how then could Guan Zhong be entirely free of reproach? Alas! Once his scholarly art was fixed, hegemony could not be turned into true kingship. As for the warning of the shot belt-hook [or the warnings given by the one who shot his belt-hook], Guan Zhong indeed enjoined him earnestly and repeatedly, yet Duke Huan himself grew lax…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
則非仲之罪也伯業且然而況於王道乎有世
道之責者可以思矣
禮記
五官致貢曰享
吳璨
同考試官教諭徐批君權臣職發揮詳確著世有功
世之志者高薦尤宜
考試官教諭劉批一氣呵成全無斧鑿
考試官教諭蔣批治貴考成是作得之
===
人臣獻功之典而明尊君之義焉夫列卿分職
人君所以成治功也因時而獻其成謂非以尊
君乎且夫帝王之建官也必分任而後可以廣
佐理之猷必考成而後可以明激勸之義今五
官各有所寄矣然豈無以稽其成哉故歲會之
時則庶績可以咸熙而舉其積累之所致者敷
奏於九重之上百工可以用乂而卽其省試之
所効者備陳於五位之前禮樂刑政吾其述之
不敢隱也而賞罰之權惟宸衷之獨斷焉工虞
punctuated:
則非仲之罪也。伯業且然，而況於王道乎？有世道之責者，可以思矣。

《禮記》
「五官致貢曰享」
吳璨〔同考試官教諭徐批：君權臣職，發揮詳確，著世有功世之志者，高薦尤宜。考試官教諭劉批：一氣呵成，全無斧鑿。考試官教諭蔣批：治貴考成，是作得之。〕

人臣獻功之典，而明尊君之義焉。夫列卿分職，人君所以成治功也；因時而獻其成，謂非以尊君乎？且夫帝王之建官也，必分任而後可以廣佐理之猷，必考成而後可以明激勸之義。今五官各有所寄矣，然豈無以稽其成哉？故歲會之時，則庶績可以咸熙，而舉其積累之所致者，敷奏於九重之上；百工可以用乂，而卽其省試之所効者，備陳於五位之前。禮樂刑政，吾其述之不敢隱也，而賞罰之權，惟宸衷之獨斷焉；工虞
translation_en:
…then that was not Guan Zhong's fault. Even the enterprise of a hegemon was like this—how much more so the Kingly Way! Those who bear responsibility for the Way of the world may well reflect on this.

Record of Rites (Liji)
"The Five Offices presenting their achievements is called 'offering' (xiang)."
By Wu Can 吳璨 [Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐: The sovereign's authority and the minister's duties are expounded in a detailed and accurate manner. It manifests the ambition of one in the world who would render service to the age [?]; recommending it for a high place is especially fitting. Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉: Written in a single breath, completely free of any trace of the chisel. Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣: Governance values the evaluation of completed work; this composition grasps that principle.]

[The Classic sets forth] the statutory rite by which subjects present their achievements, and thereby clarifies the principle of honoring the sovereign. Now, the ranking ministers divide up offices as the means by which the sovereign accomplishes the work of governance; presenting their completed results at the proper season—can this be called anything other than honoring the sovereign? Moreover, when emperors and kings establish offices, they must divide responsibilities before they can broaden the plans of administrative assistance, and they must evaluate completed work before they can clarify the principle of encouragement and exhortation. Now the Five Offices each have their respective charges; yet how could there be no means to examine their completed work? Therefore, at the time of the annual accounting, when all the myriad achievements can be made resplendent, they take up what they have brought about through cumulative effort and present a full report above to the Ninefold Palace; when all the hundred officials can be brought to order, they take what they have accomplished under inspection and trial and set it forth in full before the Sovereign's Throne. Rites, music, punishments, and administration—we recount them without daring to conceal anything, while the authority to reward and punish rests solely with the independent judgment of the imperial mind; public works, forestry and泽 [wardenries],…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
敎養吾其述之不敢飾也而黜陟之典惟大君
之是聽焉如是而不謂之享乎蓋其一德以尊
天子而效忠宣力咸輸靖獻之忱匪懈以事一
人而積事程功恪守對揚之義雖非方物之獻
也而天工之敷奏均自下而致之上焉則其享
也以誠不以文而一心之精白固肅然其不敢
懈也當其時使朝無倖位者不以此乎雖非廷
實之供也而天職之備陳均自卑而達之尊焉
則其享也以敬不以物而一念之虔恭固凜乎
===
其不敢擅也當其時使官無惰政者不以此乎
吁即五官之貢而總於天官者可知矣上有定
權下無佚志此先王之治不可及也抑六卿左
右天子分隆而情亦親矣乃以綜核之權御之
毋亦過乎噫事必有敘政必有綱人君責諸六
卿六卿綜乎百職分任責成天下不勞而理矣
彼下行臣職固非體要而姑息太過者遂不免
於積弛焉此乾綱之斷君道所以隆也
祀帝於郊敬之至也宗廟之祭仁之至也
punctuated:
敎養，吾其述之不敢飾也，而黜陟之典惟大君之是聽焉。如是而不謂之享乎？蓋其一德以尊天子，而效忠宣力，咸輸靖獻之忱；匪懈以事一人，而積事程功，恪守對揚之義。雖非方物之獻也，而天工之敷奏，均自下而致之上焉。則其享也，以誠不以文，而一心之精白，固肅然其不敢懈也。當其時，使朝無倖位者，不以此乎？雖非廷實之供也，而天職之備陳，均自卑而達之尊焉。則其享也，以敬不以物，而一念之虔恭，固凜乎其不敢擅也。當其時，使官無惰政者，不以此乎？吁！即五官之貢，而總於天官者可知矣。上有定權，下無佚志，此先王之治不可及也。抑六卿左右天子，分隆而情亦親矣，乃以綜核之權御之，毋亦過乎？噫！事必有敘，政必有綱。人君責諸六卿，六卿綜乎百職，分任責成，天下不勞而理矣。彼下行臣職，固非體要；而姑息太過者，遂不免於積弛焉。此乾綱之斷，君道所以隆也。
祀帝於郊，敬之至也；宗廟之祭，仁之至也。
translation_en:
… instruction and nourishment—we recount these without daring to embellish them, while the statutes of demotion and promotion rest solely upon the Great Sovereign's command. Could this not be called a sacrificial offering of tribute? For with united virtue they honor the Son of Heaven, and in pledging loyalty and exerting their strength, all pour forth the sincerity of quiet dedication; without laxity they serve the One Man, and in accumulating achievements and measuring merit, they reverently uphold the duty of responding to and extolling sovereign grace. Although it is not a presentation of local products, the reporting of Heaven's work is alike conveyed from below to above. Thus their offering lies in sincerity rather than outward form, and the pure integrity of their single mind remains solemnly不敢 [unwilling to] slacken. At that time, was it not because of this that the court had no undeserved posts? Although it is not a provision of courtyard treasures, the full setting forth of Heaven's offices alike reaches from the lowly to the exalted. Thus their offering lies in reverence rather than material goods, and the devout respect of their single thought remains awestruck, not daring to usurp authority. At that time, was it not because of this that officials had noremiss administration? Ah! From the tribute of performance presented by the five ministries, what was overseen as a whole by the Minister of State (Tianguan) can be known. Above, there was settled authority; below, there were no wayward ambitions—this is why the governance of the former kings cannot be matched. Yet the Six Ministers assist the Son of Heaven to his left and right; their status is exalted and their bond is intimate. To govern them through the power of comprehensive verification—is that not going too far? Alas! Affairs must have order, and governance must have a guiding cord. The ruler holds the Six Ministers accountable, and the Six Ministers oversee the hundred offices; by dividing responsibilities and demanding results, the realm is put in order without toil. Descend to performing the duties of ministers oneself is certainly contrary to the essentials of statecraft; yet those who are overly indulgent inevitably end in accumulated laxity. Such decisive control of the sovereign's guiding cord is whereby the Way of the Ruler flourishes.

Sacrificing to the Supreme Ancestor (Di) at the suburban altar is the utmost of reverence; the sacrifice in the ancestral temple is the utmost of benevolence.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
侯師皐
同考試官教諭徐批形容聖人仁敬之德字字句句
皆出心精乃藝苑中不多得者也録之
考試官教諭劉批發攄奧旨非摸擬敖
考試官教諭蔣批詞意備精尤多卓識
觀先王之享天親而各盡其心焉蓋祭之義生
於心也仁敬各極其至其先王之所以享天親
者乎且夫先王之致祭固以將崇報之忱亦必
有感孚之本吾觀於禮而知其德矣彼聖人奉
===
皇天之大統嘗於南郊而祀之藁靺之薦象其
性焉陶匏之用居其樸焉是固以質為貴矣然
豈崇儉而廢禮乎蓋德產精微舉天下之物無
足以稱其大者故大報無事於彌文而明禋必
肅於內志小心翼翼猶懼其對越之或違也昭
格遲遲猶懼其禮度之或愆也蓋以精白之衷
而仰契乎玄穹之理則至敬無文雖燔柴不為
略矣非敬之至而何哉聖人承祖考之丕緒嘗
於宗廟而祀之以順天時陰陽具陳焉以盡地
punctuated:
侯師皐

同考試官教諭徐批：形容聖人仁敬之德，字字句句皆出心精，乃藝苑中不多得者也。録之。
考試官教諭劉批：發攄奧旨，非摸擬敖。
考試官教諭蔣批：詞意備精，尤多卓識。

觀先王之享天親，而各盡其心焉。蓋祭之義生於心也。仁敬各極其至，其先王之所以享天親者乎！且夫先王之致祭，固以將崇報之忱，亦必有感孚之本。吾觀於禮，而知其德矣。彼聖人奉皇天之大統，嘗於南郊而祀之。藁靺之薦，象其性焉；陶匏之用，居其樸焉。是固以質為貴矣，然豈崇儉而廢禮乎？蓋德產精微，舉天下之物無足以稱其大者。故大報無事於彌文，而明禋必肅於內志。小心翼翼，猶懼其對越之或違也；昭格遲遲，猶懼其禮度之或愆也。蓋以精白之衷，而仰契乎玄穹之理，則至敬無文，雖燔柴不為略矣。非敬之至而何哉！聖人承祖考之丕緒，嘗於宗廟而祀之。以順天時，陰陽具陳焉；以盡地…
translation_en:
Hou Shigao 侯師皐

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐: In depicting the sage's virtues of benevolence and reverence, every word and every phrase springs from the essence of his mind. It is a rare piece in the realm of letters; record it for publication.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉: It unfolds the profound meaning, not merely an imitative composition [?].
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣: Both diction and thought are thoroughly refined, and it abounds in outstanding insight.

Observe how the former kings made offerings to Heaven and to their kin, in each case exhausting their minds therein. For the meaning of sacrifice arises from the mind. Benevolence and reverence each reaching its utmost—was this not how the former kings made offerings to Heaven and to their kin? Moreover, when the former kings performed sacrifices, while they certainly did so to convey their sincerity in honoring and repaying, there also had to be a foundation for moving and connecting with the spirits. Looking at the rites, I know their virtue. The sage, upholding the grand succession of August Heaven, offered sacrifice to It in the southern suburb. The presentation of straw mats symbolized its nature; the use of pottery and gourds resided in its simplicity. This certainly prized plainness; yet how could it be exalting frugality to the neglect of ritual? For the generative power of Heaven's virtue is subtle and minute, and among all the things in the world none is sufficient to match its greatness. Therefore, the great recompense had no need for elaborate ornament, and the pure sacrifice had to be made solemn through inner intent. Cautious and circumspect, he still feared lest in standing before Heaven he might in some way transgress; waiting long for the bright manifestation of the spirit's arrival, he still feared lest his ritual measures might in some way err. Because with a pure and spotless heart he looked up to accord with the principle of the dark vault of Heaven, supreme reverence needed no adornment, and even the burning of firewood on the altar was not considered perfunctory. If this is not the utmost of reverence, what is it? The sage, inheriting the great patrimony of his ancestors, offered sacrifice to them in the ancestral temple. title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
利水土咸列焉是固以多爲貴矣然豈侈文而
無實乎蓋親恩罔極竭天下之物猶不足以稱
其心者故愛慕既篤於由衷而聚順必隆於繼
孝心惕而奉之以禮九州之美所必竭也愛博
而將之以文萬國之懽所必聚也蓋以不匱之
思而求盡吾圖報之念則至仁無已卽備物猶
爲歉矣非仁之至而何哉夫敬至則見天於心
矣仁至則見親於心矣先王舉大典而天親交
享者信非恃其禮也蓋天親一致仁孝一理惟
===
心源瑩而俯仰無愧焉則亦臨亦保卽以事親
而善繼善述天心用豫矣若興思於雨露致敬
於繭栗特其文耳豈仁孝之實哉噫爲天地宗
廟之主者當知合一之義矣
第貳塲
論
明君德業配天
楊應兆
同考試官學正梁批虛心受善乃帝王德業之本諸作
punctuated:
利水土咸列焉，是固以多爲貴矣。然豈侈文而無實乎？蓋親恩罔極，竭天下之物猶不足以稱其心者，故愛慕既篤於由衷，而聚順必隆於繼孝。心惕而奉之以禮，九州之美所必竭也；愛博而將之以文，萬國之懽所必聚也。蓋以不匱之思，而求盡吾圖報之念，則至仁無已，卽備物猶爲歉矣，非仁之至而何哉！夫敬至則見天於心矣，仁至則見親於心矣。先王舉大典而天親交享者，信非恃其禮也。蓋天親一致，仁孝一理。惟心源瑩而俯仰無愧焉，則亦臨亦保，卽以事親；而善繼善述，天心用豫矣。若興思於雨露，致敬於繭栗，特其文耳，豈仁孝之實哉！噫！爲天地宗廟之主者，當知合一之義矣。

第貳塲

論

明君德業配天

楊應兆
同考試官學正梁批：虛心受善，乃帝王德業之本。諸作
translation_en:
… advantage of the earth, and products of water and land are all arrayed there; this indeed prizes abundance. Yet how could this be extravagant ornament without substance? For the grace of parents is boundless, and even exhausting all the things under heaven is still not enough to match one's feelings. Therefore, since loving longing is already sincere from the bottom of one's heart, the gathering of harmony must be made abundant in the continuation of filial piety. With awatchful heart, one presents offerings with ritual propriety, inevitably exhausting the finest things of the Nine Provinces; with broad love, one conducts the service with refinement, inevitably gathering the joyful allegiance of the myriad states. For when with inexhaustible longing one seeks to fulfill the desire to repay them, supreme benevolence knows no end, and even a complete array of offerings still feels insufficient—what is this if not the culmination of benevolence! Now, when reverence reaches the utmost, one beholds Heaven in one's heart; when benevolence reaches the utmost, one beholds one's parents in one's heart. That the former kings performed the great ceremonies and both Heaven and parents enjoyed the offerings was truly not because they relied merely on ritual forms. For Heaven and parents are one and the same, and benevolence and filial piety share a single principle. Only when the wellspring of the mind is pure and one feels no shame looking up or down, does one serve one's parents in the very act of being conscious of Heaven's inspection and protection; and by ably continuing their will and carrying forward their affairs, the heart of Heaven is thereby pleased. As for being moved to longing by the seasonal rains and dews, or showing reverence with a sacrificial calf whose horns are the size of a cocoon or chestnut, these are merely outward forms—how could they be the substance of benevolence and filial piety? Alas! He who serves as the lord of Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple ought to understand the meaning of their unity.

Second Session

Discourse

"The Virtue and Achievements of an Enlightened Ruler Match Heaven"

Yang Yingzhao (楊應兆)

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
多漶汗漫而子獨能根究題旨發揮殆盡且體裁高古議論開闔抑揚
卓有奇氣筞言讜誼素積於衷者敢冠多士非直以其文也
考試官敎諭劉批旨意詳盡氣格雄古積學之士也
考試官敎諭蔣批學富才雄氣昌議正瓊塲之作也
帝王以身任天下之重而懋同天之化惟其心
之虛而已矣夫天下重器也治天下重務也而
人君以一身任其責則其厝注運量容非耳目
心思所能周而所操所履又足以厭其心而天
下之善未易達焉夫負至重之責而席易盈之
===
勢以不易達之善而欲濟其難周之務將何以
善治於不窮而比隆造化哉噫此明君所以虛
其心以來天下之善而盛德大業與天無極也
請申胡氏之論夫天者羣物之祖也高明覆幬
萬禩如新業至宏也玄化之樞凝而不汩德至
精也然節其運而不過制其序而不流虧盈益
謙之理旁皇周浹於兩儀四象之中故地道上
行萬物訢合虛而不屈動而愈出而先儒以谷
神不死虛室生白爲得造化之精則天之道一
punctuated:
多漶汗漫，而子獨能根究題旨，發揮殆盡。且體裁高古，議論開闔抑揚，卓有奇氣。筞言讜誼，素積於衷者。敢冠多士，非直以其文也。
考試官敎諭劉批：旨意詳盡，氣格雄古，積學之士也。
考試官敎諭蔣批：學富才雄，氣昌議正，瓊塲之作也。
帝王以身任天下之重，而懋同天之化，惟其心之虛而已矣。夫天下，重器也；治天下，重務也。而人君以一身任其責，則其厝注運量，容非耳目心思所能周；而所操所履，又足以厭其心，而天下之善未易達焉。夫負至重之責，而席易盈之勢，以不易達之善，而欲濟其難周之務，將何以善治於不窮，而比隆造化哉？噫！此明君所以虛其心以來天下之善，而盛德大業與天無極也。請申胡氏之論。夫天者，羣物之祖也。高明覆幬，萬禩如新，業至宏也；玄化之樞，凝而不汩，德至精也。然節其運而不過，制其序而不流，虧盈益謙之理，旁皇周浹於兩儀四象之中。故地道上行，萬物訢合，虛而不屈，動而愈出。而先儒以「谷神不死」、「虛室生白」爲得造化之精，則天之道，一
translation_en:
… were mostly vague and rambling, yet you alone were able to thoroughly investigate the meaning of the topic and develop it almost to exhaustion. Moreover, the style is lofty and antique, and the argument opens and closes, rises and falls, standing out with an extraordinary spirit. Your policy words and upright principles are those long accumulated in your heart. I venture to place you at the head of the many scholars, not merely because of the literary style.

Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: The purport is detailed and exhaustive, the spirit and form vigorous and antique—a scholar of accumulated learning.

Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: Rich in learning and vigorous in talent, flourishing in spirit and upright in argument—a work that stands alone in the examination compound [? 瓊塲].

For emperors and kings to take upon their own persons the heavy burden of the world and strive for transformations equal to Heaven's, it lies solely in the emptiness of their minds. Now, the empire is a heavy vessel, and governing the empire is a heavy task. When a ruler takes on its responsibility with his single person, his arrangements and orchestrations may well be more than his own ears, eyes, and thoughts can encompass; meanwhile, the power he holds and the position he occupies are sufficient to satisfy his own mind, so that the good of the empire cannot easily reach him. Carrying the heaviest of responsibilities while occupying a position of power that easily breeds self-satisfaction, and wishing to accomplish tasks that are difficult to encompass by means of the good that cannot easily reach him—how then could he achieve good governance endlessly and match the grandeur of the creative forces of nature? Alas! This is why the enlightened ruler empties his mind to attract the good of the entire world, so that his glorious virtue and great enterprise are as boundless as Heaven. Let me expand upon Master Hu's discourse.

Now, Heaven is the ancestor of all things. High and bright, it overspreads and covers all, remaining as new through ten thousand generations—its enterprise is vast indeed! The pivot of mysterious transformation coalesces without being muddled—its virtue is pure indeed! Yet it regulates its revolutions without excess and controls its order without aberration; the principle of diminishing the full and augmenting the humble pervades everywhere within the Two Modes and the Four Images.
