Therefore, the Way of Earth ascends, and the myriad things harmoniously unite; it is empty yet never exhausted, and the more it moves, the more comes forth. Former Confucians considered the sayings "the valley spirit never dies" and "in an empty chamber, brightness is born" to have grasped the essence of nature's creativity. Thus, the Way of Heaven is simply…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
虛也虛則通萬物爲一氣而德業不毀也顧天
之於物既非根極靜篤希夷恬寂聽其自榮自
瘁於大塊之中而雕刻衆形役役焉驅萬物而
馳驟之又其所不忍則寄吾之德業而囿萬物
於無窮者人君也人君代天之任則凡待命於
天者皆待命於我者也民吾民物吾物而蒸黎
而俊乂而疲癃疾苦而僻遠幽遐殊俗異類思
以便其性居其宜者莫非吾之一體而禮樂刑
政所以整齊而約束之皆其具之不容廢者也
===
即使聰明神智高出等夷役而用之既不勝其
勞瘁而自用者不裕自是者不張天下之務遺
於聰明神智之外者多矣且位則天位祿則天
祿喜爲湛露怒爲震霆薄海内外非特不敢矯
命雄行而睨視跂望且以爲畏其環吾身而處
者又多奔走希覬諛治安而導佚樂以便其圖
安之私蓋臣志士分在得言者忸怩於利害而
不敢盡勢在可言者疎遠於日隔而不得盡即
有攄衷款素思盡繩糾之分而批鱗苦口之說
punctuated: 虛也，虛則通萬物爲一氣而德業不毀也。顧天之於物，既非根極靜篤、希夷恬寂，聽其自榮自瘁於大塊之中；而雕刻衆形，役役焉驅萬物而馳驟之，又其所不忍。則寄吾之德業，而囿萬物於無窮者，人君也。人君代天之任，則凡待命於天者，皆待命於我者也。民吾民，物吾物，而蒸黎、而俊乂、而疲癃疾苦、而僻遠幽遐殊俗異類，思以便其性、居其宜者，莫非吾之一體；而禮樂刑政所以整齊而約束之，皆其具之不容廢者也。即使聰明神智高出等夷，役而用之，既不勝其勞瘁；而自用者不裕，自是者不張，天下之務，遺於聰明神智之外者多矣。且位則天位，祿則天祿，喜爲湛露，怒爲震霆，薄海内外，非特不敢矯命雄行，而睨視跂望，且以爲畏。其環吾身而處者，又多奔走希覬，諛治安而導佚樂，以便其圖安之私。蓋臣志士，分在得言者，忸怩於利害而不敢盡；勢在可言者，疎遠於日隔而不得盡。即有攄衷款素，思盡繩糾之分，而批鱗苦口之說，
translation_en: …is emptiness; through emptiness it unites the myriad things into a single vital breath, and its virtue and achievements are never destroyed. Yet in its relation to things, Heaven does not merely root itself in extreme stillness and remain in formless, silent tranquility, leaving them to flourish or wither by themselves amidst the great earth; nor can it bear to carve out the multitude of forms and busily drive the myriad things to gallop about. Thus, the one to whom Heaven entrusts its virtue and achievements, and who encompasses the myriad things without end, is the ruler of men. Since the ruler of men takes on the charge of Heaven, all who await their mandate from Heaven await their mandate from him. The people are my people, and things are my things. Whether the common multitude, the men of talent and eminence, the crippled, infirm, and suffering, or those of strange customs and different kinds in remote, obscure, and distant lands—all whom I think to accommodate in their nature and settle in what suits them are none other than parts of my own single body; and rites, music, punishments, and governance, by which they are ordered and restrained, are all instruments that cannot be dispensed with. Even if one's intelligence and divine wisdom far surpass those of ordinary peers, to tax and employ them alone would not only bring unbearable exhaustion, but he who relies solely on himself will lack abundance, and he who considers himself always right will fail to expand; the affairs of the empire left outside the reach of his intelligence and divine wisdom would be many indeed. Moreover, his position is the Heaven-ordained position, and his emolument is the Heaven-ordained emolument; his joy is like heavy dew, and his anger like a crashing thunderbolt. Within and beyond the seas, people not only dare not defy his commands to act willfully, but even as they look askance or stand on tiptoe in expectation, they regard him with awe. Those who dwell around his person mostly bustle about in ambitious hope, flattering him with talk of peace and order and leading him into ease and pleasure so as to serve their own selfish schemes for security. Loyal ministers [reading 蓋 as 藎] and men of high principle, whose duty entitles them to speak, shrink back out of concern for advantage and harm and dare not speak fully; those whose circumstances would allow them to speak are kept distant by daily separation and cannot speak fully. Even if there are those who pour out their sincere, unadorned hearts and wish to fulfill their duty of correction and remonstrance, words that grate like scraping a dragon's scales or taste bitter to the mouth…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
又不足以投人主之意嚮而滋其所疑故天下
之庸默自保者日益衆焉善言旣壅驕侈易生
自身心性情以至設施舉措將日戾於天則而
終於不可支矣乃英明之主獨念其長於崇臺
邃闥之中坐於勾陳負扆之內旣不得周知天
下之利便疾苦而投歡獻媚者又壅遏吾之聰
明而一睫之外有泰華矣乃復狃以爲便而使
陳善責難者萌悔心焉豈計哉故威命靈爽侔
乎造化不敢侈也甘言諛行滿乎耳目不敢縱
===
也明照萬物而下芻蕘權總六合而先瞽御造
膝而陳敷心而告大臣之善也吾勤召對隆禮
貌而納之折檻而諫排闥而語諫官之善也吾
忘喜怒借顏色而容之衣食而詔菲服御而導
儉彤管紀過御瞽幾聲左右之善也吾黜忌諱
降勢分而容之推而工誦史箴士傳民謗舉天
下之人苟有規吾之闕失者卽使危言激論大
非人情之所堪而吾且以藥石愈於粱肉鍼砭
優於歡洽欣欣然樂而聽聽而用惟懼其言之
punctuated: 又不足以投人主之意嚮，而滋其所疑。故天下之庸默自保者日益衆焉。善言旣壅，驕侈易生，自身心性情以至設施舉措，將日戾於天則，而終於不可支矣。乃英明之主，獨念其長於崇臺邃闥之中，坐於勾陳負扆之內，旣不得周知天下之利便疾苦，而投歡獻媚者又壅遏吾之聰明，而一睫之外有泰華矣；乃復狃以爲便，而使陳善責難者萌悔心焉，豈計哉？故威命靈爽侔乎造化，不敢侈也；甘言諛行滿乎耳目，不敢縱也。明照萬物而下芻蕘，權總六合而先瞽御。造膝而陳、敷心而告，大臣之善也，吾勤召對、隆禮貌而納之；折檻而諫、排闥而語，諫官之善也，吾忘喜怒、借顏色而容之；衣食而詔菲、服御而導儉、彤管紀過、御瞽幾聲，左右之善也，吾黜忌諱、降勢分而容之。推而工誦、史箴、士傳、民謗，舉天下之人苟有規吾之闕失者，卽使危言激論，大非人情之所堪，而吾且以藥石愈於粱肉，鍼砭優於歡洽，欣欣然樂而聽、聽而用，惟懼其言之
translation_en:
…are furthermore insufficient to suit the ruler's inclinations, and instead only increase his suspicions. Thus, throughout the empire, those who remain mediocre and silent to protect themselves grow ever more numerous by the day. Once good counsel is blocked, arrogance and extravagance easily arise; from the ruler's own mind, heart, nature, and emotions down to his policies, enactments, and conduct, all will daily violate the principles of Heaven until at last the situation becomes unsustainable.

Yet an enlightened and sagacious ruler alone reflects upon the fact that, having grown up amidst lofty terraces and deep palace gates, and sitting within the imperial guards before the ceremonial screen, he is already unable to thoroughly know the advantages, conveniences, hardships, and sufferings of the world; meanwhile, those who cater to his pleasures and offer flattery further obstruct his sight and hearing, so that right beyond his own eyelashes stand Mount Tai and Mount Hua! If he then grows accustomed to this and regards it as convenient, causing those who set forth the good and demand difficult standards of their sovereign to conceive regret in their hearts—how could that be a wise plan?

Therefore, though his awe-inspiring mandate and spiritual intelligence equal the creative forces of nature, he dares not be extravagant; though sweet words and flattering deeds fill his ears and eyes, he dares not indulge himself. Though his insight illuminates the myriad things, he humbles himself before grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers; though his authority encompasses the six directions of the universe, he gives precedence to blind musicians and attendants. Drawing close to the sovereign's knee to set forth counsel and opening their hearts to advise—this is the goodness of great ministers; I shall diligently summon them for audiences, treat them with the highest courtesy, and accept their words. Breaking the balustrade in remonstrance and pushing open the palace doors to speak—this is the goodness of remonstrance officials; I shall set aside pleasure and anger, lend them a welcoming countenance, and tolerate them. Advising frugality in food and clothing, guiding toward economy in dress and equipage, recording faults with the red brush, and the blind musicians' subtle admonitions through music—this is the goodness of close attendants; I shall dismiss taboos, lower the barriers of rank and status, and tolerate them. Extending this further to the recitations of artisans, the admonitions of scribes, the transmitted sayings of scholars, and the criticisms of the common people—if among all the people in the world there is anyone who admonishes me for my failings and omissions, even if their alarming words and fierce arguments are utterly beyond what ordinary human sentiment can bear, I shall regard medicinal stones as better than fine grain and meat, and acupuncture needles as superior to jovial harmony, gladly delighting in listening to them, and upon listening, putting them to use, fearing only that their words…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不詳焉則上無佚志下無隱忠天下之士明目
張膽畢獻其善於吾前而砥礪既深嗜欲必寡
氣完而無妄動神定而無越思伐性斲眞之斧
不得內滑其和而潜眞守一炯炯洞洞皆天心
也出之以照天下顧有壅而不理者哉是故衣
食於饑寒拊循於疾苦居居于于帝力何有蒸
黎得其所焉論材而官程功而進勞勩者不抑
所能而巧猾者蔑以行其私俊乂得其敘焉刖
者闇而瞽者師薪不童而漁不竭禽獸可繫羈
===
而遊鵲巢可攀援而闚而雕題辮髮將梯山航
海求以被承德澤則疲癃殘疾異類遐荒莫不
若其性焉進而臧否陟罰紀綱號令犂然當於
天道人心而百靈敘秩五緯順布莫非禮樂之
敷賁焉則剛健中正吾心之於穆也高明悠乆
吾心之奠麗也景星慶雲河清海晏吾心之煕
明而愉快也大德不德與天同體大業不業與
天同用吾之德業安乎一世之人卽一世之天
矣安乎千百世之人卽千百世之天矣萬世之
punctuated: 不詳焉，則上無佚志，下無隱忠，天下之士，明目張膽，畢獻其善於吾前。而砥礪既深，嗜欲必寡，氣完而無妄動，神定而無越思，伐性斲眞之斧，不得內滑其和，而潜眞守一，炯炯洞洞，皆天心也。出之以照天下，顧有壅而不理者哉？是故衣食於饑寒，拊循於疾苦，居居于于，帝力何有，蒸黎得其所焉；論材而官，程功而進，勞勩者不抑所能，而巧猾者蔑以行其私，俊乂得其敘焉；刖者闇而瞽者師，薪不童而漁不竭，禽獸可繫羈而遊，鵲巢可攀援而闚，而雕題辮髮，將梯山航海，求以被承德澤，則疲癃殘疾、異類遐荒，莫不若其性焉。進而臧否陟罰，紀綱號令，犂然當於天道人心，而百靈敘秩，五緯順布，莫非禮樂之敷賁焉。則剛健中正，吾心之於穆也；高明悠乆，吾心之奠麗也；景星慶雲，河清海晏，吾心之煕明而愉快也。大德不德，與天同體；大業不業，與天同用。吾之德業安乎一世之人，卽一世之天矣；安乎千百世之人，卽千百世之天矣；萬世之
translation_en:
…not sufficiently detailed. Then above there will be no dissolute intentions, and below there will be no hidden loyalty; the scholars of the realm will open their eyes wide and summon their courage, offering up all their good counsel before me. Once this whetting and polishing has gone deep, indulgent desires will necessarily grow few; one's vital energy will be whole without reckless agitation, and one's spirit settled without errant thoughts. The axes that chop down one's nature and hack away at one's true essence will not be able to disturb one's harmony from within; submerging one's true essence and guarding the One, luminous and penetrating, all will be the mind of Heaven. Bringing this forth to illuminate the world, how could there be anything obstructed and left ungoverned?

Therefore, clothing and feeding the hungry and cold, comforting and caring for those in sickness and distress, so that they live in tranquil contentment, asking "What is the Emperor's power to us?"—thus the multitude of common people find their proper place. Assessing talent to bestow office and measuring achievement to grant promotion, so that those who toil are not suppressed in their abilities and the cunning and sly have no way to pursue their selfish interests—thus men of eminent talent find their proper order. Those whose feet were amputated serve as gatekeepers [闇, reading 閼/閽] and the blind serve as musicians; firewood is not stripped bare from the hills and fishing does not exhaust the waters; birds and beasts can be tethered and led about to roam, and magpies' nests can be climbed up to and peered into; while those with tattooed foreheads and braided hair will scale mountains and sail the seas, seeking to receive the grace of our virtue—thus the infirm, crippled, alien kinds, and distant wilds all follow their natural dispositions. Going further, judgments of good and bad, promotions and punishments, the web of laws and commands will all distinctly accord with the Way of Heaven and the minds of men; the hundred spirits will be in orderly rank, and the five planets will move in harmonious array—none of this failing to be the resplendent spread of rites and music.

Then firm, vigorous, balanced, and upright is the profound solemnity of my mind; lofty, brilliant, and enduring is the settled splendour of my mind; auspicious stars and propitious clouds, the Yellow River running clear and the seas calm, are the radiant brightness and joy of my mind. Great virtue does not claim virtue, sharing the same substance as Heaven; great achievement does not claim achievement, sharing the same function as Heaven. If my virtue and achievement bring peace to the people of one generation, I am the Heaven of that one generation; if they bring peace to the people of a百 or a thousand generations, I am the Heaven of those hundred or thousand generations; [if] for ten thousand generations…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
下德吾德業吾業而萬世之人舉安焉則爲萬
世之天矣又安得與造化論形體哉夫人君之
德莫盛乎乾而有亢龍之悔人君之業莫盛於
泰而有復隍之憂至於冥豫擊益惴惴然必謙
以居有豫始繼之何作易者之憂患若此耶大
都敵國外患不足爲人君之懼而恃天下無可
畏者則其大可畏者至焉蓋起於一念之盈也
滿心一恣貽患無窮謙德一崇保治無射故則
天如堯勅天如舜其德業之盛無以加矣然衢
===
室總章之訪每兢兢焉他若拜言得師四友十
輔言若甘飴歡若同體數聖人之心卽堯舜之
心故其德業卽堯舜之德業也彼其初豈故爲
卑鄙不斷之行萎然屈其萬乘之尊而道謀是
聽乎要以治理無窮而代天之責不敢負也彼
太甲成王繼體之賢者也惟其甘受逆心無逸
之語而令名迄今不衰向使其侈然以自大視
伊周之訓若贅焉則又安能必其爲何如主哉
噫山不動而人推高善容也海不運而人推廣
punctuated: 下，德吾德，業吾業，而萬世之人舉安焉，則爲萬世之天矣，又安得與造化論形體哉！夫人君之德莫盛乎《乾》，而有「亢龍」之悔；人君之業莫盛於《泰》，而有「復隍」之憂。至於「冥豫」、「擊益」，惴惴然必《謙》以居《有》、《豫》始繼之，何作《易》者之憂患若此耶？大都敵國外患不足爲人君之懼，而恃天下無可畏者，則其大可畏者至焉，蓋起於一念之盈也。滿心一恣，貽患無窮；謙德一崇，保治無射。故則天如堯，勅天如舜，其德業之盛無以加矣，然衢室、總章之訪每兢兢焉。他若拜言、得師、四友、十輔，言若甘飴，歡若同體。數聖人之心，卽堯、舜之心；故其德業，卽堯、舜之德業也。彼其初豈故爲卑鄙不斷之行，萎然屈其萬乘之尊而道謀是聽乎？要以治理無窮，而代天之責不敢負也。彼太甲、成王，繼體之賢者也，惟其甘受逆心、《無逸》之語，而令名迄今不衰。向使其侈然以自大，視伊、周之訓若贅焉，則又安能必其爲何如主哉！噫！山不動而人推高，善容也；海不運而人推廣，
translation_en:
…after ten thousand generations, if they take my virtue as their virtue and my enterprise as their enterprise, so that the people of ten thousand generations all find peace therein, then one becomes Heaven for ten thousand generations! How then could one merely compare physical forms with the creative forces of nature?

Now, the virtue of a ruler is never more flourishing than in the hexagram Qian [The Creative], yet it carries the regret of the "arrogant dragon"; the enterprise of a ruler is never more flourishing than in the hexagram Tai [Peace], yet it carries the worry of the "city wall collapsing back into the moat." As for "deluded pleasure" [in Yu] and "striking the increase" [in Yi], in fearful trepidation one must dwell in Great Possession [Dayou] through Modesty [Qian], and only then does Enthusiasm [Yu] follow it. Why did the authors of the Book of Changes (Yi) feel such deep anxiety and concern as this? In general, hostile states and external troubles are not enough to cause a ruler fear; rather, when he relies on there being nothing in the world to fear, that is when what is truly to be feared arrives—for it springs from a single thought of self-satisfaction. Once a self-satisfied mind is indulged, it leaves behind endless calamities; once the virtue of modesty is exalted, it preserves good governance without fail.

Therefore, in modeling himself on Heaven like Yao, or in cautiously obeying Heaven's mandate like Shun, the flourishing of their virtue and enterprise could not be surpassed; yet in their inquiries in the Crossroads Hall (Qushi) and the Bright Hall (Zongzhang), they were always cautious and circumspect. As for others—such as bowing to receive words of counsel, obtaining a teacher, or having the Four Friends and the Ten Assistants—they took in counsel as if it were sweet malt sugar and rejoiced in their ministers as if they shared a single body. The minds of these several sages were none other than the minds of Yao and Shun; therefore, their virtue and enterprise were none other than the virtue and enterprise of Yao and Shun. In the beginning, did they intentionally engage in lowly, mean, and indecisive conduct, listlessly bending their majesty as lords of ten thousand chariots just to listen to counsels by the wayside? The essential point was that the principles of governance are inexhaustible, and they dared not fail in their responsibility to act on behalf of Heaven.

Those rulers Tai Jia and King Cheng were worthy heirs who succeeded to the throne. Only because they willingly accepted words that went against their inclinations and the admonitions of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) has their fine reputation remained undiminished to this day. Had they been arrogantly self-important and regarded the instructions of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou as superfluous, how could anyone have been certain what sort of rulers they would have turned out to be!

Alas! A mountain does not move, yet people extol its height, because it is good at accommodating; the sea does not stir itself about, yet people extol its breadth,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
善茹也人君不出戶牖而通天下為一身善聽
也若衛士傳餐身兼臣職者則已詑詑然拒人
千里矣而欲語配天之治是却步而求前也之
數君者其求治之心不下於堯舜也顧堯舜居
已於虛而彼方恃其材智以求過於堯舜焉其
所操者不同也然猶所謂聰明深慧者也所謂
彊毅聰察者也而未之慧且毅者又將若之何
哉奈之何其恃所長而自隘其天也雖然君能
好善而不能使善言之必聞猶未好也臣能陳
===
善而不能使善言之必行猶未陳也故進言有
五要歸於誠若以忿躁激烈之私而滋浮浪迂
誕之語則上下相持而不相入惟其諭之以理
主之以誠登對自盟而不敢援之為已功邀之
為已名真若幾諫其親而不拂於國體焉則至
誠感悟而吾之說行矣噫勿欺而犯信而後諫
此萬世臣道之極也
表
擬
punctuated:
善茹也；人君不出戶牖而通天下為一身，善聽也。若衛士傳餐、身兼臣職者，則已詑詑然拒人千里矣；而欲語配天之治，是却步而求前也。之數君者，其求治之心不下於堯、舜也；顧堯、舜居已於虛，而彼方恃其材智以求過於堯、舜焉，其所操者不同也。然猶所謂聰明深慧者也，所謂彊毅聰察者也；而未之慧且毅者，又將若之何哉？奈之何其恃所長而自隘其天也！雖然，君能好善而不能使善言之必聞，猶未好也；臣能陳善而不能使善言之必行，猶未陳也。故進言有五，要歸於誠。若以忿躁激烈之私而滋浮浪迂誕之語，則上下相持而不相入。惟其諭之以理，主之以誠，登對自盟，而不敢援之為已功、邀之為已名，真若幾諫其親而不拂於國體焉，則至誠感悟而吾之說行矣。噫！「勿欺而犯」、「信而後諫」，此萬世臣道之極也。

表
擬
translation_en:
… because it is good at taking in; a ruler does not step outside his door or window and yet unites the whole world as a single body, because he is good at listening. As for those who had palace guards pass them their meals and personally took on the duties of their ministers, they had already arrogantly repelled people a thousand li away! To wish to speak of governance that matches Heaven while acting thus is to walk backward while seeking to advance. Those several rulers had a desire to seek good governance no less than that of Yao and Shun. Yet Yao and Shun abided in humility, whereas those rulers relied on their own talent and intelligence in seeking to surpass Yao and Shun; what they held to was different. Even so, they were still what might be called intelligent and deeply wise, what might be called resolute and perceptive. What then will become of those who are neither wise nor resolute? How can a ruler rely on his own strengths and thereby narrow his own Heaven-endowed capacity! Even so, if a ruler is able to love goodness yet cannot ensure that good words are selalu heard, it is as if he did not love it; if a minister is able to set forth goodness yet cannot ensure that good words are put into practice, it is as if he had not set it forth. Therefore, although there are five ways of presenting advice, in essence they all come down to sincerity. If out of selfish resentment, impatience, and vehemence one multiplies frivolous, unrestrained, impractical, and absurd talk, then ruler and minister will stand in opposition and fail to reach one another. Only when one enlightens the ruler through principle, grounds oneself in sincerity, pledges oneself upon ascending to reply in audience, and dares not claim the advice as one's own merit or use it to seek personal fame—truly as if gently remonstrating with one's own parents without offending against the dignity of the state—will utmost sincerity move and awaken the ruler, and one's counsel be put into practice. Alas! "Do not deceive him, yet withstand him to his face," and "Only after having won his confidence should one remonstrate"—these are the ultimate standards of the way of a minister for ten thousand generations.

Memorial
An imitation of …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
皇上幸太學禮成羣臣
賀表萬曆四年
楊同春
同考試官敎諭徐批我
皇上心師至聖首舉臨雍將隆億萬年文明之治非特一時之慶也是作場厲閎休宛若躬逢
其盛者宜錄以傳
考試官敎諭劉批揄揚
昭代盛典儀制具悉而崇儒重道語意藹然不止駢麗而已
考試官敎諭蔣批才思充溢詞藻流麗可以彰盛美矣錄之
===
萬曆四年八月初二日臣某等恭遇
皇上
駕幸太學禮成臣等謹奉
表稱
賀者伏以
聖主右文
道建師儒之極
明王軌世
身先禮樂之宗風動八荒敎傳千古宮牆洽
punctuated:
皇上幸太學禮成羣臣賀表〔萬曆四年〕

楊同春

同考試官敎諭徐批：我皇上心師至聖，首舉臨雍，將隆億萬年文明之治，非特一時之慶也。是作場厲閎休，宛若躬逢其盛者，宜錄以傳。

考試官敎諭劉批：揄揚昭代盛典，儀制具悉，而崇儒重道，語意藹然，不止駢麗而已。

考試官敎諭蔣批：才思充溢，詞藻流麗，可以彰盛美矣，錄之。

萬曆四年八月初二日，臣某等恭遇皇上駕幸太學禮成，臣等謹奉表稱賀者。伏以聖主右文，道建師儒之極；明王軌世，身先禮樂之宗。風動八荒，敎傳千古，宮牆洽
translation_en:
… congratulatory memorial presented by the assembled officials upon the completion of the rites for His Majesty's personal visit to the National University [Fourth year of the Wanli era (1576)].

Yang Tongchun 楊同春

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu: Our August Sovereign takes the Supreme Sage as the teacher of his heart and was the first to carry out the royal visit to the Hall of Harmony, thereby exalting civilizing governance for billions of years to come—it is not merely an occasion for celebration in a single moment. This composition uplifts and proclaims [?] this grand felicity just as though the author had personally witnessed the splendor of the event; it ought to be recorded and transmitted.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu: It extols the grand ceremony of our illustrious dynasty, setting forth the ritual regulations in full detail, while its words and sentiments regarding the veneration of Confucians and esteem for the Way are gracious and harmonious—it is not merely ornate parallel prose.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jiang: Overflowing with talent and thought, and fluent and graceful in diction, it suffices to manifest the grand beauty of the occasion. Record it.

On the second day of the eighth month of the fourth year of the Wanli era, Your servants So-and-so and others, having reverently encountered the completion of the rites of His Majesty's imperial visit to the National University, respectfully present this memorial to offer congratulations. We humbly consider that when a sage ruler esteems culture, the Way establishes the ultimate standard for teachers and scholars; when an enlightened king gives order to the age, he leads in person as the exemplar of rites and music. His transforming influence stirs the eight wildernesses, his teaching is transmitted through a thousand ages, the walls of the learning palace are steeped in…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
慶章掖增輝臣等誠懽誠抃稽首頓首竊
惟王政以敎化爲先義隆首善治世以人
才爲急道在崇儒唐堯特命司徒勞來匡
直虞舜留心胄學直簡寛温禮備兩庠執
醬執爵而養老學沿三代至德至行以明
倫慨自竹帛煙秦吾道光芒暫息幸而大
牢祀魯斯文氣脉潜回環冠帶於橋門徒
增視聽羣薪蒸於牧竪致慨蓁蕪東漢重
興授明經而謾誇車服有唐嗣起增學舘
===
而大召名儒載拜標侈乎虛文治非元祐
橫議鼎生於上舍道未熈寧豈若
昭代之弘規遂揭
中天之文運兹蓋恭遇
皇帝陛下
堯仁舜孝
禹儉湯寛
溥離照以撫
鴻圖
punctuated: 慶，章掖增輝。臣等誠懽誠抃，稽首頓首。竊惟王政以敎化爲先，義隆首善；治世以人才爲急，道在崇儒。唐堯特命司徒，勞來匡直；虞舜留心胄學，直簡寛温。禮備兩庠，執醬執爵而養老；學沿三代，至德至行以明倫。慨自竹帛煙秦，吾道光芒暫息；幸而大牢祀魯，斯文氣脉潜回。環冠帶於橋門，徒增視聽；羣薪蒸於牧竪，致慨蓁蕪。東漢重興，授明經而謾誇車服；有唐嗣起，增學舘而大召名儒。載拜標侈乎虛文，治非元祐；橫議鼎生於上舍，道未熈寧。豈若昭代之弘規，遂揭中天之文運。兹蓋恭遇皇帝陛下，堯仁舜孝，禹儉湯寛，溥離照以撫鴻圖，
translation_en: … filled with rejoicing, and scholarly robes take on added radiance. We, Your Majesty's servants, are truly joyful and truly elated, bowing our heads to the ground and kowtowing. We humbly reflect that kingly governance puts moral transformation first, exalting righteousness at the capital as the premier model of goodness; ordering the world takes men of talent as its urgent priority, and the Way lies in venerating Confucian scholars. Yao of Tang specially charged the Minister of Instruction to encourage, attract, correct, and straighten the people; Shun of Yu devoted his heart to the education of noble scions, teaching them to be upright yet gentle,寬 magnanimous yet栗 firm, straightforward yet mild, and simplified yet discerning. Rituals were complete in the two academies, where the ruler personally held the sauce-jar and the wine-cup to nourish the aged; schools were handed down through the Three Dynasties, teaching supreme virtue and supreme conduct to elucidate human relationships. Alas, once bamboo slips and silk scrolls went up in smoke under the Qin, the brilliance of our Way was temporarily extinguished; fortunately, when the grand sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig was offered in Lu, the vital pulse of this culture quietly returned. Yet surrounding the bridged gates of the academy with capped and girdled scholars merely served to augment the spectacle for eyes and ears; and when herdsboys gathered firewood there, it caused men to sigh over the overgrown weeds. When the Eastern Han rose again, it conferred honors on masters of the classics, who vainly boasted of their carriages and robes; when the Tang subsequently arose, it expanded academic halls and grandly summoned famous Confucians. Yet bowing twice before a signpost was an extravagance of empty formality, and the governance was not that of the Yuanyou era; unbridled discussions boiled up like a cauldron in the Upper Hall of the Imperial University, and the Way had not yet brought peaceful prosperityeven in the Xining era. How could they compare with the grand regulations of our Illustrious Dynasty, which have raised high the cultural destiny of the midday sky! This is indeed because we have reverently encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, possessing the benevolence of Yao and the filial piety of Shun, the frugality of Yu and the magnanimity of Tang; spreading forth the radiant illumination of the Li trigram to pacify the great enterprise, …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
履謙光而凝
駿命
任賢勿貳切商宗之舟楫鹽梅
遜志有恒邁周王之刀劒戶牖
經筵與
講幃日
御游心化理之源
郊祀與
廟祭
===
躬承加意感孚之本
鸞廻
寶翰紀庶事以脩身
電覽
御屏察百官而勵治
功勤作聖
念及臨雍乃
咨弼直而渙
綸音遂
punctuated: 履謙光而凝駿命。任賢勿貳，切商宗之舟楫鹽梅；遜志有恒，邁周王之刀劒戶牖。經筵與講幃日御，游心化理之源；郊祀與廟祭躬承，加意感孚之本。鸞廻寶翰，紀庶事以脩身；電覽御屏，察百官而勵治。功勤作聖，念及臨雍。乃咨弼直而渙綸音，遂
translation_en: … treading the path of radiant humility to consolidate the great Mandate. In employing the worthy without duplicity, You show the earnestness of the Shang monarch seeking "oars and boats" and "salt and plum"; in maintaining a humble will with constancy, You surpass the Zhou king who inscribed warnings on his swords, knives, doors, and windows. Daily attending the Classics Colloquium and the lecture curtain, You let Your mind roam at the source of transformative governance; personally conducting the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple rites, You pay special heed to the foundation of spiritual resonance and sincerity. With phoenix-like flourishes of the imperial brush, You record the myriad affairs so as to cultivate Your person; with lightning-like glances at the imperial screen, You examine the hundred officials to encourage good rule. Diligent in the work of becoming a sage, Your thoughts turn to visiting the Imperial University. Thereupon You consult Your upright aides and issue Your silken words, and consequently…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
勅儀曹以稽
令典
齋心祗事涓吉戒途節應金風
麟斿藹西崑之瑞塵清
玉輦
鳳馭騰北極之輝
葆幢出
天宮擁千官而聲聯珩珮
翠華來日觀麗萬象而光徹虹霓璧水搖波
===
學海文章增煥儒林絢綵尼山日月彌高
神晤百代之師拜瞻維謹禮隆三爵之
制登奠必親有喜
天顏
命儒臣以坐講無涯
聖澤
宣中使以傳茶
明良胥慶於一堂彝倫攸敘啟沃披颺於六籍
忠讜畢敷寶鏐
punctuated: 勅儀曹以稽令典。齋心祗事，涓吉戒途。節應金風，麟斿藹西崑之瑞；塵清玉輦，鳳馭騰北極之輝。葆幢出天宮，擁千官而聲聯珩珮；翠華來日觀，麗萬象而光徹虹霓。璧水搖波，學海文章增煥；儒林絢綵，尼山日月彌高。神晤百代之師，拜瞻維謹；禮隆三爵之制，登奠必親。有喜天顏，命儒臣以坐講；無涯聖澤，宣中使以傳茶。明良胥慶於一堂，彝倫攸敘；啟沃披颺於六籍，忠讜畢敷。寶鏐
translation_en: …commanded the Bureau of Ceremonies to consult the established statutes. Fasting the mind and reverently attending to the affair, an auspicious day was chosen and the route prepared. As the season corresponded to the autumn winds, the unicorn-pennants radiated the auspiciousness of the western Kunlun Mountains; as the dust was cleared before the jade carriage, the phoenix-steeds soared with the brilliance of the Pole Star. The feathered canopies emerged from the heavenly palace, surrounded by a thousand officials with the linked chiming of their girdle-pendants; the kingfisher-plumed banners arrived from the Sun-Viewing Pavilion, adorning the myriad phenomena with a radiance penetrating the rainbows. The circular moat rippled with waves, and the literary splendor of the sea of learning grew ever more brilliant; the forest of scholars shone with color, and the sun and moon of Mount Ni rose ever higher. Communing in spirit with the Teacher of a Hundred Generations, His Majesty bowed and gazed with the utmost reverence; exalting the rites according to the system of three libations, He ascended to present the offerings in person. With joy upon the Celestial Countenance, He commanded the Confucian officials to be seated and lecture; with boundless imperial grace, He summoned the palace envoys to serve tea. The enlightened ruler and worthy ministers rejoiced together in a single hall, whereby the invariable human relationships were set in order; enlightening counsel was unfolded and proclaimed from the Six Classics, and loyal, forthright words were fully set forth. Precious gold…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
錫珍藏欣被
龍光優渥褒衣捧
綸綍恍驚
天語叮嚀
萬壽之樂章和鳴蹌蹌獸舞三姓之子孫咸萃
濟濟雲聯鷺序鵷班瞻
玉帛萬方之化雕題辮髮仰
奎躔千載之期
鐘鼓樂辟雍人心與天心俱協
===
風聲樹寰寓道統與治統齊光豈徒飭
曠典於
煕明蓋將挽
泰運於沕穆臣等材同樸棫幸與
陶甄俎豆無聞陋桓榮之稽古曝芹未獻企
孫復之紓忠共叨有事之榮駿奔非偶莫
頌無前之
美雀躍何勝伏願
嚴事心師
punctuated: 錫珍藏，欣被龍光優渥；褒衣捧綸綍，恍驚天語叮嚀。萬壽之樂章和鳴，蹌蹌獸舞；三姓之子孫咸萃，濟濟雲聯。鷺序鵷班，瞻玉帛萬方之化；雕題辮髮，仰奎躔千載之期。鐘鼓樂辟雍，人心與天心俱協；風聲樹寰寓，道統與治統齊光。豈徒飭曠典於煕明，蓋將挽泰運於沕穆。臣等材同樸棫，幸與陶甄。俎豆無聞，陋桓榮之稽古；曝芹未獻，企孫復之紓忠。共叨有事之榮，駿奔非偶；莫頌無前之美，雀躍何勝！伏願嚴事心師，
translation_en: …bestowed from the precious treasury, they joyfully receive the abundant favor of the Dragon Countenance; in ceremonial robes holding the silken imperial edicts, they are awestruck by the earnest injunctions of the Heavenly Words. As the musical odes of Myriad Longevity chime in harmony, the beasts dance in stately rhythm; as the descendants of the Three Lineages all gather together, they form a magnificent, cloud-like array. The court officials in their ranks of egrets and phoenixes behold the civilizing influence that draws jade and silk from the myriad regions; peoples with tattooed foreheads and braided hair look up to this once-in-a-millennium conjunction of the Literary Star. Bells and drums make joyful the Imperial University (Piyong), as the hearts of men and the heart of Heaven are in complete accord; the wind of moral instruction is established throughout the realm, as the succession of the Way and the succession of governance shine with equal brilliance. How could this merely be the observance of a rare ceremonial canon in an era of resplendent clarity? Truly, it is about to restore the fortune of Great Peace in profound and serene harmony. Your servants, with talents as humble as scrub oak, have been fortunate to partake in Your molding and fashioning. Ignorant of ritual vessels, we are ashamed before Huan Rong's study of antiquity; having not yet offered our humble sunning-and-wild-celery devotion, we look up expectantly to Sun Fu's expression of loyalty. Together we are graced with the honor of participating in this service, hastening in attendance not by mere chance; unable to fully eulogize such unprecedented beauty, how can we contain our leaping joy! We humbly pray that Your Majesty will reverently serve the Teacher of the Mind,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
懋敦身敎
羹牆見聖妙契千載之真傳
箕福斂疇盡協庶徵之
皇極臣鄰師師以承
式載賡虞陛之歌
帝德蕩蕩以齊
天遍擊唐衢之壤
河清海晏敷九譯而同文
日升月恒逾萬年而過曆臣等無任瞻
===
天仰
聖激切欣躍之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第參場
策
第一問
楊應兆
punctuated:
懋敦身敎。羹牆見聖，妙契千載之真傳；箕福斂疇，盡協庶徵之皇極。臣鄰師師以承式，載賡虞陛之歌；帝德蕩蕩以齊天，遍擊唐衢之壤。河清海晏，敷九譯而同文；日升月恒，逾萬年而過曆。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切欣躍之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第參場

策

第一問

楊應兆
translation_en:
…and diligently cultivate personal instruction. Seeing the sage in soup and on walls, may You wonderfully accord with the true transmission of a thousand years; gathering the Five Blessings of the Great Plan of Jizi, may You fully harmonize the August Ultimate with all the various verifications. Ministers and aides emulate one another in receiving Your model, continuing the songs at the steps of Yu's court; Imperial virtue is vast and boundless, equal to Heaven, as the clod-tapping song resounds across the thoroughfares of Tang. With the Yellow River clear and the seas calm, civilization spreads through ninefold translations and unifies the script; like the rising sun and the waxing moon, the dynasty will surpass ten thousand years and exceed its divined span. Your servants, filled beyond measure with awe as we gaze upon Heaven and look up to the Sage in earnest and joyful elation, respectfully present this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session

Policy Essays

Question One

Yang Yingzhao

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正梁批我
皇祖及我
皇上天縱聖神心學相契眞與堯舜媲美者子能闡揚道妙推本政源而忠悃溢於辭表豈甞管窺天德者耶
考試官教諭劉批頌述發心學之精揄揚切忠藎
之獻必俊拔之士也取之
考試官教諭蔣批敷揚精切似有忠愛之實心
者錄之
帝王之所以運治者其心乎帝王之所以
純心者其敬乎蓋治統於道道原於天敬
===
則所以純其心而會天之精者也故開泰
者敬以格天則創一代之鴻圖而聲光流
於後世保泰者敬以祈天則承萬世之丕
基而紹述光於前烈厎之爲績所以運天
工也昭之爲謨所以煥天章也懿爍之治
與造化交相流焉固帝王之純學而千聖
一軌者乎知此則我
皇祖之懋昭聖學我
皇上之仰契心傳
punctuated:
同考試官學正梁批：「我皇祖及我皇上，天縱聖神，心學相契，眞與堯、舜媲美者。子能闡揚道妙，推本政源，而忠悃溢於辭表，豈甞管窺天德者耶？」
考試官教諭劉批：「頌述發心學之精，揄揚切忠藎之獻，必俊拔之士也，取之。」
考試官教諭蔣批：「敷揚精切，似有忠愛之實心者，錄之。」
帝王之所以運治者，其心乎？帝王之所以純心者，其敬乎？蓋治統於道，道原於天，敬則所以純其心而會天之精者也。故開泰者敬以格天，則創一代之鴻圖，而聲光流於後世；保泰者敬以祈天，則承萬世之丕基，而紹述光於前烈。厎之爲績，所以運天工也；昭之爲謨，所以煥天章也。懿爍之治，與造化交相流焉，固帝王之純學，而千聖一軌者乎！知此，則我皇祖之懋昭聖學，我皇上之仰契心傳，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Liang: "Our Imperial Ancestor and our reigning Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagehood and divinity, correspond to one another in the learning of the mind-and-heart, truly matching the excellence of Yao and Shun. You are able to expound the subtleties of the Way and trace the sources of governance, while loyal sincerity overflows beyond your words—how could you be one who merely peers at Heavenly virtue through a narrow tube?"
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Liu: "His eulogizing exposition brings forth the essence of the learning of the mind-and-heart, and his praise is earnest in offering loyal devotion. He must be a scholar of outstanding talent; select this."
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Jiang: "His elaboration is precise and pertinent; he seems to be one who possesses a genuine heart of loyalty and affection. Record this."
Is not that by which emperors and kings conduct governance their mind-and-heart? And is not that by which emperors and kings purify their mind-and-heart their reverence? For governance is unified in the Way, the Way originates in Heaven, and reverence is that whereby one purifies one's mind-and-heart and joins with the essence of Heaven. Therefore, he who inaugurates an era of great peace uses reverence to reach Heaven, thereby founding the grand enterprise of an age so that his renown and brilliance flow down to posterity; he who preserves an era of great peace uses reverence to pray to Heaven, thereby inheriting the great foundation of ten thousand generations so that his continuation and transmission shed lustre upon the achievements of his predecessors. Brought to realization as accomplishments, it is that whereby the work of Heaven is carried out; made manifest as counsels, it is that whereby the patterns of Heaven are illuminated. Splendid and radiant governance flows in mutual harmony with the creative transformations of nature—surely this is the pure learning of emperors and kings, in which a thousand sages follow a single track! Understanding this, then how our Imperial Ancestor strenuously illuminated sage learning, and how our reigning Emperor looks up in harmony with the transmission of the mind-and-heart, …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聖神媲美超軼萬禩者可得而揄揚其實矣請
敬陳之嘗謂天有元氣而元化充溢則天
之化天之心爲之也聖人位其位而子其
民則亦當心其心而不敢怠故精一之祕
肇自堯舜授受之間以底時雍風動之化
而史臣賛其爲欽恭者即精一之旨也乃
若舜之授禹亦惟揭斯道而傳之蓋其心
眞見夫天之可畏有能持吾之說以安天
下後世之民則吾之仰承乎天者亦可以
===
不愧此其至公至仁之心固治統所基亦
道統所自也禹湯承堯舜之傳而垂之爲
子孫之業其欽恭之心視堯舜尤惓切矣
故平成肇於祇台允殖隆於日躋堯舜之
統乃自數聖人衍之而敬止敬勝文武可
例而知也上古聖人所以開萬世之麗者
其心有一息不純於敬哉漢唐諸君開國
者闊略於草昧繼體者循習於故常諸不
暇論即如宣帝之齋居決事稱勵精矣而
punctuated: 聖神媲美，超軼萬禩者，可得而揄揚其實矣。請敬陳之。嘗謂天有元氣，而元化充溢，則天之化，天之心爲之也。聖人位其位而子其民，則亦當心其心而不敢怠。故「精一」之祕，肇自堯、舜授受之間，以底時雍、風動之化；而史臣賛其爲「欽」、「恭」者，即「精一」之旨也。乃若舜之授禹，亦惟揭斯道而傳之。蓋其心眞見夫天之可畏，有能持吾之說以安天下後世之民，則吾之仰承乎天者亦可以不愧。此其至公至仁之心，固治統所基，亦道統所自也。禹、湯承堯、舜之傳，而垂之爲子孫之業，其欽恭之心，視堯、舜尤惓切矣。故「平成」肇於「祇台」，「允殖」隆於「日躋」；堯、舜之統，乃自數聖人衍之，而「敬止」、「敬勝」，文、武可例而知也。上古聖人所以開萬世之麗者，其心有一息不純於敬哉？漢、唐諸君，開國者闊略於草昧，繼體者循習於故常，諸不暇論；即如宣帝之齋居決事，稱勵精矣，而
translation_en:
… matching in sage and divine virtue and surpassing ten thousand generations—can thus have their true substance extolled. Allow me respectfully to set this forth.

It has been said that Heaven possesses the primordial vital energy, and when primordial transformation overflows, Heaven's transformation is wrought by the mind of Heaven. When the sage occupies Heaven's position and treats its people as his children, he too must take Heaven's mind as his own mind and never dare be remiss. Therefore, the secret of being "refined and single-minded" began with the transmission between Yao and Shun, thereby achieving the transformation of universal harmony and wind-like moral influence; and what the court historian praised in them as "reverent" and "respectful" was none other than the essential meaning of being "refined and single-minded." As for Shun's transmission to Yu, he likewise held up this very Way and passed it down. For in his mind he truly perceived that Heaven is to be held in awe: if there were someone capable of upholding his teaching to bring peace to the people of the world and of future generations, then in his own reverent reception of Heaven's mandate he would have nothing of which to be ashamed. This supremely impartial and supremely benevolent mind was assuredly the foundation upon which the succession of governance rested, and also the source from which the succession of the Way arose.

Yu and Tang received the transmission of Yao and Shun and handed it down as the patrimony for their descendants; their minds of reverence and respect were even more earnest and urgent than those of Yao and Shun. Thus, the achievement of "order and completion" began with "revering my virtue," and "sincere cultivation" flourished through "daily ascending"; the succession of Yao and Shun was extended through these several sages, and from "resting in reverence" and "reverence prevailing," Kings Wen and Wu can by analogy be understood. In opening up glorious rule for ten thousand generations, did the minds of the sages of high antiquity ever for a single breath cease to be pure in reverence?

As for the various rulers of Han and Tang, the dynastic founders were rough and neglectful amid the Disorder of nascent rule, while the succeeding sovereigns merely followed routine and custom. Setting aside the rest for lack of time to discuss them, even when Emperor Xuan of Han decided affairs of state while in fasting seclusion—which was praised as diligent governance—he still…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不免雜於申韓太宗之帝範垂訓稱盛治
矣而猶多慚於內德危竿之喻致治四十
餘年損齋之記噓宋燼而再燃之似若可
馥稿竹之載者然湛靜安舒流於姑息國
威未振今猶病其損之過焉要之數君者
無得於純心之學而徒以機智材辨矯飾
一時故僅足以名季世之業而擬諸帝王
何啻碔砆之相懸也哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
===
天錫智勇締搆
邦家酬雪則功高百王廓清則
統承五帝其
駿德鴻庥混闢以來未有也乃當開創之初而
預為萬世之慮履無前之業而益操兢惕
之懷故昭揭
琬琰光映典謨諸不勝睹記而至精至要為
聖神之榘矱者如
皇明祖訓永垂燕翼自嚴祀至供用規畫井然
punctuated: 不免雜於申、韓；太宗之《帝範》垂訓，稱盛治矣，而猶多慚於內德。「危竿」之喻，致治四十餘年；《損齋》之記，噓宋燼而再燃之，似若可馥稿竹之載者。然湛靜安舒，流於姑息；國威未振，今猶病其損之過焉。要之，數君者無得於純心之學，而徒以機智材辨矯飾一時，故僅足以名季世之業；而擬諸帝王，何啻碔砆之相懸也哉！洪惟我太祖高皇帝，天錫智勇，締搆邦家；酬雪則功高百王，廓清則統承五帝，其駿德鴻庥，混闢以來未有也。乃當開創之初，而預為萬世之慮；履無前之業，而益操兢惕之懷。故昭揭琬琰，光映典謨，諸不勝睹記；而至精至要、為聖神之榘矱者，如《皇明祖訓》永垂燕翼，自嚴祀至供用，規畫井然，
translation_en:
…could not avoid mixing in the methods of Shen Buhai 申不害 and Han Fei 韓非. Taizong 太宗 [of Tang] left behind the Models for an Emperor (Difan 帝範) as instruction, and his reign was praised as an era of flourishing governance, yet he still had much to be ashamed of regarding his domestic virtue. The metaphor of the "perilous pole" [of Emperor Renzong 仁宗 of Song] brought about more than forty years of good governance, and the Record of the Studio of Diminution (Sunzhai ji 損齋記) [of Emperor Gaozong 高宗 of Song] blew upon the ashes of the Song to rekindle them—these seemed as though they might impart fragrance to the records on dried bamboo slips [?]. Yet the former's deep calm and comfortable ease slipped into laxity, while under the latter, national prestige failed to be roused, and even today people still fault him for carrying "diminution" to excess. In short, these several rulers gained nothing of the learning of the pure mind, and merely used cleverness, talent, and eloquence to put on a false display for their own time. Thus they were barely sufficient to make a name for achievements of a later age; and if compared with the ancient Emperors and Kings, how could the disparity be merely that between a common stone (wufu 碔砆) and jade!

Vast indeed was our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi 太祖高皇帝)! Heaven endowed him with wisdom and valor to found and construct the state. In avenging humiliation and wiping away shame, his merit surpassed a hundred kings; in sweeping clear the realm, his succession continued that of the Five Emperors. Such great virtue and vast blessings had never existed since the creation of the world. Yet at the very beginning of his founding of the dynasty, he took thought beforehand for ten thousand generations; occupying an unprecedented enterprise, he held all the more to an attitude of cautious vigilance. Therefore, what he luminously set forth on jade tablets, shining alongside the Canons and Counsels (Dian Mo 典謨), is more than can all be read or recorded. As for those works that are most refined and most essential, serving as the standard and model for sacred and divine rulers: for instance, the Ancestral Injunctions of the August Ming (Huang Ming zuxun 皇明祖訓) eternally hands down a protective legacy for posterity; from the solemn sacrifices to the provisions for imperial use, its regulations and plans are in perfect order…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而持守一章尤爲王政之綱焉固帝王時
幾之勅也
資世通訓表倡臣民自君道至民用法戒具
陳而尊賢遠佞尤切淬厲之衷焉固帝王
危微之訓也
敬天忠君孝親爲要而反身契篤恭之軌則
精誠一錄見於吳沉所輯者可睹也人心虛
靈乘機出入而操存密精一之學則
觀心有記見於宋濂所述者可頌也此固
===
聖祖之文謨炳麗萬禩如新者而仰窺其奧亦
不越
祖訓之所謂敬畏者而已蓋能憂天下必受
天眷大哉
皇言固統乎精誠觀心諸記而一貫之矣是非
心天之心而學堯舜之學者哉
列聖相承授守一道我
皇上
天縱聖哲
punctuated: 而「持守」一章，尤爲王政之綱焉，固帝王時幾之勅也。《資世通訓》表倡臣民，自「君道」至「民用」，法戒具陳，而尊賢遠佞，尤切淬厲之衷焉，固帝王危微之訓也。敬天、忠君、孝親爲要，而反身契篤恭之軌，則《精誠》一錄，見於吳沉所輯者可睹也。人心虛靈，乘機出入，而操存密精一之學，則《觀心》有記，見於宋濂所述者可頌也。此固聖祖之文謨炳麗，萬禩如新者；而仰窺其奧，亦不越《祖訓》之所謂「敬畏」者而已。蓋「能憂天下，必受天眷」，大哉皇言，固統乎《精誠》、《觀心》諸記而一貫之矣！是非心天之心，而學堯、舜之學者哉？列聖相承，授守一道。我皇上天縱聖哲，
translation_en: …while the chapter on "Maintaining Steadfastness" (Chishou) especially serves as the overarching principle of kingly governance; this is truly the emperors' and kings' admonition on timely attention to the subtle springs of action. The General Instructions for Benefiting the World (Zishi tongxun) sets forth a standard to guide subjects and commoners; from "The Way of the Ruler" (Jundao) to "The Practices of the People" (Minyong), models and warnings are fully laid out, while honoring the worthy and keeping sycophants at a distance especially touches upon the innermost heart of self-cultivation and exertion; this is truly the emperors' and kings' instruction on the perilousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the moral mind. Revering Heaven, being loyal to the ruler, and being filial to parents are taken as the essentials, and through self-reflection one accords with the path of earnest reverence—thus the single record of the Record of Sincerity (Jingcheng lu), as seen in what was compiled by Wu Chen 吳沉, may be beheld. The human mind is numinous and void, going out and coming in as occasion prompts, yet holding fast and preserving it refines the learning of pure and unified concentration—thus there is the account in the Record on Contemplating the Mind (Guanxin ji), as seen in what was set forth by Song Lian 宋濂, which may be recited in praise. These are indeed the resplendent literary counsels of the Sacred Ancestor, remaining as fresh as new for ten thousand generations; yet when we look up and peer into their profound depths, they do not go beyond what the Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun) call "reverence and awe." For "he who is able to be anxious for all under Heaven will surely receive the favor of Heaven"—great indeed are these august words, which truly encompass and bind together with a single thread the Record of Sincerity, the Record on Contemplating the Mind, and the other writings! Is this not taking the mind of Heaven as one's own mind, and studying the learning of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜? The successive Sacred Emperors have inherited and upheld this same Way. Our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sage wisdom…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
丕闡鴻猷
講讀則寒暑不廢
聽納則芻蕘不遺其
勅幾慎位敬承之烈莫竝也然時方
冲睿而志必企乎堯舜治雖熙洽而念每戒
乎盈成故
親灑
宸翰訓勵臣工諸不勝捧頌而至純至粹媲美
聖祖之謨烈者有一十二事
===
宣付史館以之存心則所謂
謹天戒存敬畏收放心者卽我
聖祖省躬憂恤乗機操存之意也以之保身則
所謂
慎起居慎出入節飲食者卽我
聖祖居安懐警節飲時食之慮也因扣角而慨
遺賢闢優伶而旌讜論
聖祖之貴德遠佞者切矣
皇上親賢任能遠佞納忠之
punctuated: 丕闡鴻猷。講讀則寒暑不廢，聽納則芻蕘不遺，其勅幾慎位、敬承之烈莫竝也。然時方冲睿，而志必企乎堯、舜；治雖熙洽，而念每戒乎盈成。故親灑宸翰，訓勵臣工，諸不勝捧頌，而至純至粹、媲美聖祖之謨烈者，有一十二事，宣付史館。以之存心，則所謂「謹天戒、存敬畏、收放心」者，卽我聖祖省躬憂恤、乗機操存之意也；以之保身，則所謂「慎起居、慎出入、節飲食」者，卽我聖祖居安懐警、節飲時食之慮也。因扣角而慨遺賢，闢優伶而旌讜論，聖祖之貴德遠佞者切矣；皇上「親賢任能、遠佞納忠」之
translation_en:
…greatly unfolds grand plans. In his classical lectures and readings, he does not cease for winter's cold or summer's heat; in listening to and accepting advice, he does not overlook even the words of grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers. His illustrious achievements in attending carefully to the subtle springs of affairs, guarding his position with caution, and reverently carrying on the dynastic heritage are without peer. Yet, though he is still in his youthful wisdom, his aspirations inevitably reach toward Yao and Shun; though governance is bright and harmonious, his thoughts ever guard against complacency in fullness and completion. Therefore, he has personally wielded the imperial brush to instruct and encourage his officials and ministers. While there are more writings than one could possibly finish holding up to praise, those that are most pure and unadulterated, matching in beauty the counsels and achievements of the Sacred Ancestor (Emperor Taizu), consist of twelve maxims delivered for promulgation to the Historiography Institute.

As for using them to preserve the mind, the maxims "Heed the warnings of Heaven," "Maintain reverence and awe," and "Recover the straying mind" express the very intention of our Sacred Ancestor in examining himself, feeling anxious concern, and seizing every opportunity to hold fast to his mind. As for using them to protect the person, the maxims "Be cautious in daily routine," "Be cautious in going out and coming in," and "Moderate drink and food" express the very concern of our Sacred Ancestor in remaining vigilant while dwelling in security, moderating drink, and taking food at proper times. Moved by the tale of striking the ox's horn, he sighed over neglected worthies; rejecting actors and jesters, he honored forthright counsel—how earnest was the Sacred Ancestor in prizing virtue and keeping flatterers at a distance! Does not His Majesty's [imperial decree] "Draw close to the worthy and employ the capable," "Keep flatterers at a distance and accept loyal advice"…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
旨其後先一德乎
賜張眞而威薛顯汰金飾而種隙地
聖祖之飭法愼儉者至矣
皇上明賞罰撙節用之
旨其創述一軌乎此我
皇上之睿藻輝煌光紹
祖烈者而竊探其要亦不越
宸翰之所謂敬畏者而已蓋能存敬畏則百度
惟貞旨哉
===
聖謨固統乎身心政治之詳而備舉之矣是非
心
聖祖之心學堯舜之學者哉嗟乎自放勳至我
明凡幾千禩而
皇祖之學與堯舜若同堂焉自
國初至
今日餘二百年而
皇上之學與
聖祖若面授焉得非
punctuated: 旨，其後先一德乎！賜張眞而威薛顯，汰金飾而種隙地，聖祖之飭法愼儉者至矣；皇上明賞罰、撙節用之旨，其創述一軌乎！此我皇上之睿藻輝煌，光紹祖烈者，而竊探其要，亦不越宸翰之所謂「敬畏」者而已。蓋能存敬畏，則百度惟貞。旨哉聖謨！固統乎身心政治之詳而備舉之矣。是非心聖祖之心、學堯舜之學者哉？嗟乎！自放勳至我明，凡幾千禩，而皇祖之學與堯舜若同堂焉；自國初至今日，餘二百年，而皇上之學與聖祖若面授焉。得非
translation_en: …decrees: do not the earlier and the later share the very same virtue? Bestowing rewards on Zhang Zhen 張眞 while overawing Xue Xian 薛顯, and eliminating gold ornaments while cultivating vacant palace grounds—the Sacred Ancestor's enforcement of the law and careful frugality reached the utmost; and His Majesty's decrees on clarifying rewards and punishments and restraining expenditures: do not the founder and the successor follow the very same track? Such is the radiant brilliance of our Emperor's imperial compositions, gloriously continuing the achievements of the Ancestor; yet if we humbly probe their essential point, it goes no further than what the imperial calligraphy calls "reverent awe." For when one can preserve reverent awe, all governance is rectified. How profound are the sacred counsels! Truly they encompass the full details of personal cultivation and governance and set them forth completely. Is this not taking the mind of the Sacred Ancestor as one's own mind, and learning the learning of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜? Alas! From Fangxun 放勳 [Yao] down to our Ming dynasty is several thousand years, yet the learning of our Imperial Ancestor and that of Yao and Shun are as if in the same hall; from the founding of the dynasty to the present day is more than two hundred years, yet the learning of His Majesty and that of the Sacred Ancestor are as if transmitted face to face. Is it not that…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聖神授受心心相照而一敬孚天不求其同而
自無不同者乎彼昔岣嶁之碑人爭模頌
而飛白答詔迄今以為美談蓋神禹之德
萬世猶存而貞觀之治亦希世賢君也故
翰墨一流矜詡後世矧我
聖祖之製訓
皇上之宸謨龍盤鳳翥固超墳典而麗日星者
也即如宋濂吳沉所紀不能揚
祖烈之盛而
===
皇上御極以來時和年登民康物阜炎荒奏凱
窮髮輸琛即勳華相繼與
聖祖肇造之烈不能過之雖使鴻筆之臣畫天
測海莫能鋪張萬一而愚生草茅之見執
事固欲其推本政原以裨
聖治哉然堯舜至聖不廢交儆之謨而桂彥良
養心寡欲之諷於
聖祖惓惓焉則愚生仰窺
聖心之虛敢獻曝矣夫人君深居九重而天下
punctuated: 聖神授受，心心相照，而一敬孚天，不求其同而自無不同者乎？彼昔岣嶁之碑，人爭模頌；而飛白答詔，迄今以為美談。蓋神禹之德，萬世猶存；而貞觀之治，亦希世賢君也。故翰墨一流，矜詡後世。矧我聖祖之製訓，皇上之宸謨，龍盤鳳翥，固超墳典而麗日星者也。即如宋濂、吳沉所紀，不能揚祖烈之盛；而皇上御極以來，時和年登，民康物阜，炎荒奏凱，窮髮輸琛，即勳、華相繼，與聖祖肇造之烈，不能過之。雖使鴻筆之臣，畫天測海，莫能鋪張萬一，而愚生草茅之見，執事固欲其推本政原，以裨聖治哉！然堯、舜至聖，不廢交儆之謨；而桂彥良養心寡欲之諷，於聖祖惓惓焉。則愚生仰窺聖心之虛，敢獻曝矣。夫人君深居九重，而天下
translation_en: … that through the transmission and reception of the sacred and divine, their minds illuminate one another, and through a single reverence that accords with Heaven, without seeking to be identical, they are naturally no different? In times past, people vied to take rubbings of and praise the stele of Mount Goulou, while the answering edict written in flying-white calligraphy is spoken of with admiration to this day. This is because the virtue of the divine Yu endures for ten thousand generations, and the ruler of the Zhenguan reign was likewise a rare worthy sovereign in the world; thus, once their brush and ink flowed forth, they were boasted of by later ages. How much more so the imperial instructions composed by our Sacred Progenitor and the imperial counsels of His Majesty! Like coiling dragons and soaring phoenixes, they truly surpass the Three Mounds and Five Canons (Fendian) and shine alongside the sun and stars. Even what was recorded by Song Lian 宋濂 and Wu Chen 吳沉 could not fully extol the splendor of our Progenitor's illustrious achievements. And since His Majesty ascended the throne, the seasons have been harmonious and harvests abundant, the people peaceful and goods plentiful; triumphs have been reported from the fiery wilderness of the south, and treasures offered in tribute from the barren lands of the far north. Even the succession of Yao (Fangxun) and Shun (Chonghua), or the founding achievements of our Sacred Progenitor, could not surpass this. Even if ministers of grand literary talent were to try to depict Heaven and fathom the sea, they could not set forth one ten-thousandth of it—yet Your Excellency truly wishes for this foolish student, with his humble rustic views, to trace the fundamental origins of governance so as to benefit the sacred rule! Still, though Yao and Shun were supremely sage, they did not dispense with counsels of mutual admonition; and Gui Yanliang 桂彥良 was earnest and devoted in his remonstrance to our Sacred Progenitor on nourishing the mind and lessening desires. Thus, gazing up to perceive the open-mindedness of the sacred heart, this foolish student dares to offer his humble counsel, like the peasant offering the warmth of the sun. Now, the ruler of men dwells deep within the ninefold palace, yet the people of the world…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之人洞若觀火一念壅遏則化機不流必
乾健不息者乃足以保泰凝命也矧參天
之榦養於萌蘖放海之波清於源流少成
天性習慣自然聖人惜時而慎初者大學
之所以爲豫也
皇上春秋鼎盛
天聰瑩然固靈根初植而真源未汩
宗社生靈所恃以爲乆安長治之基者也惟
卽其所謂敬畏者操之有恒養之無間
===
大廷渙號丞弼端
臨莫非出往游衍之天而蜎蜎蠖濩之中雷聲
淵默之際尤必慎於幾微鑑於
祖訓益乎吾心之天者亟充之戾乎吾心之天
者亟制之兢兢然若堯之勅幾禹之惜陰
而一十二事永爲慎脩之盤銘几戒焉則
聖質疑定
懿德淵涵氣鬯神流日新月盛而
駿烈
punctuated: 之人洞若觀火。一念壅遏，則化機不流；必乾健不息者，乃足以保泰凝命也。矧參天之榦養於萌蘖，放海之波清於源流。少成天性，習慣自然，聖人惜時而慎初者，《大學》之所以爲豫也。皇上春秋鼎盛，天聰瑩然，固靈根初植而真源未汩，宗社生靈所恃以爲乆安長治之基者也。惟卽其所謂敬畏者，操之有恒，養之無間。大廷渙號，丞弼端臨，莫非出往游衍之天；而蜎蜎蠖濩之中，雷聲淵默之際，尤必慎於幾微，鑑於祖訓。益乎吾心之天者亟充之，戾乎吾心之天者亟制之，兢兢然若堯之勅幾、禹之惜陰，而一十二事永爲慎脩之盤銘几戒焉。則聖質疑定，懿德淵涵，氣鬯神流，日新月盛，而駿烈
translation_en:
…of the world see into him as clearly as looking at fire. If a single thought becomes obstructed, the mechanism of transformation ceases to flow; only by being unceasingly vigorous like Heaven can one preserve great peace and consolidate the Mandate. How much more so since a trunk that reaches the sky is nourished from a sprout, and waves that reach the sea are clarified at their source! What is formed in youth becomes like innate nature, and habit becomes second nature; that the sages cherished time and were cautious at the beginning is what the Great Learning (Daxue) means by preparedness.

His Majesty is in the prime of his youth and his heavenly intelligence is crystal clear; truly, the numinous root has just been planted and the true source has not yet been muddied—this is what the ancestral altars and the living people rely upon as the foundation for lasting peace and enduring order. Only let him take this so-called reverence and awe, hold to it with constancy, and nourish it without interruption. When issuing proclamations in the grand court and presiding in rectitude over his輔弼 ministers, all is within the Heaven of his going forth and strolling at ease; yet within the secluded depths of the palace, amidst thunderous majesty and abyssal silence, he must be especially cautious over subtle incipient tendencies and take mirror from the Ancestral Injunctions. Whatever benefits the Heaven of his mind, let him urgently expand it; whatever violates the Heaven of his mind, let him urgently restrain it—cautious and circumspect, like Yao's ordering of the subtle springs of action and Yu's cherishing of every inch of shadow on the sundial, taking those twelve matters forever as the washbasin inscriptions and armrest admonitions for his careful self-cultivation. Then his sagely substance will be firmly established, his admirable virtue deeply infused, his vital energy harmonious and his spirit flowing, renewing daily and flourishing monthly, while his magnificent achievements…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
奎章巍然煥然人將稱爲萬世之堯舜我
皇祖諄切貽謀之心亦與天壤相爲不朽矣愚
生何幸躬逢其
盛
第二問
楊同春
同考試官教諭徐批法無寬嚴惟當而已治久人玩
行法者可事姑息乎子能參酌往事與時權衡可謂通達治體者
考試官教諭劉批博洽中有超然之趣奇士也
===
考試官教諭蔣批評議精確是知飭法振民者
聖人之愛天下也甚厚而其慮天下也常
周愛之厚則身視中國家視寰宇保抱煦
育之意必欲其並生於和平溫飫之區慮
之周則防乎其漸制乎其流使之循習於
規矩繩束之內而後寄其愛於不窮故用
法之意常主於寬而持法之術必貴於嚴
寬非徇天下也拘攣褊迫之政恐滋無聊
之心而絞鮮束濕民不堪其命焉故濟之
punctuated:
奎章巍然煥然，人將稱爲萬世之堯、舜，我皇祖諄切貽謀之心，亦與天壤相爲不朽矣。愚生何幸，躬逢其盛！

第二問
楊同春
同考試官教諭徐批：法無寬嚴，惟當而已。治久人玩，行法者可事姑息乎？子能參酌往事，與時權衡，可謂通達治體者。
考試官教諭劉批：博洽中有超然之趣，奇士也。
考試官教諭蔣批：評議精確，是知飭法振民者。

聖人之愛天下也甚厚，而其慮天下也常周。愛之厚，則身視中國，家視寰宇，保抱煦育之意，必欲其並生於和平溫飫之區；慮之周，則防乎其漸，制乎其流，使之循習於規矩繩束之內，而後寄其愛於不窮。故用法之意常主於寬，而持法之術必貴於嚴。寬非徇天下也，拘攣褊迫之政，恐滋無聊之心，而絞鮮束濕，民不堪其命焉，故濟之
translation_en:
…and imperial writings will stand lofty and resplendent, so that men will hail His Majesty as a Yao or Shun for ten thousand generations, and the earnest heart with which Our Imperial Ancestor bequeathed his counsel will likewise endure as immortally as heaven and earth. How fortunate is this humble student to witness such a flourishing age in person!

Question Two
Yang Tongchun 楊同春
Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐 comments: In the law, there is neither leniency nor severity—only what is fitting. When peace has lasted long and people grow lax, how can those who enforce the law indulge in overly寬 [indulgent] forbearance? You are able to weigh past events and balance them against the needs of the times; you may truly be called one who thoroughly understands the principles of governance.
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: Amidst broad learning there is a transcendent flair; he is an extraordinary scholar.
Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: His evaluations and arguments are precise and accurate; here is one who knows how to rectify the laws and rouse the people.

The sage's love for the world is exceedingly deep, and his forethought for the world is ever comprehensive. Because his love is deep, he regards the Central State as his own person and the entire realm as his own family; in his desire to cherish, embrace, and warmly nurture all people, he wishes them to live together in a realm of peace, warmth, and abundance. Because his forethought is comprehensive, he guards against incipient tendencies and checks their spread, causing the people to become accustomed to following within the bounds of rules and restraints, and only thus does he entrust his love to them inexhaustibly. Therefore, the intent in applying the law always gives primacy to leniency, whereas the art of upholding the law must value severity. Leniency does not mean pandering to the world: cramped and narrow-minded governance might breed a sense of hopelessness, and when administration is as harsh as mangling small fish or binding wet firewood, the people cannot bear the demands placed upon them; therefore one tempers it…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以寬成其嚴也嚴非苦天下也怠弛疎闊
之過恐生不羈之習而吞舟逸柙民不勝
其弊焉故操之以嚴成其寬也原聖人之
愛以用法存聖人之慮以操法而要於其
當譬諸御馬者急其箠而舒其轡不致跛
曳而泛駕鼓瑟者促其柱而疏其絃不致
沾滯而噍殺焉則天下無廢法無惰事而
理道可言矣敢敬陳之夫天之道好生者
也然而春溫冬肅惠風迅雷常並行於覆
幬之間如其資生之仁卽春而不冬雨而
不雪降祥而不降殃足矣而何其竝用不
廢若此也蓋不斂則不舒不震則不育天
固知其不可廢也惟陽居大夏陰居窮冬
霜雷十而二之災沴十而一之則其仁可
掬矣聖人之仁天下豈不欲其羸衣枵食
如已飫溫萎膏臏醒如已蘇快歡然若吾
家人父子之親而顧以法震之乎蓋天下
之情難固而其隙易開强掩弱衆暴寡利
punctuated:
以寬，成其嚴也。嚴非苦天下也，怠弛疎闊之過，恐生不羈之習，而吞舟逸柙，民不勝其弊焉，故操之以嚴，成其寬也。原聖人之愛以用法，存聖人之慮以操法，而要於其當。譬諸御馬者，急其箠而舒其轡，不致跛曳而泛駕；鼓瑟者，促其柱而疏其絃，不致沾滯而噍殺焉。則天下無廢法，無惰事，而理道可言矣。敢敬陳之。

夫天之道，好生者也。然而春溫冬肅，惠風迅雷，常並行於覆幬之間。如其資生之仁，卽春而不冬，雨而不雪，降祥而不降殃足矣，而何其竝用不廢若此也？蓋不斂則不舒，不震則不育，天固知其不可廢也。惟陽居大夏，陰居窮冬，霜雷十而二之，災沴十而一之，則其仁可掬矣。聖人之仁天下，豈不欲其羸衣枵食如已飫溫，萎膏臏醒如已蘇快，歡然若吾家人父子之親，而顧以法震之乎？蓋天下之情難固而其隙易開，强掩弱，衆暴寡，利
translation_en:
… with leniency, so as to accomplish its strictness. Strictness is not meant to torment the empire; when faults of negligence, laxity, and carelessness arise, one fears they may engender unbridled habits, and when fish big enough to swallow a boat slip the net and wild beasts escape their cages, the people cannot bear the resulting abuses—therefore one holds fast to it with strictness, so as to accomplish its leniency. By tracing the sage's love in applying the law, and preserving the sage's foresight in wielding the law, one arrives at what is fitting. Take for example driving horses: one plies the whip briskly while slackening the reins, so that they neither limp and drag nor bolt and overturn the carriage; or playing the zither: one sets the bridges close while spacing out the strings, so that the sound is neither sluggish and bogged down nor shrill and harsh. Then in the empire there will be no neglected laws and no slackened affairs, and the way of good governance can be spoken of. I venture respectfully to set this forth.

Now the Way of Heaven delights in life. Yet the warmth of spring and the severity of winter, gentle breezes and sudden thunder, constantly operate side by side beneath the canopy of the sky. If it were solely a matter of its benevolence in sustaining life, then having spring without winter, rain without snow, and sending down auspices without calamities would suffice—why then does it employ both together without discarding either like this? Indeed, without contraction there is no expansion, and without startling thunder there is no nurturing growth; Heaven surely knows that neither can be dispensed with. Yet because yang presides over the great summer while yin is confined to the depths of winter, and frost and thunder account for but two parts in ten while calamities and noxious气的 disturbances account for but one part in ten, its benevolence is palpable enough to be scooped up in the hands. When the sage extends his benevolence to the empire, how could he not wish that those in tattered clothes and with empty stomachs might be as warm and well-fed as himself, that those with withered flesh and severed kneecaps might be revived and restored to comfort like himself [?], all rejoicing together with the affection of family, father, and son—why instead should he awe them with the law? It is because the passions of the empire are hard to keep secure and rifts easily open: the strong overwhelm the weak, the many tyrannize the few, over profit…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不相分而相攘智不相教而相賊不有以
齊之則僭競凌獵不能有其衣食妻子甚
則冒上忘等天下之大可畏者至矣故肉
刑制於邃初而殛鯀誅苗之事去洪荒未
遠也然數聖人者不曰欽恤則曰惟中三
公八議以酌其情嘉石肺石以通其隱使
天下不困於敲扑犴狴之間輸金束矢之
罰而姦雄悍慢一與法忤毅然裁之故怙
終者不得逭其誅過誤者又得伸其枉稂
===
莠既去嘉禾乃茂聖人以爲必如是天下
後世之民始得恃吾法以無恐也故其意
藹如春煦如露而其法則嚴若峭壁迅若
轟雷神若天降地設而民不敢玩焉豈惟
民之不敢玩哉有法則固無法則潰卽制
法者亦不得而玩之也按細柳之轡而君
不得馳格主長之僕而后不得怒勇若烏
獲嬖若韓彭成若操懿而鰓鰓然恐不逃
於三尺者聖人之法固然也乃用法者曲
punctuated: 不相分而相攘，智不相教而相賊。不有以齊之，則僭競凌獵，不能有其衣食妻子；甚則冒上忘等，天下之大可畏者至矣。故肉刑制於邃初，而殛鯀誅苗之事去洪荒未遠也。然數聖人者，不曰「欽恤」，則曰「惟中」。三公八議以酌其情，嘉石、肺石以通其隱，使天下不困於敲扑犴狴之間、輸金束矢之罰；而姦雄悍慢，一與法忤，毅然裁之。故怙終者不得逭其誅，過誤者又得伸其枉。稂莠既去，嘉禾乃茂。聖人以爲必如是，天下後世之民始得恃吾法以無恐也。故其意藹如春、煦如露，而其法則嚴若峭壁、迅若轟雷，神若天降地設，而民不敢玩焉。豈惟民之不敢玩哉？有法則固，無法則潰，卽制法者亦不得而玩之也。按細柳之轡，而君不得馳；格主長之僕，而后不得怒。勇若烏獲，嬖若韓、彭，成若操、懿，而鰓鰓然恐不逃於三尺者，聖人之法固然也。乃用法者曲
translation_en: … Instead of sharing profit, they snatch it from one another; instead of using wisdom to instruct one another, they use it to harm one another. If there were nothing by which to regulate them, they would overstep their bounds in rivalry and encroach upon one another, unable even to keep their own food, clothing, wives, and children. At worst, they would offend their superiors and forget distinctions of rank, and what is most dreadful in all under Heaven would arrive. Therefore, corporal punishments were instituted in remote antiquity, and the execution of Gun 鯀 and the punishment of the Miao 苗 took place not far removed from the primordial era. Yet those several sages, if they did not speak of "reverent compassion," spoke of "clinging to the mean." They instituted the Three Dukes and the Eight Deliberations to weigh the circumstances of a case, and the Admonishing Stone (jiashi 嘉石) and the Red Stone (feishi 肺石) to give voice to hidden grievances, ensuring that the empire would not be distressed among the beatings and prisons or by the fines of metal and bundles of arrows. Yet as for the treacherous, ambitious, fierce, and arrogant, the moment they ran afoul of the law, the sages resolutely struck them down. Thus, repeat offenders could not escape execution, while those who erred by mistake were able to have their grievances redressed. Once the weeds are removed, the fine grain flourishes. The sages considered that only when things were done in this way could the people of the empire and future generations rely on their laws and be free from fear. Therefore, their intentions were as genial as spring and as warm as the dew, yet their laws were as stern as a sheer cliff, as swift as a peal of thunder, and as awe-inspiring as if sent down by Heaven and established by Earth, so that the people dared not trifle with them. And was it only the people who dared not trifle with them? With laws, the state is secure; without laws, it collapses—even those who make the laws cannot trifle with them. When the reins were held at Xiliu 細柳, the sovereign could not gallop his horse; when the servant of the Elder Princess was struck down, the Empress could not vent her anger. Though one be as brave as Wu Huo 烏獲, as favored as Han Xin 韓信 and Peng Yue 彭越, or as accomplished as Cao Cao 曹操 and Sima Yi 司馬懿, yet still trembles in fear of not escaping the three-foot statutes—such indeed is the nature of the sages' law. Yet those who administer the law are partial…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
於一隅而不知中正仁義之意故以嚴濟
嚴則威竭而不振爲咸陽之轍矣以寬濟
寬則惠褻而下不以爲恩爲元成之季矣
不有昭曠域外之觀何以維天下之法而
定持法者之評哉彼東山之征兩觀之誅
非戕懿親而違眾好也法不得徇也乃尹
鐸李牧諸賢至於墮城縱寇而公庾且矯
發焉何其剸觚恣行若是也蓋事有必集
無庸於拘攣禍迫爲也故五日告完不繕
===
非惰矣一鼓成烈縱寇非殃矣志全子母
則田叔不嫌於燬詞心在憂民則長孺不
忌於發粟若夫通融庫藏固伯淳達權濟
時之宜而循良化誨卽文饒之蒲鞭且贅
矣之數子者原聖人之意以權天下之宜
而不疑於君不訾於吏者固以寬而用嚴
者也盜器不族犯蹕不刑非輕主威而縱
惡少也法不得過也若夫武侯魏公諸賢
至於賊友抑功而噸笑且不假焉何其刻
punctuated: 於一隅，而不知中正仁義之意。故以嚴濟嚴，則威竭而不振，爲咸陽之轍矣；以寬濟寬，則惠褻而下不以爲恩，爲元、成之季矣。不有昭曠域外之觀，何以維天下之法，而定持法者之評哉？彼東山之征、兩觀之誅，非戕懿親而違眾好也，法不得徇也。乃尹鐸、李牧諸賢，至於墮城、縱寇，而公庾且矯發焉，何其剸觚恣行若是也？蓋事有必集，無庸於拘攣禍迫爲也。故五日告完，不繕非惰矣；一鼓成烈，縱寇非殃矣。志全子母，則田叔不嫌於燬詞；心在憂民，則長孺不忌於發粟。若夫通融庫藏，固伯淳達權濟時之宜；而循良化誨，卽文饒之蒲鞭且贅矣。之數子者，原聖人之意，以權天下之宜，而不疑於君，不訾於吏者，固以寬而用嚴者也。盜器不族、犯蹕不刑，非輕主威而縱惡少也，法不得過也。若夫武侯、魏公諸賢，至於賊友、抑功，而噸笑且不假焉，何其刻…
translation_en:
…to a single corner, failing to understand the meaning of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness. Therefore, when severity is supplemented with severity, authority is exhausted and cannot be roused, following in the tracks of Xianyang [the fall of Qin]; when leniency is supplemented with leniency, kindness becomes cheapened and subordinates do not regard it as grace, ending up like the late reigns of Emperors Yuan and Cheng [of Han]. Without a bright, expansive vision that transcends conventional bounds, how could one uphold the laws of the empire and settle the evaluations of those who administer the law?

Those campaigns of the Eastern Mountains [by the Duke of Zhou] and the execution beneath the Two Watchtowers [by Confucius] were not cases of harming close kin or defying popular sentiment; the law simply could not be bent for private favors. Yet worthies such as Yin Duo 尹鐸 and Li Mu 李牧 went so far as to demolish城 walls [or reduce fortifications] and let raiders go unchallenged, and public granaries were even opened by forged decree [as by Ji An 汲黯]—why did they trim the corners of the law and act so unrestrainedly? It is because when an affair must be brought to completion, there is no use in acting with cramped, narrow-minded urgency [reading 禍迫 as 局迫/褊迫]. Thus, when the walls were reported complete in five days, not having repaired them earlier was not laziness; when heroic victory was achieved at a single drumbeat, having let the raiders go was not a disaster. Because his ambition was to preserve both mother and son [Empress Dowager Dou and King孝 of Liang], Tian Shu 田叔 did not shy away from burning the testimony; because his heart lay in worrying for the people, Changru 長孺 [Ji An] did not hesitate to distribute grain from the granaries. As for flexibly shifting treasury funds, that was indeed Bochun's 伯淳 [Cheng Hao 程顥] expedient for adapting to circumstances and aiding the times; and where upright officials transform the people through instruction, even Wenrao's 文饒 [Liu Kuan 劉寬] reed whip becomes superfluous. These several gentlemen traced the intent of the sages in order to weigh what was appropriate for the empire; that they were neither suspected by their rulers nor criticized by the functionaries is because they inherently used leniency to carry out the strictness of the law.

Not exterminating the clan of one who stole sacred vessels from the imperial temple, and not executing one who trespassed on the cleared imperial roadway [as judged by Zhang Shizhi 張釋之], were not cases of slighting the ruler's majesty or indulging wicked youths; the law simply could not be exceeded. Yet worthies such as the Martial Marquis [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] and the Duke of Wei [Zhang Jun 張浚] went so far as to execute a friend or suppress merits, and would not even grant a casual frown or smile [as with Bao Zheng 包拯]—why were they so harsh…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
核寡恩若是也蓋法在必行無容於賣法
徇情爲也故不戮馬謖則祁山之師不可
出不繩曲端則符離之敗不可救欲防邊
釁宋璟非薄於靈筌欲懲悍胥一錢非忍
於張詠若夫以嚴成功固孝肅澄清輦轂
之意而豪右恣橫卽李果之峻厲非苛矣
之數子者得聖人之慮以振天下之玩而
內不逼主外不僨事固以嚴而成寬者也
要之各有當焉而非膠柱者可與議也我
===
聖祖酌古準今博稽逖覽制為成法以肅天下
臣民之心功當事事當言則賞功不當事
事不當言則誅輿馬服器邊備夷情靡不
有一定之制
神聖潤色愈精愈詳行於縣邑州郡總於監司
府部而大臣挈其綱臺諫補其闕餘二百
年道揆法守凜如也夜半出片紙卽豪宗
悍帥與四夷君長如笞小兒法令之行固
矣然巨憝遁播於山澤贓吏尚逸於刑網
punctuated: 核寡恩若是也？蓋法在必行，無容於賣法徇情爲也。故不戮馬謖，則祁山之師不可出；不繩曲端，則符離之敗不可救。欲防邊釁，宋璟非薄於靈筌；欲懲悍胥，一錢非忍於張詠。若夫以嚴成功，固孝肅澄清輦轂之意；而豪右恣橫，卽李果之峻厲非苛矣。之數子者，得聖人之慮以振天下之玩，而內不逼主，外不僨事，固以嚴而成寬者也。要之各有當焉，而非膠柱者可與議也。我聖祖酌古準今，博稽逖覽，制為成法，以肅天下臣民之心。功當事、事當言則賞，功不當事、事不當言則誅，輿馬服器、邊備夷情，靡不有一定之制。神聖潤色，愈精愈詳，行於縣邑州郡，總於監司府部，而大臣挈其綱，臺諫補其闕，餘二百年，道揆法守，凜如也。夜半出片紙，卽豪宗悍帥與四夷君長，如笞小兒，法令之行固矣。然巨憝遁播於山澤，贓吏尚逸於刑網，
translation_en:
…so harsh and unfeeling? It is because once the law is set to be enforced, there is no room for bending the law or indulging personal feelings. Thus, had Ma Su 馬謖 not been executed, the army at Mount Qi (Qishan 祁山) could not have marched forth; had Qu Duan 曲端 not been disciplined, the defeat at Fuli 符離 could not have been remedied. In seeking to prevent border provocations, Song Jing 宋璟 was not being ungenerous toward Hao Lingquan 郝靈筌; in seeking to punish an unruly clerk, Zhang Yong 張詠 was not being cruel over a single copper coin. As for achieving success through severity, that was indeed the intention of Bao拯 (Xiaosu 孝肅) in purifying the imperial capital; and when powerful magnates act with unbridled arrogance, even the sternness of Li Guo 李果 [?] is not overly harsh. These several men grasped the forethought of the sages in order to shake the realm out of its complacency; inwardly they did not crowd their ruler, and outwardly they did not ruin affairs—truly they achieved leniency through severity. In sum, each approach had its proper application, and this is not something that can be discussed with those who stubbornly cling to fixed rules.

Our Sacred Ancestor (Taizu 太祖) weighed antiquity and measured the present, conducting broad investigations and far-reaching surveys to establish definitive laws that would instill reverence in the hearts of officials and subjects throughout the realm. When achievements matched the undertaking and the undertaking matched the words, rewards were given; when achievements did not match the undertaking and the undertaking did not match the words, punishment was meted out. From carriages, horses, vestments, and implements to frontier defenses and barbarian affairs, there was nothing without a fixed regulation. Succeeding sacred emperors refined and embellished these laws, making them ever more precise and detailed. They are carried out in the districts, subprefectures, and prefectures, and drawn together by the Surveillance Commissions, Chief Military Commissions, and Ministries, while the grand ministers hold the main cords and the Censorate and Speaking Officials mend any omissions. For over two hundred years, the principles of governance and the observance of the law have been held in awe. If a single slip of paper is issued at midnight, even powerful clans, fierce commanders, and the chieftains of the four barbarian peoples submit as effortlessly as a child being switches; the enforcement of laws and ordinances is firm indeed. Yet arch-criminals still flee and scatter into the mountains and marshes, corrupt officials still escape the net of punishment,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
越獄劫餉踵踵報聞誠如執事所憂者大
都俗乆而玩情狃而偷也積弛之後利用
振刷乃慮豪傑之士觸足冒法而又以持
法太急下多不肖之心愈密愈巧焉噫此
豈法之弊哉行法者弊之也彼獸廢爪牙
則充豺虎之腸矣國無紀綱則授姦雄之
柄矣積金在市掉臂不顧置姬嬙於闉闍
而人不敢睨目者法也法其可不嚴乎蓋
使誠賢智而濫傷也誠猾傑而逸網也法
===
之過也然而不然也今之人固有跡似而
實不似者可遽信之乎即如不繕城郭擅
用庫錢果皆尹鐸伯淳之賢乎則簿書期
會之間稍存寬大涵容之意不然未可縱
也即如大言無當輕身冒敵果皆馬謖曲
端之不肖乎則壞法干紀之秋自有信賞
必罰之典不然未可繩也此心跡之當辨
者也贓吏以獄為市俗儒以寬為仁而福
田報應之說浸其骨髓往往骫法紀以惠
punctuated: 越獄劫餉，踵踵報聞，誠如執事所憂者。大都俗乆而玩，情狃而偷也。積弛之後，利用振刷，乃慮豪傑之士觸足冒法，而又以持法太急，下多不肖之心，愈密愈巧焉。噫！此豈法之弊哉？行法者弊之也。彼獸廢爪牙，則充豺虎之腸矣；國無紀綱，則授姦雄之柄矣。積金在市，掉臂不顧，置姬嬙於闉闍，而人不敢睨目者，法也。法其可不嚴乎？蓋使誠賢智而濫傷也，誠猾傑而逸網也，法之過也。然而不然也。今之人固有跡似而實不似者，可遽信之乎？即如不繕城郭，擅用庫錢，果皆尹鐸、伯淳之賢乎？則簿書期會之間，稍存寬大涵容之意；不然，未可縱也。即如大言無當，輕身冒敵，果皆馬謖、曲端之不肖乎？則壞法干紀之秋，自有信賞必罰之典；不然，未可繩也。此心跡之當辨者也。贓吏以獄為市，俗儒以寬為仁，而福田報應之說浸其骨髓，往往骫法紀以惠
translation_en: …and prison breaks and the plundering of military provisions are reported one after another—it is truly as Your Excellency worries. On the whole, when customs persist for a long time, people grow negligent; when sentiments become habituated, people turn lax. After accumulated laxity, it is beneficial to apply vigorous renewal. Yet there is concern that men of heroic talent may stumble into violating the law at every step, and also that if the law is enforced too urgently, those below will harbor unworthy intentions, becoming ever more devious as the law becomes ever more exacting. Alas! Is this really the fault of the law? Those who enforce the law have corrupted it. When a beast loses its claws and fangs, it serves only to fill the bellies of jackals and tigers; when a state lacks discipline and order, it hands the handle of power over to treacherous and ambitious men. When gold is piled up in the marketplace and passersby swing their arms without a backward glance, or when noble beauties such as Ji and Qiang are placed at the outer city gates and no one dares cast a sidelong look at them—that is due to the law. How, then, can the law not be strict? For if the truly worthy and wise were wantonly harmed, and the truly cunning and defiant escaped the net, that would be the fault of the law. Yet it is not so. Among people today, there are certainly those whose outward actions resemble something that their inner reality does not; can one hastily trust them? For instance, those who refrain from repairing city walls or who use treasury funds without authorization—are they truly all as worthy as Yin Duo 尹鐸 and Bochun 伯淳 [Cheng Hao 程顥]? If so, then amid routine accounting and administrative deadlines, one may preserve a measure of leniency and tolerance; otherwise, they must not be indulged. Or for instance, those who make grand, unfounded boasts or recklessly throw themselves against the enemy—are they truly all as unworthy as Ma Su 馬謖 and Qu Duan 曲端? If so, then in times when the law is broken and discipline violated, there are naturally the statutes of trustworthy rewards and certain punishments; otherwise, they must not be summarily restrained by the letter of the law. This is how intentions and outward actions ought to be distinguished. Corrupt officials treat litigation as a marketplace, and vulgar Confucians mistake leniency for benevolence; steeped to the marrow in doctrines of karmic merit and retribution, they frequently bend the laws and discipline to show favor to…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
姦慝其高明者爭事風力以搏虚聲希望
過聽濫肆誅求至於刻木畫地而不敢對
則寛嚴胥失其中矣此積習之當禁者也
多指亂視多言亂聽從古患之今
國家申飭法制本非益於其舊卽有不測之
恩威意在集事而耳視目聽者未究其歸
明一法則病其煩寛一人則疑其故而泄
泄然以為無擾可也無所事事可也則天
下之法竟何自而申耶此議論之當定者
===
也嗟乎今天下之士試思其所以訓子弟
束臧獲者能愛而不勞乎能粱肉而不撻
笞乎勞之笞之固成之也吾能愛天下如
其子弟如其家人足矣奈何以按法循令
者為過而為迂闊不經之論也卽謂鷹鸇
不若鸞鳳溲渤不若參苓而為天下興利
擇便以循疾苦然紀綱不嚴姦黠壅遏吾
之惠能逮於民否也棟梁相持寛則不相
固斲者不苦不甘乃成室焉此用法之平
punctuated: 姦慝；其高明者，爭事風力以搏虚聲，希望過聽，濫肆誅求，至於刻木畫地而不敢對，則寛嚴胥失其中矣。此積習之當禁者也。多指亂視，多言亂聽，從古患之。今國家申飭法制，本非益於其舊，卽有不測之恩威，意在集事，而耳視目聽者未究其歸，明一法則病其煩，寛一人則疑其故，而泄泄然以為無擾可也，無所事事可也，則天下之法竟何自而申耶？此議論之當定者也。嗟乎！今天下之士，試思其所以訓子弟、束臧獲者，能愛而不勞乎？能粱肉而不撻笞乎？勞之笞之，固成之也。吾能愛天下如其子弟、如其家人足矣，奈何以按法循令者為過，而為迂闊不經之論也？卽謂鷹鸇不若鸞鳳，溲渤不若參苓，而為天下興利擇便以循疾苦，然紀綱不嚴，姦黠壅遏，吾之惠能逮於民否也？棟梁相持，寛則不相固；斲者不苦不甘，乃成室焉。此用法之平
translation_en:
…the wicked. Meanwhile, those who consider themselves high-minded vie to display stern vigor in order to grasp at hollow fame; currying favor and listening to faulty counsel, they wantonly engage in exactions and punishments to the point where people would rather face a wooden effigy of an official or a prison drawn on the ground and dare not answer them—thus leniency and severity both lose the mean. These are ingrained habits that must be prohibited.

That too many pointing fingers confuse the sight and too many words confuse the hearing has been a trouble since antiquity. Now when the state reiterates and tightens the laws and institutions, it is not actually adding to the old ones; even where there are unfathomable acts of grace or severity, the intent is to accomplish the work of government. Yet those who see with their ears and hear with their eyes fail to examine the ultimate aim: when a single law is clarified, they criticize it as burdensome; when a single person is pardoned, they suspect an ulterior motive. Languid and remiss, they think it enough merely to avoid causing disturbance and enough to do nothing at all—how then can the laws of the empire ever be enforced? These are the debates that must be settled.

Alas! Let the scholars of the world today reflect on how they instruct their younger kinsmen and restrain their bondservants: can they love them without making them toil? Can they feed them fine grain and meat without ever flogging them? To make them toil and to flog them is truly how one brings them to completion. It would suffice if we could love the empire as we do our younger kinsmen and our own household members; why then regard those who uphold the laws and follow the ordinances as being at fault, and spin pedantic, impractical theories? Even if one says that hawks and falcons are not as good as luan-birds and phoenixes, or that purge-herbs are not as good as ginseng and poria, and wishes instead to promote benefits and choose conveniences for the empire so as to soothe the distress of the people—still, if discipline and order are not strict, and the crafty and cunning block the way, can our benevolence actually reach the common people or not? When ridgepoles and beams support one another, if the joinery is too loose they will not hold fast; only when the carpenter cuts neither too tightly nor too loosely is the house completed. This is the balance in applying the law…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也尹鐸張詠諸賢之意亦聖人之意也非
所謂商君韓非子之意也而老氏欲剖斗
折衡以求不爭正苦於民不畏死耳豈謂
寛然以廢天下之法者哉故下有截然之
規上有渾然之意使士農工賈各勤本業
賞罰進退必當功罪紳弁循矩愒玩以飭
法守而輕重出入惟
朝廷之指使焉至於
廟堂之間交儆協心振紀綱而志不狃於因
===
循維風俗而具必先於教化則元氣既厚
神氣自振嘉樂唐虞固易易也令行事集
豈足言哉
第三問
傅爾珎
同考試官教諭毛批四事方今急務未易措置是
策洞悉源委而經畫井然蓋未離畝畝而先天下之憂者也
考試官教諭劉批區畫明盡卓有遠識
考試官教諭蔣批條列四事鑿鑿可行經世之學也
punctuated:
也。尹鐸、張詠諸賢之意，亦聖人之意也，非所謂商君、韓非子之意也。而老氏欲剖斗折衡以求不爭，正苦於民不畏死耳，豈謂寛然以廢天下之法者哉？故下有截然之規，上有渾然之意，使士、農、工、賈各勤本業，賞罰、進退必當功罪，紳弁循矩，愒玩以飭法守，而輕重出入，惟朝廷之指使焉。至於廟堂之間，交儆協心，振紀綱而志不狃於因循，維風俗而具必先於教化，則元氣既厚，神氣自振，嘉樂唐、虞，固易易也，令行事集，豈足言哉！

第三問
傅爾珎
同考試官教諭毛批：四事方今急務，未易措置。是策洞悉源委，而經畫井然，蓋未離畝畝而先天下之憂者也。
考試官教諭劉批：區畫明盡，卓有遠識。
考試官教諭蔣批：條列四事，鑿鑿可行，經世之學也。
translation_en:
… [this is the fairness of applying the law.] It was the intention of worthies such as Yin Duo 尹鐸 and Zhang Yong 張詠, and also the intention of the sages—not what is meant by the intentions of Lord Shang 商君 and Han Feizi 韓非子. When Laozi 老氏 wished to smash the peck-measures and snap the steelyards in order to seek non-contention, it was precisely because he was troubled that the people did not fear death; how could he have meant indulgently abolishing the laws of the realm? Therefore, when below there are clear-cut regulations and above there is an all-embracing benevolence, causing scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants each to be diligent in their fundamental occupations; when rewards and punishments, promotions and demotions, invariably match merits and offenses; when civil and military officials abide by the rules, and those who are negligent and lax are made to rectify their observance of the law [?], while the weighing of severity and leniency follows solely the direction of the Court; and when, within the imperial ancestral temple and court, all admonish one another and unite their hearts, rousing state discipline so that their resolve does not fall into the rut of mere routine, and upholding customs while ensuring that the instruments of governance put moral transformation first—then, once the vital energy of the state is abundant, its spirit will naturally be invigorated. To achieve the joyous harmony of Tang 唐 and Yu 虞 would truly be quite easy; is the mere carrying out of orders and accomplishment of affairs even worth mentioning?

Third Policy Question
Fu Erzhen 傅爾珎
Associate Examiner and Instructor Mao 毛 comments: The four matters are urgent tasks of the present day and not easy to manage. This policy essay thoroughly understands their origins and developments, and its planning is orderly and methodical; truly, this is someone who has not yet left the fields and yet worries before the rest of the world does.
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: The planning and arrangements are clear and exhaustive, showing outstanding foresight.
Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: Setting out the four matters item by item, every point is solid and practicable—this is statecraft learning.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天下之事有不能不因乎古者有不能必
因乎古者時至而勢必趨焉勢趨而理必
從焉順必至之理而權其當爲之時宜於
法古不嫌於非今宜於準今不嫌於悖古
則時不我窮也勢不我局也而事必如吾
議矣何者時異而我之應不窮也夫聽亂
於多而事斷於獨固也然衢室總章郊祀
鹽鐵諄諄而議固以時勢之當非衆見弗
與也然局者變態神倏而不能逃於圖譜
===
之中症與方合舉而用之旬日脉候不齊
易一方而愈焉此國手也議法者何以異
此今天下之事其可議者孰有大於河患
虜患乎又孰急於
宗祿民兵乎然議之而卒莫能應之者篤於
時也夫黃河爲患從古病之三代而下議
治河者不過賈讓賈魯之策矣然讓之議
除害而非興利魯之策塞決而不濬流均
無裨於運道也
punctuated:
天下之事，有不能不因乎古者，有不能必因乎古者。時至而勢必趨焉，勢趨而理必從焉。順必至之理，而權其當爲之時，宜於法古，不嫌於非今；宜於準今，不嫌於悖古。則時不我窮也，勢不我局也，而事必如吾議矣。何者？時異而我之應不窮也。夫聽亂於多，而事斷於獨，固也；然衢室、總章、郊祀、鹽鐵，諄諄而議，固以時勢之當，非衆見弗與也。然局者變態神倏，而不能逃於圖譜之中；症與方合，舉而用之，旬日脉候不齊，易一方而愈焉，此國手也。議法者何以異此？

今天下之事，其可議者，孰有大於河患、虜患乎？又孰急於宗祿、民兵乎？然議之而卒莫能應之者，篤於時也。夫黃河爲患，從古病之。三代而下，議治河者，不過賈讓、賈魯之策矣。然讓之議，除害而非興利；魯之策，塞決而不濬流，均無裨於運道也。
translation_en:
Among the affairs of the realm, there are those in which one cannot but follow antiquity, and those in which one cannot necessarily follow antiquity. When the time arrives, the trend of circumstances inevitably moves in that direction; when the trend of circumstances moves in a direction, principle inevitably follows it. If one complies with the principle that must inevitably come to pass and weighs the time for what ought to be done—when it is appropriate to model oneself on antiquity, not shying away from criticizing the present, and when it is appropriate to take the present as the standard, not shying away from departing from antiquity—then the times will not drive us to exhaustion, circumstances will not hem us in, and affairs will surely turn out as we deliberate. Why is this? Because as the times change, our responses remain inexhaustible. Now, it is certainly true that listening to many voices breeds confusion while affairs are decided by a single mind; yet in the consultations in the Hall of the Crossroads (Qushi) and the Hall of Grand Regulation (Zongzhang), and in the court debates over the suburban sacrifices and the salt and iron monopolies, people deliberated earnestly and repeatedly simply because finding what was fitting for the times and circumstances could not be achieved without the participation of collective views. Moreover, although a game on the board changes its configurations with wondrous suddenness, it cannot escape the patterns recorded in the manuals; and when an illness matches a prescription, one takes it up and applies it, yet if after ten days the pulse and symptoms no longer correspond, changing to another prescription brings about a cure—this is the mark of a master physician of the realm. How is deliberating on laws and policies any different from this?

Among the affairs of the realm today that call for deliberation, which are greater than the disasters of the Yellow River and the menace of the northern caitiffs?
