And which are more urgent than the stipends of the imperial clan and the civilian militia? Yet the reason people deliberate over them and in the end are unable to respond effectively is that they are overly bound to the conventions of the moment. Now, the Yellow River has been a scourge and an affliction since antiquity. From the Three Dynasties downward, those who deliberated on controlling the River have gone no further than the policy proposals of Jia Rang 賈讓 and Jia Lu 賈魯. Yet Jia Rang's deliberation aimed at removing harm rather than promoting benefit, and Jia Lu's policy focused on plugging breaches rather than dredging the current; neither is of any help to the Grand Canal grain transport route.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
國家倚藉河運歲輸百萬石以實
京師今茶城淤梗蓋數年矣直沽之運旣以
漂沒告罷而境山柪石難疏膠萊海水相
隔是膠河之難竟亦勢也嘗聞
國初運道自淮達河自沁通衞兩不相妨嗣
緣河决張秋乃導汶洸諸泉之利而徐吕
險峻必資黃水行舟遂因蕭縣决口通浮
濟二洪而河始侵漕矣然猶未病也嘉靖
末年華山再决北徙茶城上侵漕河七十
===
餘里則河病而漕亦病焉有如茶城東决
橫截漕河其害可勝言哉故復符離之故
道改黃河於徐州之東而倍築長堤護衞
陵寢分河漕而兩利焉責重費鉅然至計也暫
開浮濟之淤以避茶城之害玉花諸泉引
濟徐吕或斷流而大濬焉事便工省亦近
策也然水性就下智者順之今草灣雲梯
等關日淤日壅尾閭不通上源安得而不
漫乎故移泇萊二河之費以疏其壅而又
punctuated: 國家倚藉河運，歲輸百萬石以實京師。今茶城淤梗，蓋數年矣。直沽之運，旣以漂沒告罷；而境山柪石難疏，膠萊海水相隔，是膠河之難竟，亦勢也。嘗聞國初運道，自淮達河，自沁通衞，兩不相妨。嗣緣河决張秋，乃導汶、洸諸泉之利，而徐、吕險峻，必資黃水行舟，遂因蕭縣决口，通浮濟二洪，而河始侵漕矣，然猶未病也。嘉靖末年，華山再决，北徙茶城，上侵漕河七十餘里，則河病而漕亦病焉。有如茶城東决，橫截漕河，其害可勝言哉！故復符離之故道，改黃河於徐州之東，而倍築長堤，護衞陵寢，分河漕而兩利焉，責重費鉅，然至計也。暫開浮濟之淤，以避茶城之害，玉花諸泉，引濟徐、吕，或斷流而大濬焉，事便工省，亦近策也。然水性就下，智者順之。今草灣、雲梯等關，日淤日壅，尾閭不通，上源安得而不漫乎？故移泇、萊二河之費，以疏其壅，而又
translation_en: Our dynasty relies on river transport, annually shipping millions of piculs of grain to supply the capital. Now, the channel at Chacheng 茶城 has been silted up and obstructed for several years. Sea transport via Zhigu 直沽 has already been halted due to shipwrecks and losses; meanwhile, the stubborn rock [柪石, for 礓石?] at Jingshan 境山 is difficult to dredge, and the Jiaolai 膠萊 canal route is separated by seawater, so the difficulty of completing the Jiao River project is also dictated by physical circumstances. I have heard that at the beginning of our dynasty, the grain transport route went from the Huai 淮 River to the Yellow River, and from the Qin 沁 River to the Wei 衞 River, neither interfering with the other. Later, because the Yellow River breached its banks at Zhangqiu 張秋, they channeled the waters of the Wen 汶, Guang 洸, and various springs for their benefit; and since the rapids at Xuzhou 徐州 and Lüliang 吕梁 were treacherous and steep, boats had to rely on the waters of the Yellow River to navigate. Consequently, they used the breach at Xiaoxian 蕭縣 to connect and float across the two rapids, and thus the Yellow River first began to encroach upon the Grand Canal—yet it had not become a serious affliction. In the final years of the Jiajing 嘉靖 reign (1522–1566), the river breached again at Huashan 華山, shifting northward to Chacheng and encroaching upstream into the Grand Canal for over seventy li, whereupon both the Yellow River and the Grand Canal suffered. Should it breach eastward at Chacheng and cut straight across the Grand Canal, how could the damage be fully described! Therefore, restoring the old course at Fuli 符離, diverting the Yellow River to the east of Xuzhou, and building double-strength long dikes to protect the imperial mausoleums, thereby separating the Yellow River and the Grand Canal for the benefit of both—this carries heavy responsibility and enormous expense, yet it is the ultimate plan. Temporarily dredging the silt at Fuji 浮濟 [or: dredging the silt to float across and aid the canal] to avoid the hazard at Chacheng, and drawing the Yuhua 玉花 and other springs to supply the Xuzhou and Lüliang rapids, or damming the flow to carry out a major dredging—this is convenient in execution and economical in labor, making it a practical short-term policy. Yet the nature of water is to flow downward, and the wise follow it. Today, passes such as Caowan 草灣 and Yunti 雲梯 grow more silted and blocked by the day; when the lower outlet is obstructed, how can the upper reaches fail to overflow? Therefore, redirecting the funds meant for the Jia 泇 and Jiaolai 萊 rivers to dredge these blockages, and furthermore…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
多開支河以洩怒濤北而芝蔴等莊南而
高寶等堤靡不為之實心經理而嚴其賞
罰使防河與防虜等焉庶人心競勸事懷
永圖而飛輓雲連運道其有濟矣夷狄為
患從古記之自周以來議制虜者不過撻
伐和親之策耳然迅掃幕南或失之黷和
親歲幣或失之辱均無益於國體者也
先帝威稜遠播今
上文武聖神北虜稽款邊燧不警軼曩代矣顧
===
夷馬之散處無策而羸豕之蹢躅當防其
說非過計也愚謂夷狄之强弱異時而中
國之措置異便今之夷狄其强非冒頓其
弱非呼韓也夫其不若冒頓也而歸降則
拒款市則却固不免於狹小
皇化而其不若呼韓也則又安得狃於柙虎篝
鷹而漫然不為之備也故責屯練之實効
徹桑土於未雨之時而修築大邊歸併小
堡藉羈靡而修守焉計歲程功此急務也
punctuated:
多開支河以洩怒濤。北而芝蔴等莊，南而高寶等堤，靡不為之實心經理，而嚴其賞罰，使防河與防虜等焉。庶人心競勸，事懷永圖，而飛輓雲連，運道其有濟矣。

夷狄為患，從古記之。自周以來，議制虜者，不過撻伐、和親之策耳。然迅掃幕南，或失之黷；和親歲幣，或失之辱，均無益於國體者也。先帝威稜遠播，今上文武聖神，北虜稽款，邊燧不警，軼曩代矣。顧夷馬之散處無策，而羸豕之蹢躅當防，其說非過計也。愚謂夷狄之强弱異時，而中國之措置異便。今之夷狄，其强非冒頓，其弱非呼韓也。夫其不若冒頓也，而歸降則拒，款市則却，固不免於狹小皇化；而其不若呼韓也，則又安得狃於柙虎篝鷹，而漫然不為之備也？故責屯練之實効，徹桑土於未雨之時，而修築大邊，歸併小堡，藉羈縻而修守焉，計歲程功，此急務也。
translation_en:
…opening many branch canals to vent the raging waves. To the north, at places such as Zhima Village, and to the south, along the embankments of Gaoyou and Baoying, there should be none that we do not manage with genuine commitment, enforcing strict rewards and punishments so that river defense is treated on a par with defense against the northern caitiffs. In this way, people's hearts will vie in exertion, undertakings will be planned for the long term, rapid grain transport will link up like clouds, and the Grand Canal route will be saved.

That the夷狄 [non-Chinese tribes] are a menace has been recorded since antiquity. From the Zhou dynasty onward, those who have discussed controlling the caitiffs have proposed nothing more than policies of punitive expeditions or marriage alliances. Yet sweeping clear the lands south of the desert may err in excessive militarism, while marriage alliances and annual tribute payments may err in humiliation—neither is of any benefit to the dignity of the state. The Late Emperor's awesome prestige spread far and wide, and His Present Majesty is civil and martial, sagely and divine; the northern caitiffs have bowed in submission, and the frontier beacon fires raise no alarms, surpassing former eras. Yet the argument that there is no plan for the scattered placement of barbarian horses, and that one must guard against the restless pacing of a lean pig [which is still capable of lunging], is no overly anxious calculation. In my humble view, the strength and weakness of the barbarians vary with the times, and China's handling of them varies according to expediency. As for the barbarians of today, in strength they are no Modu, and in weakness they are no Huhanye. Since they are not like Modu, to reject them when they surrender and turn them away when they seek tributary trade would surely amount to narrowing the reach of Imperial transformation; yet since they are not like Huhanye, how can we grow complacent as if they were tigers in a cage or falcons on a perch, and carelessly fail to prepare against them? Therefore, demanding real results in military farming and training, gathering mulberry root-bark to mend the nest before it rains, repairing and building the outer frontier wall, consolidating small forts, and taking advantage of the loose-rein peace to repair our defenses while assessing progress year by year—this is an urgent task. …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
散夷馬於牧場擇補薊鎮之額而寛其馬
值以綏邊民防護根本此遠猷也然萬丈
之堤慎於蟻穴今夷將遁丁紛沓内地虛
實阨塞巳竊窺之肘腋可不慮乎故必靳
重大之權以抑降將而又稽覈遁丁防其
漏逸宣大之獨石應朔關陜之甘固延寧
靡不爲之加意隄備而失防通釁仍與失
事同罰焉則可款可戰諸鎮自定而組繫
東虜夷情不足慮矣
===
國初宗屬四萬祿僅倍之而
代肅諸藩額廩千石將軍以下改官敘遷
祖訓昭昭也乃今大倍其初而祿入不繼喧嗔
公署甚則束腹待哺不若閭閻細民猶得
糊其口焉此議之所以汲汲也愚以五世
之祖尚得祧遷六世之孫封爵無紀是忍
於親盡之祖而不忍於親盡之孫舛也故
親郡世及無容議矣而
郡王之次封鎮國者可限也輔奉中尉以嫡
punctuated:
散夷馬於牧場，擇補薊鎮之額，而寛其馬值以綏邊民，防護根本，此遠猷也。然萬丈之堤，慎於蟻穴。今夷將遁丁，紛沓内地，虛實阨塞，巳竊窺之，肘腋可不慮乎？故必靳重大之權以抑降將，而又稽覈遁丁，防其漏逸。宣大之獨石、應、朔，關陜之甘、固、延、寧，靡不爲之加意隄備，而失防通釁，仍與失事同罰焉。則可款可戰，諸鎮自定，而組繫東虜，夷情不足慮矣。
國初宗屬四萬，祿僅倍之，而代、肅諸藩額廩千石，將軍以下改官敘遷，《祖訓》昭昭也。乃今大倍其初，而祿入不繼，喧嗔公署，甚則束腹待哺，不若閭閻細民猶得糊其口焉，此議之所以汲汲也。愚以五世之祖尚得祧遷，六世之孫封爵無紀，是忍於親盡之祖，而不忍於親盡之孫，舛也。故親、郡世及，無容議矣；而郡王之次封鎮國者，可限也；輔、奉中尉以嫡…
translation_en:
To disperse the barbarian horses across the pastures, selecting from them to fill the quotas of the Jizhou Defense Command (Jizhen 薊鎮), and easing the burden of horse prices so as to pacify the frontier people and protect the fundamental heartland—this is a far-sighted plan. Yet a dike ten thousand yards long requires vigilance against ant-holes. Today, barbarian commanders and runaway soldiers crowd into the interior, and they have already secretly spied out our strengths, weaknesses, and strategic passes; how can we not worry about trouble right at our elbows and armpits? Therefore, we must withhold weighty authority in order to restrain surrendered commanders, and also inspect and verify runaway soldiers to prevent them from slipping away. From Dushi 獨石, Yingzhou 應州, and Shuozhou 朔州 in Xuanfu 宣府 and Datong 大同, to Ganzhou 甘州, Guyuan 固原, Yansui 延綏, and Ningxia 寧夏 in Guanzhong 關中 and Shaanxi 陜西, there is nowhere that should not be guarded with heightened care, and any failure in defense or collusion that provokes conflict should still be punished the same as a military defeat. Then, whether making peace or waging war, the various defense commands will naturally be stabilized, we can bind the eastern caitiffs with a silken cord, and the situation of the barbarians will no longer be worth worrying about.

At the beginning of the dynasty, imperial clansmen numbered forty thousand and their stipends were barely double that; the princely fiefs of Dai 代, Su 肅, and others had a fixed stipend quota of a thousand piculs, while those of the rank of General (jiangjun 將軍) and below were reassigned to regular official posts and promoted according to merit—the Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun 祖訓) are crystal clear on this. Yet today their numbers have multiplied vastly compared to the beginning, and stipend revenues cannot keep pace. They clamor angrily in government offices, and in extreme cases bind their bellies waiting to be fed, worse off than commoners in the alleys who can still manage to feed themselves; this is why discussions on the matter are so urgent. In my humble view, since ancestors of the fifth generation are still subject to removal to the distant ancestral shrine, for descendants of the sixth generation to be enfeoffed with titles without limit is to be hard-hearted toward ancestors whose kinship has been exhausted, yet soft-hearted toward descendants whose kinship has been exhausted—which is perverse. Therefore, the hereditary succession of Imperial Princes (Qinwang 親王) and Commandery Princes (Junwang 郡王) admits of no discussion; however, the younger sons of Commandery Princes who are enfeoffed as Defenders-general of the State (Zhenguo jiangjun 鎮國將軍) may be limited. Supporter-commandants (Fuguo zhongwei 輔國中尉) and Bulwark-commandants (Fengguo zhongwei 奉國中尉) succeed through the principal…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
繼矣而奉國之降封世襲者可限也被罪
降封法當幷裁而宗女宗婿減婚貲之半
而給之祿可殺其十三矣然殺其祿而不
令治生非情也褫封之始設處閑田俾爲
世業擇其穎慧者入宗學而選舉黜陟悉
如時例盡弛出城之禁以居其宜焉固不
必株守名封貽終身之坎壈也無已則有
昔人惇宗之例乎酌處存留例銀置設院
署敦請無祿貧宗計口計日給以廩餼總
===
支領之權於
親藩而生育保勘視昔尤加慎焉非苦之也
爲厚其生也彼惇睦九族尊位重祿孰不
知之然漢之諸王庶子寢封唐宋袒免以
下俱不賜名而同姓入仕則劉更生李長
源趙汝愚諸賢可考也變而通之未必非
親睦之仁矣不然則澤不斬於五世情不
便於四業而愈衍愈繁即傾天下之賦能
供祿入之額乎
punctuated: 繼矣，而奉國之降封世襲者可限也；被罪降封，法當幷裁，而宗女、宗婿減婚貲之半而給之，祿可殺其十三矣。然殺其祿而不令治生，非情也。褫封之始，設處閑田，俾爲世業；擇其穎慧者入宗學，而選舉黜陟悉如時例；盡弛出城之禁，以居其宜焉。固不必株守名封，貽終身之坎壈也。無已，則有昔人惇宗之例乎？酌處存留例銀，置設院署，敦請無祿貧宗，計口計日，給以廩餼，總支領之權於親藩，而生育保勘，視昔尤加慎焉。非苦之也，爲厚其生也。彼惇睦九族、尊位重祿，孰不知之？然漢之諸王庶子寢封，唐、宋袒免以下俱不賜名，而同姓入仕，則劉更生、李長源、趙汝愚諸賢可考也。變而通之，未必非親睦之仁矣。不然，則澤不斬於五世，情不便於四業，而愈衍愈繁，即傾天下之賦，能供祿入之額乎？
translation_en: … inherit, then those of the Bulwark-Lieutenant of the State (fengguo zhongwei) rank who receive reduced titles by hereditary succession can be limited; for those whose titles are reduced due to offenses, by law their stipends should be concurrently cut, and if imperial clan daughters and their consorts are granted half the marriage allowance, the total stipends can be reduced by three-tenths. Yet to reduce their stipends without allowing them to make a living is contrary to human feeling. When their titles are first stripped away, idle lands should be allocated to serve as their hereditary estates; the bright and intelligent among them should be selected to enter the Imperial Clan School, with their selection, promotion, and demotion following current regulations in every respect; and the prohibition against leaving the city walls should be completely relaxed so that they may settle where it suits them. Surely they need not stubbornly cling to nominal titles, leaving themselves to a lifetime of frustration and hardship. If that is still not enough, is there not the precedent of former men for caring for the clan? We might allocate retained statutory silver to establish courtyards and offices, earnestly inviting impoverished clansmen without stipends to reside there, and providing them with grain rations calculated by head and by day; the authority over disbursement and receipt would be consolidated under the Imperial Princes of the Blood, while the verification and guarantee of births would be conducted with even greater caution than in the past. This is not to make things difficult for them, but to enrich their livelihood. As for showing generosity and harmony to the nine grades of kinsmen, and honoring their status and making their stipends generous—who does not know of this? Yet in the Han dynasty, the non-principal sons of the various kings ceased to be enfeoffed; in the Tang and Song dynasties, kinsmen beyond the fifth degree of mourning were no longer bestowed imperial names; while as for imperial clansmen entering officialdom, worthy men such as Liu Gengsheng (Liu Xiang 劉向), Li Changyuan (Li Bi 李泌), and Zhao Ruyu 趙汝愚 may be examined as precedents. To adapt and make things work is not necessarily contrary to the benevolence of kinship and harmony. Otherwise, if royal bounty is not terminated after five generations and circumstances do not permit them to engage in the four occupations, then as they multiply ever more prolifically, even if we exhausted the revenues of the entire empire, could we supply the quota of their stipends?

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
國初衞所星羅額軍餘三百萬而民壯弓兵
因地定制保甲之法規畫詳明
令甲可稽也乃今逃亡日眾尺籍漸虛借抵
操閱畢則羣然而散矣脫遇警變將何以
支此議之所以汲汲也愚以爲土著之兵
熟知利便而室家丘隴休戚相關舍土兵
之練而爲客兵之募迂也試查舊制額兵
幾何衞所不足則其餘丁可補也弓兵不
充則其族屬可募也五取其一十用其二
===
蠲其徭役登冊籍而爲兵焉則吾民卽吾
兵矣然籍其人而不授以器猶無兵也汰
弱清逋計其餘餉以爲器具之需敎閱則
逐名給散事完則歸之公庾而賞罰之費
總領之官胥此制用焉固不必增益軍儲
而待用有餘貲也乃訓練可不嚴乎三農
旣隙月必九閱責之清軍佐職簡敎技略
總殿最之權於撫巡而賞罰鼓舞悉如軍
制焉非難之也固閑其藝也彼石壕之詠
punctuated: 國初衞所星羅，額軍餘三百萬，而民壯、弓兵因地定制，保甲之法規畫詳明，令甲可稽也。乃今逃亡日眾，尺籍漸虛，借抵操閱，畢則羣然而散矣。脫遇警變，將何以支？此議之所以汲汲也。愚以爲土著之兵，熟知利便，而室家丘隴休戚相關，舍土兵之練而爲客兵之募，迂也。試查舊制額兵幾何，衞所不足，則其餘丁可補也；弓兵不充，則其族屬可募也。五取其一，十用其二，蠲其徭役，登冊籍而爲兵焉，則吾民卽吾兵矣。然籍其人而不授以器，猶無兵也。汰弱清逋，計其餘餉以爲器具之需。敎閱則逐名給散，事完則歸之公庾，而賞罰之費、總領之官，胥此制用焉，固不必增益軍儲而待用有餘貲也。乃訓練可不嚴乎？三農旣隙，月必九閱，責之清軍佐職，簡敎技略，總殿最之權於撫、巡，而賞罰鼓舞悉如軍制焉。非難之也，固閑其藝也。彼《石壕》之詠、
translation_en: At the beginning of the dynasty, guards and battalions were spread out like stars, with an established quota of over three million soldiers; meanwhile, civilian militia and archers were instituted according to local conditions, and the regulations of the mutual security (baojia) system were planned out in clear detail, as can be verified in the statutory codes. Yet today, deserters grow more numerous by the day and the military registers are gradually emptying; substitutes are borrowed to stand in at drills and reviews, and once finished they all disperse in a crowd. Should an emergency or rebellion occur, how could we hold out? This is why discussions on the matter are so urgent. In my humble opinion, native-born troops are thoroughly familiar with local advantages, and since their homes and ancestral graves share in the same weal and woe, to abandon the training of local troops in favor of recruiting outside mercenaries is impractical. Let us examine what the old quotas of troops were: where the guards and battalions fall short, their supernumerary adult males can fill the gaps; where the archers are understrength, their clan relatives can be recruited. Take one out of five, or employ two out of ten, exempt them from corvée labor, and enter them into the registers as soldiers—then our people will be our soldiers. Yet to register the men without supplying them with weapons is the same as having no soldiers at all. By weeding out the weak and clearing up absconders, we can reckon the surplus rations and use them to meet the need for equipment. During training and reviews, distribute the weapons to each man by name, and when the affair is concluded, return them to the public armories; the expenses for rewards and punishments and the officers in overall command can all be funded from this, so there will surely be no need to increase military supplies in order to have ample funds ready for use. And how could training not be strict? During the off-season from the three agricultural tasks, there must be nine reviews each month, charging the assistant officials for clearing military registers with selecting and instructing them in martial skills and tactics, while concentrating the authority to evaluate merits and demerits in the hands of the Grand Coordinator and Regional Inspector, with rewards, punishments, and incentives all following military regulations. This is not to make things difficult for them, but truly to drill them in their skills. As for the ballad of "Shihao"…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
木蘭之詞孰不憐之然漢之騎士起於田
野唐宋步兵廣銳皆出州縣而民兵奏績
若李抱真李德裕韓魏公之捷可考也酌
而行之未必非足兵之計矣不然則召募
而雞犬不寧清勾而甲乙異喙愈逃愈虚
將竭斯民之脂而募無用之兵乎夫治河
制虜古法詳而不宜於今今之議可行矣
然疏築之費不貲市易之價難定非有域
外之觀灼見其機而持之者則尤懼其說
===
鈴也
宗祿民兵今制詳而不越於古古之法當復
矣然降封幾於寡恩而募民易於賈怨非
有破調之材力肩其事而應之者則尤懼
其畫餅也萬世之便不因道謀而志隳旦
夕之安不以小利而枝癢此所謂事應於
時機斷於獨而善議者也然愚猶有一說
焉殷憂啓聖多難興邦河患虜患亦天心
仁愛人君者也惟迪德用賢以鼓天和則
punctuated:
木蘭之詞，孰不憐之？然漢之騎士起於田野，唐、宋步兵廣銳皆出州縣，而民兵奏績，若李抱真、李德裕、韓魏公之捷，可考也。酌而行之，未必非足兵之計矣。不然，則召募而雞犬不寧，清勾而甲乙異喙，愈逃愈虚，將竭斯民之脂，而募無用之兵乎？

夫治河、制虜，古法詳而不宜於今，今之議可行矣。然疏築之費不貲，市易之價難定，非有域外之觀，灼見其機而持之者，則尤懼其說鈴也。宗祿、民兵，今制詳而不越於古，古之法當復矣。然降封幾於寡恩，而募民易於賈怨，非有破調之材，力肩其事而應之者，則尤懼其畫餅也。萬世之便，不因道謀而志隳；旦夕之安，不以小利而枝癢。此所謂事應於時，機斷於獨，而善議者也。

然愚猶有一說焉。「殷憂啓聖，多難興邦。」河患、虜患，亦天心仁愛人君者也。惟迪德用賢以鼓天和，則
translation_en:
… and the Ballad of Mulan—who does not feel pity upon hearing them? Yet the cavalrymen of the Han arose from the fields and countryside, and the infantry and elite Guangrui troops of the Tang and Song all came from the prefectures and counties. The achievements of civilian militias—such as the victories of Li Baozhen 李抱真, Li Deyu 李德裕, and Duke Wei of Han (Han Qi 韓琦)—can be verified in the historical records. If we deliberate carefully and put this into practice, it may well be a sound plan for ensuring sufficient troops. Otherwise, recruitment leaves not even chickens and dogs in peace, while auditing and conscripting hereditary military households leads to conflicting claims between parties A and B; the more they desert, the more depleted the ranks become. Shall we exhaust the lifeblood of our people only to recruit useless soldiers?

Now, regarding river control and the containment of the northern Caitiffs, the ancient methods are detailed yet unsuited to the present, whereas current proposals are practicable. Even so, the costs of dredging and diking are incalculable, and the prices for horse-market trade are difficult to fix. Unless there is someone with far-reaching vision beyond the ordinary who clearly perceives the pivotal dynamics and steadfastly upholds them, one must especially fear that such talk is mere empty chatter. Regarding imperial clan stipends and civilian militias, the present regulations are detailed yet do not surpass antiquity, so the ancient methods ought to be restored. Yet reducing enfeoffment ranks borders on stinting imperial grace, and recruiting the populace easily invites resentment. Unless there is someone of extraordinary talent who breaks from convention, vigorously shoulders the task, and responds to circumstances, one must especially fear that such plans are mere painted cakes that cannot satisfy hunger. A benefit for ten thousand generations should not have its resolve ruined by consulting passersby on the road; the peace of a single morning and evening should not be disrupted by an itch for petty advantage. This is what is meant by responding to the times in affairs, making decisive judgments alone at the critical moment, and being truly skilled in deliberation.

Yet I, in my simplicity, still have one further point to make. "Deep anxiety awakens a sage; many difficulties regenerate a state." Disasters from the Yellow River and troubles with the northern Caitiffs are also ways in which the mind of Heaven shows benevolent love for the ruler of men. Only by cultivating virtue and employing the worthy to stir the harmony of Heaven can…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
治河禦虜擇便成功此其根本在
朝廷者也千金之子內贍其家外威其鄰至
足也今祿匱兵疲乏於財耳惟愼儉節財
以臻富庶則祿繼而兵自強此其節縮在
朝廷者也
聖意所加萬彙嚮應而何憂於四議乎管見如
此執事以爲何如
第四問
劉文徵
===
同考試官教諭陶批士有恒心而無定尚觀風之者
何如耳是策以選舉考覈之法廣而行之足以勵行而維風矣
考試官教諭劉批評議有見而風勵之說尤爲探本
考試官教諭蔣批氣格雄渾識見超拔非凡士也
君子所以樹天下之功者必其勵天下之
節者也君子所以勵天下之節者必其貞
天下之志者也蓋功者濟世之具而不可
倖成材者立功之本而不可苟就故砥礪
廉隅乃所以豫匡濟之略而竦節奇氣赫
punctuated:
治河禦虜，擇便成功，此其根本在朝廷者也。千金之子，內贍其家，外威其鄰，至足也。今祿匱兵疲，乏於財耳。惟愼儉節財，以臻富庶，則祿繼而兵自強，此其節縮在朝廷者也。聖意所加，萬彙嚮應，而何憂於四議乎？管見如此，執事以爲何如？

第四問
劉文徵
同考試官教諭陶批：士有恒心而無定尚，觀風之者何如耳。是策以選舉考覈之法廣而行之，足以勵行而維風矣。
考試官教諭劉批：評議有見，而風勵之說尤爲探本。
考試官教諭蔣批：氣格雄渾，識見超拔，非凡士也。

君子所以樹天下之功者，必其勵天下之節者也；君子所以勵天下之節者，必其貞天下之志者也。蓋功者，濟世之具，而不可倖成；材者，立功之本，而不可苟就。故砥礪廉隅，乃所以豫匡濟之略，而竦節奇氣，赫
translation_en:
… in controlling the Yellow River and defending against the northern caitiffs, one can choose what is advantageous and achieve success; the root of this lies in the imperial court. A son of a family worth a thousand pieces of gold supports his household within and overawes his neighbors without, simply because he has ample sufficiency. Today, imperial stipends are depleted and troops are exhausted merely because of a shortage of wealth. Only by practicing cautious frugality and economizing on expenditures to attain prosperity and abundance will stipends be sustained and the military naturally grow strong; the retrenchment for this lies in the imperial court. Wherever the sacred intention is applied, the myriad things respond toward it—what worry, then, would there be over the four matters under deliberation? Such is my humble view; what do the examiners think of it?

Fourth Question
Liu Wenzheng 劉文徵

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Tao 陶: Scholars possess a constant mind yet lack a fixed trend; it depends only on how those who inspire them act. By broadening and putting into practice the methods of selection and evaluation, this policy essay is sufficient to encourage conduct and uphold mores.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu 劉: His evaluations and deliberations show insight, and his discussion of inspiring and encouraging conduct especially probes the fundamental root.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣: His style and vigor are bold and渾厚 [deep and powerful], and his insight is outstanding—he is no ordinary scholar.
