For achievement is the instrument for aiding the world and cannot be attained by luck; talent is the foundation for establishing achievement and cannot be accomplished carelessly. Therefore, honing spotless integrity is the means to prepare strategies for rectifying and aiding the world, while lofty integrity and extraordinary spirit, shining…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
然焜燿于人之耳目者則旋乾闢坤天下
被其化書裳馥稿後世仰其休此非委靡
巽愞于平居而甞試於功名之會者爲之
也何者其所挾持者不輕而其所布置者
始不可量也向使志有不立則無以堅其
節而養其材厚其積而宏其用雖使時勢
可乘無能建明於天下即或勉强樹立姑
假烈烈之名然亦不能厭人心而杜後訾
矣又況循循然一無所就而徒失天下之
===
望者乎嗚呼士君子身負綱常寓宙皆分
事也奈之何其不自勵哉緬想唐虞之世
元氣渾融明良合德都俞吁咈相與聚精
神喜起賡歌相與召和氣無智名無勇功
無節義之號也自樂堯舜於畎畝者一舉
而救溝中之納負飛熊於渭水者一動而
振鷹揚之功人固以掀揭宇宙之勳必成
於高節令名之士而繄是則朝扣暮遊掉
寸舌而橫塞眞源奴顏隸膝效雞犬而解
punctuated: 然焜燿于人之耳目者，則旋乾闢坤，天下被其化，書裳馥稿，後世仰其休。此非委靡巽愞于平居，而甞試於功名之會者爲之也。何者？其所挾持者不輕，而其所布置者始不可量也。向使志有不立，則無以堅其節而養其材，厚其積而宏其用。雖使時勢可乘，無能建明於天下；即或勉强樹立，姑假烈烈之名，然亦不能厭人心而杜後訾矣，又況循循然一無所就，而徒失天下之望者乎？嗚呼！士君子身負綱常，寓宙皆分事也，奈之何其不自勵哉？緬想唐虞之世，元氣渾融，明良合德，都俞吁咈，相與聚精神；喜起賡歌，相與召和氣。無智名，無勇功，無節義之號也。自樂堯舜於畎畝者，一舉而救溝中之納；負飛熊於渭水者，一動而振鷹揚之功。人固以掀揭宇宙之勳，必成於高節令名之士；而繄是則朝扣暮遊，掉寸舌而橫塞眞源，奴顏隸膝，效雞犬而解…
translation_en: …brilliantly dazzling to people's eyes and ears—then they can turn the heavens and open up the earth, so that the whole world receives their transforming influence; their deeds are inscribed on ceremonial robes and leave a fragrant draft in history [?], so that future generations look up to their excellence. This is not done by those who are dispirited, submissive, and cowardly in ordinary life, yet tentatively try their luck when an opportunity for merit and fame arises. Why is that? Because only when what one upholds within is not taken lightly can what one deploys in action be truly immeasurable. Suppose one's resolve is not established; then there is no way to firm up one's integrity and nurture one's talent, or to deepen one's accumulation and broaden one's usefulness. Even if the times and circumstances offer an opportunity to seize, one will be unable to establish anything illustrious in the world; even if one forces oneself to achieve something and temporarily borrows a glorious reputation, it still will not satisfy people's hearts or forestall criticism from posterity—how much less so for those who docilely accomplish nothing at all and merely disappoint the expectations of the world! Alas! When a scholar-gentleman personally bears the cardinal moral principles, the entire universe is his rightful responsibility; how could he fail to spur himself on? Looking back fondly to the eras of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], primordial vitality was harmoniously blended, enlightened rulers and worthy ministers were united in virtue; with exclamations of approval and admonition, they gathered their spirit together; rejoicing, rising, and exchanging songs, they summoned harmonious vital energy together. There was no fame for cleverness, no merit for bravery, and no special title for integrity and righteousness. Ever since the one who delighted in the way of Yao and Shun among the ploughed fields [Yi Yin] rose in a single stroke to rescue people from being pushed into the ditches, and the one who bore the omen of the flying bear by the Wei River [Lü Shang] moved in a single action to rouse the merit of a soaring eagle, people have naturally held that universe-shaking achievements must be accomplished by men of lofty integrity and fine reputation. Yet aside from such men [?], there are those who knock on gates at dawn and roam as persuaders at dusk, wagging their inch-long tongues to perversely block the true source, or who with servile faces and slavish knees imitate cocks and dogs [petty tricksters] to unfasten…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
紐王教動則誤天下之蒼生而羞稱於君
子之口焉將益以含貞葆素之士不可多
得而貴賤之辨隨時雌黃矣即如鍾扶輿
之淑間挺寥廓之芳聲者或非時所能限
然中材之士與世浮湛則其不能脫跡於
鼓鑄濡染之區者其大較也故周之士貴
秦之士賤楊雄亦據時事而評其槩耳夫
周士貴矣而鬻熊辛甲皆周產也一以耄
年謁文王而誇策事之壯一以傾蓋遇召
===
奭而膺長子之封淟涊干進豈足貴乎不
知菁莪棫樸之教皆慷慨質直之風植節
砥行鱗集星輝二子蓋適時之行耳而周
士之貴自若也秦士賤矣而桃源海島皆
秦地也隱士竄跡而謝漁郎之問田橫殞
身而却漢主之招遺榮輕生豈可賤乎不
知狙詐坑焚之後多聲利游揚之夫鄙曲
踰閑接軫繁蔓二子特麻中之蓬耳而秦
士之賤猶故也四皓蹈跡商山而出安炎
punctuated: 紐王教，動則誤天下之蒼生，而羞稱於君子之口焉。將益以含貞葆素之士不可多得，而貴賤之辨隨時雌黃矣。即如鍾扶輿之淑，間挺寥廓之芳聲者，或非時所能限；然中材之士與世浮湛，則其不能脫跡於鼓鑄濡染之區者，其大較也。故周之士貴，秦之士賤，楊雄亦據時事而評其槩耳。夫周士貴矣，而鬻熊、辛甲皆周產也：一以耄年謁文王而誇策事之壯，一以傾蓋遇召奭而膺長子之封。淟涊干進，豈足貴乎？不知菁莪、棫樸之教，皆慷慨質直之風，植節砥行，鱗集星輝；二子蓋適時之行耳，而周士之貴自若也。秦士賤矣，而桃源、海島皆秦地也：隱士竄跡而謝漁郎之問，田橫殞身而却漢主之招。遺榮輕生，豈可賤乎？不知狙詐坑焚之後，多聲利游揚之夫，鄙曲踰閑，接軫繁蔓；二子特麻中之蓬耳，而秦士之賤猶故也。四皓蹈跡商山，而出安炎
translation_en: … unravel the royal teachings; whenever they act, they bring ruin upon the common people of the realm, so that gentlemen are ashamed even to speak their names. Thus it becomes ever clearer that scholars who cherish integrity and preserve simplicity are rarely found, and the distinction between noble and base shifts with the criticisms and judgments of the age. Even though those who embody the finest essence of heaven and earth and occasionally stand forth with a fragrant reputation reaching the vast heavens may not be constrained by their times, yet scholars of middling talent sink or swim with the world, and their inability to extricate themselves from the realm of prevailing molding and influence is the general rule. Therefore, when Yang Xiong 楊雄 said that the scholars of Zhou were noble and the scholars of Qin were base, he was merely judging their general character on the basis of the affairs of those times. Now, the scholars of Zhou were indeed noble, yet Yu Xiong 鬻熊 and Xin Jia 辛甲 were both men of Zhou: the one presented himself to King Wen in his nineties and boasted of his vigor in planning affairs; the other met Shao Shi 召奭 by chance on the road and received the enfeoffment of Zhangzi 長子. Soiled by their self-advancement, how could they be worthy of esteem? Yet one must understand that under the moral education celebrated in the odes "Jing'e" 菁莪 and "Yupu" 棫樸, all shared a spirit of generous candor and uprightness, establishing their integrity and whetting their conduct, gathering like fish scales and shining like stars; those two men were merely acting in accord with the opportunity of the moment, while the nobility of the scholars of Zhou remained unchanged. The scholars of Qin were indeed base, yet Peach Blossom Spring (Taoyuan 桃源) and the ocean island were both territories of Qin: the recluses hid their tracks and declined the fisherman's inquiries, and Tian Heng 田橫 took his own life to refuse the summons of the ruler of Han. Casting aside glory and holding life lightly, how could they be deemed base? Yet one must understand that after the deceitfulness and the burning of books and burying of scholars, there were many men who chased after fame and profit and touted themselves, vulgar, crooked, and transgressing bounds, following carriage upon carriage and spreading like weeds; those two examples were merely like fleabane growing straight among hemp, while the baseness of the scholars of Qin remained as before. The Four Hoaryheads (Si Hao 四皓) hid their tracks on Mount Shang 商山, yet came forth to secure the…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
劉之業孔明高枕南陽而起成鼎足之勳
是其操脩不苟而致用自宏也乃毛遂自
薦楚趙定從鄧禹投歸雲臺首烈而張齊
賢布衣獻策卒成賢相之功焉則異才亦
起於自售不專以養望得之者然不知暗
合道妙者不以膠柱而隳績是鄧禹諸賢
各有當也子厚締黨叔文卒投老於西粵
仲淹獻策十二乃托興於東征是其樹立
旣汙而蒙詬非過也乃樊英强起損譽漢
===
庭殷浩一出蒼生缺望而房琯素負時名
亦不免陳濤之辱焉則誤國多出於徵士
不專以干謁失之者然不知聲聞過情者
難以倖時而建功房琯諸賢固畫龍也之
數賢者就事功而論之則安劉定鼎鞏兩
主之基解紛定難皆有用之器視諸旅進
旅退貽譏黨友者相逕庭矣要心術而評
之則商山之謀出於呂氏布衣之策終為
上援方諸抱膝長吟光明俊偉者隔霄壤
punctuated: 劉之業，孔明高枕南陽而起成鼎足之勳，是其操脩不苟，而致用自宏也。乃毛遂自薦，楚、趙定從；鄧禹投歸，雲臺首烈；而張齊賢布衣獻策，卒成賢相之功焉。則異才亦起於自售，不專以養望得之者。然不知暗合道妙者，不以膠柱而隳績，是鄧禹諸賢各有當也。子厚締黨叔文，卒投老於西粵；仲淹獻策十二，乃托興於東征。是其樹立旣汙，而蒙詬非過也。乃樊英强起，損譽漢庭；殷浩一出，蒼生缺望；而房琯素負時名，亦不免陳濤之辱焉。則誤國多出於徵士，不專以干謁失之者。然不知聲聞過情者，難以倖時而建功，房琯諸賢固畫龍也。之數賢者，就事功而論之，則安劉定鼎，鞏兩主之基，解紛定難，皆有用之器，視諸旅進旅退、貽譏黨友者，相逕庭矣。要心術而評之，則商山之謀出於呂氏，布衣之策終為上援，方諸抱膝長吟、光明俊偉者，隔霄壤
translation_en: …the enterprise of the fiery Liu [the Han dynasty], and Kongming [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] slept on a high pillow in Nanyang before rising to achieve the merit of establishing the tripartite balance of power. This shows that because their personal integrity and cultivation were not lax, their practical application was naturally vast. Yet Mao Sui 毛遂 recommended himself, and the vertical alliance between Chu and Zhao was settled; Deng Yu 鄧禹 offered his allegiance, and ranked first in merit on the Cloud Terrace (Yuntai); and Zhang Qixian 張齊賢 presented policy proposals as a commoner, ultimately achieving the accomplishments of a worthy chief counselor. Thus, extraordinary talents also arise from promoting oneself, and are not obtained exclusively by cultivating a lofty reputation in retirement. However, people do not realize that those who tacitly accord with the subtleties of the Way do not ruin their achievements through rigid inflexibility; in this respect, worthies like Deng Yu each acted appropriately for their circumstances. Zihou [Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元] formed a faction with [Wang] Shuwen 王叔文 and ended up cast away in his old age in western Yue [Guangxi]; Zhongyan [Wang Tong 王通] presented twelve policy proposals, yet had to entrust his poetic inspirations to an eastward journey. This shows that once one's foundational conduct is sullied, suffering disgrace is no excess of justice. On the other hand, when Fan Ying 樊英 was forced to rise from retirement, he damaged his reputation at the Han court; as soon as Yin Hao 殷浩 came forth into office, the common people were left disappointed in their hopes; and Fang Guan 房琯, despite long bearing contemporary renown, could not avoid the humiliation of Chentao. Thus, bringing ruin to the state often comes from summoned scholars (zhengshi), and failure does not lie exclusively with those who seek advancement through self-promotion. Yet people fail to realize that those whose reputation exceeds their true substance find it hard to establish merit by relying on opportune chance; worthies like Fang Guan were truly just painted dragons. Speaking of these several worthies in terms of their practical achievements: securing the Liu clan and establishing the tripod of state consolidated the foundations of the two rulers, while resolving disputes and settling crises showed them all to be instruments of practical use—wildly different from those who merely advance and retreat with the crowd or leave behind ridicule for their factional associates. Yet if we evaluate them fundamentally by the intentions of their minds: the stratagem of Mount Shang originated from the Empress Lü 呂氏, and the commoner's policy proposals ultimately served to curry favor with superiors; compared to him who chanted long while clasping his knees [Zhuge Liang], brilliant, open, and grand, they are as far apart as heaven and earth…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
矣蓋黄綺諸賢特衆人之尤而孔明則衆
尤之尤也若桃源海島業無可見而清風
凜凜尚有餘思樊英房琯寡謀輕試而迄
今猶潤牙頰者何哉蓋世變江河士習愈
下伏車泣血而不知哭途之鄙突梯滑稽
而不知升斗之汙懊不得意坐而書空者
視諸子之時猶瀾倒焉固宜其有述於後
世也故士之於世寧爲玉碎毋爲瓦全寧
爲雉經毋爲虺曲寧爲待聘之英强起之
===
琯而毋若平原河陽自鬻以成其身焉至
於開誠布公籍爲學古之梯而澹泊寧靜
毅然藩籬其身而不敢褻雖其成功在天
不可逆睹而後彫之栢特達之圭人固仰
之爲山斗矣而況節以志堅材以節立功
以材運世豈有厚自珍惜而不能建立於
世者乎噫可貴而不可賤可周而不可秦
士人之立身行已固如是也然聞周之待
士六德六行以爲稽尚其實也三詔五贄
punctuated: 矣。蓋黄、綺諸賢，特衆人之尤，而孔明則衆尤之尤也。若桃源、海島，業無可見，而清風凜凜，尚有餘思。樊英、房琯，寡謀輕試，而迄今猶潤牙頰者，何哉？蓋世變江河，士習愈下。伏車泣血，而不知哭途之鄙；突梯滑稽，而不知升斗之汙；懊不得意，坐而書空者，視諸子之時，猶瀾倒焉，固宜其有述於後世也。故士之於世，寧爲玉碎，毋爲瓦全；寧爲雉經，毋爲虺曲；寧爲待聘之英、强起之琯，而毋若平原、河陽，自鬻以成其身焉。至於開誠布公，籍爲學古之梯，而澹泊寧靜，毅然藩籬其身而不敢褻；雖其成功在天，不可逆睹，而後彫之栢、特達之圭，人固仰之爲山斗矣。而況節以志堅，材以節立，功以材運，世豈有厚自珍惜而不能建立於世者乎？噫！「可貴而不可賤，可周而不可秦」，士人之立身行已，固如是也。然聞周之待士，六德、六行以爲稽，尚其實也；三詔、五贄
translation_en:
… apart. Indeed, worthies like Xiahuang Gong 夏黃公 and Qili Ji 綺里季 were merely outstanding among the multitude, whereas Kongming 孔明 (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮) was the most outstanding of the outstanding. As for those of Peach Blossom Spring (Taoyuan 桃源) and the sea islands, though they left no visible achievements, their pure wind blows with awe-inspiring integrity, still leaving lingering thoughts behind. Fan Ying 樊英 and Fang Guan 房琯 lacked strategy and rashly put themselves to the test, yet why is it that even today people still savor their names on their lips? It is because the world changes like rivers flowing downward, and the customs of scholars grow ever more debased. Those who prostrate themselves before carriages weeping blood without realizing the baseness of crying at the end of the road; those who are slick and obsequious without realizing the filth of a mere peck of grain in stipend; and those who, vexed at failing to get their way, sit tracing characters in the empty air—compared to the era of those gentlemen, they are like an overturned wave. Truly it is fitting that those earlier figures are still recounted in later ages!

Therefore, in his relation to the world, a scholar would rather be shattered jade than intact tile; rather die by hanging himself like a pheasant than writhe like a viper; rather be a Fan Ying awaiting recruitment or a Fang Guan forced from retirement, than be like Lu Ji 陸機 of Pingyuan 平原 or Pan Yue 潘岳 of Heyang 河陽, who peddled themselves to achieve personal advancement. As for opening one's heart and extending impartiality, taking them as a ladder for studying antiquity, and maintaining simple living and tranquil resolve, resolutely fencing oneself in so that none dare treat one with disrespect—even though ultimate success rests with Heaven and cannot be foreseen, like the cypress that is the last to wither or the jade tablet that alone commands direct audience, people will surely look up to such a man as Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper. How much more so when moral integrity is firmed by aspiration, talent is established through moral integrity, and achievement is put into motion through talent—how could there be anyone in the world who deeply cherishes himself and yet is unable to establish achievements in the world?

Alas! "He may be honored, but cannot be debased; he would serve Zhou 周, but would not serve Qin 秦"—such indeed is the way a scholar establishes his person and conducts himself. Yet I have heard that in the way the Zhou treated scholars, they examined them by means of the Six Virtues and Six Conducts, valuing their substance; with three summonses and five ceremonial gifts …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而後見遠其耻也八法八柄以辨治省其
成也故士不得不貴而治不得不隆是化
導之權在上而不在下也方
今敦尚節行振勵士風選之以科目而戒其
浮蔓課之以久任而黜其競躁其貴士養
士之心不讓成周矣而猶有窳節之材如
執事所云者何哉大抵蓬戶甕牖之志不
過風雲月露之習文藝旣攻青紫立至其
於節行標致素所未甞而旣仕之後又以
耀潤身家爲念陟巍躋膴爲期苟可得之
卽脂韋之行皆所不鄙而氣隳於積俗漸
於靡故需材愈急而應之者猶夫其初也
卽欲起敝維風豈無術乎今之選舉無遺
法矣然謂科目盡天下之材不可也枕流
漱石豈無瑰瑋卓犖出於制舉之外者乎
必舉辟薦之典責諸監司廣詢博訪有道
德隆重者有孝弟力田者有行誼脩潔者
據實陳薦不限其數而其揮霍勇毅機智
punctuated: 而後見，遠其耻也；八法、八柄以辨治，省其成也。故士不得不貴，而治不得不隆，是化導之權在上而不在下也。方今敦尚節行，振勵士風，選之以科目而戒其浮蔓，課之以久任而黜其競躁，其貴士、養士之心，不讓成周矣。而猶有窳節之材如執事所云者，何哉？大抵蓬戶甕牖之志，不過風雲月露之習。文藝旣攻，青紫立至，其於節行標致，素所未甞。而旣仕之後，又以耀潤身家爲念，陟巍躋膴爲期。苟可得之，卽脂韋之行皆所不鄙，而氣隳於積，俗漸於靡。故需材愈急，而應之者猶夫其初也。卽欲起敝維風，豈無術乎？今之選舉，無遺法矣，然謂科目盡天下之材，不可也。枕流漱石，豈無瑰瑋卓犖出於制舉之外者乎？必舉辟薦之典，責諸監司廣詢博訪，有道德隆重者，有孝弟力田者，有行誼脩潔者，據實陳薦，不限其數；而其揮霍勇毅、機智
translation_en:
… before granting an audience, so as to keep them far from shame; and it used the Eight Regulations and Eight Prerogatives to distinguish good governance, so as to inspect their accomplishments. Therefore, scholars could not help being noble, and governance could not help being prosperous; this meant that the power to transform and guide lay with those above and not with those below.

At present, our dynasty esteems moral integrity and conduct and rouses the ethos of scholars. It selects them through the examination categories while warning against superficiality and verbosity, and evaluates them through long tenures in office while dismissing those who are competitive and impatient. Its commitment to honoring and nurturing scholars does not yield to that of the flourishing Zhou! Yet why are there still men of flawed integrity such as Your Excellency describes? On the whole, the ambitions of those from humble cottages with thatched doors and jar-neck windows amount to nothing more than the habit of composing ornate verses on wind, clouds, moon, and dew. Once they have mastered literary skill, high rank and purple ribbons come immediately, whereas moral integrity and lofty bearing are things they have never experienced. Then, after entering officialdom, they set their minds on glorifying and enriching themselves and their families, and fix their hopes on ascending to exalted and lucrative posts. So long as they can obtain these, they do not disdain even greased-leather sycophancy; thus their spirit collapses through accumulation of habit, and customs gradually sink into decadence. Consequently, the more urgent the need for talent, the more those who respond remain just as they were at the beginning.

If we wish to remedy these abuses and uphold the moral ethos, how could we lack the means? Today's system of selection leaves no method overlooked, yet one cannot say that the examination categories exhaust all the talent in the Empire. Among those who pillow their heads on streams and rinse their mouths with stones in reclusion, how could there be no extraordinary and outstanding men who lie outside the regular examinations? We must revive the institution of special summons and recommendation, charging the provincial surveillance officials to inquire widely and search broadly. Whether there are men of lofty virtue, or men who are filial, fraternal, and diligent in agriculture, or men of cultivated and pure conduct and righteousness, they should be recommended according to the facts without any limit on their numbers; and as for those who are bold, resolute, and resourceful in…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
謀略可備一時緩急之需者將不病其爲
屠釣爲草野特設一科而羅之以弭天下
之變而待天下之用焉則埴之在冶惟陶
所範未有上作而下不應者也此不可以
廣選舉之所未盡乎今之考覈無遺法矣
然謂格例鼓天下之趨不可也循資躡級
豈無琦材異政限於資格之內者乎必酌
久任之法責諸銓部尚實均勞無以清華
爲捷徑無以遠地爲贅員無以流品爲定
===
局以目正耳資望兼收而其奉職循雅植
節清脩足爲一世人材之表者吾不疑其
爲吏隱爲市隱大破常調而庸之厚天下
之倡以養天下之鋒焉則一人善射百夫
拾决未有鋒在而劒不利者也此所以補
考覈之未盡者也若徒操舉業爲彀率而
逸奇行於驪黃專停解於日月而滯賢庸
於鴈次則俊茂倜儻之士安肯鄙猥自衒
而曲學以覬聲利乎噫昔人所謂用法益
punctuated: 謀略，可備一時緩急之需者，將不病其爲屠釣、爲草野，特設一科而羅之，以弭天下之變，而待天下之用焉。則埴之在冶，惟陶所範，未有上作而下不應者也。此不可以廣選舉之所未盡乎？今之考覈無遺法矣，然謂格例鼓天下之趨，不可也。循資躡級，豈無琦材異政，限於資格之內者乎？必酌久任之法，責諸銓部：尚實均勞，無以清華爲捷徑，無以遠地爲贅員，無以流品爲定局，以目正耳，資望兼收；而其奉職循雅、植節清脩，足爲一世人材之表者，吾不疑其爲吏隱、爲市隱，大破常調而庸之，厚天下之倡，以養天下之鋒焉。則一人善射，百夫拾决，未有鋒在而劒不利者也。此所以補考覈之未盡者也。若徒操舉業爲彀率，而逸奇行於驪黃；專停解於日月，而滯賢庸於鴈次，則俊茂倜儻之士，安肯鄙猥自衒，而曲學以覬聲利乎？噫！昔人所謂「用法益…
translation_en: …and strategic planning, who can meet the needs of a sudden emergency, we should not fault them for being butchers or fishermen or men from the rustic wilds, but rather establish a special category to gather them in, so as to forestall crises in the empire and await the empire's need for their service. Then, like clay in the workshop that is shaped solely by the potter's mold, never has there been a case where superiors initiate and inferiors fail to respond. Could this not broaden what the selection system fails to encompass? Today's system of performance evaluation leaves no method omitted, yet one cannot say that its statutory precedents inspire the aspirations of the entire empire. In following seniority and climbing the ranks step by step, how could there not be extraordinary talents and exceptional administrators who are confined within the bounds of qualifications and seniority? We must deliberate upon a system of long tenure and charge the Ministry of Personnel with its execution: prizing substantive achievement and equalizing hardship, not treating prestigious posts as shortcuts to advancement, not treating remote regions as places for superfluous personnel, and not treating the grading of official streams as a fixed outcome; verifying what is heard by what is seen, and taking into account both seniority and reputation. And as for those who perform their duties with refined compliance and establish their integrity through pure self-cultivation, sufficient to serve as exemplars for the talents of an entire generation, we should not suspect them of being recluses hiding in minor clerkships or in the marketplace, but rather break radically with routine appointments to employ them, strengthening leadership across the empire so as to nurture the empire's keen edge. Then, just as when one man excels at archery a hundred men pick up their thumb-rings and arm-guards, never has there been a case where the keen edge is present and the sword is not sharp. This is the way to supplement what performance evaluation fails to encompass. If instead we merely wield examination essays as our standard of archery and let extraordinary conduct slip away while fretting over whether a horse is black or yellow; or focus exclusively on halting or forwarding dossiers according to months and days of service while letting both the worthy and the mediocre stagnate in rigid, goose-file order, then how would brilliant and unconventional scholars ever deign to demean themselves by peddling their own wares and twisting their learning to angle for fame and profit? Alas! What men of the past called "the more…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
密而進人益難者其說固具在也上挽其
趨士勵其志而人材治道不古若焉愚固
未之信也
第五問
吳璨
同考試官教諭徐批〔積粟鑄錢裕民要務是作究極利弊斟酌時宜皆鑿鑿可行優於用世者也〕
考試官教諭劉批〔興利當圖久遠子言有卓識矣〕
考試官教諭蔣批〔經畫周詳不特可行於一方者〕
===
聖王之致治也必導利以厚天下之生而
操權以制天下之用蓋食者民之資以生
也弗爲之殖則耗竭而不贍故導之而充
然有餘則無不厚之生矣利者人之所必
趨也弗爲之制則扤滯而弗通故制之而
民習於義則無不足之用矣生厚用足則
財裕而不爭天下之業安所爲而不成也
執事以積貯錢帛策諸生將謂其識時務
與非其人也然敢不拾所聞以對嘗聞聖
punctuated:
密而進人益難」者，其說固具在也。上挽其趨，士勵其志，而人材、治道不古若焉，愚固未之信也。

第五問
吳璨
同考試官教諭徐批：〔積粟、鑄錢，裕民要務。是作究極利弊，斟酌時宜，皆鑿鑿可行，優於用世者也。〕
考試官教諭劉批：〔興利當圖久遠，子言有卓識矣。〕
考試官教諭蔣批：〔經畫周詳，不特可行於一方者。〕

聖王之致治也，必導利以厚天下之生，而操權以制天下之用。蓋食者，民之資以生也，弗爲之殖，則耗竭而不贍；故導之而充然有餘，則無不厚之生矣。利者，人之所必趨也，弗爲之制，則扤滯而弗通；故制之而民習於義，則無不足之用矣。生厚用足，則財裕而不爭，天下之業，安所爲而不成也？執事以積貯、錢帛策諸生，將謂其識時務與？非其人也，然敢不拾所聞以對？嘗聞聖…
translation_en:
… becomes ever stricter, advancing men becomes ever harder"—that argument still stands intact. If those above reverse the prevailing trend and scholars rouse their aspirations, yet men of talent and the way of governance still do not match antiquity—I, for one, refuse to believe it.

Fifth Policy Question
Wu Can 吳璨
Associate Examiner and County Instructor Xu 徐 comments: [Storing grain and casting coins are vital tasks for enriching the people. This essay thoroughly investigates the advantages and abuses and weighs what is suited to the times; all of its proposals are concrete and practicable, showing someone well qualified for practical statecraft.]
Examiner and County Instructor Liu 劉 comments: [In promoting public benefit one ought to plan for the long term; your words show outstanding insight.]
Examiner and County Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: [The planning is comprehensive and detailed, not merely practicable in a single region.]

When the sage-kings brought about order, they invariably channeled resources to enrich the livelihood of all under Heaven, and grasped sovereign authority to regulate the expenditures of all under Heaven. For food is what the people rely upon to live; if one does not foster its production, it will be exhausted and prove insufficient. Therefore, when one channels it so that there is an abundant surplus, there is no livelihood that is not enriched. Profit is what people inevitably pursue; if one does not regulate it, it becomes obstructed and fails to circulate. Therefore, when one regulates it so that the people grow accustomed to righteousness, there is no expenditure that falls short. When livelihood is enriched and expenditures are sufficient, wealth is abundant and there is no contention; in the enterprises of all under Heaven, what could be undertaken and not succeed? Your Excellency has posed a policy question to us students concerning grain reserves and coin and silk—is it because you suppose I understand the affairs of the times? I am not such a man, yet how could I dare not gather what I have heard in order to reply? I have heard that when a sage…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
人在上而民不凍饑者非能耕而食之織
而衣之也為開其食貨之源也故辨土地
以藝植因水旱而鑄金使四民各勤其業
而遠近咸資其利一毫一縷事為之制而
見於周官一書者尤備焉九穀之生責諸
三農國用之制以三十年為通而九府圜
法復有以濟粟之所不及當其時民有餘
粟而國有餘財蓋因其利而利之非損下
也因其足而通之非奪民也鳧鷖旣醉之
===
治有自來矣後之求理者亦常用之乃田
雖井而新自新官雖周而隋自隋者何哉
蓋古之人理其出而後之人理其入乃一
切苟且之術也豈古今異宜哉管仲九府
之制因貴賤以權輕重單穆公以錢輕為
患則量資幣而權子母焉是雖未必盡合
周官之法度而操縱以時民胥便之固謂
之得策矣李悝平糴之法因歲入為斂散
桑弘羊易以均輸則籠百貨而歸於官焉
punctuated: 人在上，而民不凍饑者，非能耕而食之、織而衣之也，為開其食貨之源也。故辨土地以藝植，因水旱而鑄金，使四民各勤其業，而遠近咸資其利。一毫一縷，事為之制，而見於《周官》一書者尤備焉。九穀之生，責諸三農；國用之制，以三十年為通；而九府圜法，復有以濟粟之所不及。當其時，民有餘粟，而國有餘財。蓋因其利而利之，非損下也；因其足而通之，非奪民也。《鳧鷖》、《旣醉》之治，有自來矣。後之求理者亦常用之，乃田雖井而新自新，官雖周而隋自隋者，何哉？蓋古之人理其出，而後之人理其入，乃一切苟且之術也，豈古今異宜哉？管仲九府之制，因貴賤以權輕重；單穆公以錢輕為患，則量資幣而權子母焉。是雖未必盡合《周官》之法度，而操縱以時，民胥便之，固謂之得策矣。李悝平糴之法，因歲入為斂散；桑弘羊易以均輸，則籠百貨而歸於官焉。
translation_en: …a sage is on the throne, the people do not suffer from cold or hunger—not because he can plow to feed them or weave to clothe them himself, but because he opens up the sources of food and commodities for them. Therefore, he distinguished the types of soil for cultivation and planting, and cast metal coins in response to floods and droughts, causing the four classes of people each to be diligent in their occupations, so that those near and far all relied on the benefits. Down to a single hair or a single thread, regulations were made for every matter, and what is seen in the book Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) is especially complete. The production of the nine grains was entrusted to the farmers of the three terrains; the regulation of state expenditures was calculated on a thirty-year cycle; and the round-coin currency system of the nine treasuries further served to supplement what grain alone could not reach. At that time, the people had surplus grain and the state had surplus wealth. This was because the ruler benefited them on the basis of what was already beneficial to them, without diminishing those below; he circulated goods on the basis of their existing sufficiency, without robbing the people. The well-governed eras celebrated in the odes "Wild Ducks" (Fuyi) and "Already Drunk" (Jizui) indeed had their origin! Those in later times who sought to manage finances also frequently used these methods; yet why is it that although the fields were divided according to the well-field system, the Xin dynasty remained the Xin, and although the offices were modeled on the Zhou, the Sui dynasty remained the Sui? It is because the ancients managed the production of wealth, whereas people of later times managed its extraction—which is merely an expedient, makeshift art. How could it be that what is appropriate differs between antiquity and the present? Guan Zhong's system of the nine treasuries weighed lightness and heaviness of currency according to whether goods were dear or cheap; Duke Mu of Shan, considering light coins to be a problem, measured resources and currency and balanced mother and child coins. Although these did not necessarily conform entirely to the laws and standards of the Offices of Zhou, they tightened and relaxed control in accordance with the times, and the people all found them convenient, so they may certainly be called successful policies. Li Kui's method of equitable grain purchasing gathered in or distributed grain according to the annual harvest; Sang Hongyang replaced this with equitable transport, monopolizing all kinds of goods and turning them over to the government. …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
是雖均爲心計之運量然平糴裕農而均
輸貿利悝固彼善於此者矣富民入粟實
邊順民心而三有所補此鼂錯積儲計也
孝文賴以富庶可謂盛矣然積貲顯融則
累行者抑姦民蒙宥則犯科者多胥天下
離制而棄本冒禍而攘利焉其錯之作俑
乎摶銅盡歸公庾禁私鑄而致福有七此
賈誼治安策也文帝竟弛錢禁非不公矣
然利權旁落則倒持太阿法網太疎則蚖
弛日衆至吳王鑄錢而富埒萬乘商賈滯
財而不佐公家焉其誼之先見乎是數子
者興一時之利便而爲司計者所宗固能
臣也然財不可聚而獨厚於上權不可移
而反歸於下其得失異致而治亂常相反
者其所操者殊也我
祖宗軫念元元節以制度墾田科稅歲有常供
官俸軍需用有定額上不侈而下常餘宇
內蒸蒸富庶者餘二百年卽滇南遠在徼
punctuated:
是雖均爲心計之運量，然平糴裕農而均輸貿利，悝固彼善於此者矣。富民入粟實邊，順民心而三有所補，此鼂錯積儲計也。孝文賴以富庶，可謂盛矣；然積貲顯融則累行者抑，姦民蒙宥則犯科者多，胥天下離制而棄本、冒禍而攘利焉，其錯之作俑乎？摶銅盡歸公庾，禁私鑄而致福有七，此賈誼治安策也。文帝竟弛錢禁，非不公矣；然利權旁落則倒持太阿，法網太疎則蚖弛日衆，至吳王鑄錢而富埒萬乘，商賈滯財而不佐公家焉，其誼之先見乎？是數子者，興一時之利便，而爲司計者所宗，固能臣也。然財不可聚而獨厚於上，權不可移而反歸於下，其得失異致而治亂常相反者，其所操者殊也。

我祖宗軫念元元，節以制度，墾田科稅，歲有常供，官俸軍需，用有定額。上不侈而下常餘，宇內蒸蒸富庶者餘二百年，卽滇南遠在徼…
translation_en:
Although both were products of calculated financial planning, the "Equitable Grain Purchase" enriched the peasantry while the "Equitable Delivery" traded for profit; thus Li Kui 李悝 was certainly superior to the latter in this regard. Having wealthy commoners contribute grain to supply the frontiers—conforming to the people's wishes and providing three distinct benefits—this was Chao Cuo's 鼂錯 plan for accumulating reserves. Emperor Xiaowen 孝文 relied on it to achieve wealth and abundance, which may well be called flourishing. Yet when amassing wealth leads to high rank and prominence, those who cultivate upright conduct are suppressed; and when wicked subjects receive pardons, those who violate the laws multiply. That the whole realm departed from regulations and abandoned fundamental agriculture, braving disaster to seize profit—was it not Cuo who initiated this evil practice? Gathering all copper into public granaries and prohibiting private minting so as to bring about seven blessings—this was Jia Yi's 賈誼 policy for securing peace and order. Emperor Wen 文帝 ultimately relaxed the prohibition on coinage, which was not ungenerous. Yet when economic authority slips away to the side, it is like holding the Tai'e sword by the blade; and when the net of the law is too loose, the unruly and lax [?] grow more numerous by the day. That it came to the Prince of Wu 吳王 minting coins and rivaling the Son of Heaven in wealth, while merchants hoarded goods and failed to assist the state—did this not show Yi's foresight? These several men promoted the conveniences and advantages of a single era and were revered by those in charge of fiscal planning; they were assuredly capable ministers. Nevertheless, wealth must not be amassed so as to enrich only those above, and authority must not be shifted so that it reverts instead to those below. That their successes and failures led to different outcomes, and that order and disorder were constantly opposed, was because the principles they held to were different.

Our Imperial Ancestors showed compassionate concern for the common people and regulated expenditures through institutional limits. Reclaimed lands were assessed for taxes, providing a regular annual supply; official salaries and military provisions had fixed quotas for expenditure. Those above were not extravagant and those below always had a surplus. Within the realm, thriving wealth and abundance lasted for over two hundred years; even Diannan 滇南 (Yunnan), far out on the frontier…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
外亦沐膏澤稱富饒矣乃者生齒日繁歳
入漸寡稍旱暵而餓夫盈途是蓄積不如
古也貨物翔踴閭里瀟然縁轉徙而額餉
日逋是財用不如古也居常無事醫瘡剜
肉已不忍聞於慈父孝子之聲而卒然有
警則安知其計之所出哉
皇上睿德性生冲虚節愛積粟之課旣
頒鑄錢之
令復下其視洪範之先食貨周官之阜民財
===
者
意尤渥也海內喁喁然思嚮
皇風而登殷阜而滇之急在燃眉者當事諸臣
將何以奉揚休美乎夫善爲治者莫不重
穀今滇民不勤本業而生寡食衆銍艾甫
停積蓄告匱粟之不足甚矣誠欲理之其
要有三屯地有定額而隱侵於豪右乾没
於武弁責餘丁以虚賠而質他室以負稅
夷民租種軍田輸稅十一額失而弊滋矣
punctuated:
外，亦沐膏澤，稱富饒矣。乃者生齒日繁，歳入漸寡，稍旱暵而餓夫盈途，是蓄積不如古也；貨物翔踴，閭里瀟然，縁轉徙而額餉日逋，是財用不如古也。居常無事，醫瘡剜肉，已不忍聞於慈父孝子之聲，而卒然有警，則安知其計之所出哉？皇上睿德性生，冲虚節愛，積粟之課旣頒，鑄錢之令復下，其視《洪範》之先食貨、《周官》之阜民財者，意尤渥也。海內喁喁然思嚮皇風而登殷阜，而滇之急在燃眉者，當事諸臣將何以奉揚休美乎？

夫善爲治者莫不重穀。今滇民不勤本業，而生寡食衆，銍艾甫停，積蓄告匱，粟之不足甚矣。誠欲理之，其要有三：屯地有定額，而隱侵於豪右，乾没於武弁，責餘丁以虚賠，而質他室以負稅，夷民租種軍田，輸稅十一，額失而弊滋矣。
translation_en:
… beyond the frontiers, also bathed in imperial grace and was acclaimed for its affluence. Recently, however, the population has grown daily more numerous while annual revenues have gradually declined. With the slightest drought, starving people fill the roads; thus our stored reserves do not match those of antiquity. Prices of goods soar, villages lie desolate, and because of displacement and migration, the fixed quotas of military rations fall further into arrears day by day; thus our financial resources do not match those of antiquity. Even in ordinary times of peace, people must gouge out flesh to heal a sore, and one can already scarcely bear to hear the cries of compassionate fathers and filial sons; if a sudden alarm should arise, how would we know what plan to resort to? His Majesty is endowed by nature with sage virtue, modest, frugal, and benevolent. Assessments for storing grain have already been promulgated, and orders for casting copper cash have again been handed down. Compared with the priority given to food and commodities in the "Great Plan" (Hongfan) and the enrichment of the people's wealth in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), His Majesty's intentions are even more generous. Within the seas, all look up expectantly, longing to turn toward the imperial wind and ascend to prosperity; yet with Yunnan's emergencies as pressing as singed eyebrows, how shall the officials in charge uphold and spread abroad His Majesty's fine beneficence?

Now, none who excel at governance fail to value grain. Today the people of Yunnan are not diligent in the fundamental occupation [agriculture]; those who produce are few while those who consume are many. No sooner have the sickles stopped harvesting than the stored reserves are reported exhausted—the shortage of grain is extreme indeed! If we truly wish to put this in order, there are three essentials: First, military state farms (tundi) have fixed quotas, yet they are covertly encroached upon by powerful families and embezzled by military officers. Supernumerary adult males (yuding) are forced to make up empty deficits, and properties are mortgaged to other households while taxes remain unpaid. Native and civilian households rent and till the military fields, paying only one-tenth in tax, so that the original land quotas are lost and abuses proliferate. …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
必按籍以稽履畝而覈番休老壯盜沽之
竇當塞也訪覈鱗圖乾没之姦當懲也則
田足贍軍而亦可以寬民此清屯田之爲
要也一夫不耕受以饑矣乃武定迷蒙荒
蕪未墾而遊食者日衆誠擇其長川廣野
可以開溝洫而畫經界者授可耕之人而
給之牛種薄征稅之入而時勸相焉則緣
南畝者多而積儲備矣此勸力作之爲要
也夫常平非李悝之法也三代之法也今
===
之春而貸秋而償善矣然栽桑紙上逋欠
日多放則利歸胥猾徵則迹涉誅求加以
潮濕浥爛又累司庾者之賠輸則孰與常
平之爲便哉必隨地而擇其亢爽立爲庾
司實以備賑之贖穀掌以茂實之耆民貴
出賤入無貲者量貸之惟其饑之上下而
不盡罄焉則貲本既有所出而浥腐亦不
爲病此立常平之爲要也夫民方艱食而
吾爲之開其源使三年九年之常蓄而凶
punctuated: 必按籍以稽，履畝而覈，番休老壯，盜沽之竇當塞也；訪覈鱗圖，乾没之姦當懲也。則田足贍軍，而亦可以寬民，此清屯田之爲要也。一夫不耕，受以饑矣，乃武定、迷蒙荒蕪未墾，而遊食者日衆。誠擇其長川廣野，可以開溝洫而畫經界者，授可耕之人，而給之牛種，薄征稅之入，而時勸相焉，則緣南畝者多，而積儲備矣，此勸力作之爲要也。夫常平非李悝之法也，三代之法也。今之春而貸、秋而償，善矣。然栽桑紙上，逋欠日多，放則利歸胥猾，徵則迹涉誅求；加以潮濕浥爛，又累司庾者之賠輸，則孰與常平之爲便哉？必隨地而擇其亢爽，立爲庾司，實以備賑之贖穀，掌以茂實之耆民，貴出賤入，無貲者量貸之，惟其饑之上下而不盡罄焉。則貲本既有所出，而浥腐亦不爲病，此立常平之爲要也。夫民方艱食，而吾爲之開其源，使三年、九年之常蓄，而凶
translation_en: One must examine the registers to investigate and inspect the fields in person; rotate the old and the able-bodied, and close the loopholes of illicit sale; investigate and verify the fish-scale land registers, and punish the fraud of embezzlement. Then the fields will suffice to support the military and relief can also be granted to the common people. This is the essential point of clearing up the military state farms. If a single man does not plow, someone suffers hunger from it; yet in Wuding 武定 and Mimeng 迷蒙 the wasteland remains uncultivated while idle consumers grow more numerous by the day. If we truly select their long rivers and broad plains where ditches and channels can be opened and boundaries delineated, grant them to people capable of farming, supply them with oxen and seed, lighten the collection of taxes, and seasonably encourage and assist them, then those working the southern acres will be many and stored reserves will be prepared. This is the essential point of encouraging diligent labor. Now the Ever-Normal Granary is not the method of Li Kui 李悝; it is the method of the Three Dynasties. The present practice of lending in spring and repaying in autumn is good indeed. Yet it is like planting mulberries on paper, and arrears grow more numerous by the day: when grain is disbursed, the profit goes to cunning clerks; when it is collected, the practice borders on extortionate demands. Added to this are dampness and rotting, which further burden those in charge of the granaries with making restitution. How then can this compare with the convenience of the Ever-Normal system? One must, according to the locality, select high and dry ground to establish granary offices, fill them with redemption grain set aside for famine relief, and place them under the charge of upright and substantial elders. Sell when prices are high and buy when prices are low; as for those without means, lend to them according to measure, adjusting to the severity of the dearth without exhausting the stores completely. Then the capital will have a source from which to come, and dampness and rot will not be a problem either. This is the essential point of establishing Ever-Normal Granaries. When the people are struggling for food, we open the source for them, ensuring regular reserves for three and nine years, so that in times of famine…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
荒水旱足以相恤如是而民生有不厚乎
善理財者以錢代貝蓋金銀細分則粍布
帛片折則廢惟錢爲便也今銅產於滇充
溢闤闠市民捐軀命以浚求之況於錢之
利而不害乎玆欲行之其要亦有三念賈
誼召禍起姦之說而操之使不旁落藉其
贏餘以周困匱則利權在我而劉濞鄧通
之徒無自作矣此私鑄之當禁也錢議最
多而莫善於孔顗者不惜銅不愛工也試
倣開元之制而定以新名務使體厚而肉
好適均製工而輪郭周正則本多工費而
天下之觸禁者少此椝式之當定也三幣
相準從古已然滇雲舊用海𧵅細微不混
故稱便焉惟令錢貝兼使二幣通融而一
準上幣以權之則俗不欺詒而賈無拆閱
矣此權宜之當酌也夫
朝有明令而吾爲之通其變使民情土俗之
相安而公輸私費得以兼資如是而財用
punctuated:
荒水旱足以相恤，如是而民生有不厚乎？

善理財者，以錢代貝。蓋金銀細分則粍，布帛片折則廢，惟錢爲便也。今銅產於滇，充溢闤闠，市民捐軀命以浚求之，況於錢之利而不害乎？玆欲行之，其要亦有三：念賈誼召禍起姦之說，而操之使不旁落，藉其贏餘以周困匱，則利權在我，而劉濞、鄧通之徒無自作矣，此私鑄之當禁也。錢議最多，而莫善於孔顗者，不惜銅、不愛工也。試倣開元之制，而定以新名，務使體厚而肉好適均，製工而輪郭周正，則本多工費，而天下之觸禁者少，此椝式之當定也。三幣相準，從古已然。滇雲舊用海𧵅，細微不混，故稱便焉。惟令錢貝兼使，二幣通融，而一準上幣以權之，則俗不欺詒，而賈無拆閱矣，此權宜之當酌也。夫朝有明令，而吾爲之通其變，使民情土俗之相安，而公輸私費得以兼資，如是而財用
translation_en:
…famine, floods, and droughts, there will be enough to provide mutual relief. If we act in this way, how could the people's livelihood fail to be enriched?

Those skilled at managing finances replace cowries with copper cash. This is because when gold and silver are divided into tiny fractions, they suffer loss through wear, and when cloth and silk are cut into pieces, they are ruined; only copper cash is convenient. Today, copper is produced in Yunnan (Dian), overflowing the markets, and townspeople risk their lives mining for it—how much more so when it comes to cash, which brings profit without harm? If we now wish to put coinage into circulation, there are likewise three essentials. First, bearing in mind Jia Yi's 賈誼 argument that free coinage invites disaster and gives rise to villainy, we must hold tight to the minting authority so that it does not slip into outside hands, and draw upon its surplus to relieve distress and scarcity; then control over profit will rest with us, and men like Liu Pi 劉濞 and Deng Tong 鄧通 will have no way to arise on their own. This is why private minting must be prohibited. Second, among the many discussions of coinage, none is better than that of Kong Yi 孔顗: do not begrudge the copper, and do not spare the labor. Let us imitate the standard of the Kaiyuan era and establish a new inscription, making sure that the body of the coin is thick with its body and central hole well-proportioned, and that the workmanship is fine with the outer and inner rims square and regular. Then, because the capital required is large and the labor costly, few in the realm will violate the prohibition against counterfeiting. This is why the standard pattern must be fixed. Third, balancing the three tiers of currency against one another has been practiced since antiquity. Yunnan has long used cowrie shells (haiba), which in small transactions are not easily confused and have therefore been deemed convenient. If we simply allow copper cash and cowries to be used together so that the two currencies circulate interchangeably, while uniformly using the superior currency [silver] as the standard by which to weigh their value, then popular custom will be free of deception and merchants will suffer no losses from selling below cost. This is why expedient adaptation must be carefully weighed. When the Court issues clear ordinances and we adapt them to changing circumstances, ensuring that popular sentiment and local customs remain at ease while both public tax payments and private expenditures are alike supplied—if we act in this way, how could financial resources…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
有不豐乎噫此富滇之術而推之富天下
可也雖然滇之可憂者豈止此乎租庸煩
苦則宜差恒産勾流寓以甦其困也隴畝
旱亢則當濬壩堰導桔橰以通其利也將
卒柔脆而無用夷玀剽掠而難捕則設武
舘以閑技略嚴保甲以訊知音者可不早
爲之防乎俗尚淫靡而惰農桑礦課虧額
而羈命吏則植棉麻以杜其澆易專官以
通其窮者可不曲爲之計乎若夫制防緬
===
甸分北沙儂又未然之憂出於積儲錢幣
之外者而要之莫非厚民計也顧豈無其
本哉彼谷永守鬱林而烏滸內附李靖撫
南粤而黎獞胥悅黃忠宣治安南而交人
不忍遽叛者得其人也今之仕者率戀中
原而厭邊徼除目一下索然無復向往之
心司銓者曲而通之遠方之吏非例廕則
遷謫不然則朴直寡援者也其視中土懸
異矣夫天下一體中原心腹也遠方四肢
punctuated: 有不豐乎？噫！此富滇之術，而推之富天下可也。雖然，滇之可憂者豈止此乎？租庸煩苦，則宜差恒産、勾流寓，以甦其困也；隴畝旱亢，則當濬壩堰、導桔橰，以通其利也。將卒柔脆而無用，夷玀剽掠而難捕，則設武舘以閑技略，嚴保甲以訊知音者，可不早爲之防乎？俗尚淫靡而惰農桑，礦課虧額而羈命吏，則植棉麻以杜其澆，易專官以通其窮者，可不曲爲之計乎？若夫制防緬甸，分北沙、儂，又未然之憂出於積儲錢幣之外者，而要之莫非厚民計也。顧豈無其本哉？彼谷永守鬱林而烏滸內附，李靖撫南粤而黎、獞胥悅，黃忠宣治安南而交人不忍遽叛者，得其人也。今之仕者，率戀中原而厭邊徼，除目一下，索然無復向往之心。司銓者曲而通之，遠方之吏，非例廕則遷謫，不然則朴直寡援者也，其視中土懸異矣。夫天下一體，中原，心腹也；遠方，四肢
translation_en:
… fail to be abundant? Alas! This is the art of enriching Yunnan, and by extension it could enrich the entire realm. Even so, how could what is worrisome about Yunnan stop at this? Where land taxes and corvée labor are burdensome and bitter, one should grade permanent property and register floating migrants in order to relieve their distress; where the fields suffer from drought and parchedness, one ought to dredge dams and weirs and introduce well-sweeps in order to open up their benefits. When generals and soldiers are soft, fragile, and useless, and the Yi and Luo peoples plunder and are difficult to capture, how can one not take early precautions by establishing military halls to train them in martial skills and strategy, and tightening the mutual security (baojia) system to interrogate those who know their tongues [or: harbour them]? When customs value extravagance and neglect farming and sericulture, and when mining tax quotas fall short and commissioned officials are held detained in liability, how can one not devise thorough plans by planting cotton and hemp to stem their frivolity, and replacing dedicated mining officials to relieve their impasse? As for restraining and defending against Burma (Miandian) and dividing andscattering the Sha and Nong peoples, these are future worries that lie beyond grain reserves and currency, yet in sum none of them is anything other than a plan to enrich the people's livelihood.

Yet how could this lack a fundamental root? In the past, when Gu Yong (谷永) served as Grand Administrator of Yulin, the Wuhu people submitted from within; when Li Jing (李靖) pacified Nanyue, the Li and Zhuang peoples all rejoiced; and when Huang Zhongxuan (黃忠宣, i.e., Huang Fu 黃福) governed Annam, the people of Jiaozhi could not bear to hastily rebel—this was because the right men were found. Those who hold office today generally cling to the Central Plain and detest the frontier borderlands; as soon as the appointment list is handed down, they become dispirited and no longer have any heart to go forward. Those in charge of personnel selection bend the rules to accommodate this, so that officials sent to distant regions are either routine-purchase or hereditary-privilege appointees (liyin) or demoted exiles; otherwise, they are simple, blunt men with few connections—how vastly different from how the central lands are treated! Now, the realm is a single body: the Central Plain is the heart and core, while distant regions are the four limbs…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也四肢病而委諸庸醫善攝生者固如是
乎故吏茲土者非廉潔不足以震威非材
識不足以批蠹非久任不足以孚夷情練
土俗而非超遷又不足以繫士望而固久
任之心也則夫計材而陟擇人而使賢者
不以避嫌邀名不肖者不以貪墨敗事足
兵食之圖養和平之福則華尊夷遁
九重寬西顧之憂矣是又在
巖廊加之意耳愚生慨此已久惟執事轉
===
聞之焉
punctuated: 也。四肢病而委諸庸醫，善攝生者固如是乎？故吏茲土者，非廉潔不足以震威，非材識不足以批蠹，非久任不足以孚夷情、練土俗，而非超遷又不足以繫士望而固久任之心也。則夫計材而陟，擇人而使，賢者不以避嫌邀名，不肖者不以貪墨敗事，足兵食之圖，養和平之福，則華尊夷遁，九重寬西顧之憂矣。是又在巖廊加之意耳。愚生慨此已久，惟執事轉聞之焉。
translation_en: … [the four limbs]. When the four limbs are ill and yet are entrusted to mediocre physicians, is this indeed how one who is skilled at nurturing life acts? Therefore, for those who serve as officials in this territory: without integrity and purity, they are insufficient to project awe-inspiring authority; without talent and insight, they are insufficient to strike at entrenched abuses; without long tenure in office, they are insufficient to win the trust of the native peoples and become well-versed in local customs; and without exceptional promotion, it is in turn insufficient to bind the aspirations of scholars and solidify their resolve for long tenure. Thus, if we assess talent in making promotions and select the right men for appointments—so that the worthy do not court reputation by avoiding suspicion, and the unworthy do not ruin affairs through avarice and corruption—and if we fulfill the plans for sufficient troops and provisions while nurturing the blessings of peace and harmony, then China will be revered and the non-Chinese tribes will submit, and the Ninefold Palace (the Emperor) will be relieved of its anxious gaze toward the west. This, again, rests simply upon the high court paying heed to it. This foolish student has lamented these matters for a long time; I only pray that Your Excellency will transmit this to the throne on my behalf.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
萬曆丙子雲南鄉試事竣錄
旣成監察御史陳文燧謂朝
鳴祗役校文宜申忠告朝鳴
遂言曰二三子舉於鄉執事
者旣歌鹿鳴而賓興之矣予
何言哉無已則申鹿鳴之旨
===
爲諸士告可矣昔叔孫穆子
聘於晉晉公享之樂歌鹿鳴
者三而後拜使行人問焉穆
子對曰鹿鳴君之所以貺使
臣而來周行美德音者也敢
不拜嘉夫君之貺臣以周行
德音爲望則其禮遇延接之
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序

萬曆丙子，雲南鄉試事竣，錄旣成，監察御史陳文燧謂朝鳴祗役校文，宜申忠告。朝鳴遂言曰：「二三子舉於鄉，執事者旣歌《鹿鳴》而賓興之矣，予何言哉？無已，則申《鹿鳴》之旨爲諸士告可矣。昔叔孫穆子聘於晉，晉公享之，樂歌《鹿鳴》者三，而後拜。使行人問焉，穆子對曰：『《鹿鳴》，君之所以貺使臣，而來周行、美德音者也，敢不拜嘉？』夫君之貺臣，以周行、德音爲望，則其禮遇延接之
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In the bingzi year of the Wanli era (1576), when the Yunnan Provincial Examination was concluded and the record had been compiled, Investigating Censor Chen Wensui 陳文燧 told me, Chaoming 朝鳴, that since I had respectfully served in grading the essays, I ought to offer a word of earnest counsel. Chaoming thereupon said: "You gentlemen have been recommended as provincial graduates, and the officials in charge have already sung 'The Cry of the Deer' (Luming 鹿鳴) and sent you forth as honored guests—what more could I have to say? If I must speak, then let me expound the meaning of 'The Cry of the Deer' by way of advice to you scholars. Of old, when Shusun Muzi 叔孫穆子 went on a diplomatic mission to Jin 晉, the Duke of Jin feasted him. Only after the musicians had sung 'The Cry of the Deer' three times did he bow in thanks. When the Duke sent a Messenger to ask the reason, Muzi replied: '"The Cry of the Deer" is that whereby the ruler bestows favor upon the envoy, inviting him to the highway of the court and praising his virtuous reputation; how could I dare not bow in gratitude for such kindness?' Now, when a ruler bestows favor upon his subject with the expectation that he will walk the highway of the court and possess a virtuous reputation, then the…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
誠已溢於琴瑟筐篚之外而
臣之所以報稱
主德者顧在於言語文字之間乎
彼其屬望嘉賓者不曰德音
孔昭則曰視民不恌而以君
子是則是傚者終之蓋謂身
無逸行則陳之為周行昭之
===
===
為德音而臣民胥範焉是周
之人君所以禮其臣者誠渥
而責之者亦誠殷也今
主上嗜學勤政
執中建極遠邁成周而
夢寐賢哲即遐陬僻壤之士必
隆禮厚宴羅而致之惟恐其
punctuated: 誠，已溢於琴瑟筐篚之外；而臣之所以報稱主德者，顧在於言語文字之間乎？彼其屬望嘉賓者，不曰「德音孔昭」，則曰「視民不恌」，而以「君子是則是傚」者終之。蓋謂身無逸行，則陳之為周行，昭之為德音，而臣民胥範焉。是周之人君所以禮其臣者誠渥，而責之者亦誠殷也。今主上嗜學勤政，執中建極，遠邁成周，而夢寐賢哲，即遐陬僻壤之士，必隆禮厚宴，羅而致之，惟恐其
translation_en:
…sincerity has already overflowed beyond the zithers, lutes, and baskets of gifts; how then could that by which a subject repays and matches the sovereign's virtue lie merely in speech and writing? What that ode expects of the honored guests—if it does not say "their virtuous reputation is grandly顯明 (kongzhao)," then it says "they show the people how not to be frivolous"—and it concludes with "the noble men take them as their model and pattern." This means that when one's personal conduct is free of waywardness, when set forth it becomes the highway of the state (zhouhang), and when made manifest it becomes a virtuous reputation (deyin), so that officials and commoners alike take it as their standard. Thus, the way the rulers of the Zhou treated their ministers with courtesy was truly generous, and what they demanded of them was also truly earnest.

Now His Majesty delights in learning and is diligent in governance, holding fast to the Mean and establishing the Supreme Standard, far surpassing the flourishing Zhou; and he longs in his dreams for the worthy and wise. Even for scholars from distant corners and remote regions, he unfailingly gathers and brings them in with grand rites and lavish banquets, fearing only that their…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
周行之說不亟聞於
上諸士生於朱提炎方去中原萬
餘里其初不過與齊民耦耳
一旦策名
天府光華燁然卽且司民社臣鄰
之寄竒哉遘也乃可衒空名
於鉛槧隤盛美於聲華而不
===
思履德蹈道以求稱塞於萬
一乎夫熊蹯豹胎不若菽粟
之味錦文綺縠不若韋布之
溫所謂不佻之德豈其踔厲
﨑崛而絕俗為異者哉惟篤
衷不欺表裏符契則其材固
君子之材文亦君子之文也
punctuated: 周行之說不亟聞於上。諸士生於朱提炎方，去中原萬餘里，其初不過與齊民耦耳。一旦策名天府，光華燁然，卽且司民社臣鄰之寄，竒哉遘也！乃可衒空名於鉛槧，隤盛美於聲華，而不思履德蹈道，以求稱塞於萬一乎？夫熊蹯豹胎，不若菽粟之味；錦文綺縠，不若韋布之溫。所謂不佻之德，豈其踔厲﨑崛而絕俗為異者哉？惟篤衷不欺，表裏符契，則其材固君子之材，文亦君子之文也。
translation_en: …counsels on the Great Way might not be promptly heard by the Sovereign. You scholars were born in the torrid southern regions of Zhuti, more than ten thousand li distant from the Central Plains, and at first you were merely the equals of the common people. Yet once your names are inscribed in the imperial archives, your splendor shines brilliantly, and before long you will be entrusted with the charge of the people and their altars, serving as ministerial assistants to the ruler—how marvelous an encounter this is! How then could you flaunt empty fame through brush and tablet, or squander such splendid excellence in the pursuit of flashy reputation, without thinking of treading the path of virtue and the Way so as to fulfill even a ten-thousandth part of your duty? Bear paws and leopard fetuses do not match the flavor of beans and grain; brocade patterns and fine gauzes do not match the warmth of leather and coarse cloth. As for what is called 'unfrivolous virtue,' how could it consist in being fiercely high-strung, ruggedly eccentric, and cutting oneself off from the world to appear extraordinary? Only when one's innermost heart is sincere and without deceit, and one's exterior and interior tally like two halves of a token, is one's talent truly the talent of a noble man, and one's writing likewise the writing of a noble man.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
今方内之士握瑜懷瑾孰不
標表藝林希高慕大孰不抵
掌先哲居常奮嘆天下之事
若以爲言之無由行之無會
汲汲然不得以其身試之然
一肩重鉅輒相牾悮無論饜
厭溫飽巽懦尠立即或建樹
===
卓犖焜耀耳目而玄覽未深
一涉於虛驕之念焉則視古
之立功立言者尚不免堂奧
之隔矣諸士脩詞績德蓋亦
有年自今謀之心揆之後其
能以周行之陳報
寵遇不佻之德視臣民乎鹿鳴之
punctuated: 今方内之士，握瑜懷瑾，孰不標表藝林？希高慕大，孰不抵掌先哲？居常奮嘆天下之事，若以爲言之無由、行之無會，汲汲然不得以其身試之。然一肩重鉅，輒相牾悮。無論饜厭溫飽、巽懦尠立，即或建樹卓犖，焜耀耳目，而玄覽未深，一涉於虛驕之念焉，則視古之立功立言者，尚不免堂奧之隔矣。諸士脩詞績德，蓋亦有年。自今謀之心、揆之後，其能以周行之陳報寵遇，不佻之德視臣民乎？鹿鳴之
translation_en: Today, among the scholars within the realm who clasp fine jade to their bosoms, who does not stand out as a paragon in the forest of letters? Aspiring to the lofty and admiring the great, who does not clap his hands in animated discussion of the former sages? In ordinary times, they rouse themselves and sigh over the affairs of the world, as though they had no way to speak out and no opportunity to act, anxiously regretting that they cannot test themselves in practice. Yet once they shoulder heavy and immense responsibilities, they are immediately at odds and fall into error. To say nothing of those who are sated with warmth and full bellies, timid and weak, achieving little—even if someone establishes extraordinary accomplishments that dazzle the eyes and ears, if his profound insight is not yet deep and he once indulges in vain and arrogant thoughts, then compared with the ancients who established merit and established words, he still cannot avoid being separated from the inner sanctum by the outer hall. You scholars have cultivated your writing and accumulated virtue for some years now. From this day forward, as you take counsel in your hearts and measure the future, will you be able to repay Imperial favor by setting forth the Great Way, and display unfrivolous virtue to the officials and people? The strains of the "Luming" [Song of the Bleating Deer] …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
音固在耳也奈之何其弗懋
哉昔人謂
君臣際會比諸雲龍而大雲五色
其下必有賢人兹省之得名
者固以彩雲自南方出也〔朝〕
〔鳴〕初歷龍華境方旱暵蒼碧
之巔雲峯硉兀咸欣欣然以
爲雨也少焉飄揭晴空日出
有曜衆且嗒然寂矣詰朝望
瀟湘木客之區雲猶是也巳
而頹飆怒雹偃苗拔木人皆
咨睢又明日陟苴蘭廻視盤
龍太華諸峯烟霧四塞褰裳
疾避乃霖霪淋漓槁甦仆植
punctuated: 音固在耳也，奈之何其弗懋哉！昔人謂君臣際會比諸雲龍，而大雲五色，其下必有賢人。兹省之得名者，固以彩雲自南方出也。〔朝〕〔鳴〕初歷龍華境，方旱暵，蒼碧之巔，雲峯硉兀，咸欣欣然以爲雨也。少焉，飄揭晴空，日出有曜，衆且嗒然寂矣。詰朝，望瀟湘、木客之區，雲猶是也。巳而頹飆怒雹，偃苗拔木，人皆咨睢。又明日，陟苴蘭，廻視盤龍、太華諸峯，烟霧四塞，褰裳疾避，乃霖霪淋漓，槁甦仆植，
translation_en: …sound [of the “Luming” ode] is certainly still in your ears; how can you not exert yourselves! Men of old compared the propitious meeting of ruler and minister to clouds and dragons, and said that beneath great clouds of five colors there must be a worthy man. That this province obtained its name [Yunnan, “South of the Clouds”] is indeed because iridescent clouds appeared from the south. When I, Chaoming, first passed through the territory of Longhua, it was just then suffering from drought and parching heat. Above the苍碧 [dark-blue and emerald] peaks, cloud-summits rose rugged and towering, and everyone rejoiced, thinking it would rain. In a little while, they drifted away and dispersed into a clear sky; the sun came out shining brightly, and the multitude fell dejected and silent. The next morning, looking toward the regions of Xiaoxiang and Muke, the clouds were just like that again. Soon after, a violent gale and furious hail flattened the sprouts and uprooted trees, leaving everyone sighing and staring in dismay. On the following day, I ascended Julan [Kunming] and looked back at the peaks of Panlong and Taihua. Mist and fog closed in on all four sides; hiking up our robes, we hastened to take shelter, whereupon a drenching, timely rain poured down, reviving the withered and raising up the fallen,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
三農籲天稱慶焉然則民何
心哉固雲之變態爾殊也今
諸士之文即祥光景雲不是
過日當服休服采雲附景從
其爲浮雲乎無咎無譽矣爲
暴雲乎眾且咨之矣惟輝煌
治理霖雨蒼生使臣鄰胥有
===
視傚則人將稱爲慶雲如昔
賢臚第不負太史之奏即滇
省人物自玆科稱盛而彩雲
之號亦惟諸士當其實矣進
而馥稿書裳垂光萬禩充之
爲虞周之傑焉又豈得以滇
雲之人物限之哉昔祁奚舉
punctuated: 三農籲天稱慶焉。然則民何心哉？固雲之變態爾殊也。今諸士之文，即祥光景雲不是過。日當服休服采，雲附景從。其爲浮雲乎？無咎無譽矣；爲暴雲乎？眾且咨之矣。惟輝煌治理，霖雨蒼生，使臣鄰胥有視傚，則人將稱爲慶雲，如昔賢臚第，不負太史之奏。即滇省人物自玆科稱盛，而彩雲之號，亦惟諸士當其實矣。進而馥稿書裳，垂光萬禩，充之爲虞、周之傑焉，又豈得以滇雲之人物限之哉？昔祁奚舉
translation_en: …and the farmers of the three terrains called out to Heaven in celebration. Why, then, do the people react so? It is surely because the shifting forms of the clouds are so different from one another. Today, the writings of you gentlemen are surpassed not even by auspicious light and bright clouds. The day will come when you serve in fine and glorious office, gathering like clouds and following like shadows. Will you be like floating clouds? Then there will be neither blame nor praise. Will you be like tempestuous clouds? Then the multitudes will sigh and glare at you. Only if you make brilliant the principles of governance, bring timely rain to the common people, and cause your fellow ministers and colleagues all to have a model to emulate, will people acclaim you as auspicious clouds—just as when the worthies of old were announced in the palace examination rankings, fulfilling the Grand Astrologer's memorial. Then the men of talent in Yunnan province will be celebrated as flourishing from this very examination onward, and it is you gentlemen alone who will truly live up to the name of "Colorful Clouds" (Caiyun, i.e., Yunnan). Going further, to leave fragrant drafts and have your deeds inscribed on ceremonial robes, shedding luster for ten thousand generations, and developing your capacities to become heroes comparable to those of Yu and Zhou—how could you then be limited merely to being talents of Yunnan? In antiquity, when Qi Xi recommended…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
善人謂惟善也故能舉其類
朝鳴非其人也追武前脩式
貽主司令名在二三子
河南汝州伊陽縣儒□□□
劉朝鳴謹序
punctuated:
善，人謂惟善也，故能舉其類。朝鳴非其人也，追武前脩，式貽主司令名，在二三子。
河南汝州伊陽縣儒□□□劉朝鳴謹序。
translation_en:
… the good, people said: "It is only because he is good that he is able to recommend those of his own kind." I, Chaoming, am not such a person. Following in the footsteps of former worthies and thereby bequeathing a fine reputation to the examiners rests with you gentlemen.

Respectfully prefaced by Liu Chaoming 劉朝鳴, Confucian [School Instructor (?)] of Yiyang County, Ruzhou, Henan.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
獻共惟
帝臣而又惓惓然振浮崇雅欲挽
士習於太古之盛
初嗣寶曆卽罷玆省採買獨於科
額增五人焉故
聖意所加百神効靈迺井璧礦金
近多縮額而抱瑋擷華之士
===
===
駸駸然倍疇曩是滇士之精
采濯於
龍光意氣觸於鼓舞視諸藩尤厚
幸也矧今歲在丙子陽德開
先文明彪炳滇境屬南方實
神聖向明之地則其含精炳靈應
運而起者非千載一時之會
punctuated: 獻，共惟帝臣，而又惓惓然振浮崇雅，欲挽士習於太古之盛。初嗣寶曆，卽罷玆省採買，獨於科額增五人焉。故聖意所加，百神効靈，迺井璧礦金，近多縮額，而抱瑋擷華之士，駸駸然倍疇曩。是滇士之精采濯於龍光，意氣觸於鼓舞，視諸藩尤厚幸也。矧今歲在丙子，陽德開先，文明彪炳，滇境屬南方，實神聖向明之地。則其含精炳靈、應運而起者，非千載一時之會
translation_en: …worthy men, together serving as subjects of the Emperor; and furthermore, he is earnestly devoted to dispelling superficiality and exalting elegance, wishing to restore the customs of scholars to the flourishing state of high antiquity. When he first succeeded to the precious calendar [the throne], he immediately halted the government purchases in this province, while uniquely increasing its examination quota by five men. Therefore, where the Sacred Intention is directed, the hundred spirits render their efficacy: thus the jade from wells and gold from mines have recently often had their quotas reduced, whereas scholars who embrace extraordinary talent and gather literary blossoms have been rapidly doubling compared to former days. Thus the vitality and brilliance of the scholars of Dian [Yunnan] are bathed in the Dragon's glory, and their spirit and ambition are stirred by encouragement, making them even more richly fortunate than those of other provinces. How much more so in this bingzi year [1576], when the virtue of yang opens the way and cultural brilliance shines forth! The territory of Dian belongs to the southern quarter, which is truly the region toward which the divine sage faces the light. Then are not those who harbor pure essence and radiant spirit, rising in response to theturn of destiny, meeting with an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
乎故縱觀多士之文初試則
典麗春融恍若蒼珉瓊玖爛
焉奪目再試則敷陳忠懇剖
議精嚴凜乎有凌逼萬仞之
勢而其明道術籌世故汪洋
宏放見諸三試者即昆洱之
吞納潤澤不能過之茲固其
===
鍾毓於古振耀於
今而天祚
聖明億萬禩無疆之治故多士之
發祥遐僻者亦卓爾不羣也
豈特爲滇士慶乎顧惟
國家以經義選士即虞周敷言
陳謨之規也名卿碩輔自茲
punctuated: 乎？故縱觀多士之文，初試則典麗春融，恍若蒼珉瓊玖，爛焉奪目；再試則敷陳忠懇，剖議精嚴，凜乎有凌逼萬仞之勢；而其明道術、籌世故，汪洋宏放，見諸三試者，即昆、洱之吞納潤澤，不能過之。茲固其鍾毓於古，振耀於今，而天祚聖明億萬禩無疆之治，故多士之發祥遐僻者，亦卓爾不羣也，豈特爲滇士慶乎？顧惟國家以經義選士，即虞、周敷言陳謨之規也。名卿碩輔，自茲
translation_en: …? Therefore, surveying the writings of the many scholars as a whole: in the first session, they were classical, elegant, and harmonious as spring, as though azure jade-stone and crimson gems were shining dazzingly before the eyes; in the second session, they set forth their views with loyal sincerity and analyzed arguments with precision and rigor, awe-inspiring with the momentum of soaring up ten thousand fathoms; and in illuminating the principles of the Way and planning for the affairs of the world, vast, surging, grand, and unrestrained as seen in the third session, even the all-embracing capacity and nourishing moisture of Kunming Lake and Erhai Lake could not surpass them. This is truly because what was nurtured and concentrated here in antiquity now shines forth in the present, and because Heaven blesses the Sacred and Enlightened Ruler with a boundless reign of ten thousand myriad years; thus the many scholars who rise to prominence from this distant and remote region are also outstanding and extraordinary above the crowd. Is this a matter of celebration merely for the scholars of Dian [Yunnan]? Yet when we reflect upon how the Dynasty selects scholars through the meaning of the Classics, it is none other than the standard of setting forth words and presenting counsels in the eras of Yu [Shun] and Zhou. Famous ministers and great statesmen from this…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
脫穎耳目不勝睹記迺今藝
藻日盛於昔而醇固愨實則
多讓之甚或渝節窳行玉表
石衷遇盤錯輒稱乏材致廑
主上諄諄敕飭將無藻繪工而太
樸散耶今主司之取諸士諸
士之見取於主司均以文耳
===
===
玉卮無當綵艦難乘其中未
必有也故滇士在昔恐其不
文而求之於今則又恐其文
之靡焉蓋近質者猶可措其
未施之巧而盡飾者則易滋
其無已之情物理固然也彼
孔子遜於躬行而必從先進
punctuated: 脫穎，耳目不勝睹記。迺今藝藻日盛於昔，而醇固愨實則多讓之；甚或渝節窳行，玉表石衷，遇盤錯輒稱乏材，致廑主上諄諄敕飭。將無藻繪工而太樸散耶？今主司之取諸士，諸士之見取於主司，均以文耳。玉卮無當，綵艦難乘，其中未必有也。故滇士在昔恐其不文，而求之於今，則又恐其文之靡焉。蓋近質者猶可措其未施之巧，而盡飾者則易滋其無已之情，物理固然也。彼孔子遜於躬行，而必從先進；
translation_en:
… emerged in abundance, more than the eye can see or memory record. Yet today, while literary embellishment flourishes day by day beyond that of the past, pure, steadfast, and honest substance largely yields to it. In extreme cases, some even abandon their integrity and engage in corrupt conduct—jade on the outside but stone within. When confronted with knotted and complex problems, there is immediately talk of a dearth of talent, causing His Majesty to issue earnest and repeated admonitions. Could it not be that as ornate decoration grows ever more skillful, primal simplicity is dispersed?

Now, when the Examiners select the scholars, and when the scholars are selected by the Examiners, it is solely on the basis of their writing. Yet a jade goblet without a bottom or a painted warship too frail to board do not necessarily possess any real utility within. Therefore, whereas in the past one feared that the scholars of Yunnan might lack literary refinement, when we seek talent among them today, we fear instead that their writing may be overly florid. For that which remains close to plain substance still allows room to apply skill not yet exercised, whereas that which is utterly given over to ornament easily breeds endless indulgence—such is inherently the principle of things. Confucius modestly disclaimed having achieved personal practice of the Way, and insisted on following the men of former times in ritual and music; …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
若滇之始華肇自武侯其澹
泊寧靜之旨亦仰宗孔氏者
也諸士頌法孔子而武侯之
烈蓋稔聞之日且依乗
風雲任致遠之責矣果能明志
尚實自靖自獻大而篤棐調
燮次而敷宣屏翰必成先資
===
之信而綦隆往哲則
聖明籲俊圖理之忱庶幾無負而
其增耀於山川者不既多乎
若乃汩溺其志揺眩其衷而
藉選舉爲聲利之媒是
上以誠求下以僞應又不若犀象
珎貝可以充實
punctuated: 若滇之始華，肇自武侯，其澹泊寧靜之旨，亦仰宗孔氏者也。諸士頌法孔子，而武侯之烈蓋稔聞之，日且依乗風雲，任致遠之責矣。果能明志尚實，自靖自獻，大而篤棐調燮，次而敷宣屏翰，必成先資之信，而綦隆往哲，則聖明籲俊圖理之忱，庶幾無負，而其增耀於山川者，不既多乎！若乃汩溺其志，揺眩其衷，而藉選舉爲聲利之媒，是上以誠求，下以僞應，又不若犀象珎貝可以充實
translation_en: As for the dawn of civilization in Yunnan, it began with the Martial Marquis (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮); his principle of tranquility and detachment from worldly desires also looked up to the teachings of Confucius as its model. You scholars chant the words of and model yourselves upon Confucius, and with the illustrious deeds of the Martial Marquis you are surely long familiar; before long you will ride the wind and clouds to shoulder responsibilities of far-reaching consequence. If indeed you can clarify your resolve and prize substance, cultivating quiet integrity with which to dedicate yourselves to the throne—in the greatest roles, devotedly assisting and harmonizing at court; in lesser ones, proclaiming imperial grace and serving as a bulwark in the provinces—determined to fulfill the trust pledged by your initial offerings and to rival the eminence of the sages and worthies of the past, then the Sacred and Enlightened Sovereign’s earnest sincerity in summoning men of talent to plan for good governance will perhaps not be betrayed, and will not the glory thereby added to the mountains and rivers of this land be abundant indeed! If, on the other hand, one drowns one’s aspirations and lets one’s inner heart be swayed and dazzled, using the examination selection merely as a stepping-stone to fame and profit, then when the ruler seeks with sincerity, the subject responds with deceit. Such men would not even equal the rhinoceros horns, ivory, and precious cowries that can at least replenish…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
國用而玀僰之刻木指劒以爲
約劑擊銅轉袂以爲禮樂者
其間能幾乎何者彼固朴而
野此則文而不慚者也夫麗
江之金斂而楊之又從而汰
之精矣洪爐一煽躍鉛沉礫
淘者安所逭其責也鶴慶之
===
劒韜以鞞琫懸以珠璣華然
麗也試之剸斷鈍若鉛刀將
無拙冶之誚乎〔遵烈〕固願諸
士鍊之愈堅試之愈銳而髖
髀鼓煽之區毅然不易所守
焉固不特裒然爲科目光而
吾屬亦以釋乎不精不鍊之
punctuated: 國用，而玀僰之刻木指劒以爲約劑、擊銅轉袂以爲禮樂者，其間能幾乎？何者？彼固朴而野，此則文而不慚者也。夫麗江之金，斂而楊之，又從而汰之，精矣；洪爐一煽，躍鉛沉礫，淘者安所逭其責也？鶴慶之劒，韜以鞞琫，懸以珠璣，華然麗也；試之剸斷，鈍若鉛刀，將無拙冶之誚乎？〔遵烈〕固願諸士鍊之愈堅，試之愈銳，而髖髀鼓煽之區，毅然不易所守焉。固不特裒然爲科目光，而吾屬亦以釋乎不精不鍊之
translation_en: …the needs of the state. And compared to the Luo and Bo peoples, who notch wood and point at swords to make covenants, and strike bronze drums and twirl their sleeves as their rites and music, how much difference would there really be between them? Why is this? Because those peoples are at least simple and rustic, whereas such men are outwardly refined yet feel no shame. Now, when the gold of Lijiang is gathered and winnowed, and then washed and sifted, it seems pure; yet once the great furnace is fanned into flame, if lead leaps out and gravel sinks to the bottom, how can the panner escape responsibility? And when a sword of Heqing is sheathed in an ornamented scabbard and hung with pearls and gems, it is splendidly beautiful; yet if when tested in cutting and severing it proves as blunt as a leaden knife, will there not be the reproach of clumsy smithing? I, [Zunlie], truly wish that you gentlemen will temper yourselves until you are ever firmer, and test yourselves until you are ever sharper, so that amidst the crucible of fanned flames and tangled joints and bones, you resolutely refuse to alter your principles. Then not only will you stand forth preeminently to bring glory to the examination system, but we officials too will be relieved of the…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
懼也若其額數之多寡則虞
帝五臣而今已九倍之周獻
十夫而今將五倍之矣豈以
多寡為盛衰哉諸士為之而
已是舉也黔國公沐昌祚節
鎮玆土雅志好文都御史王
凝迪德震威昭軌崇化鼓鑄
===
士類譽髦聿興左參政李渭
右參政張文淵張諧右參議
卜相副使許宗鎰僉事畢天
能葉憲署都指揮僉事蕭世
傑高忱參將陳世忠襄翼簾
外綜理惟勤刑部郎中錢錫
汝以讞獄至樂觀厥成副使
punctuated: 懼也。若其額數之多寡，則虞帝五臣而今已九倍之，周獻十夫而今將五倍之矣，豈以多寡為盛衰哉？諸士為之而已。是舉也，黔國公沐昌祚節鎮玆土，雅志好文；都御史王凝迪德震威，昭軌崇化，鼓鑄士類，譽髦聿興；左參政李渭、右參政張文淵、張諧、右參議卜相、副使許宗鎰、僉事畢天能、葉憲、署都指揮僉事蕭世傑、高忱、參將陳世忠襄翼簾外，綜理惟勤；刑部郎中錢錫汝以讞獄至，樂觀厥成；副使
translation_en:
…fear of our own lack of refinement and tempering. As for whether the quota of graduates is large or small: Emperor Shun of Yu had five ministers, and today's quota is already nine times that; Zhou had ten worthy men, and today's quota is nearly five times that. How could flourishing or decline depend on mere numbers? It depends solely on what the scholars themselves make of it.

In this undertaking, Mu Changzuo 沐昌祚, Duke of Qian, holds the regional command of this land and cherishes a refined devotion to letters; Censor-in-Chief Wang Ning 王凝 advances virtue and projects awe, illuminates the proper standards and exalts moral transformation, molding the community of scholars so that men of renown and talent rise up; Left Administration Vice Commissioner Li Wei 李渭, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Zhang Wenyuan 張文淵 and Zhang Xie 張諧, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Bu Xiang 卜相, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Zongyi 許宗鎰, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Bi Tianneng 畢天能 and Ye Xian 葉憲, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Xiao Shijie 蕭世傑 and Gao Chen 高忱, and Assistant Regional Commander Chen Shizhong 陳世忠 assisted outside the curtain and managed affairs with diligence; Director of a Bureau in the Ministry of Justice Qian Xiru 錢錫汝, having arrived to review judicial cases, took pleasure in witnessing the completion of the event; Surveillance Vice Commissioner…

text:
湯仰僉事田應弼以擢任行
左參議馮子京副使張明正
署都指揮僉事佘胤以入
賀往皆始有勞者也法得竝書
湖廣荆州府公安縣儒學教
諭蔣遵烈謹序
punctuated:
湯仰、僉事田應弼以擢任行，左參議馮子京、副使張明正、署都指揮僉事佘胤以入賀往，皆始有勞者也，法得竝書。

湖廣荆州府公安縣儒學教諭蔣遵烈謹序。
translation_en:
… [Vice Commissioner] Tang Yang 湯仰 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Tian Yingbi 田應弼 departed upon being promoted to new posts; Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Feng Zijing 馮子京, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Mingzheng 張明正, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner She Yin 佘胤 departed to present congratulations at the court. All of them contributed their efforts at the beginning of the preparations, and by regulation their names may also be recorded together here.

Respectfully prefaced by Jiang Zunlie 蔣遵烈, Instructor of the Confucian School of Gong'an County 公安縣, Jingzhou Prefecture 荆州府, Huguang 湖廣.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰學而時習之不亦說乎
三者天下之達德也所以行之者一也
堯以不得舜爲己憂舜以不得禹臯陶爲
己憂夫以百畝之不易爲己憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠敎人以善謂之忠
爲天下得人者謂之仁
易
===
元者善之長也
上九鼎玉鉉大吉无不利
易无思也无爲也寂然不動感而遂通天
下之故非天下之至神其孰能與於此
有大而能謙必豫故受之以豫
書
后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏
德
以承上下神祇社稷宗廟罔不祗肅天監
punctuated:
第壹場
四書：
「子曰：『學而時習之，不亦說乎？』」
「三者，天下之達德也，所以行之者一也。」
「堯以不得舜爲己憂，舜以不得禹、臯陶爲己憂。夫以百畝之不易爲己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，敎人以善謂之忠，爲天下得人者謂之仁。」
易：
「元者，善之長也。」
「上九：鼎玉鉉，大吉，无不利。」
「《易》无思也，无爲也，寂然不動，感而遂通天下之故。非天下之至神，其孰能與於此？」
「有大而能謙必豫，故受之以《豫》。」
書：
「后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。」
「以承上下神祇、社稷、宗廟，罔不祗肅。天監
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books:
"The Master said: 'To learn and in due time practice what one has learned—is this not a pleasure?'" (Analects)
"These three are the universal virtues of the world, and that by which they are practiced is one." (Doctrine of the Mean)
"Yao made it his own anxiety not to find a Shun; Shun made it his own anxiety not to find a Yu and a Gao Yao. Now, he who makes it his own anxiety that his hundred mu of land are not well cultivated is a farmer. Giving wealth to others is called kindness; teaching others to be good is called loyalty; finding the right man for the world is called benevolence." (Mencius)

Book of Changes (Yi):
"Originating (yuan) is the chief of all goodness."
"Top Nine: The cauldron has rings of jade. Great good fortune; nothing that is not advantageous."
"The Changes has no thought and no action. Still and unmoving, when acted upon it penetrates all situations under heaven. If it were not the most wondrous thing under heaven, how could it take part in this?"
"Possessing greatness and yet being capable of modesty, there is sure to be joy; therefore it is followed by the hexagram Yu (Joy/Enthusiasm)."

Book of Documents (Shu):
"When the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of being a sovereign, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of being a minister, government will be well ordered, and the black-haired people will earnestly pursue virtue."
"To serve the spirits of heaven and earth above and below, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral庙 (temples), there was none to which he did not show reverent awe. Heaven surveyed…"

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
厥德用集大命撫綏萬方
君子所其無逸
同底于道道洽政治澤潤生民四夷左衽
罔不咸賴
詩
充耳琇瑩會弁如星
大人占之衆維魚矣實維豐年旐維旟矣
室家溱溱
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸墍
===
載見辟王曰求厥章
春秋
冬城向桓公十有六年齊師宋師曹師城
邢僖公元年
齊小白入于齊莊公九年公會齊人宋人
救鄭莊公二十有八年齊人救邢閔公
元年秋八月諸侯盟于首止僖公五年
九月戊辰諸侯盟于葵丘僖公九年
季子來歸閔公元年
punctuated:
厥德，用集大命，撫綏萬方。
君子所其無逸。
同底于道；道洽政治，澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。

《詩》：
充耳琇瑩，會弁如星。
大人占之：衆維魚矣，實維豐年；旐維旟矣，室家溱溱。
百辟卿士，媚于天子；不解于位，民之攸墍。
載見辟王，曰求厥章。

《春秋》：
冬，城向（桓公十有六年）。齊師、宋師、曹師城邢（僖公元年）。
齊小白入于齊（莊公九年）。公會齊人、宋人救鄭（莊公二十有八年）。齊人救邢（閔公元年）。秋八月，諸侯盟于首止（僖公五年）。九月戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘（僖公九年）。
季子來歸（閔公元年）。
translation_en:
…his virtue, and therefore caused the great Mandate to alight upon him, to soothe and pacify the myriad regions.
"The noble man makes 'taking no ease' his dwelling place."
"…together reach the Way. When the Way deeply permeates and governance is well-ordered, blessings moisten the living people, and among the four barbarian tribes who fold their robes to the left, there are none who do not depend on them."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"His ear-plugs are of fine, lustrous stones; the seams of his leather cap gleam like stars."
"The chief diviner interprets it: 'Swarms of locusts becoming fish—truly it will be a year of abundance; tortoise-and-snake banners becoming falcon banners—households and families will teem in multitudes.'"
"The hundred regional rulers and high ministers show loving devotion to the Son of Heaven; never lax in their positions, they bring rest to the people."
"Then they appear before their sovereign king, to seek from him their ceremonial regulations."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"In winter, [they] walled Xiang" (Duke Huan, 16th year). "The army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Cao walled Xing" (Duke Xi, 1st year).
"Xiaobai of Qi entered Qi" (Duke Zhuang, 9th year). "The Duke met with men of Qi and men of Song to rescue Zheng" (Duke Zhuang, 28th year). "Men of Qi rescued Xing" (Duke Min, 1st year). "In autumn, in the eighth month, the feudal lords made a covenant at Shouzhi" (Duke Xi, 5th year). "In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu" (Duke Xi, 9th year).
"Jizi returned" (Duke Min, 1st year).

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄

Record of Rites (Liji)
"When the five offices present their tribute, it is called offering (xiang)."
