title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
轉解官物
禁止迎送
優恤軍屬
修理倉庫
第參場
策五道
問帝王相傳必有心法堯以欽明配天舜
以溫恭協帝萬世治統自茲權輿嗣若
祗台日躋敬止敬義視欽恭之說無同
===
異而齋居決事帝範垂訓危竿之喻損
齋之記其視帝王之學有同否也我
聖祖開天立極締造之初
制為
皇明祖訓
貽謀萬世
資世通訓播告臣民及
精誠錄
觀心記見於儒臣所纂述者與堯舜之欽恭
punctuated:
轉解官物、禁止迎送、優恤軍屬、修理倉庫。

第參場
策五道

問：帝王相傳，必有心法。堯以欽明配天，舜以溫恭協帝，萬世治統，自茲權輿。嗣若祗台、日躋、敬止、敬義，視欽、恭之說，無同異？而齋居決事、《帝範》垂訓、危竿之喻、《損齋》之記，其視帝王之學，有同否也？我聖祖開天立極，締造之初，制為《皇明祖訓》，貽謀萬世；《資世通訓》，播告臣民；及《精誠錄》、《觀心記》見於儒臣所纂述者，與堯、舜之欽、恭…
translation_en:
…Forwarding Official Goods; Prohibiting Official Welcoming and Sending-off; Showing Compassion to Military Dependents; Repairing Granaries and Treasuries.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: In the transmission of authority from one sovereign to the next, there has always been a method of cultivating the mind. Yao matched Heaven through reverent illumination, and Shun harmonized with the Lord on High through gentle deference; the succession of governance for ten thousand generations had its origins right here. Later expressions such as "revering our virtue" (zhi yi), "daily ascending" (ri ji), "resting in reverence" (jing zhi), and "reverence and righteousness" (jing yi)—are there no similarities or differences when compared with the doctrines of "reverence" (qin) and "deference" (gong)? Moreover, as for deciding state affairs while residing in a hall of abstinence, handing down instructions in the Models for an Emperor (Difan), the metaphor of the precarious pole, and the "Record of the Studio of Diminishing" (Sunzhai ji)—how do these compare with the learning of the ancient emperors and kings: are they the same or not? When Our Sacred Ancestor opened up Heaven and established the supreme standard, at the very beginning of founding the dynasty, he formulated the Ancestral Injunctions of the August Ming (Huang Ming zuxun) to bequeath a plan for ten thousand generations, and the Comprehensive Instructions for Aiding the World (Zishi tongxun) to proclaim to officials and the common people; together with the Record of Utmost Sincerity (Jingcheng lu) and the Record of Observing the Mind (Guanxin ji) as seen in the compilations of Confucian officials—these and the reverence and deference of Yao and Shun…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
爲一轍矣可得而詳其實歟抑其指歸
固有在歟我
皇上
天縱英資
日新聖學
萬幾之暇
親灑宸翰一十二事
宣付史館
心法精純道化隆洽其與
===
聖祖之合德堯舜者將無後先媲美歟卽十二
事之中亦有其要歟夫誦
聖謨而揚厲儒生事也際
日中而獻曝藎臣志也其尚推本政源仰裨
聖治於萬一有司者將藉以
獻焉
問人君宰制羣動齊一天下者法也案法
治官人臣之義乃其說有不盡然者彼
東山之役兩觀之誅嚴而當矣而晉陽
punctuated:
爲一轍矣。可得而詳其實歟？抑其指歸固有在歟？我皇上天縱英資，日新聖學，萬幾之暇，親灑宸翰一十二事，宣付史館。心法精純，道化隆洽，其與聖祖之合德堯舜者，將無後先媲美歟？卽十二事之中，亦有其要歟？夫誦聖謨而揚厲，儒生事也；際日中而獻曝，藎臣志也。其尚推本政源，仰裨聖治於萬一，有司者將藉以獻焉。

問：人君宰制羣動、齊一天下者，法也；案法治官，人臣之義。乃其說有不盡然者。彼東山之役、兩觀之誅，嚴而當矣；而晉陽
translation_en:
…follow the exact same track. Can you set forth their substance in detail? Or is there indeed an underlying central purpose to which they point? Our Emperor is endowed by Heaven with heroic talents and daily renews his sagely learning. In his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he personally wielded the imperial brush to write out twelve maxims and had them proclaimed and delivered to the Historiography Institute. His method of the mind is pure and refined, and his moral transformation is flourishing and pervasive. Does he not rival in beauty, across past and present, the Sacred Ancestor in matching the virtue of Yao and Shun? And even among those twelve items, is there also an essential core? Now, to recite the sagely counsels and extol them is the business of Confucian scholars; to offer the warmth of the sun on one's back when meeting the midday sun is the aspiration of a loyal subject. May you trace the origins of governance to their root so as to aid His Majesty's sagely rule in some small measure; the authorities will rely upon your responses to present them to the throne.

Question: That by which a ruler governs the myriad activities and unifies the realm is the law; to regulate offices according to the law is the duty of a subject. Yet there are respects in which this doctrine does not wholly hold true. Look at the campaign to the Eastern Mountains [by the Duke of Zhou] and the execution beneath the twin watchtowers [by Confucius]—these were strict and yet fitting. Conversely, at Jinyang…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之不繕城郭鴈門之縱虜入犯勘河中
者矯制命按梁國者燒獄詞初令晋城
擅用庫錢而蒲鞭不施迄今稱循吏焉
是又法不可必行者歟犯蹕不刑盜噐
不族寬而當矣而街亭之按其故人富
平之繩及國士抑靈臺者忌殊功誅一
錢者持峻議彈壓京兆笑比河清而驚
破鬼膽迄今有能聲焉是又寬不可必
用者歟方今
===
皇綱震竦寓內乂安而宿賊巨猾尚多逋匿則
法固有未盡行者所當起而震之乃或
慮似是者之濫抑而法令愈密避者愈
巧焉將無俗尚積弛而不便於繩束之
具歟兹欲法令風行事功輻輳當有衷
論其試言之
問古者國有大事必合天下之議所以集
衆思而求至當也當今之務孰非諸士
所當料理然有重且急者焉
punctuated:
之不繕城郭，鴈門之縱虜入犯，勘河中者矯制命，按梁國者燒獄詞，初令晋城擅用庫錢，而蒲鞭不施，迄今稱循吏焉。是又法不可必行者歟？犯蹕不刑，盜噐不族，寬而當矣。而街亭之按其故人，富平之繩及國士，抑靈臺者忌殊功，誅一錢者持峻議，彈壓京兆，笑比河清，而驚破鬼膽，迄今有能聲焉。是又寬不可必用者歟？方今皇綱震竦，寓內乂安，而宿賊巨猾尚多逋匿，則法固有未盡行者，所當起而震之；乃或慮似是者之濫抑，而法令愈密，避者愈巧焉。將無俗尚積弛，而不便於繩束之具歟？兹欲法令風行，事功輻輳，當有衷論，其試言之。

問：古者國有大事，必合天下之議，所以集衆思而求至當也。當今之務，孰非諸士所當料理？然有重且急者焉。
translation_en:
… the failure to repair the city walls and ramparts at Jinyang, the allowing of the caitiffs to invade at Yanmen, the commissioner investigating Hezhong forging an imperial decree, the investigator of the kingdom of Liang burning the trial transcripts, and the newly appointed magistrate of Jincheng unauthorizedly using treasury funds—along with not even applying a cattail whip—have all been praised down to the present day as the acts of model officials. Does this mean that the law cannot necessarily be enforced in every case? Not executing someone for intruding upon the imperial procession and not exterminating the clan of someone who stole ritual vessels from the imperial temple were lenient and fitting. Yet prosecuting an old friend after Jieting, applying the full rigor of the law to a peerless talent of the state in Fuping, denying a portrait on the Lingtai terrace out of wariness of extraordinary merit, upholding a harsh sentence to execute someone over a single coin, and maintaining stern order in the Capital Prefecture—where the official's smile was compared to the clearing of the Yellow River and his presence struck terror into the hearts of ghosts—have all earned reputations for administrative capability down to the present day. Does this mean that leniency cannot necessarily be employed in every case? At present, the imperial authority inspires awe and the realm within the seas is peaceful and secure. Yet inveterate bandits and great scoundrels still frequently evade capture and hide away. Thus there are indeed areas where the law is not fully carried out, and we ought to rise up and enforce it with awe-inspiring vigor. However, some worry about the excessive suppression of those whose cases are ambiguous; meanwhile, the denser the laws and ordinances become, the more cunningly people evade them. Could it be that customs have long been lax and are ill-suited to the instruments of strict restraint? Now, if we wish for laws and ordinances to sweep through like the wind and for administrative achievements to converge like spokes at a hub, there must be a balanced discourse on the matter. Try to set it forth.

Question: In antiquity, whenever the state faced a great affair, it would invariably gather the deliberations of the entire realm, thereby collecting the thoughts of the multitude to seek the most fitting course of action. Among the affairs of the present day, which is not something that you gentlemen ought to manage and put in order? Yet there are some that are particularly weighty and urgent. …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
國家倚藉運河歲致數百萬石以實
京都近者漕河多梗直沽之運既不得行萊
泇二河又未竟緒則欲為乆安之策者
果安在歟
京師切近胡虜向苦繹騷乃今稽首款
貢九邊寧謐既數年矣而夷馬漸繁散處無
術豺狼難厭蹢躅可虞則欲為遠馭之
計者固有歸歟
天潢浩衍祿入不繼澤難斬於五世而情不
===
便於四業將何以通其窮也行伍空虛
寓內公患憲臣欲議罷遣而招募又慮
勞費將何以救其敝也諸生先天下之
憂其仰屋而借筯者有年矣願攄宿籌
以備經
國者採焉
問周之士貴秦之士賤其大較然矣然九
十而誇策事之壯一言而獲長子之封
亦周士也而引迹桃源懼有漁郎之問
punctuated:
國家倚藉運河，歲致數百萬石以實京都。近者漕河多梗，直沽之運既不得行，萊、泇二河又未竟緒，則欲為乆安之策者，果安在歟？京師切近胡虜，向苦繹騷，乃今稽首款貢，九邊寧謐，既數年矣；而夷馬漸繁，散處無術，豺狼難厭，蹢躅可虞，則欲為遠馭之計者，固有歸歟？天潢浩衍，祿入不繼，澤難斬於五世，而情不便於四業，將何以通其窮也？行伍空虛，寓內公患，憲臣欲議罷遣，而招募又慮勞費，將何以救其敝也？諸生先天下之憂，其仰屋而借筯者有年矣，願攄宿籌，以備經國者採焉。
問：周之士貴，秦之士賤，其大較然矣。然九十而誇策事之壯，一言而獲長子之封，亦周士也；而引迹桃源，懼有漁郎之問，
translation_en:
The state relies on the Grand Canal to deliver several million piculs of grain every year in order to supply the capital. Recently, the grain transport canal has suffered frequent blockages. Since coastal transport via Zhigu cannot be carried out, and work on the two canals at Jiaolai and the Jia River has not yet been brought to completion, where indeed does a policy for lasting security lie? The capital is in close proximity to the northern nomads and in the past suffered from their constant harassment. Now they bow their heads in submission to present tribute, and the Nine Frontier Defense Commands have been peaceful and tranquil for several years. Yet the tribute horses of the nomads are gradually multiplying and there is no good method for distributing them; wolves are hard to satiate, and their restless pacing is cause for concern. Is there indeed a settled conclusion for a plan of long-term control? The imperial clan has proliferated vastly, and revenue cannot keep pace with their stipends. While it is difficult to cut off the dynasty's grace after five generations, practical sentiment makes it inconvenient to allow them to pursue the four common occupations—how, then, are we to relieve their predicament? The depletion of the military ranks is a common affliction throughout the empire. Censorial officials wish to deliberate on disbanding and sending away superfluous troops, yet when it comes to recruiting new soldiers, they worry about the toil and expense—how, then, are we to remedy this abuse? You students worry before the rest of the world worries; for years you have gazed at the ceiling in thought and borrowed chopsticks to devise plans. We hope you will set forth your long-held strategies so that those who govern the state may select from them.

Question: That scholars of the Zhou were noble and scholars of the Qin were base is true in broad outline. Yet the one who at ninety boasted of his vigor in devising stratagems, and the one who with a single word won enfeoffment at Zhangzi, were also scholars of the Zhou; whereas those who withdrew their tracks to Peach Blossom Spring for fear of inquiries from the fisherman, …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
殉義海島不忘宗國之思不幾於貴乎
繄是而商山一出計安國本隆中三顧
卒成鼎峙此勳伐砥於廉隅也然脫穎
自薦一言定從杖策投歸雲臺首烈而
布衣獻策者卒不負佳士之許焉何磊
磊者亦足以集事乎締黨叔文自隕令
緒河陽獻策貽譏士紳此芳猷隳於瓦
合也然孝廉强起樹建萎然深源一出
蒼生失望而素負時名者卒無救於陳
===
===
濤之辱焉將表表者無益於人國乎方
今振勵士風標表節行愼選精覈無遺計矣
然未聞士習丕變而材諝日充何歟抑
當有推而廣之者歟幸言之以觀志學
廣賢路焉
問洪範八政食貨爲先周官一書經畫具
備後世用之鮮有成績豈古今之異宜
乎彼積儲楮幣其議詳於食貨志而或
通輕重或權子母或善平糴或置均輸
punctuated:
殉義海島，不忘宗國之思，不幾於貴乎？繄是而商山一出，計安國本；隆中三顧，卒成鼎峙：此勳伐砥於廉隅也。然脫穎自薦，一言定從；杖策投歸，雲臺首烈；而布衣獻策者，卒不負佳士之許焉。何磊磊者亦足以集事乎？締黨叔文，自隕令緒；河陽獻策，貽譏士紳：此芳猷隳於瓦合也。然孝廉强起，樹建萎然；深源一出，蒼生失望；而素負時名者，卒無救於陳濤之辱焉。將表表者無益於人國乎？方今振勵士風，標表節行，愼選精覈，無遺計矣。然未聞士習丕變，而材諝日充，何歟？抑當有推而廣之者歟？幸言之，以觀志學、廣賢路焉。
問：《洪範》八政，食貨爲先；《周官》一書，經畫具備。後世用之，鮮有成績，豈古今之異宜乎？彼積儲、楮幣，其議詳於《食貨志》，而或通輕重，或權子母，或善平糴，或置均輸，
translation_en:
…and dying for righteousness on a sea island without forgetting longing for one's ancestral state—do these not come close to being noble? Following this, emerging once from Mount Shang to devise a plan that secured the foundation of the state, and receiving three visits at Longzhong to ultimately achieve the tripartite balance of power—these were cases where meritorious achievements were honed by moral integrity. Yet recommending oneself like an awl's point poking through a bag and sealing an alliance with a single word; leaning on a riding whip to pledge allegiance and ranking first in merit on the Cloud Terrace (Yuntai); and presenting strategies as a commoner while ultimately living up to the praise of being a fine scholar—how is it that such uninhibited figures were also able to accomplish great deeds? Forming a faction with Shuwen (Wang Shuwen 王叔文) and thereby ruining one's own fine reputation, or presenting strategies at Heyang and drawing ridicule from the literati and gentry—these were cases where fragrant counsels were destroyed by base association. Yet when a Filial and Incorrupt (xiaolian) nominee was compelled to take office, his accomplishments were withered; when Shenyuan (Yin Hao 殷浩, courtesy name Shenyuan) emerged from retirement, the common people were disappointed; and one who had long borne contemporary renown ultimately could not prevent the humiliation at Chentao—could it be that men ofoutstanding reputation are of no benefit to a state? At present, the ethos of the literati is being roused and encouraged, moral integrity and conduct are being honored and displayed, and careful selection and precise verification leave no measure overlooked. Yet we have not heard that the customs of the literati have undergone a great transformation or that men of talent and wisdom are daily becoming more abundant—why is this? Or is there something that ought to be extended and broadened? Pray speak on this, so that we may observe your aspirations and learning and broaden the path for the worthy.

Question: Among the Eight政 (Eight Goverances) of the "Great Plan" (Hongfan), food and commodities come first; in the book of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), administrative plans are completely provided. When later ages applied them, they rarely achieved success—could it be that what is appropriate differs between ancient and modern times? Those discussions of grain storage and paper currency are detailed in the "Treatise on Food and Money" (Shihuo zhi); and whether circulating light and heavy coins, weighing mother and child denominations, excelling at the equitable purchase of grain (pingdi), or establishing equitable delivery (junshu)…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
此甲彼乙莫能相尚其法果孰便與漢
臣謂順民心而所補者三除博禍而致
福者七其言當歟滇境環圍壘嶂舟楫
不通歲入僅給饔飧稍旱則穀價踊貴
且帑藏空虛物力胥竭緩急之際司計
者詘策焉頃者積粟屢課鑄錢有
令
德意固甚渥也然設義倉則本貲無厝貯官庾
則浥腐難堪積粟之法將何道而可久
===
也銅本滇產冶鑄甚易顧銅廣則私鑄
之徒易於作姦而俗乆用貝卒難變更
且慮夷民搖惑焉變通之法果安在歟
夫食土之毛必灼利弊茲欲積粟鑄錢
使官民胥給遠追成周之盛諸生固有
慨於中者願悉所見以對
punctuated: 此甲彼乙，莫能相尚，其法果孰便與？漢臣謂「順民心而所補者三」、「除博禍而致福者七」，其言當歟？滇境環圍壘嶂，舟楫不通，歲入僅給饔飧，稍旱則穀價踊貴。且帑藏空虛，物力胥竭，緩急之際，司計者詘策焉。頃者，積粟屢課，鑄錢有令，德意固甚渥也。然設義倉則本貲無厝，貯官庾則浥腐難堪，積粟之法，將何道而可久也？銅本滇產，冶鑄甚易，顧銅廣則私鑄之徒易於作姦，而俗乆用貝，卒難變更，且慮夷民搖惑焉，變通之法，果安在歟？夫食土之毛，必灼利弊。茲欲積粟鑄錢，使官民胥給，遠追成周之盛，諸生固有慨於中者，願悉所見以對。
translation_en:
… With one favoring this and another favoring that, none able to surpass the others, which of these methods is truly the most convenient? Han dynasty officials spoke of "complying with the people's hearts and thereby remedying three things" and "eliminating widespread calamities and thereby bringing about seven blessings"—were their words fitting?

The territory of Yunnan (Dian 滇) is ringed by layered mountain peaks and cannot be reached by boat; its annual revenues barely suffice for daily meals, and at the slightest drought the price of grain leaps upward. Moreover, the state treasuries are empty and material resources are altogether exhausted; in times of emergency, those in charge of fiscal planning are at their wits' end for a policy. Recently, storing up grain has been repeatedly assessed and an order has been issued for minting coins—His Majesty's benevolent intentions are certainly most generous. Yet if charity granaries (yicang 義倉) are established, there is nowhere to raise the initial capital; if grain is stored in official granaries, the dampness and rot are hard to bear. By what way, then, can the method of storing grain be made enduring? Copper is native to Yunnan, so smelting and casting are very easy. However, because copper is abundant, illicit minters can easily engage in fraud; furthermore, local custom has long used cowrie shells (bei 貝), which cannot be suddenly changed, and there is the added worry that the indigenous peoples and commoners may be unsettled and confused. Where, indeed, does the method for flexible adaptation lie?

Those who eat the produce of this land must surely have a clear understanding of its advantages and disadvantages. Now we wish to store grain and mint coins so that officials and the common people are both supplied, emulating from afar the flourishing age of the Zhou dynasty. You students surely have deep feelings about this within you; I hope you will set forth all your views in reply.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰學而時習之不亦說乎
楊應兆
同考試官學正梁批典雅冲淡理意渾然蓋有心
得者允宜首錄
考試官敎諭劉批不落塵筌詞藻自麗
考試官敎諭蔣批鎔意鑄詞極為密緻
聖人首著心得之學亦在乎熟之而已矣夫學
===
求有得於心也所學者熟而心有不自得哉此
萬世道學之原也夫子揭以示人若曰人心通
乎太虛未有不說於道者也惟不學則不知道
而學之未熟則苦難而弗說矣誠知人不可以
不學也而仰法前脩以為進趨之準知學之不
可以已也而遜志時敏以勤服習之功習其所
知而明善之學時亹亹焉將求通於性命而瞬
息之無間也習其所行而誠身之學時汲汲焉
將求進於聖神而動息之有養也夫向往旣專
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

「子曰：『學而時習之，不亦說乎？』」

楊應兆

同考試官學正梁批：典雅冲淡，理意渾然，蓋有心得者，允宜首錄。
考試官敎諭劉批：不落塵筌，詞藻自麗。
考試官敎諭蔣批：鎔意鑄詞，極為密緻。

聖人首著心得之學，亦在乎熟之而已矣。夫學，求有得於心也；所學者熟，而心有不自得哉？此萬世道學之原也，夫子揭以示人，若曰：人心通乎太虛，未有不說於道者也；惟不學則不知道，而學之未熟，則苦難而弗說矣。誠知人不可以不學也，而仰法前脩，以為進趨之準；知學之不可以已也，而遜志時敏，以勤服習之功。習其所知，而明善之學時亹亹焉，將求通於性命，而瞬息之無間也；習其所行，而誠身之學時汲汲焉，將求進於聖神，而動息之有養也。夫向往旣專，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: "To learn and in due time to practice what one has learned—is this not a pleasure?"

Yang Yingzhao 楊應兆

Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Liang 梁: Classically elegant and serenely unpretentious, its principle and meaning form a seamless whole. Clearly written by one who has attained genuine personal realization, it truly deserves to be recorded in first place.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Liu 劉: Free of worldly clichés, its diction is naturally beautiful.
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Jiang 蔣: In smelting ideas and casting phrases, it is extremely tight and refined.

When the Sage first sets forth the learning of personal realization in the mind, it lies simply in bringing it to maturity through familiarity. Now, learning seeks to attain something within the mind; when what one learns has become familiar and mature, how could the mind fail to find satisfaction in itself? This is the source of the Learning of the Way for ten thousand generations. The Master held it up to show to others, as if to say: The human mind communicates with the Great Void, and there is no one who does not take pleasure in the Way. Only, if one does not learn, one does not know the Way; and if one's learning has not yet reached familiarity, one suffers from its difficulty and finds no pleasure in it. If one truly knows that a person cannot do without learning, and looks up to emulate the worthy predecessors as the standard for one's advance and pursuit; and if one knows that learning cannot be broken off, and keeps a humble will while being constantly diligent, working hard at the effort of practice and repetition—practicing what one knows, so that the learning of illuminating goodness is at all times tireless, seeking to penetrate human nature and Heaven's mandate without a single moment's interruption; and practicing what one does, so that the learning of making the person sincere is at all times unremitting, seeking to advance toward the realm of the sagely and spiritual while maintaining cultivation in both activity and rest. Now, once one's aspiration and direction are focused,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
則精神自聚而喜意爲之潛滋積習有常則旨
趣自通而天機爲之渙發知以涵泳而熟焉性
命一源不苦於扞格也愈精明則愈融液固獨
覺其妙而不能言者乎行以敦篤而熟焉神聖
一心不苦於矜持也愈進脩則愈浹洽固自得
其趣而不能已者乎是學非外於心也所以還
吾順適之眞也說非離於學也所以要吾敏學
之趣也以之錫類而所說不孤以之貞遇而所
說不改斯其爲天下之全學也豈或作或輟者
===
可與幾哉彼耳順從心吾夫子蓋得乎說之妙
者而其敏求發憤必至於七十而始化焉是聖
人固自志學以至終身而始要其成矣天縱生
知其功如此則說心之妙豈易言哉噫竭才立
卓顏其幾矣而願息之請亦爲聖人之徒焉此
時習之學夫子所以首垂訓也
三者天下之達德也所以行之者一也
楊同春
同考試官教諭徐 批 只用本色語而旨趣雋永可
punctuated:
則精神自聚，而喜意爲之潛滋；積習有常，則旨趣自通，而天機爲之渙發。知以涵泳而熟焉，性命一源，不苦於扞格也；愈精明則愈融液，固獨覺其妙而不能言者乎？行以敦篤而熟焉，神聖一心，不苦於矜持也；愈進脩則愈浹洽，固自得其趣而不能已者乎？是學非外於心也，所以還吾順適之眞也；說非離於學也，所以要吾敏學之趣也。以之錫類而所說不孤，以之貞遇而所說不改，斯其爲天下之全學也，豈或作或輟者可與幾哉？彼耳順從心，吾夫子蓋得乎說之妙者，而其敏求發憤，必至於七十而始化焉。是聖人固自志學以至終身，而始要其成矣。天縱生知，其功如此，則說心之妙豈易言哉？噫！竭才立卓，顏其幾矣，而願息之請，亦爲聖人之徒焉。此時習之學，夫子所以首垂訓也。
「三者天下之達德也，所以行之者一也。」
楊同春
同考試官教諭徐批：只用本色語而旨趣雋永，可愛，佳士也，錄之。
translation_en:
…then the spirit naturally gathers, and a feeling of joy quietly grows because of it; when accumulated practice is constant, the underlying meaning and flavor naturally become clear, and the heavenly mechanism bursts forth because of it. When knowledge becomes ripe through immersion and contemplation, human nature and Heaven's mandate are seen as a single source, and one does not suffer from resistance or obstruction; the more lucid it becomes, the more thoroughly it blends and dissolves—is this not indeed perceiving its subtlety alone without being able to put it into words? When action becomes ripe through earnestness and sincerity, the spiritual and the sage are of one mind, and one does not suffer from forced restraint; the more one advances in self-cultivation, the more thoroughly one is steeped in harmony—is this not indeed attaining its zest for oneself without being able to stop? Thus learning is not external to the mind; it is the means to restore our true state of ease and contentment. Joy is not separate from learning; it is the means to secure the zest of our diligent study. When through it one extends goodness to one's kind [when friends come from afar], what one delights in is not solitary; when through it one remains steadfast in adversity [when others do not recognize one], what one delights in does not change. This is what constitutes the complete learning of the world—how could those who work by fits and starts ever come close to it? As for having an obedient ear at sixty and following the heart's desires at seventy, our Master indeed attained the subtlety of joy, yet in his diligent seeking and eager enthusiasm, it was necessary to reach seventy before achieving complete transformation. Thus the sage surely began from setting his heart on learning and continued to the end of his life before bringing it to completion. If for one whom Heaven endowed with innate knowledge the effort was like this, how can the subtlety of a joyous mind be easily spoken of? Alas! Exhausting his talent before what stood towering above, Yan Hui came close to it; yet he who asked to rest [Zigong] was also a disciple of the sage. This learning of constant practice is why the Master handed it down as his very first teaching.

"These three are the universal virtues of the world, and the means by which they are practiced is one."
Yang Tongchun 楊同春
Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐 comments: He uses only plain, natural language, yet the meaning and flavor are rich and enduring—delightful… A fine scholar; I select it…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
愛佳士也錄之
考試官教諭劉批認理精深一洗俗調
考試官教諭蔣批大雅之文可式多士
中庸指德之爲達而約之於誠焉夫誠者德之
精也德通天下而非誠其何以行之哉夫子以
此進魯君若曰治固貴乎敦本道必先於存誠
明於道德之原而脩身立政者裕如矣彼達道
有五而三德行之智仁勇是也之三者賦出維
皇而明通公溥皆其本然之懿善緣民秉而剛
===
健貞固乃其各足之良達之一世之天下此心
同則此德同蓋自眞精妙合之初不以聖愚爲
厚薄也達之萬世之天下均是性則均是德蓋
自理氣凝成之後不以古今爲異同也夫是之
謂達德也以此三者行此五者其惟一誠乎蓋
至理惟一則不虛而貫徹乎綱常者本無僞妄
之間人心惟一則不雜而經綸乎物則者自妙
推行之通統三德於一誠則心精之內裕固粹
然其無疵焉心爲實心道有所據而自凝矣其
punctuated:
愛，佳士也，錄之。
考試官教諭劉批：認理精深，一洗俗調。
考試官教諭蔣批：大雅之文，可式多士。
《中庸》指德之爲達，而約之於誠焉。夫誠者，德之精也。德通天下，而非誠，其何以行之哉？夫子以此進魯君，若曰：治固貴乎敦本，道必先於存誠，明於道德之原，而脩身立政者裕如矣。彼達道有五，而三德行之，智、仁、勇是也。之三者，賦出維皇，而明通公溥，皆其本然之懿；善緣民秉，而剛健貞固，乃其各足之良。達之一世之天下，此心同則此德同，蓋自眞精妙合之初，不以聖愚爲厚薄也；達之萬世之天下，均是性則均是德，蓋自理氣凝成之後，不以古今爲異同也。夫是之謂達德也。以此三者行此五者，其惟一誠乎！蓋至理惟一則不虛，而貫徹乎綱常者，本無僞妄之間；人心惟一則不雜，而經綸乎物則者，自妙推行之通。統三德於一誠，則心精之內裕，固粹然其無疵焉；心爲實心，道有所據而自凝矣，其…
translation_en:
… lovable; he is a fine scholar. Record it.
Examiner Instructor Liu劉 comments: His grasp of principle is refined and profound, completely washing away vulgar conventions.
Examiner Instructor Jiang蔣 comments: Writing of great elegance that can serve as a model for the many scholars.
The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) points out that these virtues are universal, and reduces them to sincerity (cheng). Now, sincerity is the essence of virtue. Although virtue extends throughout all under Heaven, without sincerity, how could it be practiced? The Master presented this to the ruler of Lu, as if to say: Governance surely values strengthening the root, and the Way must begin with preserving sincerity; once one is clear about the source of the Way and of virtue, cultivating the person and establishing governance will be effortlessly ample. Those universal Ways are five, and three virtues put them into practice: wisdom, benevolence, and courage. These three are endowed by the August Heaven, so that illumination, penetration, impartiality, and universality are all their inherent excellence; goodness follows from what the people hold fast, so that firmness, vigor, rectitude, and steadfastness are the innate goodness sufficient in each person. Extended across all under Heaven in a single generation, because this mind is the same, this virtue is the same—for from the very beginning when the true and subtle essences wonderfully combined, it is not made thicker or thinner according to whether one is a sage or a simpleton. Extended across all under Heaven for ten thousand generations, because the nature is shared equally, the virtue is shared equally—for once principle and vital force have coalesced and taken form, it does not differ between antiquity and the present. This is what is meant by "universal virtues." To practice those five by means of these three—does it not lie solely in a single sincerity! For when the ultimate principle is one, it is not empty, and what penetrates the three bonds and five constant virtues originally has no falsity or delusion mixed into it; when the human mind is one, it is not adulterated, and what orders the patterns of things naturally achieves the wondrous通 [fluency/comprehension] of putting them into practice. When the three virtues are unified in a single sincerity, the inner abundance of the mind's essence is indeed pure and without flaw; the mind becomes a real mind, and the Way has something to rely upon and naturally consolidates itself. Is this not…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天秩之所以敘乎運一誠於三德則性真之流
行固渾然其無累焉行為實行理有所依而自
立矣其人紀之所以脩乎是一以函三則心極
純而德備三以行五則身極建而道脩文武之
止信惇信以立人極者胥此耳公其勉之哉雖
然誠者天德之精非徒真妄錯雜不足以立德
而擇善固執之際少有意念之牿焉亦非聖人
純懿之學矣況魯公之實不足成者而能慰夫
子東周之望乎彼外施仁義固不足效唐虞而
===
執實御虛則亦術數之學耳而又何責於公也
噫王道本於誠意信哉
堯以不得舜為已憂舜以不得禹皐陶為
已憂夫以百畝之不易為已憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠教人以善謂之忠
為天下得人者謂之仁
傅爾珍
同考試官教諭毛批此題頭緒頗多作之獨無痕
跡且氣𧹞訓雅足覘邃學允宜高薦
punctuated:
天秩之所以敘乎！運一誠於三德，則性真之流行，固渾然其無累焉。行為實行，理有所依而自立矣，其人紀之所以脩乎！是一以函三，則心極純而德備；三以行五，則身極建而道脩。文、武之止信、惇信以立人極者，胥此耳，公其勉之哉！雖然，誠者天德之精，非徒真妄錯雜不足以立德，而擇善固執之際，少有意念之牿焉，亦非聖人純懿之學矣。況魯公之實不足成者，而能慰夫子東周之望乎？彼外施仁義，固不足效唐、虞，而執實御虛，則亦術數之學耳，而又何責於公也！噫！王道本於誠意，信哉！

堯以不得舜為已憂，舜以不得禹、皐陶為已憂。夫以百畝之不易為已憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠，為天下得人者謂之仁。

傅爾珍

同考試官教諭毛批：此題頭緒頗多，作之獨無痕跡，且氣𧹞訓雅，足覘邃學，允宜高薦。
translation_en:
…whereby the heavenly order is set in array! When one exercises a single sincerity through the three virtues, the flowing forth of the true nature is indeed whole and unencumbered; one's actions are genuine actions, and principle has that upon which to rely and establish itself—is this not whereby the human bounds are cultivated! Thus, when the one encompasses the three, the supreme standard of the mind is pure and virtue is complete; when the three are used to put the five into practice, the supreme standard of the person is established and the Way is cultivated. That by which Kings Wen and Wu abided in trustworthiness and esteemed trustworthiness so as to establish the supreme standard of humanity was altogether nothing other than this. May the Duke strive at it! Even so, sincerity is the essence of heavenly virtue. Not only is a mixture of truth and falsity insufficient to establish virtue, but in choosing the good and holding fast to it, if there is the slightest fettering of intent and thought, it is likewise not the pure and admirable learning of the sages. How much less could the Duke of Lu, whose genuineness was insufficient to bring things to completion, fulfill the Master's hope for an Eastern Zhou? Those who outwardly display benevolence and righteousness are certainly inadequate to emulate Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], while those who grasp reality to control emptiness practice merely the learning of statecraft and calculation—and what more could one demand of the Duke! Alas! Truly, the Kingly Way is rooted in making the intentions sincere!

"Yao took not getting Shun as his own worry; Shun took not getting Yu and Gao Yao as his own worry. Now, he who takes the failure to till his hundred mu as his own worry is a farmer. Sharing wealth with others is called kindness; teaching others to be good is called loyalty; getting worthy men for the Empire is called benevolence."

By Fu Erzhen 傅爾珍.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Mao: This topic has quite a few threads, yet this composition alone shows no artificial traces. Moreover, its vital force is vigorous [?] and its diction refined, which suffices to reveal profound learning. It truly deserves a high recommendation.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉批精瑩老練迥異諸作
考試官教諭蔣批意高詞古一結尤精
觀聖君憂在得賢而其仁天下者大矣夫賢者
人君之所寄以仁天下者也聖君之憂所以必
先其大乎且夫帝王以身任君師之責其心於
天下者無窮也然有不能必爲之勢焉惟得人
以寄其心而已彼堯欲仁有唐之天下其可憂
者多矣然而堯不憂也憂不得舜而已惟得舜
而其心始慰焉舜欲仁有虞之天下其可憂者
===
多矣然而舜不憂也憂不得禹皐陶而已惟得
禹皐陶而其心始慰焉若夫百畝不易農夫之
憂耳而豈堯舜之所以爲憂乎夫聖人所憂之
大若此而不可以知其仁天下之大者哉蓋財
爲民命自我分之惠矣而不足以盡利也善爲
民性自我教之忠矣而不足以盡神也惟夫爲
天下得人者以司導利之寄則養賢及民輔吾
力之不及天下被容保之仁而不知其爲惠也
豈若小惠之未徧哉以托綏猷之任則得賢弘
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉批：精瑩老練，迥異諸作。
考試官教諭蔣批：意高詞古，一結尤精。
觀聖君憂在得賢，而其仁天下者大矣。夫賢者，人君之所寄以仁天下者也；聖君之憂，所以必先其大乎！且夫帝王以身任君師之責，其心於天下者無窮也；然有不能必爲之勢焉，惟得人以寄其心而已。彼堯欲仁有唐之天下，其可憂者多矣，然而堯不憂也，憂不得舜而已；惟得舜，而其心始慰焉。舜欲仁有虞之天下，其可憂者多矣，然而舜不憂也，憂不得禹、皐陶而已；惟得禹、皐陶，而其心始慰焉。若夫百畝不易，農夫之憂耳，而豈堯、舜之所以爲憂乎？夫聖人所憂之大若此，而不可以知其仁天下之大者哉！蓋財爲民命，自我分之，惠矣，而不足以盡利也；善爲民性，自我教之，忠矣，而不足以盡神也。惟夫爲天下得人者，以司導利之寄，則養賢及民，輔吾力之不及，天下被容保之仁，而不知其爲惠也，豈若小惠之未徧哉？以托綏猷之任，則得賢弘…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: Refined, lucid, and seasoned; markedly different from the other compositions.

Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: Lofty in conception and archaic in diction; the concluding passage is especially fine.

When we observe that the sage rulers' concern lay in finding worthy men, we see how great was their benevolence toward the world. Now, worthy men are those upon whom a ruler relies to extend benevolence to the world; is this not why the concern of sage rulers must first address what is great? Moreover, when emperors and kings personally assume the responsibilities of both ruler and teacher, their concern for the world is boundless; yet by the nature of their position they cannot do everything themselves, and can only find the right men in whom to entrust their intentions. When Yao wished to bring benevolence to the world of Tang, there were many things worthy of concern, yet Yao did not worry about them; his only concern was not finding Shun, and only upon finding Shun was his heart set at ease. When Shun wished to bring benevolence to the world of Yu, there were many things worthy of concern, yet Shun did not worry about them; his only concern was not finding Yu and Gao Yao, and only upon finding Yu and Gao Yao was his heart set at ease. As for a hundred mu of land not being properly tilled, that is merely the concern of a farmer—how could that be what Yao and Shun took as their concern? Since what the sages worried about was as great as this, can one not know from it the greatness of their benevolence toward the world? For wealth is the lifeblood of the people: if I distribute it myself, that is kindness, yet it is insufficient to exhaust all benefit. Goodness is the nature of the people: if I teach it myself, that is devotion, yet it is insufficient to exhaust the transformative spirit. Only one who finds men for the world—by charging them with the trust of guiding benefits—nurtures the worthy so as to reach the people, supplementing what my own strength cannot reach, so that the world receives the benevolence of tolerant protection without even knowing it as kindness; how could this be like petty kindnesses that fail to reach everyone? And by entrusting them with the duty of tranquil governance, one obtains the worthy to broaden…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
化濟吾道之所同天下被錫類之仁而忘其所
以教也豈若徒忠之未孚哉故禹皐之仁卽舜
之仁也舜之仁卽堯之仁也惟其仁之大是以
憂之急而又何容於耕乎吁充並耕之說不過
分財教善之意而其術且窮矣雖然聖人憂在
得賢則岳牧羣工皆其所急而獨憂不得舜禹
皐者爲重端揆之任也蓋端揆得人則衆職咸
舉玄德升聞而元愷彙進其機之類應固如此
噫親賢之中有先務焉仁天下者法堯舜而已
===
易
元者善之長也
傅爾珍
同考試官教諭毛批 通篇發揮元德不著色相而
理意充然可掬蓋大手筆也
考試官教諭劉批 筆力遒勁文采爛然
考試官教諭蔣批 意正詞腴可以式矣
文言於乾德之元而著其統天下之善焉夫元
固天德之大始也自人具之而天下之善不統
punctuated:
化，濟吾道之所同，天下被錫類之仁，而忘其所以教也，豈若徒忠之未孚哉？故禹、皐之仁，卽舜之仁也；舜之仁，卽堯之仁也。惟其仁之大，是以憂之急，而又何容於耕乎？吁！充並耕之說，不過分財、教善之意，而其術且窮矣。雖然，聖人憂在得賢，則岳、牧、羣工皆其所急，而獨憂不得舜、禹、皐者，爲重端揆之任也。蓋端揆得人，則衆職咸舉；玄德升聞，而元、愷彙進，其機之類應固如此。噫！親賢之中有先務焉，仁天下者法堯、舜而已。
易
「元者善之長也。」
傅爾珍
同考試官教諭毛批：通篇發揮元德，不著色相，而理意充然可掬，蓋大手筆也。
考試官教諭劉批：筆力遒勁，文采爛然。
考試官教諭蔣批：意正詞腴，可以式矣。
《文言》於乾德之元，而著其統天下之善焉。夫元固天德之大始也，自人具之，而天下之善不統
translation_en:
… transformation, aiding what our Way holds in common; the world receives the benevolence that bestows blessings on one's kind and forgets the means by which it was taught. How could this be like mere personal devotion that has not yet won trust? Therefore, the benevolence of Yu and Gao Yao is none other than the benevolence of Shun, and the benevolence of Shun is none other than the benevolence of Yao. Precisely because their benevolence was so great, their anxiety was so urgent—what room, then, could there be for plowing? Alas! Even if one carries the doctrine of ruler and subject plowing together to its fullest extent, it amounts to no more than the idea of dividing wealth and teaching goodness in person, and as a method it would soon be exhausted. Even so, since the sages' anxiety lay in finding worthy men, the Four Mountains, the Twelve Pastors, and all the officials were their urgent concern; yet that they worried solely about not finding a Shun, a Yu, or a Gao Yao was because they attached supreme weight to the office of the chief minister. For when the right man is found for the chief ministership, all the other offices are Thereby upheld: when hidden virtue rises to be heard above, the Eight Worthies (Baryuan) and Eight Harmonies (Bakai) advance together as a class—such is naturally the sympathetic response of the mechanism of governance. Ah! Even within the duty ofingeing close to the worthy, there is a foremost priority; he who would bring benevolence to the world need only model himself on Yao and Shun.

The Book of Changes (Yi)
"Originating (yuan) is the chief of all goodness."
Fu Erzhen
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Mao: The entire essay elaborates on the virtue of Originating (yuan) without clinging to superficial forms, yet its principle and meaning are so full they can almost be scooped up in the hands—truly the work of a master hand.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Liu: The brushwork is vigorous and powerful, its literary brilliance resplendent.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Jiang: The thought is orthodox and the diction rich; it can serve as a model.

The "Words on the Text" (Wenyan) commentary, in speaking of "Originating" (yuan) among the virtues of the Creative (Qian), sets forth how it encompasses and governs all the goodness in the world. Now, Originating is indeed the great beginning of Heaven's virtue; once human beings are endowed with it, is not all the goodness in the world encompassed…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
於是乎昔文言之意若曰天之有元也造化由
之以綱維羣生由之以立命夫固爲天德之首
矣而其在人也何如蓋天生萬物而元始之則
吾人得之於賦予者惟此理爲最先天有四德
而元統之則吾人受之爲秉彝者惟此善爲至
大故繼善之後萬理咸備而一元之根於太始
者實有以開萬理之原成性之中衆善悉有而
一元之通乎太極者實有以主衆善之妙秩之
爲五常善固各有定體也而肫肫懇至之意聯
===
貫於其中者爲能兼總而不遺焉維皇降衷之
懿玆其莫之與京者矣散之爲百行善固不可
勝用也而生生不息之理渾融於其內者爲能
宰制而無外焉上帝賦畀之良玆其莫之與竝
者矣要之未有物先則是元爲天地莫先之德
既有物後則是元爲人心統體之全天下固未
有一善而不統於元亦未有外元而可以爲善
者也不謂善之長而何哉吁元之在人其大若
此故聖人得之爲首出庶物之資體之爲克長
punctuated: 於是乎？昔《文言》之意若曰：天之有元也，造化由之以綱維，羣生由之以立命，夫固爲天德之首矣。而其在人也何如？蓋天生萬物而元始之，則吾人得之於賦予者，惟此理爲最先；天有四德而元統之，則吾人受之爲秉彝者，惟此善爲至大。故繼善之後，萬理咸備，而一元之根於太始者，實有以開萬理之原；成性之中，衆善悉有，而一元之通乎太極者，實有以主衆善之妙。秩之爲五常，善固各有定體也，而肫肫懇至之意聯貫於其中者，爲能兼總而不遺焉；維皇降衷之懿，玆其莫之與京者矣。散之爲百行，善固不可勝用也，而生生不息之理渾融於其內者，爲能宰制而無外焉；上帝賦畀之良，玆其莫之與竝者矣。要之，未有物先，則是元爲天地莫先之德；既有物後，則是元爲人心統體之全。天下固未有一善而不統於元，亦未有外元而可以爲善者也。不謂善之長而何哉？吁！元之在人，其大若此。故聖人得之爲首出庶物之資，體之爲克長…
translation_en: …unified under it? Of old, the meaning of the "Commentary on the Words of the Text" (Wenyan) was as if to say: Heaven possesses origination (yuan), through which creative transformation maintains its overarching order and the multitude of living things establish their destiny; thus it is assuredly the foremost of Heaven's virtues. Yet how does it manifest within humanity? Now, Heaven gives birth to the myriad things and origination initiates them; therefore, in what we humans receive from Heaven's endowment, this principle alone comes first. Heaven possesses four virtues and origination encompasses them; therefore, in what we humans receive as our constant moral nature, this goodness alone is the greatest. Thus, after the succession of goodness, all the myriad principles are fully present, and the single origination rooted in the Great Beginning truly opens up the source of the myriad principles; within the completed nature, all forms of goodness are wholly contained, and the single origination that communes with the Supreme Ultimate truly presides over the subtlety of all forms of goodness. Ordered into the Five Constant Virtues, each goodness indeed has its definite substance, yet the earnest and sincere intent that threads through them is able to encompass and unite them all without omission—among the splendors of the moral sense sent down by the August One, nothing can rival this! Dispersed into the hundred conducts, goodness is indeed inexhaustible in its application, yet the principle of ceaseless generation that blends harmoniously within them is able to govern them with nothing left outside—among the innate goodnesses endowed by the Lord on High, nothing can stand as an equal to this! In sum, before anything exists, this origination is the virtue of Heaven and Earth that nothing precedes; after things have come into existence, this origination is the complete, unified totality of the human mind. In all the world, there is assuredly no single goodness that is not encompassed by origination, nor is there anything outside of origination that can be counted as goodness. If we do not call it the chief of all goodness, what else could it be? Ah! Such is the greatness of origination as it exists within humanity. Therefore, the sage attains it as the resource by which he rises preeminent above the multitude of things, and embodies it as the Way of being able to serve as a leader…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
克君之道者亦惟一元而已乾元之大至是其
無餘蘊乎雖然人君法天致治體元爲先而所
以會乎元德之精者惟學而已蓋天以元運而
神功昭心以學純而天德粹故如天好生萬古
稱元良焉其精一之學可想也噫體元者當懋
於學而調元者其亦加之意乎
有大而能謙必豫故受之以豫
劉師周
同考試官教諭毛批保泰之旨發明殆盡且格調
不凡易義之絕唱者
考試官教諭劉批理精詞典深於易者
考試官教諭蔣批善發序卦之旨
===
觀持盈者之致豫而易卦相承之義昭矣甚矣
有之不可恃也能謙而天下之豫應之矣序卦
之旨深哉且夫治道以太和爲極隆而王者以
謙虛爲盛節大而易盈欲致天下之和也難矣
誠使撫盈成之運而懷抑畏之忱德欲其盛不
敢驕以亢也際亨大之期而存挹損之戒禮欲
punctuated:
克君之道者，亦惟一元而已。乾元之大，至是其無餘蘊乎！雖然，人君法天致治，體元爲先，而所以會乎元德之精者，惟學而已。蓋天以元運而神功昭，心以學純而天德粹。故如天好生，萬古稱元良焉，其精一之學可想也。噫！體元者當懋於學，而調元者其亦加之意乎！

有大而能謙必豫，故受之以豫。
劉師周
同考試官教諭毛批：保泰之旨，發明殆盡，且格調不凡，易義之絕唱者。
考試官教諭劉批：理精詞典，深於《易》者。
考試官教諭蔣批：善發《序卦》之旨。

觀持盈者之致豫，而易卦相承之義昭矣。甚矣，「有」之不可恃也！能謙而天下之豫應之矣。《序卦》之旨深哉！且夫治道以太和爲極隆，而王者以謙虛爲盛節。大而易盈，欲致天下之和也難矣。誠使撫盈成之運，而懷抑畏之忱，德欲其盛，不敢驕以亢也；際亨大之期，而存挹損之戒，禮欲
translation_en:
… the way of being able to serve as a ruler also lies solely in this single Originating Principle (yuan). Does not the greatness of the Originating Principle of Qian (the Creative) reach its fullest expression here without anything left unexhausted? Even so, when a ruler models himself on Heaven to bring about good governance, embodying the Originating Principle comes first, yet the means by which he grasps the essence of this Originating Virtue is learning alone. For Heaven revolves through the Originating Principle and its marvelous work is made manifest; the mind is purified through learning and its heavenly virtue becomes unalloyed. Thus, loving life as Heaven does, he is praised for ten thousand generations as supremely good (yuanliang); his learning of pure and unified concentration can well be imagined. Ah! Those who embody the Originating Principle ought to exert themselves in learning, and should not those who harmonize the Originating Principle also pay special heed to this!

"Possessing what is great and being able to be modest, there is sure to be joy and harmony (Yu); hence it is followed by the hexagram Yu (Enthusiasm/Harmony)."
Liu Shizhou 劉師周
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Mao: The meaning of preserving great prosperity is expounded almost to exhaustion, and its style is extraordinary—an unsurpassed masterpiece among essays on the Book of Changes.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu: Refined in principle and classical in diction; one who is profound in the Book of Changes.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Jiang: Skillfully elucidates the purport of the "Sequence of the Hexagrams" (Xugua).

When we observe how one who maintains fullness brings about joy and harmony, the meaning of how the hexagrams of the Changes succeed one another becomes clear. Extreme indeed is the fact that "great possession" cannot be presumed upon! When one is able to be modest, the joy and harmony of the world respond to him. How profound is the purport of the "Sequence of the Hexagrams"! Moreover, the way of governance takes supreme harmony as its highest flourishing, and a true king takes modest humility as his finest virtue. When what is great easily becomes full to overflowing, desiring to bring about harmony in the world is difficult indeed. If in truth, while presiding over an era of fullness and completion, one cherishes a sincere feeling of self-restraint and reverence—desiring one's virtue to be abundant and not daring to be arrogant or overbearing; and while meeting with a time of flourishing greatness, one maintains the warning ofladling out and diminishing—desiring one's propriety to be…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
其恭不敢矜以肆也則滿而不溢吾心有至和
焉而協應者成不言之孚上而能下吾身以順
動焉而從欲者妙無心之應撝謙崇於一人而
禮讓刑於百辟以庶官則和於朝焉喜起之風
可想也溫恭隆於五位而雍穆達於萬邦以兆
民則和於野焉熈皡之治可繼也蓋謙不期豫
而有必豫之理矣故序卦者於謙而受之以豫
非有所強也先天下而憂者後天下而樂機之
相因則然也受豫而先之以謙非無所爲也知
===
===
無疆之恤者享無疆之休道之相通則然也謙
豫相承之義謂不有取於是哉是則豫所以保
天下之有而謙所以和天下之心聖王之治夫
固考之易理而不悖者矣有大者其可以盈乎
噫世之德色於治平者可鑑矣雖然君道盡於
乾而不欲其亢皆謙之意也顧謙主於巽而易
於不振焉故泰之包荒必曰馮河而威如之吉
可以孚交是又以健制謙之道也若後之謙而
未遑寬而無制其亦沉潛而不能剛克者歟故
punctuated: 其恭，不敢矜以肆也。則滿而不溢，吾心有至和焉，而協應者成不言之孚；上而能下，吾身以順動焉，而從欲者妙無心之應。撝謙崇於一人，而禮讓刑於百辟，以庶官則和於朝焉，喜起之風可想也；溫恭隆於五位，而雍穆達於萬邦，以兆民則和於野焉，熈皡之治可繼也。蓋謙不期豫，而有必豫之理矣。故《序卦》者於謙而受之以豫，非有所強也，先天下而憂者後天下而樂，機之相因則然也；受豫而先之以謙，非無所爲也，知無疆之恤者享無疆之休，道之相通則然也。謙、豫相承之義，謂不有取於是哉？是則豫所以保天下之有，而謙所以和天下之心，聖王之治，夫固考之《易》理而不悖者矣。有大者其可以盈乎？噫！世之德色於治平者可鑑矣。雖然，君道盡於乾而不欲其亢，皆謙之意也；顧謙主於巽而易於不振焉，故泰之「包荒」必曰「馮河」，而「威如之吉」可以孚交，是又以健制謙之道也。若後之謙而未遑，寬而無制，其亦沉潛而不能剛克者歟？故
translation_en: … to be reverent, not daring to be boastful or unbridled. Then, being full yet not overflowing, there is supreme harmony within one's own mind, and those who respond in concert achieve a wordless trust; being on high yet able to lower oneself, one's person acts in accordance with顺 (compliance), and those who follow their desires manifest the marvelous response of an uncontrived mind. When modest humility is exalted in the One Man, and ritual yielding sets the example for the hundred lords, then as for the numerous officials, they are harmonious at court, and the spirit of joyful encouragement can be envisioned; when gentle reverence flourishes in the Fifth Position [the ruler's seat], and harmonious concord reaches the myriad states, then as for the millions of people, they are harmonious in the countryside, and the governance of bright tranquility can be continued. Indeed, Modesty (Qian) does not seek Delight (Yu), yet it possesses the principle that inevitably leads to Delight. Therefore, that the Sequence of the Hexagrams (Xugua) follows Modesty with Delight is not something forced: he who worries before the world rejoices after the world—such is the mutual causation of tendencies. That it receives Delight only after preceding it with Modesty is not without purpose: he who knows boundlesssolicitude enjoys boundless blessings—such is the mutual permeation of the Way. How could it be said that the meaning of Modesty and Delight succeeding one another does not draw upon this? Thus, Delight is that whereby one preserves the possessions of the world, and Modesty is that whereby one harmonizes the minds of the world. The governance of the sage-kings, when examined against the principles of the Changes (Yi), is indeed not at odds with them. Can one who possesses greatness afford to be full of himself? Alas! Those in the world who put on a self-satisfied air in times of peace and order may take this as a mirror. Nevertheless, the Way of the ruler is fully realized in the Creative (Qian) yet desires not to be overbearing—all of this is the meaning of Modesty. Yet Modesty is governed by compliance and easily falls into a lack of vigor; therefore, in Peace (Tai), "embracing the荒 (wild/uncultivated)" must be paired with "crossing a river without a boat," and the good fortune of "majestic dignity" (in Daren/Dayou) can inspire mutual trust—this, in turn, is the way of regulating Modesty with strength. As for those in later times whose modesty leaves them no leisure for action, and whose leniency lacks regulation—are they not what is called "sunken and retiring" yet unable to "prevail by firmness"? Therefore…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
曰明剛柔之節而後可以言治也
書
