德
阮和咸
同考試官教諭徐批作此多泥體裁致忽本旨結
搆自然詞理精到僅見是文耳錄之
考試官教諭劉批認意精深措詞渾雅
考試官教諭蔣批精確有體脉絡尤明
===
大臣陳謨於君惟欲交儆以成化焉夫君臣萬
化之原也能交脩而政乂民善矣大臣陳謨及
此其願治無窮之心乎想其祗承于帝若曰天
下之治致之固不易保之亦甚難今之時雖平
成矣而乘時以保治者其敢不慎乎彼人君主
文命之治其道固惟艱也是必思天心難享而
惕若以凝其精治功難成而奮勵以鼓其志孜
孜然立政安民之憂蓋不敢以治安為幸而實
能圖其艱矣人臣輔文命之治其道亦甚艱也
punctuated:
曰：明剛柔之節，而後可以言治也。

書

「后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。」

阮和咸

同考試官教諭徐批：作此多泥體裁，致忽本旨。結構自然，詞理精到，僅見是文耳，錄之。
考試官教諭劉批：認意精深，措詞渾雅。
考試官教諭蔣批：精確有體，脉絡尤明。

大臣陳謨於君，惟欲交儆以成化焉。夫君臣，萬化之原也，能交脩而政乂民善矣。大臣陳謨及此，其願治無窮之心乎？想其祗承于帝，若曰：天下之治，致之固不易，保之亦甚難。今之時雖平成矣，而乘時以保治者，其敢不慎乎？彼人君主文命之治，其道固惟艱也。是必思天心難享，而惕若以凝其精；治功難成，而奮勵以鼓其志。孜孜然立政安民之憂，蓋不敢以治安為幸，而實能圖其艱矣。人臣輔文命之治，其道亦甚艱也。
translation_en:
… say: Only after illuminating the proper measure of firmness and gentleness can one speak of governance.

Book of Documents (Shu)

"If the sovereign can realize the difficulty of his sovereignty, and the minister can realize the difficulty of his ministry, government will be well ordered, and the black-haired people will sedulously seek after virtue."

Ruan Hexian 阮和咸

Associate Examiner, Confucian School Instructor (jiaoyu) Xu comments: Most who write on this topic are overly bound by formal conventions, causing them to neglect the fundamental purport. A natural structure and refined diction and reasoning are seen only in this essay; let it be recorded.
Examiner, Confucian School Instructor Liu comments: The comprehension of the meaning is profound, and the phrasing is consummate and elegant.
Examiner, Confucian School Instructor Jiang comments: Precise and fitting in form, with a particularly clear thread of argument.

When the great minister set forth his counsels before the sovereign, he desired only that they mutually caution one another so as to bring about transformative governance. Now, sovereign and minister are the source of the myriad transformations; if they can mutually cultivate their duties, then governance will be well ordered and the people made good. When the great minister's counsels reached this point, was it not out of a boundless desire for good governance? One may imagine him reverently responding to the Emperor, as if to say: Order in the realm is assuredly not easy to bring about, and it is also exceedingly difficult to preserve. Although the present age has achieved peace and order, how could those who take advantage of the times to preserve good governance dare not be cautious? The sovereign presides over the governance of civilizing instruction, and his Way is assuredly full of difficulty. Thus he must reflect that the heart of Heaven is hard to satisfy, and remain vigilantly apprehensive so as to concentrate his spirit; and that the achievements of governance are hard to consummate, and rouse himself to stir his resolve. Tirelessly concerned with establishing order and giving rest to the people, he dares not regard peace and stability as mere good fortune, and is truly able to attend to the difficulties of his office. The minister assists in the governance of civilizing instruction, and his Way is likewise exceedingly difficult. …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
是必思身繫安危而愈勵乎精白之念力勝艱
大而益操乎敬事之忱汲汲然惟輔政保民之
圖蓋不敢以豫大爲慶而實克盡其難矣如是
而治化其容已乎吾知政以人而舉也惟上下
旣協於同心則百揆乃底於時敘大綱舉焉萬
目張焉蓋業廣於勤而朝於是乎無廢政矣使
交脩之未至能必政之盡乂乎民以德而化也
惟表則旣會於明良則兆民自底於從欲易其
惡焉至其中焉蓋民從所好而野於是乎無頑
===
===
俗矣使交儆之或怠能必民之盡化乎噫大禹
保治之心至矣夫兢業如帝無以復加而克艱
之說禹復惓惓若此豈好爲危言者哉蓋惟舜
有至虛之心故禹之責難不知其過若舜之命
禹而遂以四海困窮危之則其情益切矣豈非
以禹之不自滿假其心猶之已乎噫保治者其
求諸二聖之心可也
君子所其無逸
孫愈賢
punctuated:
是必思身繫安危，而愈勵乎精白之念；力勝艱大，而益操乎敬事之忱。汲汲然惟輔政保民之圖，蓋不敢以豫大爲慶，而實克盡其難矣。如是而治化其容已乎？吾知政以人而舉也。惟上下旣協於同心，則百揆乃底於時敘，大綱舉焉，萬目張焉。蓋業廣於勤，而朝於是乎無廢政矣。使交脩之未至，能必政之盡乂乎？民以德而化也。惟表則旣會於明良，則兆民自底於從欲，易其惡焉，至其中焉。蓋民從所好，而野於是乎無頑俗矣。使交儆之或怠，能必民之盡化乎？噫！大禹保治之心至矣。夫兢業如帝，無以復加，而「克艱」之說，禹復惓惓若此，豈好爲危言者哉？蓋惟舜有至虛之心，故禹之責難不知其過；若舜之命禹，而遂以「四海困窮」危之，則其情益切矣。豈非以禹之不自滿假，其心猶之已乎？噫！保治者，其求諸二聖之心可也。

「君子所其無逸。」
孫愈賢
translation_en:
…Therefore, he must reflect on how his own person is bound up with safety and danger, and all the more rouse his resolve for pure devotion; he must bear up under great and difficult burdens, and all the more hold fast to his sincerity in reverently attending to affairs. Anxiously and untiringly, he plans only to assist in governance and protect the people; indeed, he dares not rejoice in ease and abundance, but is truly able to fulfill the difficulties of his office. When it is like this, how could good governance and moral transformation possibly cease? 

I know that governance is raised up through men. Only when sovereign and minister are already united in one mind do all the general affairs of state reach timely order—the great guiding principles are upheld, and the myriad details are spread out in array. For great enterprises are broadened through diligence, and thus in the court there are no neglected measures of governance. If their mutual cultivation had not reached the utmost, could one be certain that governance would be completely well-ordered? The people are transformed through virtue. Only when the standard of conduct is already united in an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers do the millions of people naturally come to follow what is desired of them—changing their evil ways and attaining the mean. For the people follow what their superiors love, and thus in the countryside there are no obstinate customs. If their mutual admonition were ever lax, could one be certain that the people would be completely transformed?

Alas! Great Yu’s心 (heart-and-mind) in preserving good governance reached the utmost. Now, in caution and apprehension, none could surpass the Emperor [Shun], and yet with this doctrine of "being able to attend to the difficulties," Yu was still so earnestly insistent—was he merely fond of uttering alarming words? It was only because Shun possessed an utterly open and receptive mind that Yu, in urging difficult standards upon him, did not realize he was going so far. And when Shun in turn charged Yu, and went so far as to warn him with the peril of "the four seas falling into distress and poverty," his feelings were even more urgent! Was it not because Yu, in not being self-satisfied or presumptuous, had a mind just like Shun's own? Alas! Those who seek to preserve good governance should simply look for it in the minds of these two sages.

"The noble man makes 'taking no ease' his abiding place." [Book of Documents, "Wu yi" (Against Luxurious Ease)]
Sun Yuxian 孫愈賢

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭徐批周公忠愛勤懇子能言之且
不費詞擅場之作也
考試官教諭劉批語意懇到得忠告體
考試官教諭蔣批理明詞達義之隹者
大臣表君子之居勤忠告之意至矣夫天下之
治成於勤也以勤作所其君子之所以致治乎
周公因成王初政而欲防其漸也故儆之若曰
王業難於持盈君心貴於慎始嗣王新服厥命
尚其仰法於君子乎蓋君子一身天下之安危
===
係焉居已於逸而欲貽天下之安者難矣故以
崇高非得肆之地也而天行為健隨在皆兢業
之圖以盈成非可恃之業也而日強為敬無往
非勵精之念自昧爽以至日昃時雖屢遷而居
之愈微則防之愈切將以為居身之珍而夙夜
罔不勤焉自臨御以至宴息居雖不齊而所處
益密則所操益慎將以為宅身之要而出入罔
不欽焉上而祈天則精明之念與於穆相為感
孚而兢兢然對越之不違蓋不待承之祭祀而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭徐批：「周公忠愛勤懇，子能言之，且不費詞，擅場之作也。」
考試官教諭劉批：「語意懇到，得忠告體。」
考試官教諭蔣批：「理明詞達，義之隹者。」
大臣表君子之居勤，忠告之意至矣。夫天下之治，成於勤也；以勤作所，其君子之所以致治乎！周公因成王初政，而欲防其漸也，故儆之若曰：王業難於持盈，君心貴於慎始。嗣王新服厥命，尚其仰法於君子乎！蓋君子一身，天下之安危係焉。居已於逸，而欲貽天下之安者，難矣。故以崇高非得肆之地也，而天行為健，隨在皆兢業之圖；以盈成非可恃之業也，而日強為敬，無往非勵精之念。自昧爽以至日昃，時雖屢遷，而居之愈微，則防之愈切，將以為居身之珍，而夙夜罔不勤焉；自臨御以至宴息，居雖不齊，而所處益密，則所操益慎，將以為宅身之要，而出入罔不欽焉。上而祈天，則精明之念與於穆相為感孚，而兢兢然對越之不違，蓋不待承之祭祀，而
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Xu comments: "You are able to express the Duke of Zhou's loyal affection and earnest diligence, and without wasting words—a work that commands the examination hall."
Examiner Instructor Liu comments: "The words and meaning are earnest and thorough, capturing the style of loyal admonition."
Examiner Instructor Jiang comments: "The principles are clear and the phrasing is fluent—an excellent exposition."
When the great minister sets forth how the noble man abides in diligence, the intent of his loyal admonition reaches its utmost. Now, the good governance of the world is achieved through diligence; taking diligence as one's dwelling place—is this not how the noble man brings about order! Because King Cheng was just beginning his personal rule, the Duke of Zhou wished to guard against gradual lapses from the outset, and so he cautioned him as if to say: In the royal enterprise it is difficult to preserve fullness, and for the ruler's mind what is valued is prudence at the beginning. Now that the successor king has newly taken up his mandate, may he look up and model himself upon the noble man! For upon the single person of the noble man hangs the security or peril of the world. To place oneself in ease and yet wish to bequeath peace to the world is difficult indeed. Therefore, considering that an exalted station is no place for self-indulgence, he matches the vigorous movement of Heaven, making every situation an occasion for cautious diligence; considering that fullness and accomplishment are no patrimony to be relied upon, he takes daily self-strengthening as his reverence, having no moment without thoughts of rousing his spirit. From early dawn until the sun inclines to the west, though the hours repeatedly shift, the more subtle his situation, the more urgent his precautions; taking this as a treasure in which to abide, morning and night there is nothing in which he is not diligent. From holding court to retiring for rest, though his settings vary, the more intimate his surroundings, the more circumspect his conduct; taking this as the essential place in which to settle himself, in going out and coming in there is nothing in which he is not reverent. Above, in praying to Heaven, his pure and bright thoughts correspond in mutual resonance with the profound and august unseen, and cautiously he stands before it without departing; indeed, he does not wait until he is performing the sacrificial rites, and yet…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
莫非上帝攸臨之所矣其斯以煕鴻號於無窮
乎下而保民則憂勤之衷與衆志相爲聨屬而
皇皇然保乂之不懈蓋不必措諸設施而莫非
顧畏民畧之所矣其斯以基鴻業於弗替乎要
之開泰者垂懿恭之範保泰者紹緝煕之傳無
逸乃逸而天下萬世享其安矣吾王其懋之哉
雖然害治之弊非一端而周公獨以無逸爲戒
何哉蓋人情勞則思善逸則思淫縱欲敗度皆
自逸之一念啓之也故創業之君常恐佚豫之
===
不足以貽謀而繼體者敢不慎哉噫成王幼冲
之年逸欲未萌而周公豫防之此其忠之所以
爲大也
詩
大人占之衆維魚矣實維豐年旐維旟矣
室家溱溱
楊應兆
同考試官學正梁 批 中興氣象模寫粲然而末歸
保終意尤覺深邃宜錄以式
punctuated:
莫非上帝攸臨之所矣，其斯以煕鴻號於無窮乎！下而保民，則憂勤之衷與衆志相爲聨屬，而皇皇然保乂之不懈，蓋不必措諸設施，而莫非顧畏民畧之所矣，其斯以基鴻業於弗替乎！要之，開泰者垂懿恭之範，保泰者紹緝煕之傳，無逸乃逸，而天下萬世享其安矣。吾王其懋之哉！雖然，害治之弊非一端，而周公獨以無逸爲戒，何哉？蓋人情勞則思善，逸則思淫，縱欲敗度，皆自逸之一念啓之也。故創業之君，常恐佚豫之不足以貽謀，而繼體者敢不慎哉！噫！成王幼冲之年，逸欲未萌，而周公豫防之，此其忠之所以爲大也。

《詩》：「大人占之：衆維魚矣，實維豐年；旐維旟矣，室家溱溱。」
楊應兆
同考試官學正梁批：中興氣象，模寫粲然，而末歸保終，意尤覺深邃，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…there is nowhere that is not a place where the Lord on High descends to watch. Is it not by this means that one makes the grand title shine forth endlessly! Below, in protecting the people, one’s anxious and diligent heart is bound together with the will of the multitude, and one urgently and untiringly protects and governs them; indeed, one need not wait to put this into concrete measures before every place is one where one regards with awe the perils of the common people [reading 畧 for 碞]. Is it not by this means that one lays the foundation of the grand enterprise so that it never declines! In sum, he who initiates an era of great peace leaves behind a model of admirable reverence, and he who preserves that great peace continues the transmission of radiant and unceasing devotion. By taking no ease, one achieves true ease, and All under Heaven for ten thousand generations enjoys its tranquility. May our King exert himself in this! Even so, the abuses that harm governance are not of a single kind; why then did the Duke of Zhou warn solely against taking ease? It is because in human nature, when people toil they think of goodness, and when they are at ease they think of licentiousness. Giving rein to desires and ruining the norms all begin from a single thought of ease. Therefore, a ruler who founds a dynasty always fears that idleness and pleasure will be insufficient to pass down good counsel to his descendants—how then could a successor to the throne dare not be cautious! Alas! In King Cheng’s young and tender years, desires for ease had not yet sprouted, yet the Duke of Zhou guarded against them in advance; this is why his loyalty was so great.

Classic of Poetry (Shijing): “The great diviner interprets it: The multitudes of locusts turned into fish—truly it will be a year of abundance; the tortoise-and-snake banners turned into falcon banners—households and families will be teeming.”
Yang Yingzhao 楊應兆.
Associate Examiner Subprefectural Instructor Liang comments: The atmosphere of dynastic revival is depicted with brilliant clarity, and the conclusion returning to the preservation of the end feels especially profound. It ought to be recorded as a model.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉批〔舂融典麗結意獨精〕
考試官教諭蔣批〔鋪張盛治意到詞足〕
詩人於牧人之夢而决其富庶之徵焉夫國家
以富庶爲祥也而占於牧人之夢焉不可以觀
中興之氣象乎詩詠無羊以志治者若曰國家
之興也固必有鬼神以司其柄亦必有禎祥以
顯其機眾維魚而旐維旟牧人之夢誠異矣大
人者司占而决疑者也其將謂之何哉蓋我周
以農事開國而豐年綏於萬邦維昔之富不可
===
及矣今夢眾而魚固以少致多者也其必天祐
斯民而歲月無易貽之以順成之休帝昭明賜
而稼穡用登溥之以豐穰之慶以足民食則三
農不匱也以厚邦儲則九賦可繼也蓋吾王憂
旱之志固足以兆康而茲特洩其祕耳𠀌視自
古有年之盛不重光乎我周以聚民立國而庶
繁徵於奕世維昔之庶不可及矣今夢旐而旟
固以寡致眾者也其必太和洋溢而生齒日繁
相安於樂利之境順治鼓舞而歸附日眾益顯
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉批：〔舂融典麗，結意獨精。〕
考試官教諭蔣批：〔鋪張盛治，意到詞足。〕

詩人於牧人之夢，而决其富庶之徵焉。夫國家以富庶爲祥也，而占於牧人之夢焉，不可以觀中興之氣象乎？詩詠《無羊》以志治者，若曰：國家之興也，固必有鬼神以司其柄，亦必有禎祥以顯其機。「眾維魚」而「旐維旟」，牧人之夢誠異矣。大人者，司占而决疑者也，其將謂之何哉？蓋我周以農事開國，而豐年綏於萬邦，維昔之富不可及矣。今夢眾而魚，固以少致多者也。其必天祐斯民，而歲月無易，貽之以順成之休；帝昭明賜，而稼穡用登，溥之以豐穰之慶。以足民食，則三農不匱也；以厚邦儲，則九賦可繼也。蓋吾王憂旱之志，固足以兆康，而茲特洩其祕耳。𠀌視自古有年之盛，不重光乎？我周以聚民立國，而庶繁徵於奕世，維昔之庶不可及矣。今夢旐而旟，固以寡致眾者也。其必太和洋溢，而生齒日繁，相安於樂利之境；順治鼓舞，而歸附日眾，益顯…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: [Harmonious, mellow, and classically elegant; the concluding thought is uniquely refined.]
Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: [It elaborates grandly upon flourishing governance, with thought reaching its mark and diction fully sufficient.]

From the herdsman's dream, the poet determines the portents of wealth and a populous realm. Now, the state takes wealth and a numerous populace as auspicious signs, and when these are divined from the dream of a herdsman, can we not thereby observe the spirit of dynastic revival? He who composed the ode "Wu yang" (No Sheep) to record good governance seems to say: When a state rises, there must surely be ghosts and spirits to hold its handle of authority, and there must also be auspicious omens to manifest its incipient workings. "Locusts—no, fishes!" and "A tortoise-and-snake banner—no, a falcon banner!"—the herdsman's dream was truly extraordinary. The grand diviner is one who takes charge of prognostication and resolves doubts; what then will he say of this?

Indeed, our Zhou dynasty founded the state upon agriculture, and years of abundance brought peace to the myriad domains; the wealth of former times seemed unattainable. Now, to dream of locusts becoming fishes is surely a sign of going from few to many. It must be that Heaven blesses these people, and with the seasons and months unaltered, bestows upon them the blessing of smooth harvests; the Supreme Lord displays his bright largesse, and as the sown and reaped grain is brought in, spreads far and wide the joy of bountiful plenty. To suffice for the people's food, the three classes of farmers will not be in want; to enrich the state's reserves, the nine revenues can be sustained. Indeed, our King's anxious concern over drought was already sufficient to presage prosperity, and this dream merely reveals its secret! Compared with the flourishing harvests of antiquity, does this not shine with renewed splendor?

Our Zhou dynasty established the state by gathering the people, and a thriving populace was attested across successive generations; the populousness of former times seemed unattainable. Now, to dream of a tortoise-and-snake banner becoming a falcon banner is surely a sign of going from scarcity to multitude. It must be that supreme harmony overflows, and as the registered population grows more numerous day by day, they rest content together in a realm of joy and benefit; harmonious governance inspires them, and as those who turn in allegiance grow more numerous day by day, it all the more manifests…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
乎明昌之運列之邦畿無怨曠也布之甸服無
仳離也蓋吾王還定之仁固足以得衆而玆特
示其端耳其視咸和萬民之盛不再見乎吁民
富則君不患貧矣民庶則君不患寡矣以極治
之象而兆於牧人之微詩人之頌亦婉矣哉蓋
宣王側身脩行回天保民富庶之祥乃其自致
而時方懼其鮮終焉故托之夢兆而歆其無忘
厥初耳惜千畝不藉料民太原而無羊之響息
矣憂國者其慎諸
===
百辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸墍
李維美
同考試官學正梁批致願嫡嗣用答君福詩人意也
此作得之宜錄
考試官教諭劉批發明保治安民詞理具備
考試官教諭蔣批溫厚懇切得詩人旨
詩人願臣之愛君而切於保泰之慮焉夫君心
係天下之安危也政勤而民安焉非忠君者之
至願哉想其願君福而致望於嫡嗣者有曰君
punctuated:
乎明昌之運。列之邦畿，無怨曠也；布之甸服，無仳離也。蓋吾王還定之仁，固足以得衆，而玆特示其端耳。其視咸和萬民之盛，不再見乎？吁！民富則君不患貧矣，民庶則君不患寡矣。以極治之象而兆於牧人之微，詩人之頌亦婉矣哉！蓋宣王側身脩行，回天保民，富庶之祥，乃其自致。而時方懼其鮮終焉，故托之夢兆，而歆其無忘厥初耳。惜千畝不藉，料民太原，而《無羊》之響息矣。憂國者其慎諸！

百辟卿士，媚于天子；不解于位，民之攸墍。
李維美
同考試官、學正梁批：致願嫡嗣，用答君福，詩人意也。此作得之，宜錄。
考試官、教諭劉批：發明保治安民，詞理具備。
考試官、教諭蔣批：溫厚懇切，得詩人旨。

詩人願臣之愛君，而切於保泰之慮焉。夫君心係天下之安危也，政勤而民安焉，非忠君者之至願哉？想其願君福而致望於嫡嗣者，有曰：君
translation_en:
… the fortune of bright prosperity. Arrayed within the royal domain, there are none who resent being unmarried; spread throughout the royal territories, there are none who suffer separation. Indeed, our king's benevolence in resettling and stabilizing the people is certainly sufficient to win the multitude, and this dream merely reveals its beginning. Compared to the flourishing age when all the myriad people were brought into harmony, is that not seen once again? Ah! When the people are wealthy, the ruler need not worry about poverty; when the people are numerous, the ruler need not worry about scarcity. To have the signs of utmost order portended through humble herdsmen—how subtle and tactful is the poet's eulogy! Indeed, King Xuan cultivated his conduct in awe and trepidation, turning back Heaven's wrath and protecting the people; the auspicious signs of wealth and population were brought about by himself. Yet contemporaries were just then afraid that he might rarely hold fast to the end, and so the poet entrusted his message to the omens of dreams, moving the king not to forget his initial resolve. Alas, when he failed to plow the thousand-mu sacred field and numbered the people at Taiyuan, the echoes of "No Sheep" (Wu yang) died away. Let those who worry for the state take heed!

"The hundred regional rulers and the ministers and grandees show love for the Son of Heaven; unremitting in their positions, they are those through whom the people find rest."
Li Weimei
Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Director of Studies: Expressing good wishes for the legitimate heir as a response to the ruler's blessings—such is the poet's intent. This composition grasps it and ought to be selected.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: It elucidates the preservation of order and the pacification of the people, complete in both diction and principle.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Gentle, generous, and earnest, it grasps the poet's purport.

The poet wishes for the ministers to love their ruler, and is earnest in his concern for preserving great peace. Now, the ruler's mind-and-heart is tied to the security and peril of all under Heaven; that governance be diligent and the people at peace—is this not the ultimate wish of one loyal to his ruler? One may imagine that in wishing blessings upon the ruler and extending his hopes to the legitimate heir, he said in effect: The relationship between ruler…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
臣相遇以喜起爲情以交儆爲益者也王嗣立
綱紀以燕及其臣矣乃諸臣之心何如哉彼百
辟屏翰於外願治爲甚殷也仰明聖之度自切
翼戴之忱而元首股肱其情油然不容已焉卿
士輔相於內分義爲愈厚也幸際遇之隆益懷
圖報之念而手足腹心其情藹然不能釋焉然
豈敢以治安爲獻而不爲國家深長之慮者乎
蓋謹始而慮終者人君之所以保其泰也憂治
而危明者忠臣之所以防其漸也故惟明於治
===
忽之理而迪德凝命遠紹乎無逸之風察於否
泰之機而慎位保民丕振乎永清之烈以總乾
綱雖盈成猶初服焉則上有恒心下有恒愛而
熙洽之運將怙冒於無疆也吾君宜民之治玆
其有寄乎以飭法紀雖厚終猶虔始焉則勞以
一人逸以天下而治安之澤固昭升於不替也
吾君保佑之命玆其益申乎此則諸臣之心而
君福之所以爲隆者也吁君以善治安其臣臣
以保治媚其君一頌禱而計切國家忠哉周臣
punctuated: 臣相遇，以喜起爲情，以交儆爲益者也。王嗣立綱紀，以燕及其臣矣，乃諸臣之心何如哉？彼百辟屏翰於外，願治爲甚殷也；仰明聖之度，自切翼戴之忱，而元首股肱，其情油然不容已焉。卿士輔相於內，分義爲愈厚也；幸際遇之隆，益懷圖報之念，而手足腹心，其情藹然不能釋焉。然豈敢以治安爲獻，而不爲國家深長之慮者乎？蓋謹始而慮終者，人君之所以保其泰也；憂治而危明者，忠臣之所以防其漸也。故惟明於治忽之理，而迪德凝命，遠紹乎無逸之風；察於否泰之機，而慎位保民，丕振乎永清之烈。以總乾綱，雖盈成猶初服焉，則上有恒心，下有恒愛，而熙洽之運將怙冒於無疆也，吾君宜民之治，玆其有寄乎！以飭法紀，雖厚終猶虔始焉，則勞以一人，逸以天下，而治安之澤固昭升於不替也，吾君保佑之命，玆其益申乎！此則諸臣之心，而君福之所以爲隆者也。吁！君以善治安其臣，臣以保治媚其君，一頌禱而計切國家，忠哉周臣
translation_en:
…when sovereign and ministers meet, their feelings are those of joyous exaltation, and their mutualbenefit lies in reciprocal admonition. The royal heir establishes the guiding laws and regulations so as to extend peace and comfort to his ministers; what, then, are the hearts of the various ministers like? Those hundred lords serving as a protective screen in the outer domains are most ardent in their desire for good governance; looking up to his sagely and enlightened magnanimity, they naturally feel an earnest sincerity in supporting and upholding him, and between the head and the limbs, that affection wells up irrepressibly. The grandees and court officials assisting within the capital are bound by an even deeper sense of duty and status; fortunate in the splendor of their encounter with their ruler, they cherish all the more the thought of repaying his grace, and like hands, feet, heart, and vitals, their warm devotion cannot be set aside. Yet how could they dare merely offer up congratulations on peace and order without taking deep and far-reaching thought for the state?

For to be cautious at the beginning and mindful of the end is how a ruler preserves his era of great peace; to be anxious in times of order and fearful of danger in times of enlightenment is how a loyal minister guards against gradual decline. Therefore, one wishes only that he be clear about the principles of order and neglect, walking in virtue and consolidating the Mandate, so as to carry on from afar the spirit of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi); and that he discern the subtle turning points of misfortune and prosperity, being cautious on the throne and protecting the people, so as to grandly revitalize the meritorious achievement of eternal pacification. By grasping the sovereign authority, even in the fullness of achievement he acts as though at the very beginning of his reign; then above there will be a constant mind, below there will be constant affection, and a destiny of bright harmony will shelter and cover all without bound—shall not our sovereign's governance suited to the people find its reliance here! By rectifying the laws and discipline, even in bringing things to a generous conclusion he remains as reverent as at the start; then through the toil of the One Man, the whole world enjoys ease, and the blessings of peace and order will surely rise brightly without cease—shall not our sovereign's Mandate of protection and aid be renewed even further here! This, then, is the heart of the various ministers, and the reason why the sovereign's felicity is so abundant.

Ah! The sovereign brings peace to his ministers through good governance, and the ministers show devotion to their sovereign by preserving that governance. Even in a single prayer of praise, their counsels are earnestly devoted to the state—how loyal indeed is the Zhou ministers'…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之愛君也蓋假樂之陳用答鳧鷖固未知其嫡
嗣為何如而勤政之効婉然可即得非以王儲
為國本無逸為家法而謀及其子孫者亦以規
及其君耶噫作之者顯德宜人述之者勤政致
媚信乎天下之治必君臣交泰而成也
春秋
冬城向桓公十有六年齊師宋師曹師城
邢僖公元年
劉文徵
===
同考試官教諭陶批聖人慎用民力意在言外此
作以麗詞發至理而體裁峻潔非徒作者
考試官教諭劉批對待森然峻整可誦
考試官教諭蔣批詞意嚴整經世之見也
春秋兩紀役之合時義者欲人君之重民力也
甚矣仁君不盡民之力也此春秋於城向城邢
而竝書以示意乎且夫善為國者先保其民善
保民者必愛其力嘗觀春秋城向城邢之書而
知之矣彼向圮其城魯於冬而城之孰不曰龍
punctuated:
之愛君也！蓋《假樂》之陳，用答《鳧鷖》，固未知其嫡嗣為何如，而勤政之効，婉然可即。得非以王儲為國本，無逸為家法，而謀及其子孫者，亦以規及其君耶？噫！作之者顯德宜人，述之者勤政致媚，信乎天下之治，必君臣交泰而成也。

《春秋》
「冬，城向。」（桓公十有六年）「齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。」（僖公元年）
劉文徵
同考試官教諭陶批：聖人慎用民力，意在言外。此作以麗詞發至理，而體裁峻潔，非徒作者。
考試官教諭劉批：對待森然，峻整可誦。
考試官教諭蔣批：詞意嚴整，經世之見也。

《春秋》兩紀役之合時義者，欲人君之重民力也。甚矣，仁君不盡民之力也！此《春秋》於「城向」、「城邢」而竝書以示意乎？且夫善為國者，先保其民；善保民者，必愛其力。嘗觀《春秋》「城向」、「城邢」之書而知之矣。彼向圮其城，魯於冬而城之，孰不曰龍…
translation_en:
… in loving their ruler! For when the ode "Jia le" (Felicitous and Joyous) was presented in reply to "Fu yi" (Wild Ducks), although it could not yet be known what the legitimate heir would be like, the efficacy of diligent governance could gently be approached. Was it not because they regarded the royal heir as the foundation of the state and "taking no ease" as the family law, so that in taking counsel for his descendants they were also offering admonition to their ruler? Ah! Those who initiated it displayed illustrious virtue suited to the people, and those who carried it on practiced diligent governance to win devotion. Truly, the good order of All-under-Heaven can only be achieved when ruler and ministers are in harmonious communion!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In winter, [they] walled Xiang." (Sixteenth year of Duke Huan) "The army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Cao walled Xing." (First year of Duke Xi)
Liu Wenzheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Tao: The Sage's caution in employing the people's strength lies beyond the literal words. This composition uses elegant phrasing to bring forth ultimate principle, and its structure is lofty and pure—no mere ordinary writer.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu: The parallelisms are strictly arrayed; lofty, well-ordered, and worthy of recitation.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Jiang: The diction and meaning are rigorous and orderly; it shows a vision for statecraft.

When the Spring and Autumn Annals twice records labor services that accorded with both season and righteousness, it desires that the ruler of men value the strength of the people. How extreme is a benevolent ruler's refusal to exhaust the people's strength! Is it for this reason that the Spring and Autumn Annals records both the walling of Xiang and the walling of Xing to convey its meaning? Moreover, he who is skilled at governing a state first protects his people; he who is skilled at protecting the people necessarily cherishes their strength. I have observed the entries in the Spring and Autumn Annals on "walling Xiang" and "walling Xing" and come to know this. Now, when the walls of Xiang fell into ruin and Lu walled it in winter, who would not say that when the Dragon…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
見戒事火見致用時可以使民矣殊不知役可
以時而興勞不以時而免也耕穫甫畢於三時
而勤動未息於終歲將無苦於力作而興楊柳
雨雪之悲者乎使以時而略之則牛羊其人者
皆以時爲辭而不恤其私矣君子謂時而不勞
乎民可無誌也時而不能不勞乎民寧不爲之
動念哉此城向之所以書也邢遷於狄齊率衆
而城之孰不曰彌縫其闕匡救其災義可以役
民矣殊不知民可以義而役力不以義而弛也
===
干戈甫息於捍患而版築遂興於設防將無疲
於奔命而起束薪束蒲之嘆者乎使因義而削
之則秦越其民者皆以義爲解而不體其情矣
君子謂義而不勞乎民可無紀也義而不能不
勞乎民能不爲之致意哉此城邢之所以書也
吁合時猶愼而况於不時乎合義且謹而况於
不義乎知此而重民力則食足生遂化行俗美
胥有賴矣春秋之望於仁君者至哉雖然魯納
突而城向義未盡協也特視夏城中丘彼善於
punctuated: 見戒事，火見致用，時可以使民矣？殊不知役可以時而興，勞不以時而免也。耕穫甫畢於三時，而勤動未息於終歲，將無苦於力作而興楊柳雨雪之悲者乎？使以時而略之，則牛羊其人者，皆以時爲辭，而不恤其私矣。君子謂時而不勞乎民，可無誌也；時而不能不勞乎民，寧不爲之動念哉？此城向之所以書也。邢遷於狄，齊率衆而城之，孰不曰彌縫其闕，匡救其災，義可以役民矣？殊不知民可以義而役，力不以義而弛也。干戈甫息於捍患，而版築遂興於設防，將無疲於奔命而起束薪束蒲之嘆者乎？使因義而削之，則秦越其民者，皆以義爲解，而不體其情矣。君子謂義而不勞乎民，可無紀也；義而不能不勞乎民，能不爲之致意哉？此城邢之所以書也。吁！合時猶愼，而况於不時乎？合義且謹，而况於不義乎？知此而重民力，則食足生遂，化行俗美，胥有賴矣。《春秋》之望於仁君者至哉！雖然，魯納突而城向，義未盡協也，特視夏城中丘，彼善於
translation_en:
…appears, preparations for construction are warned to begin, and when the Fire Star appears, materials are put to use, so the season permits employing the people? Yet they fail to realize that although corvée labor may be initiated in the proper season, the toil is not exempted merely because it is seasonal. When plowing and harvesting have barely concluded across the three agricultural seasons, yet diligent toil does not cease at the end of the year, will they not suffer from the hard labor and give rise to the sorrow of 'the weeping willows' and 'the falling snow'? If the record were omitted simply because the work was timely, then rulers who treat their people like cattle and sheep would all use timeliness as a pretext and show no compassion for their private needs. The gentleman says that if an undertaking is timely and does not weary the people, it need not be recorded; but if it is timely and yet cannot avoid wearying the people, how could one not be moved to concern for them? This is why the walling of Xiang was recorded.

When Xing relocated because of the Di tribes, Qi led the multitude to wall its city. Who would not say that in patching up their deficiencies and rescuing them from calamity, righteousness permitted mobilizing the people for corvée? Yet they fail to realize that although the people may be mobilized in the name of righteousness, their physical strength is not spared merely because the cause is righteous. When shields and spears have barely rested from warding off disaster, and rammed-earth construction is immediately begun to erect defenses, will they not be exhausted by running about on orders and raise the lament of 'bound firewood' and 'bound rushes'? If the entry were expunged simply because the act was righteous, then rulers who regard their people with the indifference of Qin toward Yue would all use righteousness as an excuse and fail to sympathize with their plight. The gentleman says that if an undertaking is righteous and does not weary the people, it need not be chronicled; but if it is righteous and yet cannot avoid wearying the people, how could one not pay heed to them? This is why the walling of Xing was recorded.

Alas! If even timely undertakings require caution, how much more so those that are untimely? If even righteous undertakings demand care, how much more so those that are unrighteous? If a ruler understands this and values the people's strength, then sufficient food and fulfilled livelihoods, the spread of moral transformation and the beauty of customs, will all depend on this. How profound is the expectation that the Spring and Autumn Annals places upon a benevolent ruler! Even so, when Lu installed Tu and walled Xiang, its righteousness was not entirely fitting; it is only that compared to walling Zhongqiu in summer, the former was somewhat better than…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
此耳若邢被狄難一旅可却乃師次聶北俟其
遷而城之得無養亂以爲功乎噫薄德之譏桓
固有以來之也
齊小白入于齊〔莊公九年〕公會齊人宋人
救鄭〔莊公二十有八年〕齊人救邢〔閔公
元年〕秋八月諸侯盟于首止〔僖公五年〕
九月戊辰諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
彭商英
同考試官敎諭陶批君臣分義勞効條括不遺而
===
議論正大深得屬詞之體宜錄之以式明經者
考試官敎諭劉批不牽文義獨暢本旨
考試官敎諭蔣批是非定於聖人桓仲當爲心服
春秋明嗣君之當立因有取於其臣之功焉夫
桓之有齊分之正也卽管仲功不廢于天下而
不益見其當立乎昔子糾爭立而小白入齊內
無所稟上無所承白亦猶之糾也而春秋獨繫
之齊者何哉君子曰少不先長分也位定於分
制也臨淄之地白所宜居而觀於管仲之功尤
punctuated:
此耳。若邢被狄難，一旅可却，乃師次聶北，俟其遷而城之，得無養亂以爲功乎？噫！薄德之譏，桓固有以來之也。

「齊小白入于齊」〔莊公九年〕、「公會齊人、宋人救鄭」〔莊公二十有八年〕、「齊人救邢」〔閔公元年〕、「秋八月，諸侯盟于首止」〔僖公五年〕、「九月戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘」〔僖公九年〕。
彭商英
同考試官敎諭陶批：君臣分義、勞効，條括不遺，而議論正大，深得屬詞之體，宜錄之以式明經者。
考試官敎諭劉批：不牽文義，獨暢本旨。
考試官敎諭蔣批：是非定於聖人，桓、仲當爲心服。

《春秋》明嗣君之當立，因有取於其臣之功焉。夫桓之有齊，分之正也；卽管仲功不廢于天下，而不益見其當立乎？昔子糾爭立而小白入齊，內無所稟，上無所承，白亦猶之糾也，而《春秋》獨繫之齊者，何哉？君子曰：少不先長，分也；位定於分，制也。臨淄之地，白所宜居，而觀於管仲之功，尤
translation_en:
… this one. As for Xing suffering the disaster brought by the Di tribes, a single brigade could have repelled them; yet the army halted at Niebei, waiting until Xing relocated before walling its city—was this not nurturing disorder so as to claim credit for oneself? Alas! As for the criticism of his thin virtue, Duke Huan certainly brought it upon himself.

"Xiaobai of Qi entered Qi" [9th year of Duke Zhuang]; "The Duke met with men of Qi and men of Song to rescue Zheng" [28th year of Duke Zhuang]; "Men of Qi rescued Xing" [1st year of Duke Min]; "In autumn, in the eighth month, the feudal lords covenanted at Shouzhi" [5th year of Duke Xi]; "In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, the feudal lords covenanted at Kuiqiu" [9th year of Duke Xi].
Peng Shangying
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Tao: The status, duty, and meritorious efforts of ruler and minister are summarized without omission, while the argument is upright and grand, deeply grasping the style of stringing together Spring and Autumn passages; it should be recorded as a model for those who illuminate the Classics.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu: Not fettered by the literal wording, he alone gives full expression to the fundamental purport.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jiang: Right and wrong are settled by the Sage; Duke Huan and Guan Zhong would surely be convinced at heart.

The Spring and Autumn Annals clarifies that the successor ruler ought to be enthroned, and accordingly approves the achievements of his minister. Now, Duke Huan's possession of Qi was proper according to his status; judging from the fact that Guan Zhong's achievements were not repudiated in the world, does it not show all the more clearly that Duke Huan ought to have been enthroned? In the past, when Zijiu contended for the throne and Xiaobai entered Qi, within the state there was no command to receive and above there was no mandate from the king to inherit—Xiaobai was in the same position as Jiu. Why then did the Spring and Autumn Annals alone attach "Qi" to his name? The gentleman says: That the younger does not precede the elder is a matter of status; that the throne is settled by status is the institution. The territory of Linzi was where Xiaobai ought to dwell, and when one looks at the achievements of Guan Zhong, it is especially…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
足徵焉蓋君子能爲可用而不能必用故必事
君以自顯亦必得君而有成也若仲之事桓豈
苟且以赴功名之會者哉徙義致主既以其才
而成當時之富强長慮遠謀又以其身而係天
下之輕重故桓之時夷狄橫矣中國諸侯誰與
安之乃仲獨相桓而以其節制之師一救乎鄭
再救乎邢焉冠裳鱗介凜然其防而夷不敢以
干夏者非其廟筭之鎭定乎桓之時周道衰矣
中國諸侯誰其尊之乃仲獨相桓而以其秩序
===
之經一盟首止再盟葵丘焉國儲王禁昭然其
分而下不敢以僭上者非其偉略之運用乎故
功在當時則當時稱其仁功在後世則後世蒙
其賜萬世公論定於聖人而獨於仲亟許之信
乎仲之無可議也而仲之所事者復何議哉故
曰小白之當立也雖然夫子之許仲固謂其擇
君而成事也乃不能致桓於王道而伯業且未
竟焉則仲豈粹然無議者乎噫學術既定伯不
可以王矣若射鈞之戒仲固諄諄而桓自怠焉
punctuated: 足徵焉。蓋君子能爲可用，而不能必用；故必事君以自顯，亦必得君而有成也。若仲之事桓，豈苟且以赴功名之會者哉？徙義致主，既以其才而成當時之富强；長慮遠謀，又以其身而係天下之輕重。故桓之時，夷狄橫矣，中國諸侯誰與安之？乃仲獨相桓，而以其節制之師，一救乎鄭，再救乎邢焉。冠裳鱗介，凜然其防，而夷不敢以干夏者，非其廟筭之鎭定乎？桓之時，周道衰矣，中國諸侯誰其尊之？乃仲獨相桓，而以其秩序之經，一盟首止，再盟葵丘焉。國儲王禁，昭然其分，而下不敢以僭上者，非其偉略之運用乎？故功在當時，則當時稱其仁；功在後世，則後世蒙其賜。萬世公論定於聖人，而獨於仲亟許之，信乎仲之無可議也，而仲之所事者復何議哉？故曰小白之當立也。雖然，夫子之許仲，固謂其擇君而成事也；乃不能致桓於王道，而伯業且未竟焉，則仲豈粹然無議者乎？噫！學術既定，伯不可以王矣；若射鈞之戒，仲固諄諄，而桓自怠焉，
translation_en: …suffices as proof of this. For a gentleman can make himself worthy of employment, yet he cannot guarantee that he will be employed; therefore, just as he must serve a ruler in order to distinguish himself, he must also find the right ruler in order to achieve success. When it came to Guan Zhong's (仲) service to Duke Huan (桓), how could he have been someone who compromised his principles merely to seize an opportunity for merit and fame? Turning toward righteousness and devoting himself to his lord, he used his talents to achieve wealth and power in his own time; with far-reaching foresight and deep planning, he bore upon his own person the weight of the entire realm. Thus, in the time of Duke Huan, when the barbarian tribes ran rampant, who among the feudal lords of the Central States could bring peace to them? Yet Guan Zhong alone served as minister to Duke Huan, and with his disciplined armies rescued Zheng (鄭) once and rescued Xing (邢) a second time. That the barrier between those in caps and robes and the scaly creatures stood in awe-inspiring strictness, so that the barbarians did not dare to encroach upon the Chinese states (夏)—was this not due to the stabilizing power of his court strategies? In the time of Duke Huan, when the Way of Zhou (周) had declined, who among the feudal lords of the Central States revered it? Yet Guan Zhong alone served as minister to Duke Huan, and through his principles of hierarchical order, he forged a covenant once at Shouzhi (首止) and a second time at Kuiqiu (葵丘). That the distinctions regarding the royal heir apparent and the king's prohibitions were made manifestly clear, so that inferiors did not dare to usurp the place of superiors—was this not due to the exercise of his grand strategy? Therefore, because his achievements benefited his own time, his contemporaries praised his benevolence; because his achievements benefited later generations, posterity received his blessings. The impartial judgment of ten thousand generations was settled by the Sage, who repeatedly and uniquely praised Guan Zhong. Truly, Guan Zhong is beyond reproach—and how, then, could the ruler whom Guan Zhong served be open to reproach? Thus it is said that Xiaobai (小白) was the one who ought to have been enthroned. Even so, the Master's praise of Guan Zhong surely meant that he chose the right ruler and accomplished great deeds; yet he was unable to lead Duke Huan to the Kingly Way, and even the enterprise of hegemony was left unfinished—so how could Guan Zhong be entirely free of criticism? Alas! Once his learning and statecraft were fixed in their course, hegemony could no longer be transformed into true kingship. As for the warning of the arrow that struck the belt-hook [reading 鈞 as 鉤], Guan Zhong indeed gave earnest and repeated counsel, yet Duke Huan himself grew lax…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
則非仲之罪也伯業且然而況於王道乎有世
道之責者可以思矣
禮記
五官致貢曰享
吳璨
同考試官教諭徐批君權臣職發揮詳確苦心之士
世之志者高薦尤宜
考試官教諭劉批一氣呵成全無斧鑿
考試官教諭蔣批治貴考成是作得之
===
人臣獻功之典而明尊君之義焉夫列卿分職
人君所以成治功也因時而獻其成謂非以尊
君乎且夫帝王之建官也必分任而後可以廣
佐理之猷必考成而後可以明激勸之義今五
官各有所寄矣然豈無以稽其成哉故歲會之
時則庶績可以咸熙而舉其積累之所致者敷
奏於九重之上百工可以用乂而卽其省試之
所効者備陳於五位之前禮樂刑政吾其述之
不敢隱也而賞罰之權惟宸衷之獨斷焉工虞
punctuated:
則非仲之罪也。伯業且然，而況於王道乎？有世道之責者可以思矣。

《禮記》
「五官致貢曰享。」
吳璨
同考試官教諭徐批：君權臣職，發揮詳確，苦心之士，世之志者，高薦尤宜。
考試官教諭劉批：一氣呵成，全無斧鑿。
考試官教諭蔣批：治貴考成，是作得之。

人臣獻功之典，而明尊君之義焉。夫列卿分職，人君所以成治功也；因時而獻其成，謂非以尊君乎？且夫帝王之建官也，必分任而後可以廣佐理之猷，必考成而後可以明激勸之義。今五官各有所寄矣，然豈無以稽其成哉？故歲會之時，則庶績可以咸熙，而舉其積累之所致者，敷奏於九重之上；百工可以用乂，而卽其省試之所効者，備陳於五位之前。禮樂刑政，吾其述之不敢隱也，而賞罰之權，惟宸衷之獨斷焉；工虞
translation_en:
…then it was not Guan Zhong’s fault. If even hegemonic enterprise was thus, how much more so the Kingly Way! Those who bear responsibility for the Way of the world may well ponder this.

Record of Rites (Liji)
"When the five officers present their achievements, it is called an offering (xiang)."
Wu Can 吳璨
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xu 徐: The sovereign's authority and the ministers' duties are expounded in a detailed and precise manner. A scholar of painstaking diligence and one with ambitions for the world [?]—it is especially fitting to recommend him highly.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu 劉: Written in a single breath, completely without trace of artificial chiseling.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣: Governance values the evaluation of completed achievements; this composition has grasped that.

[The Classic records] the statute for ministers presenting their achievements, and thereby clarifies the principle of honoring the sovereign. Now, arranging the high ministers and dividing their duties is the means by which the sovereign accomplishes the achievements of governance; presenting their completed results at the proper season—can this be said not to be a way of honoring the sovereign? Moreover, when emperors and kings establish offices, they must divide responsibilities before they can broaden the plans of administrative assistance, and they must evaluate completed work before they can clarify the principle of encouragement and stimulation. Now the five officers have each been entrusted with their respective charges, yet how could there be no means to examine their completed results? Therefore, at the time of the annual accounting, when the myriad achievements can all be made resplendent, they take what they have brought about through cumulative effort and set it forth in memorials before the ninefold gates of the throne; when the hundred officials can thereby bring about order, they take the results demonstrated under inspection and trial and lay them out in full before the sovereign's seat. Rites, music, punishments, and administration—we recount them without daring to conceal anything, while the authority to reward and punish rests solely with the independent judgment of the imperial mind; public works, natural resources,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
教養吾其述之不敢飾也而黜陟之典惟大君
之是聽焉如是而不謂之享乎蓋其一德以尊
天子而效忠宣力咸輸靖獻之忱匪懈以事一
人而積事程功恪守對揚之義雖非方物之獻
也而天工之敷奏均自下而致之上焉則其享
也以誠不以文而一心之精白固肅然其不敢
懈也當其時使朝無倖位者不以此乎雖非廷
實之供也而天職之備陳均自卑而達之尊焉
則其享也以敬不以物而一念之虔恭固凜乎
===
其不敢擅也當其時使官無惰政者不以此乎
吁即五官之貢而總於天官者可知矣上有定
權下無佚志此先王之治不可及也抑六卿左
右天子分隆而情亦親矣乃以綜核之權御之
毋亦過乎噫事必有敘政必有綱人君責諸六
卿六卿綜乎百職分任責成天下不勞而理矣
彼下行臣職固非體要而姑息太過者遂不免
於積弛焉此乾綱之斷君道所以隆也
祀帝於郊敬之至也宗廟之祭仁之至也
punctuated:
教養，吾其述之不敢飾也，而黜陟之典惟大君之是聽焉。如是而不謂之享乎？蓋其一德以尊天子，而效忠宣力，咸輸靖獻之忱；匪懈以事一人，而積事程功，恪守對揚之義。雖非方物之獻也，而天工之敷奏，均自下而致之上焉，則其享也以誠不以文，而一心之精白，固肅然其不敢懈也。當其時，使朝無倖位者，不以此乎？雖非廷實之供也，而天職之備陳，均自卑而達之尊焉，則其享也以敬不以物，而一念之虔恭，固凜乎其不敢擅也。當其時，使官無惰政者，不以此乎？吁！即五官之貢，而總於天官者可知矣。上有定權，下無佚志，此先王之治不可及也。抑六卿左右天子，分隆而情亦親矣，乃以綜核之權御之，毋亦過乎？噫！事必有敘，政必有綱。人君責諸六卿，六卿綜乎百職，分任責成，天下不勞而理矣。彼下行臣職，固非體要，而姑息太過者，遂不免於積弛焉。此乾綱之斷，君道所以隆也。

祀帝於郊，敬之至也；宗廟之祭，仁之至也。
translation_en:
…education and nourishment—we report upon them without daring to embellish; and the statutes of demotion and promotion are left solely to the judgment of the Great Sovereign. Being thus, can this not be called making an offering (xiang)? For with united virtue they honor the Son of Heaven, and in devoting their loyalty and exerting their strength, they all pour forth the sincerity of quiet dedication; unremittingly they serve the One Man, and in accumulating achievements and measuring merit, they reverently uphold the principle of responding to and extolling his grace. Although it is not a presentation of local tribute goods, the reporting on Heaven's work is equally conveyed from below up to the superior; thus their offering is made through sincerity rather than outward form, and the pure integrity of their single heart is truly solemn and dares not be remiss. At that time, was it not because of this that the court had no undeserved positions? Although it is not a provision of gifts filling the court, the full account of Heaven's offices is equally communicated from the humble up to the exalted; thus their offering is made through reverence rather than material things, and the devout respect of their single thought is truly awestruck and dares not presume. At that time, was it not because of this that officials had no neglectful governance? Ah! From the tribute of achievement of the Five Offices, that which is gathered under the Minister of State (Tianguan) can be known. Above, there is fixed authority; below, there are no wayward ambitions—this is why the governance of the former kings cannot be equaled. Yet the Six Ministers assist the Son of Heaven to his left and right; their status is exalted and their bond is intimate. To govern them by the power of comprehensive verification—is that not going too far? Alas! Affairs must have order, and governance must have a guiding cord. The ruler holds the Six Ministers accountable, and the Six Ministers oversee the hundred offices; by dividing responsibilities and demanding results, the realm is put in order without toil. Descending to perform the duties of ministers oneself is certainly not the essential principle of governance, yet those who are overly indulgent inevitably end in accumulated laxity. It is through this decisive exercise of sovereign authority that the Way of the Ruler flourishes.

"Sacrificing to the Supreme Lord in the suburbs is the ultimate of reverence; the sacrifice in the ancestral temple is the ultimate of benevolence."

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
侯師皐
同考試官教諭徐批形容聖人仁敬之德字字句句
皆出心精乃藝苑中不多得者也錄之
考試官教諭劉批發敭奧旨非摸軀殻
考試官教諭蔣批詞意備精尤多卓識
觀先王之享天親而各盡其心焉蓋祭之義生
於心也仁敬各極其至其先王之所以享天親
者乎且夫先王之致祭固以將崇報之忱亦必
有感孚之本吾觀於禮而知其德矣彼聖人奉
===
皇天之大統嘗於南郊而祀之藁靺之薦象其
性焉陶匏之用居其樸焉是固以質爲貴矣然
豈崇儉而廢禮乎蓋德產精微舉天下之物無
足以稱其大者故大報無事於彌文而明禋必
肅於內志小心翼翼猶懼其對越之或違也昭
格遲遲猶懼其禮度之或愆也蓋以精白之衷
而仰契乎玄穹之理則至敬無文雖燔柴不爲
略矣非敬之至而何哉聖人承祖考之丕緒嘗
於宗廟而祀之以順天時陰陽具陳焉以盡地
punctuated:
侯師皐
同考試官教諭徐批：「形容聖人仁敬之德，字字句句皆出心精，乃藝苑中不多得者也。錄之。」
考試官教諭劉批：「發敭奧旨，非摸軀殻。」
考試官教諭蔣批：「詞意備精，尤多卓識。」

觀先王之享天親，而各盡其心焉。蓋祭之義生於心也，仁敬各極其至，其先王之所以享天親者乎！且夫先王之致祭，固以將崇報之忱，亦必有感孚之本，吾觀於禮而知其德矣。彼聖人奉皇天之大統，嘗於南郊而祀之。藁靺之薦，象其性焉；陶匏之用，居其樸焉。是固以質爲貴矣，然豈崇儉而廢禮乎？蓋德產精微，舉天下之物無足以稱其大者，故大報無事於彌文，而明禋必肅於內志。小心翼翼，猶懼其對越之或違也；昭格遲遲，猶懼其禮度之或愆也。蓋以精白之衷，而仰契乎玄穹之理，則至敬無文，雖燔柴不爲略矣。非敬之至而何哉？聖人承祖考之丕緒，嘗於宗廟而祀之。以順天時，陰陽具陳焉；以盡地…
translation_en:
Hou Shigao 侯師皐

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐: "In depicting the sage's virtues of benevolence and reverence, every word and sentence comes from the essence of the mind. It is a rare piece in the realm of letters. Record it."
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉: "It brings forth the profound meaning, rather than merely tracing the outer shell."
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣: "Both the diction and the ideas are thoroughly refined, and it is especially rich in outstanding insight."

Observe how the former kings made offerings to Heaven and to their kin, and how in each case they exhausted their minds therein. Indeed, the meaning of sacrifice arises from the mind; carrying benevolence and reverence each to its utmost—is this not whereby the former kings made offerings to Heaven and to their kin? Moreover, when the former kings performed sacrifices, while they certainly did so to convey the sincerity of their veneration and repayment, there also necessarily had to be a foundation for moving and inspiring trust; I observe the rites and thereby know their virtue. The sage, upholding the grand succession of August Heaven, once sacrificed to It in the southern suburb. The mat of straw on which offerings are placed represents Its nature; the use of earthenware and gourds abides in simplicity. This certainly values unadorned substance, yet how could it mean exalting frugality to the neglect of ritual? For the generative power of Heaven's virtue is subtle and profound, and taking all the things in the world, none is sufficient to match Its greatness. Therefore, the Great Repayment has no need for elaborate ornament, whereas the pure sacrifice must be made reverent through inner intent. Cautious and circumspect, he still fears lest in standing before Heaven he might in some way transgress; waiting long for the bright manifestation of Its presence, he still fears lest his ritual measures might in some way err. For when with a pure and spotless heart one looks up to accord with the principles of the dark vault of Heaven, then the utmost reverence needs no ornament, and even burning firewood on the altar is not considered cursory. What is this if not the utmost of reverence? The sage, inheriting the great patrimony of his ancestors, once sacrificed to them in the ancestral temple. To accord with the seasons of Heaven, the products of yin and yang are all set forth; to exhaust the [bounties of] earth…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
利水土咸列焉是固以多爲貴矣然豈侈文而
無實乎蓋親恩罔極竭天下之物猶不足以稱
其心者故愛慕旣篤於由衷而聚順必隆於繼
孝心惕而奉之以禮九州之美所必竭也愛博
而將之以文萬國之懽所必聚也蓋以不匱之
思而求盡吾圖報之念則至仁無巳卽備物猶
爲歉矣非仁之至而何哉夫敬至則見天於心
矣仁至則見親於心矣先王舉大典而天親交
享者信非恃其禮也蓋天親一致仁孝一理惟
===
心源瑩而俯仰無愧焉則亦臨亦保卽以事親
而善繼善述天心用豫矣若興思於雨露致敬
於繭栗特其文耳豈仁孝之實哉噫爲天地宗
廟之主者當知合一之義矣
第貳塲
論
明君德業配天
楊應兆
同考試官學正梁批虛心受善乃帝王德業之本諸作
punctuated:
利，水土咸列焉，是固以多爲貴矣，然豈侈文而無實乎？蓋親恩罔極，竭天下之物猶不足以稱其心者，故愛慕旣篤於由衷，而聚順必隆於繼孝。心惕而奉之以禮，九州之美所必竭也；愛博而將之以文，萬國之懽所必聚也。蓋以不匱之思，而求盡吾圖報之念，則至仁無巳，卽備物猶爲歉矣，非仁之至而何哉？夫敬至則見天於心矣，仁至則見親於心矣。先王舉大典而天親交享者，信非恃其禮也。蓋天親一致，仁孝一理，惟心源瑩而俯仰無愧焉，則亦臨亦保，卽以事親；而善繼善述，天心用豫矣。若興思於雨露，致敬於繭栗，特其文耳，豈仁孝之實哉？噫！爲天地宗廟之主者，當知合一之義矣。

第貳塲
論
明君德業配天
楊應兆
同考試官學正梁批：虛心受善，乃帝王德業之本。諸作
translation_en:
…resources of the earth, the products of water and land are all arrayed therein. This indeed prizes abundance; yet how could it be extravagant in ornament while lacking in substance? For the grace of one's parents is boundless, and exhausting all the things in the world would still not suffice to match one's heart. Therefore, since loving longing is already sincere from within, the gathering of harmony must be abundantly manifested in continuing filial piety. With a vigilant heart, one serves them with ritual, and the finest products of the Nine Provinces must be exhausted; with broad love, one presents it with refinement, and the joyful allegiance of the myriad states must be gathered. For when, with unfailing remembrance, one seeks to fulfill one's desire to repay them, supreme benevolence knows no end, and even preparing all things still feels insufficient. What is this if not the utmost of benevolence?

Now, when reverence reaches the utmost, one beholds Heaven in one's heart; when benevolence reaches the utmost, one beholds one's parents in one's heart. That the former kings performed the great ceremonies and both Heaven and parents enjoyed the offerings was truly not because they relied merely on ritual forms. For Heaven and parents are of one unity, and benevolence and filial piety are of one principle. Only when the wellspring of the heart is pure and one feels no shame looking up or down can one, as if overseen and protected by Heaven, thereby serve one's parents; and by skillfully continuing their wills and carrying forward their affairs, the heart of Heaven is thereby delighted. As for being moved to remembrance by the falling of rain and dew, or offering reverence with a calf having horns the size of a cocoon or chestnut, these are merely outward forms—how could they be the substance of benevolence and filial piety? Alas! He who serves as the lord of Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple ought to understand the meaning of their unity.

Second Session
Discourse
"The Enlightened Ruler's Virtue and Achievements Match Heaven"
Yang Yingzhao

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
多涉汗漫而子獨能根究題旨發揮殆盡且體裁高古議論開闢後場
抑揚卓有奇氣策言讜誼素積於衷者取冠多士非直以其文也
考試官敎諭劉批旨意詳盡氣格雄古積學之士也
考試官敎諭蔣批學富才雄氣昌議正優場之作也
帝王以身任天下之重而懋同天之化惟其心
之虛而已矣夫天下重器也治天下重務也而
人君以一身任其責則其厝注運量容非耳目
心思所能周而所操所履又足以厭其心而天
下之善未易達焉夫負至重之責而席易盈之
===
勢以不易達之善而欲濟其難周之務將何以
善治於不窮而比隆造化哉噫此明君所以虛
其心以來天下之善而盛德大業與天無極也
請申胡氏之論夫天者羣物之祖也高明覆幬
萬禩如新業至宏也玄化之樞凝而不汩德至
精也然節其運而不過制其序而不流虧盈益
謙之理旁皇周浹於兩儀四象之中故地道上
行萬物訢合虛而不屈動而愈出而先儒以谷
神不死虛室生白為得造化之精則天之道一
punctuated:
多涉汗漫，而子獨能根究題旨，發揮殆盡。且體裁高古，議論開闢；後場抑揚，卓有奇氣；策言讜誼，素積於衷者。取冠多士，非直以其文也。
考試官敎諭劉批：旨意詳盡，氣格雄古，積學之士也。
考試官敎諭蔣批：學富才雄，氣昌議正，優場之作也。
帝王以身任天下之重，而懋同天之化，惟其心之虛而已矣。夫天下，重器也；治天下，重務也。而人君以一身任其責，則其厝注運量，容非耳目心思所能周；而所操所履，又足以厭其心，而天下之善未易達焉。夫負至重之責，而席易盈之勢，以不易達之善，而欲濟其難周之務，將何以善治於不窮，而比隆造化哉？噫！此明君所以虛其心以來天下之善，而盛德大業與天無極也。請申胡氏之論。夫天者，羣物之祖也。高明覆幬，萬禩如新，業至宏也；玄化之樞，凝而不汩，德至精也。然節其運而不過，制其序而不流，虧盈益謙之理，旁皇周浹於兩儀四象之中。故地道上行，萬物訢合，虛而不屈，動而愈出。而先儒以「谷神不死」、「虛室生白」為得造化之精，則天之道一…
translation_en:
…mostly stray into diffuse rambling, yet you alone are able to trace the root of the topic's meaning and expound it almost exhaustively. Moreover, the style is lofty and ancient, and the arguments open up new ground; in the later sessions, the cadence and modulation stand out with extraordinary vigor; and the policy essays speak with forthright counsel that has long been stored in your heart. Selecting you to head the multitude of scholars is not merely on account of your literary style.
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: The purport is thorough and complete, the spirit and form vigorous and ancient—a scholar of accumulated learning.
Examiner and Instructor Jiang comments: Rich in learning and bold in talent, with flourishingvitality and upright arguments—an outstanding work of the examination compound.
For an emperor or king to take upon his own person the heavy burden of the world and strive for transformations matching those of Heaven, it comes down solely to the emptiness of his mind—its receptivity—and nothing more. Now, the empire is a heavy vessel, and governing the empire is a heavy task. When a ruler takes responsibility for it in his single person, his arrangements, measures, and scope of operation cannot possibly be fully encompassed by his own ears, eyes, and thoughts alone; yet what he holds and occupies is sufficient to satisfy his own mind, so that the good counsel of the world cannot easily reach him. Carrying the heaviest of responsibilities while seated in a position prone to self-satisfaction, and wishing to accomplish tasks difficult to encompass by means of good counsel that does not easily reach him—how then shall he achieve good governance without end and match the grandeur of nature's creative transformation? Alas! This is why an enlightened ruler empties his mind to invite the good of the entire world, so that his splendid virtue and great achievement are boundless along with Heaven. Allow me to elaborate upon Master Hu's thesis.
Now, Heaven is the ancestor of all things. High, bright, and overarching, through ten thousand generations it remains as new—its achievement is vast indeed; the pivot of mysterious transformation coalesces without being muddled—its virtue is most refined. Yet it regulates its revolutions without excess and orders its sequence without aberration, as the principle of diminishing the full and augmenting the humble pervades everywhere within the Two Modes and Four Emblems. Therefore the Way of Earth ascends, the myriad things joyfully harmonize, being empty yet inexhaustible, moving and bringing forth ever more. And since earlier Confucians regarded "the valley spirit never dies" and "an empty chamber engenders brightness" as capturing the essence of creative transformation, the Way of Heaven is entirely…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
虛也虛則通萬物爲一氣而德業不毁也顧天
之於物既非根極靜篤希夷恬寂聽其自榮自
瘁於大塊之中而雕刻衆形役役焉驅萬物而
馳驟之又其所不忍則寄吾之德業而囿萬物
於無窮者人君也人君代天之任則凡待命於
天者皆待命於我者也民吾民物吾物而蒸黎
而俊乂而疲癃疾苦而僻遠幽遐殊俗異類思
以便其性居其宜者莫非吾之一體而禮樂刑
政所以整齊而約束之皆其具之不容廢者也
===
卽使聰明神智高出等夷役而用之既不勝其
勞瘁而自用者不裕自是者不張天下之務遺
於聰明神智之外者多矣且位則天位祿則天
祿喜爲湛露怒爲震霆薄海內外非特不敢矯
命雄行而睨視跂望且以爲畏其環吾身而處
者又多奔走希覬諛治安而導佚樂以便其圖
安之私蓋臣志士分在得言者忸怩於利害而
不敢盡勢在可言者疎遠於日隔而不得盡卽
有攄衷款素思盡繩糾之分而批鱗苦口之說
punctuated: 虛也。虛則通萬物爲一氣，而德業不毁也。顧天之於物，既非根極靜篤、希夷恬寂，聽其自榮自瘁於大塊之中；而雕刻衆形，役役焉驅萬物而馳驟之，又其所不忍。則寄吾之德業，而囿萬物於無窮者，人君也。人君代天之任，則凡待命於天者，皆待命於我者也。民吾民，物吾物，而蒸黎，而俊乂，而疲癃疾苦，而僻遠幽遐、殊俗異類，思以便其性、居其宜者，莫非吾之一體；而禮樂刑政，所以整齊而約束之，皆其具之不容廢者也。卽使聰明神智高出等夷，役而用之，既不勝其勞瘁，而自用者不裕，自是者不張，天下之務遺於聰明神智之外者多矣。且位則天位，祿則天祿，喜爲湛露，怒爲震霆，薄海內外，非特不敢矯命雄行，而睨視跂望，且以爲畏；其環吾身而處者，又多奔走希覬，諛治安而導佚樂，以便其圖安之私。蓋臣志士，分在得言者，忸怩於利害而不敢盡；勢在可言者，疎遠於日隔而不得盡。卽有攄衷款素，思盡繩糾之分，而批鱗苦口之說，
translation_en: …emptiness. Through emptiness, it connects the myriad things as a single vital force, so that its virtue and achievements are never destroyed. However, in Heaven's relation to things, on the one hand it is not rooted in extreme stillness and quietude—inaudible, invisible, and serenely detached—leaving things to flourish or wither by themselves upon the great earth; on the other hand, to carve and chisel the multitude of forms, toilfully driving the myriad things to gallop about, is also what it cannot bear to do. Therefore, the one to whom Heaven entrusts its virtue and achievements, so as to encompass the myriad things endlessly, is the ruler of men. Since the ruler of men takes on the responsibility on behalf of Heaven, all who await their mandate from Heaven are awaiting their mandate from him. The people are my people, and things are my things; the multitude of commoners, the men of talent and virtue, the crippled, infirm, and suffering, as well as those in remote and obscure regions with different customs and of alien kinds—all who long to find comfort for their natures and dwell in what suits them—are none of them not of one body with me. And rites, music, punishments, and governance—the means by which to order and restrain them—are all instruments that cannot be dispensed with. Even if one's intelligence and divine wisdom far surpass those of one's peers, to tax and employ them alone would not only bring unbearable exhaustion, for he who relies solely on himself will lack abundance, and he who considers himself always right will fail to expand; thus, the affairs of the world left outside the reach of his intelligence and divine wisdom would be many indeed. Moreover, his position is the Heaven-ordained position, and his emolument is the Heaven-ordained emolument; his joy is like soaking dew, and his wrath is like crashing thunder. Within and beyond the seas, people not only dare not defy his commands or act wilfully, but even when glancing sidelong or standing on tiptoe to look from afar, they regard him with awe. Meanwhile, those who dwell around his person mostly bustle about in greedy anticipation, flattering him about peace and order and leading him toward ease and pleasure, so as to serve their own selfish schemes for personal security. Loyal ministers [?] and men of high principle whose duty entitles them to speak out shrink back in hesitation over considerations of benefit and harm, daring not speak to the fullest; those whose position would allow them to speak are kept at a distance by daily estrangement, unable to speak to the fullest. Even if there are those who pour out their sincere and unadorned feelings, hoping to fulfill their duty of remonstrance and correction, yet words that brush against the dragon's reverse scales and are bitter to the mouth…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
又不足以投人主之意嚮而滋其所疑故天下
之庸默自保者日益衆焉善言旣壅驕侈易生
自身心性情以至設施舉措將日戾於天則而
終於不可支矣乃英明之主獨念其長於崇臺
邃闥之中坐於勾陳負扆之內旣不得周知天
下之利便疾苦而投歡獻媚者又壅遏吾之聰
明而一睫之外有泰華矣乃復狃以為便而使
陳善責難者萌悔心焉豈計哉故威命靈爽侔
乎造化不敢侈也甘言諛行滿乎耳目不敢縱
===
也明照萬物而下芻蕘權總六合而先瞽御造
膝而陳敷心而告大臣之善也吾勤召對隆禮
貌而納之折檻而諫排闥而語諫官之善也吾
忘喜怒借顏色而容之衣食而詔菲服御而導
儉彤管紀過御瞽幾聲左右之善也吾黜忌諱
降勢分而容之推而工誦史箴士傳民謗舉天
下之人苟有規吾之闕失者卽使危言激論大
非人情之所堪而吾且以藥石愈於粱肉鍼砭
優於歡洽欣欣然樂而聽聽而用惟懼其言之
punctuated: 又不足以投人主之意嚮，而滋其所疑，故天下之庸默自保者日益衆焉。善言旣壅，驕侈易生，自身心性情以至設施舉措，將日戾於天則，而終於不可支矣。乃英明之主，獨念其長於崇臺邃闥之中，坐於勾陳負扆之內，旣不得周知天下之利便疾苦，而投歡獻媚者又壅遏吾之聰明，而一睫之外有泰華矣；乃復狃以為便，而使陳善責難者萌悔心焉，豈計哉？故威命靈爽侔乎造化，不敢侈也；甘言諛行滿乎耳目，不敢縱也；明照萬物而下芻蕘，權總六合而先瞽御。造膝而陳、敷心而告，大臣之善也，吾勤召對、隆禮貌而納之；折檻而諫、排闥而語，諫官之善也，吾忘喜怒、借顏色而容之；衣食而詔菲、服御而導儉、彤管紀過、御瞽幾聲，左右之善也，吾黜忌諱、降勢分而容之。推而工誦、史箴、士傳、民謗，舉天下之人，苟有規吾之闕失者，卽使危言激論，大非人情之所堪，而吾且以藥石愈於粱肉、鍼砭優於歡洽，欣欣然樂而聽、聽而用，惟懼其言之
translation_en:
…are moreover insufficient to cater to the ruler's inclinations, instead only increasing his doubts. Consequently, throughout the realm, those who remain mediocre and silent to preserve themselves grow ever more numerous by the day. Once good counsel is blocked, arrogance and extravagance easily arise; from one's own mind, body, nature, and emotions to policy measures and administrative actions, everything will daily violate the principles of Heaven, until at last it becomes unsustainable.

Yet an enlightened ruler reflects specifically on how, having grown up amid lofty terraces and deep palace chambers, and sitting within the imperial guards before the ceremonial screen, he is already unable to thoroughly know the advantages, conveniences, hardships, and sufferings of the realm; meanwhile, those who court favor and offer flattery further obstruct his sight and hearing, so that right beyond his eyelashes stand Mount Tai and Mount Hua! If he then grows accustomed to this as convenient, causing those who set forth the good and demand difficult standards of their sovereign to conceive regret in their hearts—how could that be a wise plan?

Therefore, though his august commands and numinous splendor equal those of nature's creative forces, he dares not be extravagant; though sweet words and flattering deeds fill his ears and eyes, he dares not be self-indulgent. Though his intelligence illuminates the myriad things, he humbles himself before grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers; though his authority encompasses the six directions of the universe, he puts blind musicians and attendants first. Approaching the ruler's knee to set forth views and opening one's heart to offer counsel—this is the goodness of great ministers; I diligently summon them for audiences and treat them with exalted courtesy to accept their words. Breaking the balustrade in remonstrance and pushing open the palace doors to speak—this is the goodness of remonstrance officials; I set aside joy and anger and lend them a welcoming countenance to tolerate them. In matters of clothing and food, urging frugality; in apparel and carriages, guiding toward thrift; recording faults with the red-lacquered brush; and having blind musicians examine the court music—this is the goodness of close attendants; I cast aside taboos and humble my exalted status to tolerate them. Extending this further to artisans reciting admonitions, scribes offering exhortations, scholars passing on counsel, and the common people voicing criticisms—among all the people of the realm, if anyone admonishes me regarding my failings and errors, even if their alarming words and vehement arguments are utterly beyond what ordinary human feelings can bear, I shall regard medicinal stones as better than fine grain and meat, and acupuncture needles as superior to jovial harmony, gladly listening to them with delight and putting what I hear to use, fearing only that their words…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不詳焉則上無佚志下無隱忠天下之士明目
張膽畢獻其善於吾前而砥礪既深嗜欲必寡
氣完而無妄動神定而無越思伐性斵真之斧
不得內滑其和而潛真守一炯炯洞洞皆天心
也出之以照天下顧有壅而不理者哉是故衣
食於饑寒拊循於疾苦居居于于帝力何有蒸
黎得其所焉論材而官程功而進勞勩者不抑
所能而巧猾者蔑以行其私俊乂得其敘焉刖
者闇而瞽者師薪不童而漁不竭禽獸可繫羈
===
而遊鵲巢可攀援而闚而雕題辮髮將梯山航
海求以被承德澤則疲癃殘疾異類遐荒莫不
若其性焉進而臧否陟罰紀綱號令犁然當於
天道人心而百靈敘秩五緯順布莫非禮樂之
敷賁焉則剛健中正吾心之於穆也高明悠乆
吾心之奠麗也景星慶雲河清海晏吾心之熈
明而愉快也大德不德與天同體大業不業與
天同用吾之德業安乎一世之人卽千百世之
人安乎千百世之人卽一世之天矣萬世之
punctuated: 不詳焉，則上無佚志，下無隱忠，天下之士明目張膽，畢獻其善於吾前。而砥礪既深，嗜欲必寡，氣完而無妄動，神定而無越思，伐性斵真之斧不得內滑其和，而潛真守一，炯炯洞洞，皆天心也。出之以照天下，顧有壅而不理者哉？是故衣食於饑寒，拊循於疾苦，居居于于，帝力何有，蒸黎得其所焉；論材而官，程功而進，勞勩者不抑所能，而巧猾者蔑以行其私，俊乂得其敘焉；刖者闇而瞽者師，薪不童而漁不竭，禽獸可繫羈而遊，鵲巢可攀援而闚，而雕題辮髮將梯山航海，求以被承德澤，則疲癃殘疾、異類遐荒，莫不若其性焉。進而臧否陟罰、紀綱號令，犁然當於天道人心，而百靈敘秩，五緯順布，莫非禮樂之敷賁焉。則剛健中正，吾心之於穆也；高明悠乆，吾心之奠麗也；景星慶雲、河清海晏，吾心之熈明而愉快也。大德不德，與天同體；大業不業，與天同用。吾之德業安乎一世之人，卽千百世之人；安乎千百世之人，卽一世之天矣。萬世之
translation_en:
… not thorough enough. Then above there will be no dissolute ambitions, and below there will be no hidden loyalties; the scholars of the realm will open their eyes wide and summon their courage, offering up all their goodness before me. When self-cultivation is deep, sensual desires will surely be few; one's vital氣 (qi) will be whole without reckless agitation, and one's spirit settled without wayward thoughts. The axes that chop away at one's nature and hew at one's true essence will not be able to inwardly disturb one's harmony. Immersing oneself in truth and guarding unity, bright and pellucid—all this is the Mind of Heaven. Bringing it forth to illuminate the world, how could anything remain blocked up and ungoverned?

Therefore, clothing and feeding the hungry and cold, comforting and tending to the sick and suffering, people live in tranquil contentment, asking "What is the Emperor's power to us?"—thus the multitude of commoners find their proper place. Assessing talent to bestow office and measuring achievement to grant promotion, those who toil are not suppressed in their abilities while the cunning and crafty have no way to pursue their selfish ends—thus men of eminent talent find their proper order. Those with amputated feet serve as gatekeepers [reading 闇 as 閼/閽] and the blind serve as musicians; firewood is not stripped bare from the hills and fishing does not exhaust the waters; birds and beasts can be tethered and led about, and magpie nests can be climbed to and peered into; while those with tattooed foreheads and braided hair will scale mountains and sail the seas, seeking to receive and partake of virtuous beneficence—thus the infirm, crippled, exotic species, and distant wilds all follow their natural dispositions. 

Going further, evaluations of good and bad, promotions and punishments, and institutional principles and commands all accord clearly with the Way of Heaven and the minds of men; the hundred spirits are arrayed in order, and the five planets move smoothly in their courses—none of this is anything other than the radiant spread of rites and music. Thus, firm, vigorous, central, and correct—this is the profound solemnity of my mind; lofty, brilliant, and enduring—this is the settled attachment of my mind; auspicious stars and propitious clouds, a clear Yellow River and calm seas—this is the bright illumination and joyful harmony of my mind. Great virtue does not claim virtue, sharing the same substance as Heaven; great enterprise does not claim enterprise, sharing the same function as Heaven. If my virtue and enterprise bring peace to the people of one generation, they are the people of a thousand or a hundred generations; if they bring peace to the people of a thousand or a hundred generations, I am the Heaven of this one generation. For ten thousand generations…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
下德吾德業吾業而萬世之人舉安焉則爲萬
世之天矣又安得與造化論形體哉夫人君之
德莫盛乎乾而有亢龍之悔人君之業莫盛於
泰而有復隍之憂至於冥豫擊益惴惴然必謙
以居有豫始繼之何作易者之憂患若此耶大
都敵國外患不足爲人君之懼而恃天下無可
畏者則其大可畏者至焉蓋起於一念之盈也
滿心一恣貽患無窮謙德一崇保治無射故則
天如堯勅天如舜其德業之盛無以加矣然衢
===
室總章之訪每兢兢焉他若拜言得師四友十
輔言若甘飴歡若同體數聖人之心卽堯舜之
心故其德業卽堯舜之德業也彼其初豈故爲
卑鄙不斷之行萎然屈其萬乘之尊而道謀是
聽乎要以治理無窮而代天之責不敢負也彼
太甲成王繼體之賢者也惟其甘受逆心無逸
之語而令名迄今不衰向使其侈然以自大視
伊周之訓若贅焉則又安能必其爲何如主哉
噫山不動而人推高善容也海不運而人推廣
punctuated: 下，德吾德、業吾業，而萬世之人舉安焉，則爲萬世之天矣，又安得與造化論形體哉！夫人君之德莫盛乎《乾》，而有「亢龍」之悔；人君之業莫盛於《泰》，而有「復隍」之憂。至於「冥豫」、「擊益」，惴惴然必《謙》以居《有》、《豫》始繼之，何作《易》者之憂患若此耶？大都敵國外患不足爲人君之懼，而恃天下無可畏者，則其大可畏者至焉，蓋起於一念之盈也。滿心一恣，貽患無窮；謙德一崇，保治無射。故則天如堯，勅天如舜，其德業之盛無以加矣，然衢室、總章之訪，每兢兢焉。他若拜言、得師，四友、十輔，言若甘飴，歡若同體。數聖人之心，卽堯、舜之心；故其德業，卽堯、舜之德業也。彼其初豈故爲卑鄙不斷之行，萎然屈其萬乘之尊，而道謀是聽乎？要以治理無窮，而代天之責不敢負也。彼太甲、成王，繼體之賢者也，惟其甘受逆心、《無逸》之語，而令名迄今不衰。向使其侈然以自大，視伊、周之訓若贅焉，則又安能必其爲何如主哉！噫！山不動而人推高，善容也；海不運而人推廣，
translation_en:
… generations take my virtue as their virtue and my achievements as their achievements, so that the people of ten thousand generations are all brought to peace, then one becomes Heaven for ten thousand generations! How then could one merely discuss physical form alongside the creative forces of nature?

Now, the virtue of a ruler is never more flourishing than in the hexagram Qian (The Creative), yet there is the regret of the "arrogant dragon"; the achievement of a ruler is never more flourishing than in the hexagram Tai (Peace), yet there is the anxiety of the "city wall collapsing back into the moat." As for "deluded pleasure" (in the hexagram Yu) and "striking one who seeks increase" (in the hexagram Yi), why was the author of the Book of Changes (Yi) so filled with anxious concern that one must tremblingly dwell in Great Possession (Dayou) through Modesty (Qian) before Enthusiasm (Yu) can follow? In general, hostile states and external troubles are not enough to cause a ruler fear; rather, when he presumes that there is nothing in the world to be feared, then that which is truly to be feared arrives. This springs from a single thought of self-satisfaction. Once a self-satisfied mind is indulged, it leaves behind endless calamities; once the virtue of modesty is exalted, it preserves good order without fail.

Therefore, in modeling himself on Heaven like Yao, and in cautiously attending to Heaven's mandate like Shun, the flourishing of their virtue and achievements could not be surpassed. Yet in their inquiries in the Audience Hall (Qushi) and the Bright Hall (Zongzhang), they were always cautious and trembling. As for others—such as Yu, who bowed upon hearing good words, and Tang, who found a teacher; or King Wen with his Four Friends and King Wu with his Ten Assistants—they treated good counsel like sweet syrup and rejoiced in their ministers as though sharing a single body. The minds of these several sages were none other than the minds of Yao and Shun; therefore, their virtue and achievements were none other than the virtue and achievements of Yao and Shun. In the beginning, did they intentionally engage in lowly, demeaning, and indecisive conduct, listlessly humbling their majesty as lords of ten thousand chariots just to listen to the counsels of passersby on the road? The essential point was that the principles of governance are inexhaustible, and they dared not fail in their responsibility of acting on behalf of Heaven.

Taijia and King Cheng were worthy rulers who succeeded to the throne. Only because they willingly accepted words that grated on their minds and the admonitions of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) has their fine reputation remained undiminished to this day. Had they been extravagantly self-important and regarded the instructions of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou as superfluous, how could anyone be certain what sort of rulers they would have turned out to be?

Alas! The mountains do not move, yet men extol their height, because they are good at accommodating; the seas do not stir themselves, yet men extol their vastness, …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
善茹也人君不出戶牖而通天下爲一身善聽
也若衛士傳餐身兼臣職者則已訑訑然拒人
千里矣而欲語配天之治是却步而求前也之
數君者其求治之心不下於堯舜也顧堯舜居
已於虛而彼方恃其材智以求過於堯舜焉其
所操者不同也然猶所謂聰明深慧者也所謂
彊毅聰察者也而未之慧且毅者又將若之何
哉奈之何其恃所長而自隘其天也雖然君能
好善而不能使善言之必聞猶未好也臣能陳
===
善而不能使善言之必行猶未陳也故進言有
五要歸於誠若以忿躁激烈之私而滋浮浪迂
誕之語則上下相持而不相入惟其諭之以理
主之以誠登對自盟而不敢援之爲已功邀之
爲已名眞若幾諫其親而不拂於國體焉則至
誠感悟而吾之說行矣噫勿欺而犯信而後諫
此萬世臣道之極也
表
擬
punctuated:
善茹也；人君不出戶牖而通天下爲一身，善聽也。若衛士傳餐、身兼臣職者，則已訑訑然拒人千里矣，而欲語配天之治，是却步而求前也。之數君者，其求治之心不下於堯、舜也，顧堯、舜居已於虛，而彼方恃其材智以求過於堯、舜焉，其所操者不同也。然猶所謂聰明深慧者也，所謂彊毅聰察者也；而未之慧且毅者，又將若之何哉？奈之何其恃所長而自隘其天也！雖然，君能好善，而不能使善言之必聞，猶未好也；臣能陳善，而不能使善言之必行，猶未陳也。故進言有五，要歸於誠。若以忿躁激烈之私，而滋浮浪迂誕之語，則上下相持而不相入。惟其諭之以理，主之以誠，登對自盟，而不敢援之爲已功、邀之爲已名，眞若幾諫其親而不拂於國體焉，則至誠感悟，而吾之說行矣。噫！「勿欺而犯」、「信而後諫」，此萬世臣道之極也。

表

擬
translation_en:
…because it is good at absorbing all waters; and a ruler, without stepping outside his doors and windows, unites the entire world into a single body because he is good at listening. As for those who had palace guards pass them their meals while taking the duties of their ministers upon themselves, they already wore a self-satisfied air that kept others a thousand li away; to wish to speak of governance that matches Heaven in such a state is like walking backward while seeking to move forward. These several rulers had a desire for good governance no less than that of Yao and Shun; yet whereas Yao and Shun kept themselves in a state of receptivity, those rulers relied on their own talents and intelligence in seeking to surpass Yao and Shun—what they held to was different. Even so, they were still what may be called intelligent and deeply wise, or resolute and discerning; what then will become of those who are neither wise nor resolute? How can a ruler rely on his strengths only to narrow his own heaven-endowed capacity!

Even so, if a ruler is capable of loving the good, yet cannot ensure that good words are必ず heard, it is as though he does not yet love it; if a minister is capable of setting forth the good, yet cannot ensure that good words are put into practice, it is as though he has not yet set them forth. Therefore, although there are five ways of presenting advice, in essence they all come down to sincerity. If, out of private feelings of anger, impatience, and vehemence, one multiplies frivolous, unrestrained, impractical, and extravagant talk, then ruler and minister will stand at odds and fail to reach each other. Only when one enlightens the ruler through principle and grounds oneself in sincerity—pledging oneself when ascending to reply in audience, never daring to claim the advice as one's own merit or use it to seek personal fame, truly as if gently remonstrating with one's own parents without offending against the dignity of the state—will utmost sincerity move and awaken the ruler, and one's counsel be put into practice. Ah! "Do not deceive him, yet withstand him to his face," and "Only after winning his trust should one remonstrate"—these are the ultimate standard of the way of a minister for ten thousand generations.

Memorial

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
皇上幸太學禮成羣臣
賀表萬曆四年
楊同春
同考試官教諭徐批我
皇上心師至聖首舉臨雍將隆億萬年文明之治非特一時之慶也是作場厲閎休宛若躬逢
其盛者宜錄以傳
考試官教諭劉批揄揚
昭代盛典儀制具悉而崇儒重道語意藹然不止駢麗而已
考試官教諭蔣批才思充溢詞藻流麗可以彰盛美矣錄之
===
萬曆四年八月初二日臣某等恭遇
皇上
駕幸太學禮成臣等謹奉
表稱
賀者伏以
聖主右文
道建師儒之極
明王軌世
身先禮樂之宗風動八荒教傳千古宮牆洽
punctuated:
皇上幸太學禮成羣臣賀表〔萬曆四年〕

楊同春

同考試官教諭徐批：我皇上心師至聖，首舉臨雍，將隆億萬年文明之治，非特一時之慶也。是作場厲閎休，宛若躬逢其盛者，宜錄以傳。
考試官教諭劉批：揄揚昭代盛典，儀制具悉，而崇儒重道，語意藹然，不止駢麗而已。
考試官教諭蔣批：才思充溢，詞藻流麗，可以彰盛美矣。錄之。

萬曆四年八月初二日，臣某等恭遇皇上駕幸太學禮成，臣等謹奉表稱賀者。伏以聖主右文，道建師儒之極；明王軌世，身先禮樂之宗。風動八荒，教傳千古。宮牆洽…
translation_en:
…[Draft of a] Congratulatory Memorial from the Assembled Officials on the Completion of the Rites for His Majesty's Imperial Visit to the Directorate of Education [Fourth Year of Wanli (1576)].

Yang Tongchun 楊同春.

Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐 comments: Our August Emperor takes the Most Sage [Confucius] as the teacher of his mind and has inaugurated the ceremony of visiting the Imperial Academy, which will exalt a civil and enlightened rule for hundreds of millions of years—it is not merely a celebration for a single moment. This composition extols [?] the grand blessings as vividly as if the author had personally witnessed the splendor; it ought to be recorded and transmitted.
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: In praising the grand ceremony of our illustrious dynasty, the ritual regulations are fully detailed, while in honoring Confucian scholars and revering the Way, the words and ideas are gracious and harmonious—it goes beyond mere parallel-prose elegance.
Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: Brimming with talent and thought, with flowing and elegant diction, it suffices to manifest this grand beauty. Record it.

On the second day of the eighth month of the fourth year of the Wanli reign [August 25, 1576], Your servants so-and-so and others, having reverently encountered the completion of the rites for Your Majesty's imperial visit to the Directorate of Education, respectfully present this memorial of congratulation. Your servants humbly consider that the Sage Ruler esteems civil culture, his Way establishing the ultimate standard for teachers and scholars; the Enlightened King sets the norm for the world, in his own person taking the lead as the exemplar of rites and music. His moral influence stirs the eight wildernesses, and his teachings are transmitted for a thousand ages. Within the walls of the Academy, [joy] pervades…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
慶章掖增輝臣等誠懽誠抃稽首頓首竊
惟王政以敎化爲先義隆首善治世以人
才爲急道在崇儒唐堯特命司徒勞來匡
直虞舜留心胄學直簡寛温禮備兩庠執
醬執爵而養老學沿三代至德至行以明
倫慨自竹帛煙秦吾道光芒暫息幸而大
牢祀魯斯文氣脉潜回環冠帶於橋門徒
增視聽羣薪蒸於牧竪致慨蓁蕪東漢重
興授明經而謾誇車服有唐嗣起增學舘
===
而大召名儒載拜標侈乎虛文文治非元祐
横議鼎生於上舍道未煕寧豈若
昭代之弘規遂揭
中天之文運玆蓋恭遇
皇帝陛下
堯仁舜孝
禹儉湯寛
溥離照以撫
鴻圖
punctuated: 慶，章掖增輝。臣等誠懽誠抃，稽首頓首。竊惟王政以敎化爲先，義隆首善；治世以人才爲急，道在崇儒。唐堯特命司徒，勞來匡直；虞舜留心胄學，直簡寛温。禮備兩庠，執醬執爵而養老；學沿三代，至德至行以明倫。慨自竹帛煙秦，吾道光芒暫息；幸而大牢祀魯，斯文氣脉潜回。環冠帶於橋門，徒增視聽；羣薪蒸於牧竪，致慨蓁蕪。東漢重興，授明經而謾誇車服；有唐嗣起，增學舘而大召名儒。載拜標侈乎虛文，文治非元祐；横議鼎生於上舍，道未煕寧。豈若昭代之弘規，遂揭中天之文運！玆蓋恭遇皇帝陛下：堯仁舜孝，禹儉湯寛。溥離照以撫鴻圖，
translation_en: …rejoicing, and scholars in their robes add radiance. Your servants, truly joyful and truly elated, bow our heads to the ground. We humbly reflect that kingly governance takes moral transformation through education as its first priority, exalting the principle of establishing a model in the capital; ordering the world takes the cultivation of talent as its urgent task, and the Way lies in venerating Confucian scholars. Tang Yao specially charged the Minister of Education to encourage, attract, correct, and straighten the people; Yu Shun devoted his heart to the education of noble youths, teaching them to be upright yet mild, and broad-minded yet栗 [? gentle/firm: 寬溫]. Rites were complete in the two schools of the虞 and Xia, where the ruler personally held the sauce-jar and wine-cup to nourish the aged; learning was passed down through the Three Dynasties, inculcating supreme virtue and supreme conduct so as to clarify human moral relations. Alas, after bamboo slips and silk scrolls went up in smoke under the Qin, the brilliance of our Way was temporarily extinguished; fortunately, when the grand sacrifice of an ox, sheep, and pig was offered in Lu, the vital pulse of this culture quietly revived. Yet surrounding the bridged gates of the Imperial Academy with capped and girdled scholars merely served to impress the eye and ear; and when herd-boys gathered firewood there, it aroused lamentation over the overgrown weeds. When the Eastern Han rose anew, it conferred classical erudition yet boastfully displayed carriages and robes; when the Tang dynasty succeeded, it expanded academic halls and grandly summoned renowned scholars. Performing repeated bows merely paraded empty ceremony—such cultural governance was not even that of the Yuanyou era (1086–1094); reckless debates boiled up in the Upper Hall of the Imperial University—the Way had not even reached peace in the Xining era (1068–1077). How could they compare with the grand regulations of our Illustrious Dynasty, which have held aloft the literary destiny of mid-heaven! This is because we have reverently encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, possessing the benevolence of Yao and the filial piety of Shun, the frugality of Yu and the magnanimity of Tang. Diffusing the radiant illumination of the Li trigram to pacify the great enterprise,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
履謙光而凝
駿命
任賢勿貳切商宗之舟楫鹽梅
遜志有恒邁周王之刀劒戶牖
經筵與
講幃日
御游心化理之源
郊祀與
廟祭
===
躬承加意感孚之本
鸞迴
寶翰紀庶事以脩身
電覽
御屏察百官而勵治
功勤作聖
念及臨雍乃
咨弼直而渙
綸音遂
punctuated: 履謙光而凝駿命。任賢勿貳，切商宗之舟楫鹽梅；遜志有恒，邁周王之刀劒戶牖。經筵與講幃日御，游心化理之源；郊祀與廟祭躬承，加意感孚之本。鸞迴寶翰，紀庶事以脩身；電覽御屏，察百官而勵治。功勤作聖，念及臨雍。乃咨弼直而渙綸音，遂
translation_en: …and treads the path of luminous humility to consolidate the grand Mandate. In employing the worthy without duplicity, He earnestly matches the Shang high ancestor's reliance on "boats and oars" and "salt and plum"; in maintaining a humble mind with constancy, He surpasses the Zhou king's inscriptions on swords, knives, doors, and windows. The Classics Colloquia and the lecture curtains He attends daily, letting His mind roam at the source of transformative governance; the suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temple rites He personally performs, paying special heed to the root of spiritual resonance and sincerity. With phoenix-like flourishes of His precious brush, He records the myriad affairs so as to cultivate His person; with lightning-like glances at the imperial screen, He examines the hundred officials so as to encourage good rule. Diligent in the work of becoming a sage, His thoughts turn to visiting the Imperial University. Thereupon He consulted His upright輔弼 [councillors] and issued His silken sounds [imperial decree], consequently…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
勅儀曹以稽
令典
齋心祗事涓吉戒途節應金風
麟斿藹西崑之瑞塵清
玉輦
鳳馭騰北極之輝
葆幢出
天宮擁千官而聲聯珩珮
翠華來日觀麗萬象而光徹虹霓璧水搖波
===
學海文章增煥儒林絢綵尼山日月彌高
神晤百代之師拜瞻維謹禮隆三爵之
制登奠必親有喜
天顏
命儒臣以坐講無涯
聖澤
宣中使以傳茶
明良胥慶於一堂彝倫攸敘啓沃披颺於六籍
忠讜畢敷寶鏐
punctuated: 勅儀曹以稽令典。齋心祗事，涓吉戒途。節應金風，麟斿藹西崑之瑞；塵清玉輦，鳳馭騰北極之輝。葆幢出天宮，擁千官而聲聯珩珮；翠華來日觀，麗萬象而光徹虹霓。璧水搖波，學海文章增煥；儒林絢綵，尼山日月彌高。神晤百代之師，拜瞻維謹；禮隆三爵之制，登奠必親。有喜天顏，命儒臣以坐講；無涯聖澤，宣中使以傳茶。明良胥慶於一堂，彝倫攸敘；啓沃披颺於六籍，忠讜畢敷。寶鏐
translation_en: …ordered the Bureau of Ceremonies to examine the statutory rites. With purified heart and reverent attendance, an auspicious day was chosen to prepare the route. The season responded to the autumn wind, as unicorn-pennants radiated the auspiciousness of Western Kunlun; the dust was cleared before the jade carriage, as the phoenix-steeds soared with the brilliance of the North Pole. Feathered canopies emerged from the heavenly palace, surrounded by a thousand officials whose jade pendants chimed in unison; kingfisher banners arrived at the sun-viewing pavilion, adorning the myriad phenomena as their radiance pierced the rainbow. The circular moat rippled with waves, and the literary splendor of the sea of learning grew ever brighter; the forest of Confucians shone with colors, and the sun and moon of Mount Ni rose ever higher. In spiritual communion with the Teacher of a Hundred Generations, Your Majesty bowed and gazed with utmost reverence; exalting the ritual system of the three libations, Your Majesty ascended to present the offerings in person. With joy on the Imperial countenance, Confucian officials were commanded to sit and lecture; with boundless sagely grace, palace eunuchs were summoned to serve tea. Enlightened sovereign and worthy ministers rejoiced together in a single hall, whereby the invariable human relationships were set in order; edifying counsel was expounded and exalted from the Six Classics, and loyal, forthright words were fully set forth. Precious gold…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
錫珍藏欣被
龍光優渥褒衣捧
綸綍恍驚
天語叮嚀
萬壽之樂章和鳴蹌蹌獸舞三姓之子孫咸萃
濟濟雲聯鷺序鵷班瞻
玉帛萬方之化雕題辮髮仰
奎躔千載之期
鐘鼓樂辟雍人心與天心俱協
===
風聲樹寰寓道統與治統齊光豈徒飭
曠典於
熙明蓋將挽
泰運於沕穆臣等材同樸棫幸與
陶甄俎豆無聞陋桓榮之稽古曝芹未獻企
孫復之紓忠共叨有事之榮駿奔非偶莫
頌無前之
美雀躍何勝伏願
嚴事心師
punctuated: 錫珍藏，欣被龍光優渥；褒衣捧綸綍，恍驚天語叮嚀。萬壽之樂章和鳴，蹌蹌獸舞；三姓之子孫咸萃，濟濟雲聯。鷺序鵷班，瞻玉帛萬方之化；雕題辮髮，仰奎躔千載之期。鐘鼓樂辟雍，人心與天心俱協；風聲樹寰寓，道統與治統齊光。豈徒飭曠典於熙明，蓋將挽泰運於沕穆。臣等材同樸棫，幸與陶甄。俎豆無聞，陋桓榮之稽古；曝芹未獻，企孫復之紓忠。共叨有事之榮，駿奔非偶；莫頌無前之美，雀躍何勝！伏願嚴事心師，
translation_en:
…bestowed from the imperial treasury, they rejoice in being bathed in abounding dragon-grace; in wide-sleeved scholar's robes they hold up the silken edicts, startled with awe by the earnest admonitions of the heavenly words. The musical pieces of "Ten Thousand Years of Longevity" sound in harmony, as birds and beasts dance in stately step; the descendants of the Three Lineages all gather, massed like clouds in dignified array. The ranks of egrets and rows of phoenixes gaze upon a civilizing transformation that draws jade and silk from the ten thousand regions; those with tattooed foreheads and braided hair look up to the auspicious era that appears in the literary stars once in a thousand years. Bells and drums make joyful the Biyong imperial hall, as human hearts and the mind of Heaven are brought into full accord; a moral example is raised throughout the realm, as the succession of the Way and the succession of governance shine with equal brilliance. How could this merely be the observance of a rare rite in an age ofsplendid enlightenment? Rather, it will draw back the fortune of Great Peace from antiquity's profound depths.

Your servants, in talent like scrub oak, are fortunate to partake in Your Majesty's molding and fashioning. Unrenowned in matters of sacrificial vessels, we fall short of Huan Rong's study of antiquity; having yet to offer the humble gift of sun-warmed cress, we look up to Sun Fu's unfolding of loyalty. Together we enjoy the unmerited honor of officiating at the ceremony, hastening to our duties by no mere chance; unable to fully praise such unprecedented beauty, how could we contain our leaping joy! We humbly pray that Your Majesty will reverently serve the teacher within the mind,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
懋敦身教
