羹墻見聖妙契千載之真傳
箕福斂疇盡協庶徵之
皇極臣鄰師師以承
式載賡虞陛之歌
帝德蕩蕩以齊
天遍擊唐衢之壤
河清海晏敷九譯而同文
日升月恒逾萬年而過曆臣等無任瞻
===
天仰
聖激切欣躍之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
楊應兆
punctuated:
懋敦身教。羹墻見聖，妙契千載之真傳；箕福斂疇，盡協庶徵之皇極。臣鄰師師以承式，載賡虞陛之歌；帝德蕩蕩以齊天，遍擊唐衢之壤。河清海晏，敷九譯而同文；日升月恒，逾萬年而過曆。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切欣躍之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叁場
策
第一問
楊應兆
translation_en:
…and earnestly cultivate teaching by personal example. Seeing the former sages in your soup and on your walls, may you subtly accord with the true transmission of a thousand years; gathering the Five Blessings of the Great Plan of Jizi, may the august ultimate of the sovereign fully harmonize the various verifications. Your ministers and assistants emulate one another in receiving your model, once more continuing the songs of the steps of Shun's court; your imperial virtue is vast and boundless, equal to Heaven, as the clod-tapping game is played across all the thoroughfares of Yao's realm. With the Yellow River clear and the seas calm, your influence spreads through nine translations to unify the written script; like the rising sun and the waxing moon, may your dynasty surpass ten thousand years and exceed its allotted calendar. Your servants, unable to contain the utmost earnestness and joyous elation in gazing upon Heaven and looking up to the Sage, respectfully present this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Yang Yingzhao…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正梁批我
皇祖及我
皇上天縱聖神心學相契眞與堯舜媲美者子能闡揚道妙推本政源而忠悃溢於辭表豈嘗管窺天德者耶
考試官教諭劉批頌述發心學之精揄揚切忠藎
之獻必俊拔之士也取之
考試官教諭蔣批敷揚精切似有忠愛之實心
者錄之
帝王之所以運治者其心乎帝王之所以
純心者其敬乎蓋治統於道道原於天敬
則所以純其心而會天之精者也故開泰
者敬以格天則創一代之鴻圖而聲光流
於後世保泰者敬以祈天則承萬世之丕
基而紹述光於前烈底之爲績所以運天
工也昭之爲謨所以煥天章也懿爍之治
與造化交相流焉固帝王之純學而千聖
一軌者乎知此則我
皇祖之懋昭聖學我
皇上之仰契心傳
punctuated:
同考試官學正梁批：我皇祖及我皇上，天縱聖神，心學相契，眞與堯舜媲美者。子能闡揚道妙，推本政源，而忠悃溢於辭表，豈嘗管窺天德者耶？
考試官教諭劉批：頌述發心學之精，揄揚切忠藎之獻，必俊拔之士也。取之。
考試官教諭蔣批：敷揚精切，似有忠愛之實心者。錄之。
帝王之所以運治者，其心乎！帝王之所以純心者，其敬乎！蓋治統於道，道原於天，敬則所以純其心而會天之精者也。故開泰者敬以格天，則創一代之鴻圖，而聲光流於後世；保泰者敬以祈天，則承萬世之丕基，而紹述光於前烈。底之爲績，所以運天工也；昭之爲謨，所以煥天章也。懿爍之治，與造化交相流焉，固帝王之純學，而千聖一軌者乎！知此，則我皇祖之懋昭聖學，我皇上之仰契心傳，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng): Our Imperial Ancestor and Our reigning Sovereign, endowed by Heaven with sage and divine qualities, tally with each other in the learning of the mind-and-heart (xinxue), truly matching the excellence of Yao and Shun. You are able to elucidate and extol the subtleties of the Way and trace governance back to its source, while your loyal sincerity overflows beyond your words—have you not indeed caught a glimpse of Heavenly virtue?

Comment by Examiner Liu, County Instructor (jiaoyu): His eulogistic exposition brings forth the essence of the learning of the mind-and-heart, and his praise earnestly presents an offering of loyal devotion; he must be a man of outstanding talent. Select this.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, County Instructor (jiaoyu): His exposition and praise are precise and earnest, as of one who possesses a genuine heart of loyalty and affection. Record this.

That by which emperors and kings conduct governance—is it not their mind-and-heart? That by which emperors and kings purify their mind-and-heart—is it not their reverence? Indeed, governance is unified in the Way, the Way originates in Heaven, and reverence is that by which one purifies one's mind-and-heart and comprehends the essence of Heaven. Therefore, those who inaugurate an era of grand peace use reverence to reach Heaven, thereby founding the grand plan of a dynasty and causing their renown and brilliance to flow down to later generations; those who preserve an era of grand peace use reverence to pray to Heaven, thereby inheriting the great foundation of ten thousand generations and making their continuation shine upon the achievements of their predecessors. Brought to realization as accomplishments, it is that by which they carry out the work of Heaven; made manifest as counsels, it is that by which they illuminate the patterns of Heaven. When admirable and resplendent governance flows in mutual harmony with the creative forces of nature, is this not indeed the pure learning of emperors and kings, in which a thousand sages follow a single track? Understanding this, then how Our Imperial Ancestor earnestly made bright the sage learning, and how Our reigning Sovereign reverently tallied with the transmission of the mind-and-heart,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聖神媲美超軼萬禩者可得而揄揚其實矣請
敬陳之嘗謂天有元氣而元化充溢則天
之化天之心爲之也聖人位其位而子其
民則亦當心其心而不敢怠故精一之秘
肇自堯舜授受之間以底時雍風動之化
而史臣贊其爲欽恭者即精一之旨也乃
若舜之授禹亦惟揭斯道而傳之蓋其心
真見夫天之可畏有能持吾之說以安天
下後世之民則吾之仰承乎天者亦可以
===
不愧此其至公至仁之心固治統所基亦
道統所自也禹湯承堯舜之傳而垂之爲
子孫之業其欽恭之心視堯舜尤惓切矣
故平成肇於祗台允殖隆於日躋堯舜之
統乃自數聖人衍之而敬止敬勝文武可
例而知也上古聖人所以開萬世之麗者
其心有一息不純於敬哉漢唐諸君開國
者闊略於草昧繼體者循習於故常諸不
暇論即如宣帝之齋居決事稱勵精矣而
punctuated:
聖神媲美，超軼萬禩者，可得而揄揚其實矣。請敬陳之。

嘗謂天有元氣，而元化充溢，則天之化，天之心爲之也。聖人位其位而子其民，則亦當心其心而不敢怠。故精一之秘，肇自堯、舜授受之間，以底時雍風動之化；而史臣贊其爲欽恭者，即精一之旨也。乃若舜之授禹，亦惟揭斯道而傳之。蓋其心真見夫天之可畏，有能持吾之說以安天下後世之民，則吾之仰承乎天者，亦可以不愧。此其至公至仁之心，固治統所基，亦道統所自也。禹、湯承堯、舜之傳，而垂之爲子孫之業，其欽恭之心，視堯、舜尤惓切矣。故平成肇於祗台，允殖隆於日躋。堯、舜之統，乃自數聖人衍之，而「敬止」、「敬勝」，文、武可例而知也。上古聖人所以開萬世之麗者，其心有一息不純於敬哉？

漢、唐諸君，開國者闊略於草昧，繼體者循習於故常，諸不暇論。即如宣帝之齋居決事，稱勵精矣，而
translation_en:
…how their sacred and divine virtues match each other in beauty and surpass ten thousand generations—their realities may thus be extolled and set forth. Allow me to reverently state them.

I have heard it said that Heaven possesses the primal vital breath (yuanqi), and its primal transformation overflows; thus, the transformation of Heaven is wrought by the mind of Heaven. When the sage occupies His position and treats His people as His children, he too ought to take Heaven's mind as his own mind and never dare be remiss. Therefore, the secret of being "refined and single-minded" (jingyi) originated in the transmission and reception between Yao and Shun, thereby achieving the transformation of harmonious times and wind-like influence; and when the historian praised them for being reverent and respectful (qingong), that was precisely the purport of being refined and single-minded. As for Shun's transmission to Yu, he likewise held up this very Way and passed it down. For in his mind he truly perceived that Heaven is to be held in awe: if there were someone capable of upholding his teaching so as to bring peace to the people of the world and of future generations, then in his own reverent reception of Heaven's charge he too would have nothing to be ashamed of. This supremely impartial and supremely benevolent mind is surely the foundation of the lineage of governance (zhitong) and also the source of the lineage of the Way (daotong). Yu and Tang received the transmission of Yao and Shun and handed it down as a patrimony for their descendants; their reverent and respectful minds were even more earnestly devoted than those of Yao and Shun. Thus, peace and order (pingcheng) began with "reverently leading by my own example" (zhitai), and sincere flourishing (yunzhi) rose high through "daily ascending" (riji). The lineage of Yao and Shun was extended through these several sages, and by "resting in reverence" (jingzhi) and "reverence prevailing" (jingsheng), the examples of King Wen and King Wu may likewise be understood by analogy. In opening up a glorious enterprise for ten thousand generations, was there ever a single breath in which the minds of the sages of high antiquity were not pure in reverence?

As for the various rulers of the Han and Tang dynasties, the dynastic founders were rough and neglectful amid the rudeness of incipient order, while the succeeding rulers merely followed along in established routines—I have no leisure to discuss them all. Even in the case of Emperor Xuan of the Han, who decided affairs of state while residing in his fasting chamber and was praised for his vigorous dedication to governance, yet…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不免雜於申韓太宗之帝範垂訓稱盛治
矣而猶多慚於內德危竿之喻致治四十
餘年損齋之記噓宋燼而再燃之似若可
馥稿竹之載者然湛靜安舒流於姑息國
威未振今猶病其損之過焉要之數君者
無得於純心之學而徒以機智材辨矯飾
一時故僅足以名季世之業而擬諸帝王
何啻碔砆之相懸也哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
===
天錫智勇締構
邦家酬雪則功高百王廓清則
統承五帝其
駿德鴻庥混闢以來未有也乃當開創之初而
預爲萬世之慮履無前之業而益操兢惕
之懷故昭揭
琬琰光映典謨諸不勝睹記而至精至要爲
聖神之榘矱者如
皇明祖訓永垂燕翼自嚴祀至供用規畫井然
punctuated: 不免雜於申、韓；太宗之《帝範》垂訓，稱盛治矣，而猶多慚於內德。「危竿」之喻，致治四十餘年；《損齋》之記，噓宋燼而再燃之，似若可馥稿竹之載者。然湛靜安舒，流於姑息，國威未振，今猶病其損之過焉。要之，數君者無得於純心之學，而徒以機智材辨矯飾一時，故僅足以名季世之業，而擬諸帝王，何啻碔砆之相懸也哉！洪惟我太祖高皇帝，天錫智勇，締構邦家。酬雪則功高百王，廓清則統承五帝，其駿德鴻庥，混闢以來未有也。乃當開創之初，而預爲萬世之慮；履無前之業，而益操兢惕之懷。故昭揭琬琰，光映典謨，諸不勝睹記，而至精至要、爲聖神之榘矱者，如《皇明祖訓》，永垂燕翼，自「嚴祀」至「供用」，規畫井然，
translation_en:
… could not avoid being adulterated with the doctrines of Shen Buhai 申不害 and Han Fei 韓非; Taizong 太宗 handed down instructions in his Models for an Emperor (Difan 帝範), which was praised as an era of flourishing governance, yet he still had much to be ashamed of regarding his inner virtue. The metaphor of the "precarious pole" [of Song Renzong 宋仁宗] brought about good governance for over forty years; the record of the Studio of Diminution (Sunzhai 損齋) [of Song Gaozong 宋高宗] breathed upon the ashes of the Song and rekindled them, seeming as though they might leave a fragrant scent in the records of withered bamboo slips [?]. Yet tranquil quietude and easy comfort degenerated into laxity [under Renzong], and when the prestige of the state failed to be roused [under Gaozong], even today people fault his excessive "diminution." In short, these several rulers gained nothing from the learning of a pure mind, and merely usedcleverness, talent, and eloquence to put on an artificial display for their own time. Thus, their achievements were barely enough to make a name in later ages; if compared to the ancient Emperors and Kings, how is the disparity between them any less than that between a worthless pebble (wufu 碔砆) and jade!

Let us reverently reflect upon our Taizu, Emperor Gao 太祖高皇帝: Heaven endowed him with wisdom and valor to found and construct the state. In avenging humiliation, his merit surpassed a hundred kings; in sweeping clear the realm, his succession continued that of the Five Emperors. His great virtue and vast blessings have been unprecedented since the creation of the world. Yet at the very beginning of his founding of the dynasty, he took forethought for ten thousand generations; walking in the midst of an unprecedented enterprise, he held all the more to an attitude of cautious vigilance. Therefore, what he brightly displayed on jade tablets, shining alongside the Canons and Counsels (Dian Mo 典謨), is too numerous to be fully read or recorded. As for those works that are most refined and essential, serving as the standard and rule of his sagely and divine spirit: there is the Ancestral Injunctions of the August Ming (Huang Ming zuxun 皇明祖訓), eternally handing down guidance to shelter his descendants; from "Revering Sacrifices" (Yansi 嚴祀) to "Provisions and Expenditures" (Gongyong 供用), its regulations and plans are in perfect order, …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而持守一章尤爲王政之綱焉固帝王時
幾之勅也
資世通訓表倡臣民自君道至民用法戒具
陳而尊賢遠佞尤切淬厲之衷焉固帝王
危微之訓也
敬天忠君孝親爲要而反身契篤恭之軌則
精誠一錄見於吳沉所輯者可睹也人心虛
靈乗機出入而操存密精一之學則
觀心有記見於宋濂所述者可頌也此固
===
聖祖之文謨炳麗萬禩如新者而仰窺其奧亦
不越
祖訓之所謂敬畏者而已蓋能憂天下必受
天眷大哉
皇言固統乎精誠觀心諸記而一貫之矣是非
心天之心而學堯舜之學者哉
列聖相承授守一道我
皇上
天縱聖哲
punctuated: 而持守一章，尤爲王政之綱焉，固帝王時幾之勅也。《資世通訓》表倡臣民，自君道至民用，法戒具陳，而尊賢遠佞，尤切淬厲之衷焉，固帝王危微之訓也。敬天、忠君、孝親爲要，而反身契篤恭之軌，則《精誠》一錄，見於吳沉所輯者可睹也。人心虛靈，乗機出入，而操存密精一之學，則《觀心》有記，見於宋濂所述者可頌也。此固聖祖之文謨炳麗，萬禩如新者，而仰窺其奧，亦不越《祖訓》之所謂敬畏者而已。蓋「能憂天下，必受天眷」，大哉皇言，固統乎《精誠》、《觀心》諸記而一貫之矣！是非心天之心，而學堯、舜之學者哉？列聖相承，授守一道。我皇上天縱聖哲，
translation_en:
… while the chapter on "Maintaining and Preserving" (Chishou) especially serves as the overarching principle of kingly governance; it is truly the emperors' and kings' admonition to attend to the right moment and the subtle incipient tendencies. The Comprehensive Admonitions for Aiding the World (Zishi tongxun) sets an example for officials and the common people; from the Way of the Ruler down to the daily needs of the people, models and warnings are fully set forth, while honoring the worthy and keeping flatterers at a distance touches especially closely upon the inner resolve of self-cultivation and exertion; it is truly the emperors' and kings' instruction on the precariousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the moral mind. Taking reverence for Heaven, loyalty to the ruler, and filiality to parents as essential, and reflecting upon oneself to accord with the standard of steadfast reverence—this can be seen in the Record of Utmost Sincerity (Jingcheng lu) as compiled by Wu Chen 吳沉. The human mind is numinous and void, going out and coming in as opportunity prompts, and holding fast and preserving it to perfect the learning of refinement and single-mindedness—this can be praised in the Record of Contemplating the Mind (Guanxin ji) as recounted by Song Lian 宋濂.

All these are indeed the resplendent literary plans of our Sacred Ancestor, remaining as fresh as new for ten thousand generations; yet when we look up to peer into their profound depths, they do not go beyond what the Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun) call "reverence and awe." For "one who is able to be anxious for all under Heaven will surely receive the favor of Heaven"—great indeed are the august words, which truly encompass and unify the Record of Utmost Sincerity, the Record of Contemplating the Mind, and the other records with a single thread! Is this not taking the mind of Heaven as one's own mind, and learning the learning of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜?

The successive Sacred Emperors have inherited and upheld the same Way. Our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sage wisdom, …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
丕闡鴻猷
講讀則寒暑不廢
聽納則芻蕘不遺其
勅幾慎位敬承之烈莫竝也然時方
冲睿而志必企乎堯舜治雖熙洽而念每戒
乎盈成故
親灑
宸翰訓勵臣工諸不勝捧頌而至純至粹媲美
聖祖之謨烈者有一十二事
===
宣付史館以之存心則所謂
謹天戒存敬畏收放心者即我
聖祖省躬憂恤乘機操存之意也以之保身則
所謂
慎起居慎出入節飲食者即我
聖祖居安懷警節飲時食之慮也因扣角而慨
遺賢闢優伶而旌讜論
聖祖之貴德遠佞者切矣
皇上親賢任能遠佞納忠之
punctuated: 丕闡鴻猷。講讀則寒暑不廢，聽納則芻蕘不遺，其勅幾慎位、敬承之烈莫竝也。然時方冲睿，而志必企乎堯、舜；治雖熙洽，而念每戒乎盈成。故親灑宸翰，訓勵臣工，諸不勝捧頌，而至純至粹、媲美聖祖之謨烈者，有一十二事，宣付史館。以之存心，則所謂「謹天戒」、「存敬畏」、「收放心」者，即我聖祖省躬憂恤、乘機操存之意也。以之保身，則所謂「慎起居」、「慎出入」、「節飲食」者，即我聖祖居安懷警、節飲時食之慮也。因扣角而慨遺賢，闢優伶而旌讜論，聖祖之貴德遠佞者切矣；皇上「親賢任能」、「遠佞納忠」之
translation_en:
…greatly expands upon the grand plan. In his lectures and readings, he does not cease for winter cold or summer heat; in listening to and accepting counsel, he does not overlook even the grass-cutters and wood-gatherers. His illustrious achievements in attending to the subtle springs of action, being cautious on the throne, and reverently carrying on the heritage are peerless. Yet, though he is still in his youthful wisdom, his aspirations inevitably reach toward Yao and Shun; and though his governance is already harmonious and flourishing, his thoughts ever guard against complacency in fullness and completion. Therefore, he personally wielded the imperial brush to instruct and encourage his officials. All of these writings are more than one can reverently praise in full, yet among them, those most pure and unalloyed, which match the beauty of the Sacred Ancestor's counsels and achievements, comprise twelve matters that have been proclaimed and delivered to the Historiography Institute.

As for using them to preserve the mind: what are called "Heeding Heaven's Warnings," "Preserving Reverence and Awe," and "Recovering the Straying Mind" embody the very intention of our Sacred Ancestor in examining himself, worrying for and commiserating with the people, and seizing every opportunity to hold fast to his mind. As for using them to protect the person: what are called "Being Cautious in Daily Routine," "Being Cautious in Going Out and Coming In," and "Moderating Drink and Food" embody the very concern of our Sacred Ancestor in remaining vigilant while dwelling in security and moderating drink and taking food at proper times. Being moved by the story of striking the ox's horn to sigh over neglected worthies, and dismissing actors and jesters while honoring forthright counsel—how earnest was the Sacred Ancestor in prizing virtue and keeping flatterers at a distance! Does not His Majesty's [decree on] "Drawing Close to the Worthy and Employing the Capable" and "Keeping Flatterers at a Distance and Accepting Loyal Counsel"…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
旨其後先一德乎
賜張眞而威薛顯汰金飾而種隙地
聖祖之飭法愼儉者至矣
皇上明賞罰撙節用之
旨其創述一軌乎此我
皇上之睿藻輝煌光紹
祖烈者而竊探其要亦不越
宸翰之所謂敬畏者而已蓋能存敬畏則百度
惟貞旨哉
===
聖謨固統乎身心政治之詳而備舉之矣是非
心
聖祖之心學堯舜之學者哉嗟乎自放勳至我
明凡幾千禩而
皇祖之學與堯舜若同堂焉自
國初至
今日餘二百年而
皇上之學與
聖祖若面授焉得非
punctuated: 旨，其後先一德乎！賜張眞而威薛顯，汰金飾而種隙地，聖祖之飭法愼儉者至矣；皇上明賞罰、撙節用之旨，其創述一軌乎！此我皇上之睿藻輝煌，光紹祖烈者，而竊探其要，亦不越宸翰之所謂「敬畏」者而已。蓋能存敬畏，則百度惟貞。旨哉！聖謨固統乎身心政治之詳而備舉之矣。是非心聖祖之心、學堯舜之學者哉？嗟乎！自放勳至我明凡幾千禩，而皇祖之學與堯舜若同堂焉；自國初至今日餘二百年，而皇上之學與聖祖若面授焉。得非
translation_en: …edicts—are they not one and the same in virtue from first to last? Bestowing gifts upon Zhang Zhen 張眞 while overawing Xue Xian 薛顯, and eliminating gold ornaments while cultivating idle land: in enforcing the law and exercising prudent frugality, the Sacred Ancestor reached the utmost! And in His Majesty's edicts clarifying rewards and punishments and economizing on expenditures, do not founder and successor follow a single track? Herein lies the resplendent imperial composition of His Majesty, gloriously continuing the ancestral achievements; yet if one humbly seeks its essence, it does not go beyond what the imperial calligraphy calls "reverent awe" (jingwei 敬畏). For if one can preserve reverent awe, then all measures of governance will be upright. How profound in meaning! The sacred counsels indeed encompass the full details of personal cultivation and governance and set them forth completely. Is this not taking the mind of the Sacred Ancestor as one's own mind, and studying the learning of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜? Alas! From Fangxun 放勳 [Yao] down to our Ming dynasty is several thousand years, yet the learning of the Imperial Ancestor is as though in the same hall with Yao and Shun; from the founding of the dynasty down to the present day is more than two hundred years, yet the learning of His Majesty is as though personally transmitted face-to-face by the Sacred Ancestor. Could it not be that…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聖神授受心心相照而一敬孚天不求其同而
自無不同者乎彼昔岣嶁之碑人爭模頌
而飛白答詔迄今以為美談蓋神禹之德
萬世猶存而貞觀之治亦希世賢君也故
翰墨一流矜詡後世矧我
聖祖之製訓
皇上之宸謨龍盤鳳翥固超墳典而麗日星者
也即如宋濂吳沉所紀不能揚
祖烈之盛而
===
皇上御極以來時和年登民康物阜炎荒奏凱
窮髮輸琛即勳華相繼與
聖祖肇造之烈不能過之雖使鴻筆之臣畫天
測海莫能鋪張萬一而愚生草茅之見執
事固欲其推本政原以裨
聖治哉然堯舜至聖不廢交儆之謨而桂彥良
養心寡欲之諷於
聖祖惓惓焉則愚生仰窺
聖心之虛敢獻曝矣夫人君深居九重而天下
punctuated: 聖神授受，心心相照，而一敬孚天，不求其同而自無不同者乎？彼昔岣嶁之碑，人爭模頌；而飛白答詔，迄今以為美談。蓋神禹之德，萬世猶存；而貞觀之治，亦希世賢君也。故翰墨一流，矜詡後世。矧我聖祖之製訓，皇上之宸謨，龍盤鳳翥，固超墳典而麗日星者也。即如宋濂、吳沉所紀，不能揚祖烈之盛；而皇上御極以來，時和年登，民康物阜，炎荒奏凱，窮髮輸琛，即勳華相繼，與聖祖肇造之烈，不能過之。雖使鴻筆之臣，畫天測海，莫能鋪張萬一；而愚生草茅之見，執事固欲其推本政原，以裨聖治哉！然堯、舜至聖，不廢交儆之謨；而桂彥良養心寡欲之諷，於聖祖惓惓焉。則愚生仰窺聖心之虛，敢獻曝矣。夫人君深居九重，而天下
translation_en: … handed down from sage and divine rulers, mind illuminating mind, and with a single-minded reverence matching Heaven, not seeking to be identical and yet naturally without any difference? In the past, people vied to take rubbings of and eulogize the stele on Mount Goulou, while the reply edict written in the "flying white" calligraphic style is spoken of with admiration to this day. This is because the virtue of the divine Yu still endures for ten thousand generations, and the ruler of the Zhenguan reign was likewise a worthy sovereign rarely seen in the world; thus, once their calligraphy and writings spread, they were boasted of and praised by later generations. How much more so the imperial instructions composed by our Sacred Ancestor and the imperial counsels of His Majesty! Like coiling dragons and soaring phoenixes, they truly surpass the Three Mounds and Five Canons (Fendian) and shine alongside the sun and stars. Even the records written by Song Lian and Wu Chen could not fully extol the magnificence of the Ancestor's meritorious achievements; and since His Majesty ascended the throne, the seasons have been harmonious and the harvests abundant, the people prosperous and things plentiful, the fiery wildernesses of the south have reported victories, and the barren lands of the far north have offered up precious tribute. Even the succession of Yao (Xun) and Shun (Hua), together with the founding achievements of the Sacred Ancestor, could not surpass this. Even if ministers of grand literary talent were to try to depict Heaven and fathom the seas, they could not set forth even one ten-thousandth of it; yet Your Excellency truly wishes this foolish student, with his rustic views from the thatched hut, to trace the roots and sources of governance so as to benefit the Sacred Reign! Nevertheless, though Yao and Shun were supremely sage, they did not dispense with counsels of mutual admonition; and Gui Yanliang's remonstrance on nourishing the mind and lessening desires was offered with earnest devotion to the Sacred Ancestor. Looking up and glimpsing the receptivity of the Sacred Mind, this foolish student dares to offer his humble counsel, like the peasant offering the warmth of the sun. Now, the ruler of men dwells deep within the ninefold palace, yet the people of the world…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之人洞若觀火一念壅遏則化機不流必
乾健不息者乃足以保泰凝命也矧參天
之榦養於萌蘖放海之波清於源流少成
天性習慣自然聖人惜時而慎初者大學
之所以爲豫也
皇上春秋鼎盛
天聰瑩然固靈根初植而真源未汨
宗社生靈所恃以爲乂安長治之基者也惟
卽其所謂敬畏者操之有恒養之無間
===
大廷渙號丞弼端
臨莫非出往游衍之天而蜎蜎蠖濩之中雷聲
淵默之際尤必慎於幾微鑑於
祖訓益乎吾心之天者亟充之戾乎吾心之天
者亟制之兢兢然若堯之勅幾禹之惜陰
而一十二事求爲慎脩之盤銘几戒焉則
聖質疑定
懿德淵涵氣鬯神流日新月盛而
駿烈
punctuated: 之人洞若觀火。一念壅遏，則化機不流；必乾健不息者，乃足以保泰凝命也。矧參天之榦，養於萌蘖；放海之波，清於源流。少成天性，習慣自然，聖人惜時而慎初者，《大學》之所以爲豫也。皇上春秋鼎盛，天聰瑩然，固靈根初植，而真源未汨，宗社生靈所恃以爲乂安長治之基者也。惟卽其所謂敬畏者，操之有恒，養之無間，大廷渙號，丞弼端臨，莫非出往游衍之天；而蜎蜎蠖濩之中，雷聲淵默之際，尤必慎於幾微，鑑於祖訓。益乎吾心之天者，亟充之；戾乎吾心之天者，亟制之。兢兢然若堯之勅幾、禹之惜陰，而一十二事求爲慎脩之盤銘几戒焉。則聖質疑定，懿德淵涵，氣鬯神流，日新月盛，而駿烈
translation_en:
… [the people] see through him as clearly as watching a fire. If a single thought becomes obstructed, the vital mechanism of moral transformation ceases to flow; only he who is as vigorous and unceasing as Heaven suffices to preserve peace and consolidate the Mandate. How much more so given that a trunk towering to the sky is nourished from a tender shoot, and waves reaching the sea are kept clear at their source and stream! What is formed in youth becomes like innate nature, and what is practiced habitually becomes spontaneous; that the sages cherished time and were cautious at the beginning is what is meant in the Great Learning (Daxue) [or Record on Education] by "prevention beforehand."

His Majesty is in the prime of his youth, and his heavenly intelligence is radiantly clear. Truly, the spiritual root is newly planted and the true source is not yet muddied; this is what the ancestral altars and the living people rely upon as the foundation for enduring peace and lasting order. Let him only take this so-called reverence and awe, hold fast to it with constancy, and nourish it without interruption. When proclaiming decrees in the great court and presiding uprightly over his chief ministers and assistants, all is within the Heaven of his going forth and strolling at ease; yet in the seclusion of the deep palace halls, in moments of thunderous majesty and abyssal silence, he must be especially cautious over the most subtle incipient stirrings and take warning from the Ancestral Injunctions. Whatever benefits the Heaven within one's mind, let him urgently expand it; whatever violates the Heaven within one's mind, let him urgently restrain it. Let him be ever cautious and wary, like Yao ordering the subtle springs of action and Yu cherishing every fraction of time, taking those twelve matters as basin inscriptions and armrest admonitions for careful self-cultivation. Then his sage substance will be firmly established, his admirable virtue deeply infused, his vital energy harmonious and his spirit flowing, daily renewed and monthly flourishing, while his magnificent achievements…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
奎章巍然煥然人將稱爲萬世之堯舜我
皇祖諄切貽謀之心亦與天壤相爲不朽矣愚
生何幸躬逢其
盛
第二問
楊同春
同考試官教諭徐批法無寬嚴惟當而已治久人玩
行法者可事姑息乎子能叅酌往事與時權衡可謂通達治體者
考試官教諭劉批博洽中有超然之趣奇士也
===
考試官教諭蔣批評議精確是知飭法振民者
聖人之愛天下也甚厚而其慮天下也常
周愛之厚則身視中國家視寰宇保抱煦
育之意必欲其並生於和平溫飫之區慮
之周則防乎其漸制乎其流使之循習於
規矩繩束之内而後寄其愛於不窮故用
法之意常主於寬而持法之術必貴於嚴
寬非徇天下也拘攣褊迫之政恐滋無聊
之心而絞鮮束濕民不堪其命焉故濟之
punctuated:
奎章巍然煥然，人將稱爲萬世之堯、舜，我皇祖諄切貽謀之心，亦與天壤相爲不朽矣。愚生何幸，躬逢其盛！

第二問
楊同春
同考試官教諭徐批：〔法無寬嚴，惟當而已。治久人玩，行法者可事姑息乎？子能叅酌往事，與時權衡，可謂通達治體者。〕
考試官教諭劉批：〔博洽中有超然之趣，奇士也。〕
考試官教諭蔣批：〔評議精確，是知飭法振民者。〕

聖人之愛天下也甚厚，而其慮天下也常周。愛之厚，則身視中國，家視寰宇，保抱煦育之意，必欲其並生於和平溫飫之區；慮之周，則防乎其漸，制乎其流，使之循習於規矩繩束之内，而後寄其愛於不窮。故用法之意常主於寬，而持法之術必貴於嚴。寬非徇天下也，拘攣褊迫之政，恐滋無聊之心，而絞鮮束濕，民不堪其命焉，故濟之
translation_en:
…and Imperial writings will be towering and resplendent. People will acclaim His Majesty as the Yao and Shun of ten thousand generations, and the earnest heart with which our August Ancestor bequeathed his counsel will likewise endure as immortally as heaven and earth. How fortunate is this foolish student to witness such splendor in person!

Second Question
Yang Tongchun 楊同春
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xu: [In law there is neither leniency nor severity, only what is fitting. When peace has lasted long and people grow lax, can those who enforce the law indulge in misplaced tolerance? You are able to consult and weigh past events and balance them with the times; you may be called one who thoroughly understands the essentials of governance.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu: [Amidst broad learning there is a transcendent flair; an extraordinary scholar.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Jiang: [The evaluations and discussions are precise and accurate; this is someone who knows how to tighten the laws and rouse the people.]

The sage's love for the world is exceedingly deep, and his concern for the world is ever comprehensive. Because his love is deep, he regards the Central State as his own person and the whole universe as his own family; in his intent to embrace, cherish, and warmly nurture all people, he surely wishes them to live together in a realm of peace, warmth, and abundance. Because his concern is comprehensive, he guards against incipient tendencies and checks their spread, causing the people to follow and accustom themselves to the bounds of rules and restraints, and only thus does he lodge his love in perpetuity. Therefore, the intent in applying the law always gives primacy to leniency, whereas the art of upholding the law must value severity. Leniency is not a matter of pandering to the world: restrictive, cramped, and oppressive governance might breed hearts of hopelessness, and when measures are as harsh as mangling small fish or binding wet kindling, the people cannot bear the demands placed upon them; therefore one tempers it…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
以寬成其嚴也嚴非苦天下也怠弛疎闊
之過恐生不羈之習而吞舟逸柙民不勝
其弊焉故操之以嚴成其寬也原聖人之
愛以用法存聖人之慮以操法而要於其
當譬諸御馬者急其箠而舒其轡不致跛
曳而泛駕皷瑟者促其柱而疏其絃不致
沾滯而噍殺焉則天下無廢法無惰事而
理道可言矣敢敬陳之夫天之道好生者
也然而春溫冬肅惠風迅雷常並行於覆
===
幬之間如其資生之仁卽春而不冬雨而
不雪降祥而不降殃足矣而何其並用不
廢若此也蓋不斂則不舒不震則不育天
固知其不可廢也惟陽居大夏陰居窮冬
霜雷十而二之災沴十而一之則其仁可
掬矣聖人之仁天下豈不欲其羸衣枵食
如已飫溫萎膏臏醒如已蘇快歡然若吾
家人父子之親而顧以法震之乎蓋天下
之情難固而其隙易開强掩弱衆暴寡利
punctuated:
以寬，成其嚴也；嚴非苦天下也，怠弛疎闊之過，恐生不羈之習，而吞舟逸柙，民不勝其弊焉，故操之以嚴，成其寬也。原聖人之愛以用法，存聖人之慮以操法，而要於其當。譬諸御馬者，急其箠而舒其轡，不致跛曳而泛駕；皷瑟者，促其柱而疏其絃，不致沾滯而噍殺焉。則天下無廢法，無惰事，而理道可言矣。敢敬陳之：
夫天之道，好生者也。然而春溫冬肅，惠風迅雷，常並行於覆幬之間。如其資生之仁，卽春而不冬，雨而不雪，降祥而不降殃，足矣；而何其並用不廢若此也？蓋不斂則不舒，不震則不育，天固知其不可廢也。惟陽居大夏，陰居窮冬，霜雷十而二之，災沴十而一之，則其仁可掬矣。聖人之仁天下，豈不欲其羸衣枵食如已飫溫，萎膏臏醒如已蘇快，歡然若吾家人父子之親，而顧以法震之乎？蓋天下之情難固而其隙易開，强掩弱，衆暴寡，利
translation_en:
… with leniency, thus fulfilling its strictness. Strictness is not meant to torment the world; rather, the fault of negligence, laxity, and carelessness might breed unbridled habits, and when fish large enough to swallow a boat slip the net or wild beasts escape their cages, the people cannot bear the resulting abuses—therefore one upholds it with strictness, thus fulfilling its leniency. Tracing the sage's love in applying the law, and preserving the sage's foresight in upholding the law, the key lies in achieving due measure. It is like driving horses: one plies the whip briskly yet keeps a gentle rein, so that the horses neither limp and drag nor bolt and overturn the carriage; or like playing the zither: one sets the bridges close yet spaces out the strings, so that the notes are neither sluggish and clogged nor shrill and hurried. Then in all under Heaven no laws are neglected, no affairs are slighted, and the way of governance can be spoken of. I venture respectfully to set this forth.

Now, the Way of Heaven delights in life. Yet the warmth of spring and the severity of winter, the gentle breeze and the sudden thunderclap, constantly operate together beneath the canopy of the sky. If it were solely a matter of its life-giving benevolence, then having spring without winter, rain without snow, and sending down auspices without calamities would suffice; why, then, does it employ both together without discarding either like this? Because without contraction there is no expansion, and without shock there is no nurturing; Heaven surely knows that neither can be dispensed with. Only because yang presides over great summer while yin is confined to the depths of winter, and because frost and thunder make up two parts in ten while calamities and pestilences make up one part in ten, its benevolence is palpable enough to be scooped up in the hands. In showing benevolence to the world, how could the sage not wish that those in tattered clothes and with empty stomachs be as though already warm and well-fed, and those with withered flesh and crippled kneecaps awaken [?] as though already revived and comfortable, all rejoicing together like the close kin of one's own family, father and son—why, instead, would he awe them with the law? It is because the sentiments of the world are hard to secure and its rifts are easy to open: the strong overwhelm the weak, the many oppress the few, profit …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
不相分而相攘智不相教而相賊不有以
齊之則僭競凌獵不能有其衣食妻子甚
則冒上忘等天下之大可畏者至矣故肉
刑制於邃初而殛鯀誅苗之事去洪荒未
遠也然數聖人者不曰欽恤則曰惟中三
公八議以酌其情嘉石肺石以通其隱使
天下不困於敲扑狴犴之間輸金束矢之
罰而姦雄悍慢一與法忤毅然裁之故怙
終者不得逭其誅過誤者又得伸其枉稂
===
莠既去嘉禾乃茂聖人以為必如是天下
後世之民始得恃吾法以無恐也故其意
藹如春煦如露而其法則嚴若峭壁迅若
轟雷神若天降地設而民不敢玩焉豈惟
民之不敢玩哉有法則固無法則潰即制
法者亦不得而玩之也按細柳之轡而君
不得馳格主長之僕而后不得怒勇若烏
獲嬖若韓彭成若操懿而鰓鰓然恐不逃
於三尺者聖人之法固然也乃用法者曲
punctuated: 不相分而相攘，智不相教而相賊。不有以齊之，則僭競凌獵，不能有其衣食妻子；甚則冒上忘等，天下之大可畏者至矣。故肉刑制於邃初，而殛鯀誅苗之事，去洪荒未遠也。然數聖人者，不曰「欽恤」，則曰「惟中」。三公八議以酌其情，嘉石肺石以通其隱，使天下不困於敲扑狴犴之間、輸金束矢之罰，而姦雄悍慢一與法忤，毅然裁之。故怙終者不得逭其誅，過誤者又得伸其枉。稂莠既去，嘉禾乃茂。聖人以為必如是，天下後世之民始得恃吾法以無恐也。故其意藹如春，煦如露，而其法則嚴若峭壁，迅若轟雷，神若天降地設，而民不敢玩焉。豈惟民之不敢玩哉？有法則固，無法則潰，即制法者亦不得而玩之也。按細柳之轡而君不得馳，格主長之僕而后不得怒。勇若烏獲，嬖若韓彭，成若操懿，而鰓鰓然恐不逃於三尺者，聖人之法固然也。乃用法者曲
translation_en: … is not shared with one another, so they steal from each other; wisdom is not taught to one another, so they harm each other. If there is nothing with which to make them uniform, they will usurp, compete, encroach, and prey upon one another, unable even to keep their own clothing, food, wives, and children; in extreme cases, they will offend against their superiors and forget their proper ranks, and what is most to be feared in the world will arrive. Therefore, corporal punishments were instituted in remote antiquity, and the events of executing Gun 鯀 and putting the Miao 苗 to death were not far removed from the era of primeval chaos. Yet those several sages, if they did not speak of "reverent compassion," spoke of "holding to the mean." They used the Three Dukes and the Eight Deliberations to weigh the circumstances of offenses, and the Fine Stone (jiashi 嘉石) and the Red Stone (feishi 肺石) to give vent to hidden grievances, ensuring that the world would not be distressed amid beatings and prisons or by the fines of contributing metal and bundles of arrows; yet whenever treacherous magnates or fierce and arrogant men onceran afoul of the law, they resolutely cut them down. Thus, those who persisted in wrongdoing could not escape their execution, while those who erred by mistake were able to have their injustices redressed. Once the weeds are removed, the fine grain flourishes. The sages considered that only when it is like this can the people of the world and of later generations rely on our laws and be free from fear. Therefore, their intention was as mild as spring and as nurturing as dew, yet their laws were as stern as a precipitous cliff, as swift as a crash of thunder, and as awe-inspiring as if sent down from Heaven and established by Earth, so that the people dared not trifle with them. And was it only the people who dared not trifle with them? Where there is law, there is stability; where there is no law, there is collapse—even those who institute the laws cannot trifle with them. When the reins were held in check at Xiliu 細柳, the ruler could not gallop his horse; when the servant of the Elder Princess was struck down, the Empress could not vent her anger. Though one be as brave as Wu Huo 烏獲, as favored as Han Xin 韓信 and Peng Yue 彭越, or as accomplished as Cao Cao 曹操 and Sima Yi 司馬懿, yet still be anxiously fearful of not escaping the three-foot bamboo tablets of the law—such is inherently the nature of the sages' law. Yet when those who apply the law are cramped…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
於一隅而不知中正仁義之意故以嚴濟
嚴則威竭而不振爲咸陽之轍矣以寬濟
寬則惠褻而下不以爲恩爲元成之季矣
不有昭曠域外之觀何以維天下之法而
定持法者之評哉彼東山之征兩觀之誅
非戕懿親而違衆好也法不得徇也乃尹
鐸李牧諸賢至於墮城縱寇而公庾且矯
發焉何其剸觚恣行若是也蓋事有必集
無庸於拘攣禍迫焉也故五日告完不繕
===
非惰矣一鼓成烈縱寇非殃矣志全子母
則田叔不嫌於燬詞心在憂民則長孺不
忌於發粟若夫通融庫藏固伯淳達權濟
時之宜而循良化誨卽文饒之蒲鞭且贅
矣之數子者原聖人之意以權天下之宜
而不疑於君不訾於吏者固以寬而用嚴
者也盜器不族犯蹕不刑非輕主威而縱
惡少也法不得過也若夫武侯魏公諸賢
至於賊友抑功而噸笑且不假焉何其刻
punctuated: 於一隅，而不知中正仁義之意。故以嚴濟嚴，則威竭而不振，爲咸陽之轍矣；以寬濟寬，則惠褻而下不以爲恩，爲元、成之季矣。不有昭曠域外之觀，何以維天下之法，而定持法者之評哉？彼東山之征、兩觀之誅，非戕懿親而違衆好也，法不得徇也。乃尹鐸、李牧諸賢，至於墮城、縱寇，而公庾且矯發焉，何其剸觚恣行若是也？蓋事有必集，無庸於拘攣禍迫焉也。故五日告完，不繕非惰矣；一鼓成烈，縱寇非殃矣。志全子母，則田叔不嫌於燬詞；心在憂民，則長孺不忌於發粟。若夫通融庫藏，固伯淳達權濟時之宜；而循良化誨，卽文饒之蒲鞭且贅矣。之數子者，原聖人之意，以權天下之宜，而不疑於君，不訾於吏者，固以寬而用嚴者也。盜器不族，犯蹕不刑，非輕主威而縱惡少也，法不得過也。若夫武侯、魏公諸賢，至於賊友、抑功，而噸笑且不假焉，何其刻
translation_en:
…confined to one corner, without understanding the meaning of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness. Therefore, when severity is supplemented with severity, authority is exhausted and fails to rouse, following in the tracks of Xianyang [the Qin dynasty]; when leniency is supplemented with leniency, kindness becomes cheapened and subordinates do not regard it as grace, ending up like the declining years of Emperors Yuan and Cheng [of the Han]. Without a bright, expansive vision that transcends conventional bounds, how could one uphold the laws of the realm and settle the evaluations of those who administer the law?

Now, the Eastern Mountain campaign [of the Duke of Zhou] and the execution beneath the Two Watchtowers [by Confucius] were not cases of harming close kin or defying popular sentiment; rather, the law could not be bent for private favors. Yet worthies such as Yin Duo 尹鐸 and Li Mu 李牧 went so far as to lower city walls and let raiders go unchallenged, or even to open public granaries by feigning imperial orders—how could they act with such disregard for the rules and such unrestrained license? It is because when an undertaking must be brought to completion, there is no use in being bound and narrowly constrained [reading 褊迫 for 禍迫?]. Thus, when repairs were reported complete in five days, not having fortified earlier was not negligence; when heroic victory was achieved at a single drumbeat, having let the raiders go earlier was no disaster. Because his resolve was to preserve the bond between mother and son [Empress Dowager Dou and Emperor Jing], Tian Shu 田叔 did not shrink from burning the interrogation records; because his heart was set on relieving the people's distress, Changru 長孺 [Ji An 汲黯] did not hesitate to distribute grain from the granaries. As for flexibly reallocating treasury funds, that was indeed Bochun's 伯淳 [Cheng Hao 程顥] expedient measure to adapt to circumstances and aid the times; and when upright officials transform the people through moral instruction, even Wenrao's 文饒 [Liu Kuan 劉寬] reed whip becomes superfluous. These several gentlemen traced the intent of the sages in order to weigh what was appropriate for the realm; neither suspected by their rulers nor criticized by the legal officials, they were truly those who employed severity through leniency.

Not exterminating the clan of one who stole sacred vessels from the imperial temple, and not executing one who startled the imperial cortege [as judged by Zhang Shizhi 張釋之], were not cases of slighting the ruler's majesty or indulging wicked youths; rather, the law could not be exceeded. Yet worthies such as Marquis Wu 武侯 [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] and Duke Wei 魏公 [Zhang Jun 張浚] went so far as to execute a friend or suppress rewards for merit, and would not even grant a frown or a smile lightly—how could they be so harsh…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
核寡恩若是也蓋法在必行無容於賣法
徇情焉也故不戮馬謖則祁山之師不可
出不繩曲端則符離之敗不可救欲防邊
釁宋璟非薄於靈筌欲懲悍胥一錢非忍
於張詠若夫以嚴成功固孝肅澄清輦轂
之意而豪右恣橫卽李果之峻厲非苛矣
之數子者得聖人之慮以振天下之玩而
內不逼主外不僨事固以嚴而成寬者也
要之各有當焉而非膠柱者可與議也我
===
===
聖祖酌古準今博稽逖覽制為成法以肅天下
臣民之心功當事事當言則賞功不當事
事不當言則誅輿馬服器邊備夷情靡不
有一定之制
神聖潤色愈精愈詳行於縣邑州郡總於監司
府部而大臣挈其綱臺諫補其闕餘二百
年道揆法守凜如也夜半出片紙卽豪宗
悍帥與四夷君長如笞小兒法令之行固
矣然巨憝逋播於山澤贓吏尚逸於刑網
punctuated: 核寡恩若是也？蓋法在必行，無容於賣法徇情焉也。故不戮馬謖，則祁山之師不可出；不繩曲端，則符離之敗不可救。欲防邊釁，宋璟非薄於靈筌；欲懲悍胥，一錢非忍於張詠。若夫以嚴成功，固孝肅澄清輦轂之意；而豪右恣橫，卽李果之峻厲非苛矣。之數子者，得聖人之慮以振天下之玩，而內不逼主，外不僨事，固以嚴而成寬者也。要之各有當焉，而非膠柱者可與議也。我聖祖酌古準今，博稽逖覽，制為成法，以肅天下臣民之心。功當事、事當言則賞，功不當事、事不當言則誅，輿馬服器、邊備夷情，靡不有一定之制。神聖潤色，愈精愈詳，行於縣邑州郡，總於監司府部，而大臣挈其綱，臺諫補其闕，餘二百年，道揆法守，凜如也。夜半出片紙，卽豪宗悍帥與四夷君長，如笞小兒，法令之行固矣。然巨憝逋播於山澤，贓吏尚逸於刑網，
translation_en:
…and ungracious to such a degree? This is because the law must be enforced, leaving no room for perverting the law to indulge personal feelings. Thus, had Ma Su 馬謖 not been executed, the campaign at Mount Qi 祁山 could not have been launched; had Qu Duan 曲端 not been disciplined by law, the defeat at Fuli 符離 could not have been remedied. Wishing to prevent border incidents, Song Jing 宋璟 was not being ungenerous toward Hao Lingquan 郝靈筌; wishing to punish an unruly clerk, Zhang Yong 張詠 was not being cruel over a single coin. As for achieving success through severity, this was indeed the intent of Lord Xiaosu 孝肅 (Bao Zheng 包拯) in purifying the imperial capital; and when powerful families acted with unbridled arrogance, even the sternness of Li Guo 李果 [?] was not overly harsh. These several men grasped the forethought of the sages in order to shake the realm out of its complacency; inwardly they did not encroach upon the ruler, and outwardly they did not ruin affairs—truly, they achieved leniency through severity. In sum, each was appropriate to his circumstances, and this is not something that can be discussed with those who stubbornly cling to fixed rules.

Our Sacred Ancestor weighed antiquity and took the present as his standard; conducting broad investigations and far-reaching surveys, he established immutable laws to inspire awe in the hearts of officials and commoners throughout the realm. When achievements matched the undertaking and the undertaking matched the words, there were rewards; when achievements did not match the undertaking and the undertaking did not match the words, there was punishment. From carriages, horses, garments, and utensils to frontier defenses and barbarian affairs, there was nothing without a fixed regulation. Successive divine sages embellished and refined these laws, making them ever more precise and detailed. They are carried out in the districts, prefectures, and subprefectures, and brought together under the Surveillance Commissions, Chief Military Commissions, and Ministries, while the grand ministers hold the guiding cords and the Censorate and Speaking Officials mend any omissions. For over two hundred years, the principles of governance and the observance of the law have been held in awe. If a slip of paper is issued at midnight, even powerful clans, fierce commanders, and the chieftains of the four barbarian quarters obey as submissively as a small child being whipped; the enforcement of laws and ordinances is firm indeed. Yet great malefactors still flee and hide in the mountains and marshes, corrupt officials still escape the net of punishment,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
越獄劫餉踵踵報聞誠如執事所憂者大
都俗乆而玩情狃而偷也積弛之後利用
振刷乃慮豪傑之士觸足冒法而又以持
法太急下多不肖之心愈密愈巧焉噫此
豈法之弊哉行法者弊之也彼獸廢爪牙
則充豺虎之腸矣國無紀綱則授姦雄之
柄矣積金在市掉臂不顧置姬嬙於闤闠
而人不敢睨目者法也法其可不嚴乎蓋
使誠賢智而濫傷也誠猾傑而逸網也法
===
===
之過也然而不然也今之人固有跡似而
實不似者可遽信之乎即如不繕城郭擅
用庫錢果皆尹鐸伯淳之賢乎則簿書期
會之間稍存寬大涵容之意不然未可縱
也即如大言無當輕身冒敵果皆馬謖曲
端之不肖乎則壞法干紀之秋自有信賞
必罰之典不然未可繩也此心跡之當辨
者也贓吏以獄爲市俗儒以寬爲仁而福
田報應之說浸其骨髓往往骯法紀以惠
punctuated: 越獄劫餉，踵踵報聞，誠如執事所憂者。大都俗乆而玩，情狃而偷也。積弛之後，利用振刷，乃慮豪傑之士觸足冒法，而又以持法太急，下多不肖之心，愈密愈巧焉。噫！此豈法之弊哉？行法者弊之也。彼獸廢爪牙，則充豺虎之腸矣；國無紀綱，則授姦雄之柄矣。積金在市，掉臂不顧；置姬嬙於闤闠，而人不敢睨目者，法也。法其可不嚴乎？蓋使誠賢智而濫傷也，誠猾傑而逸網也，法之過也；然而不然也。今之人固有跡似而實不似者，可遽信之乎？即如不繕城郭、擅用庫錢，果皆尹鐸、伯淳之賢乎？則簿書期會之間，稍存寬大涵容之意；不然，未可縱也。即如大言無當、輕身冒敵，果皆馬謖、曲端之不肖乎？則壞法干紀之秋，自有信賞必罰之典；不然，未可繩也。此心跡之當辨者也。贓吏以獄爲市，俗儒以寬爲仁，而福田報應之說浸其骨髓，往往骯法紀以惠…
translation_en: …and jailbreaks and the plundering of military provisions are repeatedly reported—truly just as Your Excellency worries. On the whole, when customs endure for a long time, people grow negligent; when sentiments become habituated, people grow lax. After a long accumulation of laxity, it is advantageous to rouse and sweep things clean. Yet there is concern that heroic and outstanding men might trip and run afoul of the law, and furthermore that if the law is enforced too urgently, those below will harbor many unworthy intentions—the tighter the net, the more cunning they become. Alas! How could this be the fault of the law? It is those who administer the law who corrupt it. If a beast discards its claws and fangs, it merely fills the bellies of jackals and tigers; if a state lacks discipline and order, it hands the handle of power to treacherous and ambitious men. When gold is piled up in the marketplace and passersby swing their arms without a backward glance, or when noble beauties are placed in the city thoroughfares and no one dares cast a sidelong glance at them—that is due to the law. How, then, can the law not be strict? For if those who are truly worthy and wise were to be indiscriminately harmed, or those who are truly cunning and recalcitrant were to escape the net, that would be the fault of the law; yet that is not the case. Among people today, there are certainly those whose outward actions resemble something that their inner reality does not—can one hastily trust them? For instance, when officials fail to repair city walls or unauthorizedly spend treasury funds, do they all possess the worthiness of Yin Duo and Bochun (Cheng Hao 程顥)? If so, then amidst account books and scheduled deadlines, one may preserve a measure of leniency and tolerance; otherwise, they must not be indulged. Or for instance, when men boast without substance or rashly hurl themselves at the enemy, are they all as unworthy as Ma Su and Qu Duan? If so, then in times when laws are ruined and discipline is violated, there are naturally the statutes of trustworthy rewards and certain punishments; otherwise, they must not be mechanically restrained. This is the distinction that ought to be made between intention and outward deed. Corrupt officials treat litigation as a marketplace, while vulgar scholars regard leniency as benevolence; steeped to the marrow in doctrines of karmic merit and retribution, they frequently bend the laws and discipline in order to show favor to…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
姦慝其高明者爭事風力以搏虚聲希望
過聽濫肆誅求至於刻木畫地而不敢對
則寛嚴胥失其中矣此積習之當禁者也
多指亂視多言亂聽從古患之今
國家申飭法制本非益於其舊即有不測之
恩威意在集事而耳視目聽者未究其歸
明一法則病其煩寛一人則疑其故而泄
泄然以為無擾可也無所事事可也則天
下之法竟何自而申耶此議論之當定者
===
也嗟乎今天下之士試思其所以訓子弟
束臧獲者能愛而不勞乎能粱肉而不撻
笞乎勞之笞之固成之也吾能愛天下如
其子弟如其家人足矣奈何以按法循令
者為過而為迂闊不經之論也即謂鷹鸇
不若鸞鳳溲渤不若參苓而為天下興利
擇便以循疾苦然紀綱不嚴姦黠壅遏吾
之惠能逮於民否也棟梁相持寛則不相
固斲者不苦不甘乃成室焉此用法之平
punctuated: 姦慝。其高明者，爭事風力，以搏虚聲，希望過聽，濫肆誅求，至於刻木畫地而不敢對，則寛嚴胥失其中矣。此積習之當禁者也。多指亂視，多言亂聽，從古患之。今國家申飭法制，本非益於其舊，即有不測之恩威，意在集事，而耳視目聽者未究其歸。明一法則病其煩，寛一人則疑其故，而泄泄然以為無擾可也，無所事事可也，則天下之法竟何自而申耶？此議論之當定者也。嗟乎！今天下之士，試思其所以訓子弟、束臧獲者，能愛而不勞乎？能粱肉而不撻笞乎？勞之、笞之，固成之也。吾能愛天下如其子弟、如其家人，足矣。奈何以按法循令者為過，而為迂闊不經之論也？即謂鷹鸇不若鸞鳳，溲渤不若參苓，而為天下興利擇便以循疾苦，然紀綱不嚴，姦黠壅遏，吾之惠能逮於民否也？棟梁相持，寛則不相固，斲者不苦不甘，乃成室焉。此用法之平…
translation_en: … the wicked and deceitful. Meanwhile, those who consider themselves high-minded vie in displaying forceful resolve to win empty reputation, currying favor by pandering to mistaken hearings and wantonly engaging in extortion and harsh exactions, to the point where people dread carving wooden effigies of jailers or drawing lines on the ground as prisons and dare not answer them. Thus both leniency and severity miss the due mean. This is an entrenched habit that must be prohibited. That many pointing fingers confuse the sight and many words confuse the hearing has been a malady since antiquity. Now, when the state reiterates and tightens laws and institutions, it is not actually adding to what existed of old; even if there are unfathomable acts of grace and severity, the intention is to accomplish the work of government, yet those who see with their ears and hear with their eyes fail to examine their ultimate purpose. When a single law is clarified, they criticize it as burdensome; when a single person is shown leniency, they suspect some ulterior motive. Listlessly, they think it suffices not to cause disturbance and suffices not to busy oneself with anything—how then can the laws of the empire ever be enforced? This is why public discussion must be settled. Alas! Let the scholars and officials of the empire today reflect on how they instruct their younger kinsmen and restrain their household servants: can one love them without making them toil? Can one feed them fine grain and meat without ever using the rod and whip? To make them toil and to flog them is in truth to bring them to completion. If we can love the empire as we love our younger kinsmen and our own family members, that is enough. Why then regard those who uphold the laws and follow ordinances as being at fault, and indulge in pedantic and preposterous arguments? Even if one says that hawks and falcons are not as good as luan-birds and phoenixes, or that dregs and horse-urine herbs are not as good as ginseng and poria, and wishes to promote benefits and choose conveniences for the empire in order to soothe its distress and suffering—yet if discipline and order are not strict, and the wicked and cunning block the way, can our kindness ever reach the common people? When ridgepoles and beams support one another, if the joints are too loose they will not hold fast together; only when the carpenter cuts them neither too tight nor too loose is a house completed. This is the evenhandedness of applying the law…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也尹鐸張詠諸賢之意亦聖人之意也非
所謂商君韓非子之意也而老氏欲剖斗
折衡以求不爭正苦於民不畏死耳豈謂
寛然以廢天下之法者哉故下有截然之
規上有渾然之意使士農工賈各勤本業
賞罰進退必當功罪紳弁循矩愒玩以飭
法守而輕重出入惟
朝廷之指使焉至於
廟堂之間交儆協心振紀綱而志不狃於因
===
循維風俗而具必先於敎化則元氣旣厚
神氣自振嘉樂唐虞固易易也令行事集
豈足言哉
第三問
傅爾珎
同考試官敎諭毛批四事方今急務未易措置是
策洞悉源委而經畫井然蓋未離畝畝而先天下之憂者也
考試官敎諭劉批區畫明盡卓有遠識
考試官敎諭蔣批條列四事鑿鑿可行經世之學也
punctuated:
也。尹鐸、張詠諸賢之意，亦聖人之意也，非所謂商君、韓非子之意也。而老氏欲剖斗折衡以求不爭，正苦於民不畏死耳，豈謂寛然以廢天下之法者哉？故下有截然之規，上有渾然之意，使士、農、工、賈各勤本業，賞罰進退必當功罪，紳弁循矩，愒玩以飭法守，而輕重出入，惟朝廷之指使焉。至於廟堂之間，交儆協心，振紀綱而志不狃於因循，維風俗而具必先於敎化，則元氣旣厚，神氣自振，嘉樂唐、虞，固易易也；令行事集，豈足言哉！

第三問
傅爾珎
同考試官敎諭毛批：四事方今急務，未易措置。是策洞悉源委，而經畫井然，蓋未離畝畝而先天下之憂者也。
考試官敎諭劉批：區畫明盡，卓有遠識。
考試官敎諭蔣批：條列四事，鑿鑿可行，經世之學也。
translation_en:
… [This is] the balanced application of the law. The intent of such worthies as Yin Duo 尹鐸 and Zhang Yong 張詠 is also the intent of the sages; it is not what is meant by the intent of Lord Shang 商君 or Master Han Fei 韓非子. And when Laozi 老氏 wished to split the peck-measure and break the balance-beam in order to seek non-contention, it was precisely because he was distressed that the people did not fear death; how could he have meant to abolishing the laws of the empire out of sheer leniency? Therefore, when below there are clear-cut regulations, and above there is an all-encompassing magnanimity—causing scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants each to be diligent in their fundamental occupations; ensuring that rewards and punishments, promotions and demotions invariably match merits and offenses; making civil officials and military officers follow the rules, and curbing negligence and laxity [?] to rectify adherence to the law, while the weighing of severity and leniency rests solely at the direction of the Court—and when, within the imperial halls, ruler and ministers mutually admonish one another and unite their hearts, rousing the綱紀 (institutions and laws) with a resolve that does not fall into the rut of routine, and upholding customs with measures that necessarily put moral transformation first, then once the vital energy of the state is rich, its spiritual vigor will naturally be roused. Achieving the joyous prosperity of Tang 唐 and Yu 虞 will truly be quite easy; what need is there even to speak of orders being carried out and affairs being accomplished!

Question Three
Fu Erzhen 傅爾珎
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Mao 毛: The four matters are urgent tasks of the present day and are not easy to manage. This policy essay thoroughly understands their origins and developments, and its planning is orderly and methodical. Truly, here is one who has not yet left the furrowed fields and yet already worries before the rest of the world worries.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉: The planning is clear and exhaustive, outstandingly possessing far-sighted vision.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣: It sets out the four matters item by item in a manner that is indisputably practicable—this is statecraft learning.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
天下之事有不能不因乎古者有不能必
因乎古者時至而勢必趨焉勢趨而理必
從焉順必至之理而權其當爲之時宜於
法古不嫌於非今宜於準今不嫌於悖古
則時不我窮也勢不我局也而事必如吾
議矣何者時異而我之應不窮也夫聽亂
於多而事斷於獨固也然衢室總章郊祀
鹽鐵諄諄而議因以時勢之當非衆見弗
與也然局者變態神倏而不能逃於圖譜
===
之中症與方合舉而用之旬日脉候不齊
易一方而愈焉此國手也議法者何以異
此今天下之事其可議者孰有大於河患
虜患乎又孰急於
宗祿民兵乎然議之而卒莫能應之者篤於
時也夫黃河爲患從古病之三代而下議
治河者不過賈讓賈魯之策矣然讓之議
除害而非興利魯之策塞決而不濬流均
無裨於運道也
punctuated:
天下之事，有不能不因乎古者，有不能必因乎古者。時至而勢必趨焉，勢趨而理必從焉。順必至之理，而權其當爲之時。宜於法古，不嫌於非今；宜於準今，不嫌於悖古。則時不我窮也，勢不我局也，而事必如吾議矣。何者？時異而我之應不窮也。夫聽亂於多，而事斷於獨，固也；然衢室、總章，郊祀、鹽鐵，諄諄而議，因以時勢之當，非衆見弗與也。然局者變態神倏，而不能逃於圖譜之中；症與方合，舉而用之，旬日脉候不齊，易一方而愈焉，此國手也。議法者何以異此？

今天下之事，其可議者，孰有大於河患、虜患乎？又孰急於宗祿、民兵乎？然議之而卒莫能應之者，篤於時也。夫黃河爲患，從古病之。三代而下，議治河者，不過賈讓、賈魯之策矣。然讓之議除害而非興利，魯之策塞決而不濬流，均無裨於運道也。
translation_en:
Among the affairs of the realm, there are those in which one cannot but follow antiquity, and those in which one cannot insist on following antiquity. When the times arrive, circumstances inevitably incline in a certain direction; when circumstances incline, principle inevitably follows. If one conforms to the principle of what must inevitably arrive and weighs the appropriate time to act—when it is fitting to model on antiquity, not hesitating to reject the present, and when it is fitting to adapt to the present, not hesitating to depart from antiquity—then the times will not exhaust us, circumstances will not confine us, and affairs will surely turn out as we deliberate. Why is this? Because the times change, yet our responses are inexhaustible. Now, it is certainly true that listening to many confuses the hearing while affairs are decided by a single mind; yet in the consultations of the Audience Hall at the Crossroads (Qushi) and the Hall of Light (Zongzhang), and the debates over the suburban sacrifices and the salt and iron monopolies, people deliberated earnestly because determining what suited the times and circumstances required the participation of collective views. Likewise, a board game changes its configuration with marvelous suddenness, yet it cannot escape the patterns of the manuals; when a symptom matches a prescription, one applies it, and if after ten days the pulse and signs vary, one changes the prescription and cures the illness—this is a master physician (guoshou). How do those who deliberate on laws differ from this?

Among the affairs of the realm today that call for deliberation, which are greater than the disasters of the Yellow River and the menace of the northern caitiffs? And which are more urgent than the stipends of the imperial clan and the civilian militia? Yet the reason people deliberate on them without finally being able to respond effectively is that they are overly bound to the present moment [?]. Now, the Yellow River causing disasters has been a malady since antiquity. From the Three Dynasties onward, those who deliberated on controlling the River have gone no further than the plans of Jia Rang 賈讓 and Jia Lu 賈魯. Yet Jia Rang's deliberations were about eliminating harm rather than promoting benefit, and Jia Lu's plan was about plugging breaches rather than dredging the current; neither is of any help to the grain transport canal.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
國家倚藉河運歲輸百萬石以實
京師今茶城淤梗蓋數年矣直沽之運旣以
漂沒告罷而境山柪石難疏膠萊海水相
隔是膠河之難竟亦勢也嘗聞
國初運道自淮達河自沁通衞兩不相妨嗣
緣河决張秋乃導汶洸諸泉之利而徐吕
險峻必資黃水行舟遂因蕭縣决口通浮
濟二洪而河始侵漕矣然猶未病也嘉靖
末年華山再决北徙茶城上侵漕河七十
===
餘里則河病而漕亦病焉有如茶城東决
橫截漕河其害可勝言哉故復符離之故
道改黃河於徐州之東而倍築長堤護衞
陵寢分河漕而兩利焉責重費鉅然至計也暫
開浮濟之淤以避茶城之害玉花諸泉引
濟徐吕或斷流而大濬焉事便工省亦近
策也然水性就下智者順之今草灣雲梯
等關日淤日壅尾閭不通上源安得而不
漫乎故移泇萊二河之費以疏其壅而又
punctuated: 國家倚藉河運，歲輸百萬石以實京師。今茶城淤梗，蓋數年矣。直沽之運，旣以漂沒告罷，而境山柪石難疏，膠萊海水相隔，是膠河之難竟，亦勢也。嘗聞國初運道，自淮達河，自沁通衞，兩不相妨。嗣緣河决張秋，乃導汶、洸諸泉之利，而徐、吕險峻，必資黃水行舟，遂因蕭縣决口，通浮、濟二洪，而河始侵漕矣，然猶未病也。嘉靖末年，華山再决，北徙茶城，上侵漕河七十餘里，則河病而漕亦病焉。有如茶城東决，橫截漕河，其害可勝言哉！故復符離之故道，改黃河於徐州之東，而倍築長堤，護衞陵寢，分河、漕而兩利焉，責重費鉅，然至計也。暫開浮、濟之淤，以避茶城之害，玉花諸泉引濟徐、吕，或斷流而大濬焉，事便工省，亦近策也。然水性就下，智者順之。今草灣、雲梯等關，日淤日壅，尾閭不通，上源安得而不漫乎？故移泇、萊二河之費以疏其壅，而又
translation_en: The Dynasty relies on river transport, annually shipping millions of piculs of grain to supply the Capital. Now Chacheng 茶城 has been silted up and obstructed for several years. Sea transport via Zhigu 直沽 has already been discontinued due to shipwrecks and losses, while at Jingshan 境山 [for the proposed Jia River 泇河 route] the stubborn rock is difficult to excavate, and along the Jiaolai 膠萊 canal the sea waters are blocked off from one another—thus the difficulty of completing the Jiaolai and Jia River projects is also dictated by the terrain. I have heard that at the founding of the Dynasty, the transport route went from the Huai 淮 River to the Yellow River, and from the Qin 沁 River to the Wei 衞 River, neither interfering with the other. Later, because the Yellow River breached its banks at Zhangqiu 張秋, the benefits of the Wen 汶, Guang 洸, and other springs were channeled in; yet because the rapids at Xuzhou 徐州 and Lüliang 吕梁 were险峻 (precipitous), boats had to rely on the waters of the Yellow River to pass. Consequently, taking advantage of the breach at Xiaoxian 蕭縣, the waters were connected to the two rapids of Fushan 浮山 and Jining 濟寧 [?], and from then on the Yellow River began to encroach upon the Grand Canal—yet it had not become a grave affliction. In the final years of the Jiajing 嘉靖 reign (1522–1566), the river breached again at Huashan 華山, shifting northward to Chacheng and encroaching upward upon the Grand Canal for more than seventy li, whereupon both the Yellow River and the Grand Canal suffered. Should it breach eastward at Chacheng and cut straight across the Grand Canal, could the harm possibly be described in words! Therefore, restoring the old course at Fuli 符離, diverting the Yellow River to the east of Xuzhou, building double-strength long dikes to protect the Imperial Tombs, and separating the Yellow River from the Grand Canal so that both benefit—though the responsibility is heavy and the expense vast, this is the ultimate plan. Temporarily dredging the silt of the Fu and Ji channels to avoid the hazard at Chacheng, drawing the Yuhua 玉花 and other springs to supply the Xuzhou and Lüliang rapids, or damming the flow to carry out a major dredging—being convenient to execute and economical in labor, this is also an immediate policy. Yet the nature of water is to flow downward, and the wise follow it. Nowadays, passes such as Caowan 草灣 and Yunti 雲梯 grow more silted and blocked by the day. When the outlet to the sea is obstructed, how can the upper reaches fail to overflow? Therefore, redirecting the funds meant for the Jia and Jiaolai rivers to dredge out these blockages, and furthermore…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
多開支河以洩怒濤北而芝麻等莊南而
高寶等堤靡不為之實心經理而嚴其賞
罰使防河與防虜等焉庶人心競勸事懷
永圖而飛輓雲連運道其有濟矣夷狄為
患從古記之自周以來議制虜者不過撻
伐和親之策耳然迅掃幕南或失之黷和
親歲幣或失之辱均無益於國體者也
先帝威稜遠播今
上文武聖神北虜稽款邊燧不警軼曩代矣顧
===
夷馬之散處無策而羸豕之蹢躅當防其
說非過計也愚謂夷狄之强弱異時而中
國之措置異便今之夷狄其强非冒頓其
弱非呼韓也夫其不若冒頓也而歸降則
拒款市則却固不免於狹小
皇化而其不若呼韓也則又安得狃於柙虎篝
鷹而漫然不為之備也故責屯練之實効
徹桑土於未雨之時而修築大邊歸併小
堡藉羈縻而修守焉計歲程功此急務也
punctuated:
多開支河以洩怒濤，北而芝麻等莊，南而高、寶等堤，靡不為之實心經理，而嚴其賞罰，使防河與防虜等焉。庶人心競勸，事懷永圖，而飛輓雲連，運道其有濟矣。

夷狄為患，從古記之。自周以來，議制虜者，不過撻伐、和親之策耳。然迅掃幕南，或失之黷；和親歲幣，或失之辱，均無益於國體者也。先帝威稜遠播，今上文武聖神，北虜稽款，邊燧不警，軼曩代矣。顧夷馬之散處無策，而羸豕之蹢躅當防，其說非過計也。愚謂夷狄之强弱異時，而中國之措置異便。今之夷狄，其强非冒頓，其弱非呼韓也。夫其不若冒頓也，而歸降則拒，款市則却，固不免於狹小皇化；而其不若呼韓也，則又安得狃於柙虎篝鷹，而漫然不為之備也？故責屯練之實効，徹桑土於未雨之時，而修築大邊，歸併小堡，藉羈縻而修守焉，計歲程功，此急務也。
translation_en:
…open many branch canals to drain the raging torrents. To the north, at places such as Zhima Village, and to the south, along the dikes of Gaoyou and Baoying, we must manage every part with genuine commitment and strictly enforce rewards and punishments, treating river defense as equal in importance to defense against the northern caitiffs. In this way, people's hearts will be spurred to diligence, affairs will be planned with a view to lasting results, grain transport barges will stream in like clouds, and the Grand Canal will be saved.

That the non-Chinese tribes are a menace has been recorded since antiquity. Since the Zhou dynasty, those who have discussed controlling the caitiffs have proposed nothing more than policies of punitive expeditions or marriage alliances. Yet sweeping clean the lands south of the desert sometimes errs in excessive militarism, while marriage alliances and annual tribute payments sometimes err in humiliation; neither is of any benefit to the dignity of the state. The awe-inspiring prestige of the Late Emperor spread far and wide, and His Present Majesty is accomplished in both the civil and military arts, sagely and divine. The northern caitiffs have bowed their heads in submission, the frontier beacon fires raise no alarms, and the achievements of past eras have been surpassed. Yet those who argue that there is no plan for the dispersed placement of the tribesmen's horses, and that we must guard against the restless pacing of a tethered pig, are not being overly anxious.

In my humble view, the strength and weakness of the non-Chinese tribes vary with the times, and China's measures should vary according to what is expedient. As for the tribes of today, in their strength they are no Modu, and in their weakness they are no Huhanye. Since they are not like Modu, to reject them when they surrender and to refuse them when they seek tribute and horse markets would surely be to construe the Imperial transformative influence too narrowly. And since they are not like Huhanye, how can we grow complacent, treating them as caged tigers and hooded falcons, and negligently fail to make preparations against them? Therefore, demanding substantive results from military farms and troop training, gathering mulberry root-bark before it rains, repairing and building the outer frontier walls, consolidating small forts, and taking advantage of the "loose-rein" peace to repair our defenses while assessing progress year by year—this is our urgent task.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
散夷馬於牧場擇補薊鎮之額而寛其馬
值以綏邊民防護根本此遠猷也然萬丈
之堤慎於蟻穴今夷將通丁紛沓內地虛
實阨塞巳竊窺之肘腋可不慮乎故必靳
重大之權以抑降將而又稽覈通丁防其
漏逸宣大之獨石應朔關陝之甘固延寧
靡不爲之加意隄備而失防通釁仍與失
事同罰焉則可款可戰諸鎮自定而組繫
東虜夷情不足慮矣
===
國初宗屬四萬祿僅倍之而
代肅諸藩額廩千石將軍以下改官敘遷
祖訓昭昭也乃今大倍其初而祿入不繼喧嗔
公署甚則束腹待哺不若閭閻細民猶得
糊其口焉此議之所以汲汲也愚以五世
之祖尚得祧遷六世之孫封爵無紀是忍
於親盡之祖而不忍於親盡之孫舛也故
親郡世及無容議矣而
郡王之次封鎮國者可限也輔奉中尉以嫡
punctuated:
散夷馬於牧場，擇補薊鎮之額，而寛其馬值，以綏邊民，防護根本，此遠猷也。然萬丈之堤，慎於蟻穴。今夷將通丁，紛沓內地，虛實阨塞，巳竊窺之，肘腋可不慮乎？故必靳重大之權以抑降將，而又稽覈通丁，防其漏逸。宣、大之獨石、應、朔，關、陝之甘、固、延、寧，靡不爲之加意隄備，而失防通釁，仍與失事同罰焉。則可款可戰，諸鎮自定，而組繫東虜，夷情不足慮矣。

國初宗屬四萬，祿僅倍之，而代、肅諸藩額廩千石，將軍以下改官敘遷，《祖訓》昭昭也。乃今大倍其初，而祿入不繼，喧嗔公署，甚則束腹待哺，不若閭閻細民猶得糊其口焉。此議之所以汲汲也。愚以五世之祖尚得祧遷，六世之孫封爵無紀，是忍於親盡之祖，而不忍於親盡之孫，舛也。故親、郡世及，無容議矣；而郡王之次封鎮國者，可限也；輔、奉、中尉以嫡…
translation_en:
Dispersing the barbarians' horses among our pasturelands, selecting the best to fill the quotas of Jizhen Defense Command, and being generous with horse valuations to pacify the frontier people and protect the dynastic heartland—this is a far-sighted plan. Yet a dike of ten thousand zhang must be guarded against a single ant-hole. Today, barbarian generals and interpreter-soldiers mingle in throngs throughout the interior; they have already secretly spied out our strengths, weaknesses, and strategic passes. How can we not worry about trouble right at our elbows and armpits? Therefore, we must withhold weighty authority in order to curb surrendered generals, and also inspect and verify the interpreter-soldiers to prevent them from leaking intelligence or absconding. At Dushi, Yingzhou, and Shuozhou in Xuanfu and Datong, and at Gansu, Guyuan, Yansui, and Ningxia in Guanzhong and Shaanxi, there is nowhere that we should not take special care to guard and prepare; and failure to prevent collusion that stirs up border hostilities should still be punished the same as military defeat. Then whether we make peace terms or wage war, all the defense commands will naturally be secure, we can bind the Eastern Caitiffs with a cord, and barbarian affairs will no longer be a cause for worry.

At the beginning of the dynasty, imperial clan members numbered forty thousand, and their stipends were merely double that, while the various princely fiefs such as Dai and Su had fixed grain stipends of a thousand piculs, and those of the rank of General and below were reassigned to regular official posts and promoted by merit—the Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun) are crystal clear on this. Yet today their numbers have multiplied vastly beyond the beginning, and stipend revenues cannot keep pace. They clamor angrily in government offices, and in extreme cases bind their bellies waiting to be fed, worse off than humble commoners of the alleys who can still manage to feed themselves. This is why discussions on the matter are so urgent. In my humble view, since ancestors at the fifth generation are still subject to removal to the distant ancestral shrine, for descendants at the sixth generation to receive noble titles without limit is to be hard-hearted toward ancestors whose kinship has expired while being soft-hearted toward descendants whose kinship has expired—which is perverse. Therefore, hereditary succession for Imperial Princes of the Blood and Commandery Princes admits of no discussion; however, the younger sons of Commandery Princes who are enfeoffed as Defenders-General of the State can be limited; and Bulwark-Generals, Supporters-General, and Commandants who succeed through the principal line…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
繼矣而奉國之降封世襲者可限也被罪
降封法當幷裁而宗女宗婿减婚貲之半
而給之祿可殺其十三矣然殺其祿而不
令治生非情也褫封之始設處閑田俾爲
世業擇其穎慧者入宗學而選舉黜陟悉
如時例盡弛出城之禁以居其宜焉固不
必株守名封貽終身之坎壈也無已則有
昔人惇宗之例乎酌處存留例銀置設院
署敦請無祿貧宗計口計日給以廩養總
===
支領之權於
親藩而生育保勘視昔尤加愼焉非苦之也
爲厚其生也彼惇睦九族尊位重祿孰不
知之然漢之諸王庶子寢封唐宋袒免以
下俱不賜名而同姓入仕則劉更生李長
源趙汝愚諸賢可考也變而通之未必非
親睦之仁矣不然則澤不斬於五世情不
便於四業而愈衍愈繁卽傾天下之賦能
供祿入之額乎
punctuated: 繼矣，而奉國之降封世襲者可限也。被罪降封，法當幷裁；而宗女、宗婿减婚貲之半而給之，祿可殺其十三矣。然殺其祿而不令治生，非情也。褫封之始，設處閑田，俾爲世業；擇其穎慧者入宗學，而選舉黜陟悉如時例；盡弛出城之禁，以居其宜焉，固不必株守名封，貽終身之坎壈也。無已，則有昔人惇宗之例乎？酌處存留例銀，置設院署，敦請無祿貧宗，計口計日，給以廩養，總支領之權於親藩，而生育保勘視昔尤加愼焉。非苦之也，爲厚其生也。彼惇睦九族、尊位重祿，孰不知之？然漢之諸王庶子寢封，唐、宋袒免以下俱不賜名，而同姓入仕，則劉更生、李長源、趙汝愚諸賢可考也。變而通之，未必非親睦之仁矣。不然，則澤不斬於五世，情不便於四業，而愈衍愈繁，卽傾天下之賦，能供祿入之額乎？
translation_en: … succeeded by the principal heir, whereas the hereditary succession by reduced enfeoffment for Defenders of the State (fengguo) can be limited. For those reduced in enfeoffment due to offenses, by law their stipends should be concurrently curtailed; and if the marriage allowances for imperial clanswomen and their consorts are reduced by half when granted, the stipends can be cut by three-tenths. Yet to cut their stipends without allowing them to make a living is contrary to human feeling. When first discontinuing their enfeoffments, we should allocate uncultivated lands to serve as their hereditary property; select the intelligent among them to enter the Imperial Clan Schools, with their selection, promotion, and demotion following current regulations in every respect; and completely relax the prohibition on leaving the city walls so they may settle where it suits them. Truly, they need not stubbornly cling to nominal titles, bequeathing a lifetime of hardship and frustration. If that is not enough, is there not the precedent of the ancients for generously supporting the clan? We could deliberate on allocating retained quota silver to establish courtyard compounds, cordially inviting unfeoffed impoverished clansmen and providing them with grain rations calculated by head and by day, consolidating the authority over disbursement and receipt in the hands of the Imperial Princes of the Blood, while making the verification and guarantee of births even more rigorous than in the past. This is not to make things hard for them, but to enrich their livelihood. As for showing generosity and harmony to the nine grades of kinsmen, and honoring their rank and making generous their stipends—who does not know of this? Yet in the Han dynasty, the enfeoffment of secondary sons of princes was discontinued; in the Tang and Song, those beyond the fifth degree of mourning (tanmian) were no longer bestowed imperial names; while as for members of the imperial surname entering officialdom, worthy men such as Liu Gengsheng (Liu Xiang 劉向), Li Changyuan (Li Mi 李泌), and Zhao Ruyu 趙汝愚 may be examined as precedents. To adapt and make flexible changes is not necessarily contrary to the benevolence of kinship and harmony. Otherwise, if royal grace is not terminated after five generations and circumstances do not allow them to engage in the four occupations, then as they multiply more and more, even if we exhausted the revenues of the entire empire, could we supply the quota for their stipends?

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
國初衞所星羅額軍餘三百萬而民壯弓兵
因地定制保甲之法規畫詳明
令甲可稽也乃今逃亡日眾尺籍漸虛借抵
操閱畢則羣然而散矣脫遇警變將何以
支此議之所以汲汲也愚以爲土著之兵
熟知利便而室家丘隴休戚相關舍土兵
之練而爲客兵之募迂也試查舊制額兵
幾何衞所不足則其餘丁可補也弓兵不
充則其族屬可募也五取其一十用其二
===
蠲其徭役登冊籍而爲兵焉則吾民卽吾
兵矣然籍其人而不授以器猶無兵也汰
弱清逋計其餘餉以爲器具之需敎閱則
逐名給散事完則歸之公庾而賞罰之費
總領之官胥此制用焉固不必增益軍儲
而待用有餘貲也乃訓練可不嚴乎三農
旣隙月必九閱責之清軍佐職簡敎技略
總殿最之權於撫巡而賞罰鼓舞悉如軍
制焉非難之也固閑其藝也彼石壕之詠
punctuated: 國初衞所星羅，額軍餘三百萬，而民壯、弓兵因地定制，保甲之法規畫詳明，令甲可稽也。乃今逃亡日眾，尺籍漸虛，借抵操閱，畢則羣然而散矣。脫遇警變，將何以支？此議之所以汲汲也。愚以爲土著之兵，熟知利便，而室家丘隴，休戚相關。舍土兵之練而爲客兵之募，迂也。試查舊制額兵幾何，衞所不足，則其餘丁可補也；弓兵不充，則其族屬可募也。五取其一，十用其二，蠲其徭役，登冊籍而爲兵焉，則吾民卽吾兵矣。然籍其人而不授以器，猶無兵也。汰弱清逋，計其餘餉以爲器具之需。敎閱則逐名給散，事完則歸之公庾，而賞罰之費、總領之官，胥此制用焉，固不必增益軍儲，而待用有餘貲也。乃訓練可不嚴乎？三農旣隙，月必九閱，責之清軍佐職，簡敎技略，總殿最之權於撫巡，而賞罰鼓舞悉如軍制焉。非難之也，固閑其藝也。彼《石壕》之詠、
translation_en: At the beginning of the dynasty, guards and battalions (weisuo) were spread out like stars, with an established quota of over three million soldiers, while militia (minzhuang) and archers (gongbing) were instituted according to local conditions, and the regulations for the mutual security (baojia) system were planned out in clear detail—all of which can be verified in the statutory codes. Yet nowadays, desertions grow more numerous by the day and the military registers gradually become empty; substitutes are borrowed to fill in at drills and reviews, and once those are finished they disperse in a crowd. Should an emergency or rebellion suddenly arise, wherewith would we withstand it? This is why discussions of the matter are so urgent. In my humble opinion, native-born troops are thoroughly familiar with local advantages, and since their homes, families, and ancestral graves are there, they share in the community's weal and woe. To abandon the training of local troops in favor of recruiting mercenary soldiers from elsewhere is impractical. Let us examine how many quota soldiers there were under the old system: if the guards and battalions are short, their supernumerary able-bodied males (yuding) can be used to fill the gaps; if the archers are not up to strength, their kinsmen can be recruited. Take one out of five, or employ two out of ten, exempt them from corvée labor, and enter them on the registers to serve as soldiers; then our common people will be our soldiers. Yet to register the men without supplying them with weapons is the same as having no soldiers at all. By weeding out the weak and clearing out absconders, we can reckon the surplus rations and use them to meet the need for equipment. At training reviews, distribute the weapons by name to each man, and when the affair is concluded, return them to the public storehouses; the expenses for rewards and punishments and for the commanding officers can all be defrayed from these funds, so that there is truly no need to increase military supplies, and yet there will be surplus resources ready for use. Furthermore, how could training and drill not be strict? Once the three agricultural seasons have entered their slack period, there must be nine reviews each month, charging the assistant officials responsible for clearing the military registers with selecting and instructing them in martial skills and tactics, while concentrating the authority to evaluate merits and demerits in the hands of the Grand Coordinator (fuxun), and conducting all rewards, punishments, and encouragement strictly according to military regulations. This is not done to make things difficult for them, but rather to familiarize them with their martial arts. As for the lament of the "Stone Moat" ("Shihao")…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
木蘭之詞孰不憐之然漢之騎士起於田
野唐宋步兵廣銳皆出州縣而民兵奏績
若李抱真李德裕韓魏公之捷可考也酌
而行之未必非足兵之計矣不然則召募
而雞犬不寧清勾而甲乙異喙愈逃愈虚
將竭斯民之脂而募無用之兵乎夫治河
制虜古法詳而不宜於今今之議可行矣
然疏築之費不貲市易之價難定非有域
外之觀灼見其機而持之者則尤懼其說
===
鈴也
宗祿民兵今制詳而不越於古古之法當復
矣然降封幾於寡恩而募民易於賈怨非
有破調之材力肩其事而應之者則尤懼
其畫餅也萬世之便不因道謀而志隳旦
夕之安不以小利而技癢此所謂事應於
時機斷於獨而善議者也然愚猶有一說
焉殷憂啓聖多難興邦河患虜患亦天心
仁愛人君者也惟迪德用賢以鼓天和則
punctuated:
《木蘭》之詞，孰不憐之？然漢之騎士起於田野，唐、宋步兵廣銳皆出州縣，而民兵奏績，若李抱真、李德裕、韓魏公之捷，可考也。酌而行之，未必非足兵之計矣。不然，則召募而雞犬不寧，清勾而甲乙異喙，愈逃愈虚，將竭斯民之脂，而募無用之兵乎？

夫治河、制虜，古法詳而不宜於今，今之議可行矣。然疏築之費不貲，市易之價難定，非有域外之觀，灼見其機而持之者，則尤懼其說鈴也。宗祿、民兵，今制詳而不越於古，古之法當復矣。然降封幾於寡恩，而募民易於賈怨，非有破調之材，力肩其事而應之者，則尤懼其畫餅也。萬世之便，不因道謀而志隳；旦夕之安，不以小利而技癢。此所謂事應於時，機斷於獨，而善議者也。

然愚猶有一說焉：殷憂啓聖，多難興邦。河患、虜患，亦天心仁愛人君者也。惟迪德用賢以鼓天和，則
translation_en:
… and the "Ballad of Mulan," who does not feel pity for them? Yet the cavalrymen of the Han arose from the fields and countryside, and the infantry and Elite Broad (Guangrui) units of the Tang and Song all came from the prefectures and counties; the achievements of civilian militias, such as the victories under Li Baozhen, Li Deyu, and Duke Han of Wei [Han Qi], can all be verified. If we deliberate and put this into practice, it may well be a viable plan for ensuring sufficient troops. Otherwise, recruitment will leave not even chickens and dogs in peace, and clearing the military registers to draft replacements will lead to conflicting testimonies between parties; the more men desert, the more depleted the ranks become. Are we to exhaust the very lifeblood of the people just to recruit useless soldiers?

Now, regarding river control and subduing the northern caitiffs, the ancient methods are detailed yet unsuited to the present, whereas present-day proposals are practicable. Even so, the costs of dredging and diking are immeasurable, and the prices in border horse-markets are difficult to fix; unless there is someone with vision beyond the ordinary who clearly perceives the pivotal dynamics and holds firm to them, one especially fears that such talk will amount to mere jingling bells [empty chatter]. Regarding imperial clan stipends and civilian militias, present institutions are detailed yet do not surpass antiquity, so the ancient methods ought to be restored. Even so, reducing enfeoffment ranks borders on scant grace, and recruiting the common people easily invites resentment; unless there is someone of extraordinary talent who vigorously shoulders the task and responds to the challenge, one especially fears it will remain a painted cake [an empty illusion]. Advantage for ten thousand generations is not undermined in its resolve by counsels along the roadside; peace for a single morning and evening does not itch to act for the sake of petty gain. This is what is meant by responding to the times in one's affairs, deciding at the critical juncture on one's own authority, and excelling in deliberation.

Yet I humbly have one further point to make: deep sorrow awakens a sage, and many difficulties revive a state. The disasters of the Yellow River and the menace of the caitiffs are also ways in which the mind of Heaven shows benevolent love for the ruler of men. Only by pursuing virtue and employing the worthy so as to rouse the harmony of Heaven will…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
治河禦虜擇便成功此其根本在
朝廷者也千金之子內贍其家外威其鄰至
足也今祿匱兵疲乏於財耳惟慎儉節財
以臻富庶則祿繼而兵自强此其節縮在
朝廷者也
聖意所加萬彙嚮應而何憂於四議乎管見如
此執事以爲何如
第四問
劉文徴
===
同考試官教諭陶批士有恒心而無定向觀風之者
何如耳是策以選舉考覈之法廣而行之足以勵行而維風矣
考試官教諭劉批評議有見而風勵之說尤爲探本
考試官教諭蔣批氣格雄渾識見超拔非凡士也
君子所以樹天下之功者必其勵天下之
節者也君子所以勵天下之節者必其貞
天下之志者也蓋功者濟世之具而不可
倖成材者立功之本而不可苟就故砥礪
廉隅乃所以豫匡濟之略而竦節奇氣赫
punctuated:
治河禦虜，擇便成功，此其根本在朝廷者也。千金之子，內贍其家，外威其鄰，至足也。今祿匱兵疲，乏於財耳。惟慎儉節財，以臻富庶，則祿繼而兵自强，此其節縮在朝廷者也。聖意所加，萬彙嚮應，而何憂於四議乎？管見如此，執事以爲何如？

第四問
劉文徴
同考試官教諭陶批：士有恒心而無定向，觀風之者何如耳。是策以選舉考覈之法廣而行之，足以勵行而維風矣。
考試官教諭劉批：評議有見，而風勵之說尤爲探本。
考試官教諭蔣批：氣格雄渾，識見超拔，非凡士也。

君子所以樹天下之功者，必其勵天下之節者也；君子所以勵天下之節者，必其貞天下之志者也。蓋功者，濟世之具，而不可倖成；材者，立功之本，而不可苟就。故砥礪廉隅，乃所以豫匡濟之略；而竦節奇氣，赫
translation_en:
… managing the rivers and defending against the northern tribes will succeed by choosing what is expedient; for these matters, the foundation lies in the Imperial Court. The son of a family worth a thousand pieces of gold supports his household within and commands respect from his neighbors without, because his resources are thoroughly sufficient. Today, imperial stipends are depleted and the troops are exhausted simply from a lack of funds. Only by exercising careful frugality and economizing on wealth to achieve abundance and prosperity will stipends be sustained and the military naturally grow strong; for these matters, the retrenchment lies in the Imperial Court. Wherever the Sacred Intention is applied, the myriad things respond to it—what need is there to worry over these four deliberations? Such is my humble view; what does Your Excellency think of it?

Fourth Question
Liu Wenzheng 劉文徴
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Tao 陶: Scholars possess a constant mind yet lack a fixed direction; it all depends on how those who guide them set the example. This policy essay broadens and applies the methods of selection and evaluation, which is sufficient to encourage moral conduct and uphold public mores.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu 劉: His evaluations and deliberations show insight, and his discussion of inspiring and encouraging scholars especially gets to the root of the matter.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Jiang 蔣: His style and vigour are grand and浑厚 (vigorous and profound), and his insight is outstanding—he is no ordinary scholar.

That by which the superior man establishes achievements throughout the realm is surely that by which he encourages moral integrity throughout the realm; and that by which the superior man encourages moral integrity throughout the realm is surely that by which he makes steadfast the aspirations of the realm. For achievement is the instrument for aiding the world, and cannot be accomplished by mere luck; talent is the foundation for establishing achievement, and cannot be attained carelessly. Therefore, honing one's integrity and uprightness is the means to prepare in advance the strategies for rectifying and aiding the world; while towering integrity and extraordinary spirit, brilliantly…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
然焜耀于人之耳目者則旋乾闢坤天下
被其化書裳馥稿後世仰其休此非委靡
巽懦于平居而嘗試於功名之會者爲之
也何者其所挾持者不輕而其所布置者
始不可量也向使志有不立則無以堅其
節而養其材厚其積而宏其用雖使時勢
可乘無能建明於天下即或勉强樹立姑
假烈烈之名然亦不能厭人心而杜後訾
矣又况循循然一無所就而徒失天下之
===
望者乎嗚呼士君子身負綱常宇宙皆分
事也奈之何其不自勵哉緬想唐虞之世
元氣渾融明良合德都俞吁咈相與聚精
神喜起賡歌相與召和氣無智名無勇功
無節義之號也自樂堯舜於畎畝者一舉
而救溝中之納負飛熊於渭水者一動而
振鷹揚之功人固以掀揭宇宙之勳必成
於高節令名之士而緊是則朝扣暮遊掉
寸舌而横塞真源奴顏隸膝效雞犬而解
punctuated: 然焜耀于人之耳目者，則旋乾闢坤，天下被其化，書裳馥稿，後世仰其休。此非委靡巽懦于平居，而嘗試於功名之會者爲之也。何者？其所挾持者不輕，而其所布置者始不可量也。向使志有不立，則無以堅其節而養其材，厚其積而宏其用。雖使時勢可乘，無能建明於天下；即或勉强樹立，姑假烈烈之名，然亦不能厭人心而杜後訾矣。又况循循然一無所就，而徒失天下之望者乎？嗚呼！士君子身負綱常，宇宙皆分事也，奈之何其不自勵哉？緬想唐、虞之世，元氣渾融，明良合德，都俞吁咈，相與聚精神；喜起賡歌，相與召和氣。無智名，無勇功，無節義之號也。自樂堯、舜於畎畝者，一舉而救溝中之納；負飛熊於渭水者，一動而振鷹揚之功。人固以掀揭宇宙之勳，必成於高節令名之士；而緊是則朝扣暮遊，掉寸舌而横塞真源，奴顏隸膝，效雞犬而解…
translation_en:
…blazingly before the eyes and ears of men—then he can turn heaven and open earth so that the entire realm receives his transforming influence, and with his deeds inscribed on banners and his drafts left fragrant, later generations look up to his excellence. This is not done by those who are listless and timid in ordinary times and merely try their luck when an opportunity for merit and fame arises. Why is this? Because only when what one upholds within is not taken lightly can what one sets in motion be beyond measure. Suppose one's resolve is not established: then there is no way to strengthen one's integrity and nurture one's talent, or to deepen one's accumulation and broaden one's application. Even if the times and circumstances offer an opportunity to seize, one will be unable to establish anything illustrious in the world; and even if one forces oneself to achieve something and temporarily borrows a blazing reputation, it still will not satisfy men's hearts or forestall criticism from posterity. How much more so for those who plod along achieving nothing at all, merely disappointing the hopes of the world!

Alas! A scholar-gentleman bears theThree Bonds and Five Constant Virtues upon his person; the entire universe is his proper business. How could he fail to spur himself on? Looking back in thought to the age of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], the primordialvitality was harmoniously blended, enlightened rulers and worthy ministers were united in virtue, and with exclamations of agreement and dissent they gathered their spirit together; rejoicing and rising to continue one another's songs, they summoned forth harmonious vital energy. There were no reputations for cleverness, no feats of bravery, and no titles of lofty integrity and righteousness. Ever since the one who delighted in the way of Yao and Shun among the furrowed fields [Yi Yin 伊尹] rose at a single stroke to rescue the people from being pushed into the ditches, and the one who bore the omen of the flying bear by the Wei River [Lü Shang 呂尚] moved at a single stroke to rouse achievements like a soaring hawk, people have naturally held that world-shaking merits must be accomplished by scholars of lofty integrity and fine reputation. Yet close behind this [?], men knock on gates at dawn and roam as persuaders at dusk, wagging an inch of tongue to perversely block the true source, or with slavish faces and servile knees imitate cocks and dogs to unfasten…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
紐王教動則誤天下之蒼生而羞稱於君
子之口焉將益以含貞葆素之士不可多
得而貴賤之辨隨時雌黃矣即如鍾扶輿
之淑間挺寥廓之芳聲者或非時所能限
然中材之士與世浮湛則其不能脫跡於
鼓鑄濡染之區者其大較也故周之士貴
秦之士賤楊雄亦據時事而評其槩耳夫
周士貴矣而鬻熊辛甲皆周產也一以耄
年謁文王而誇策事之壯一以傾蓋遇召
===
奭而膺長子之封淟涊干進豈足貴乎不
知菁莪棫樸之教皆慷慨質直之風植節
砥行鱗集星輝二子蓋適時之行耳而周
士之貴自若也秦士賤矣而桃源海島皆
秦地也隱士竄跡而謝漁郎之問田橫殞
身而却漢主之招遺榮輕生豈可賤乎不
知狙詐坑焚之後多聲利游揚之夫鄙曲
踰閑接軫繁蔓二子特麻中之蓬耳而秦
士之賤猶故也四皓蹈跡商山而出安炎
punctuated: 紐王教，動則誤天下之蒼生，而羞稱於君子之口焉。將益以含貞葆素之士不可多得，而貴賤之辨隨時雌黃矣。即如鍾扶輿之淑，間挺寥廓之芳聲者，或非時所能限；然中材之士與世浮湛，則其不能脫跡於鼓鑄濡染之區者，其大較也。故周之士貴，秦之士賤，楊雄亦據時事而評其槩耳。夫周士貴矣，而鬻熊、辛甲皆周產也，一以耄年謁文王而誇策事之壯，一以傾蓋遇召奭而膺長子之封，淟涊干進，豈足貴乎？不知菁莪棫樸之教，皆慷慨質直之風，植節砥行，鱗集星輝，二子蓋適時之行耳，而周士之貴自若也。秦士賤矣，而桃源、海島皆秦地也，隱士竄跡而謝漁郎之問，田橫殞身而却漢主之招，遺榮輕生，豈可賤乎？不知狙詐坑焚之後，多聲利游揚之夫，鄙曲踰閑，接軫繁蔓，二子特麻中之蓬耳，而秦士之賤猶故也。四皓蹈跡商山，而出安炎
translation_en: … unravel the kingly teaching; whenever they act, they mislead the common people of the empire, and gentlemen are ashamed even to speak of them. Consequently, scholars who cherish integrity and preserve simplicity are ever more regarded as hard to find, while the distinction between noble and base shifts with the changing judgments of the age. To be sure, those who are endowed with the pureessence of heaven and earth and occasionally stand forth with a fragrant reputation across the vast expanse may not be confined by their times; yet scholars of middling talent rise and sink with the world, so that in general they are unable to extricate themselves from the realm of its molding and steeping influence. Thus, when Yang Xiong (楊雄) said that the scholars of Zhou were noble and the scholars of Qin were base, he too was merely judging the general trend on the basis of contemporary affairs. Now, the scholars of Zhou were indeed noble, yet Yu Xiong (鬻熊) and Xin Jia (辛甲) were both products of Zhou: the one presented himself to King Wen in extreme old age and boasted of his vigor in planning affairs; the other met Shao Shi (召奭) by chance on the road and received enfeoffment at Zhangzi (長子). Sullied by their eager pursuit of advancement, how could they be worthy of esteem? Yet one must realize that under the moral transformation celebrated in the odes "Luxuriant Tarragon" (Jing'e) and "The Oak Clumps" (Yupu), all shared a spirited, honest, and upright ethos, establishing their integrity and whetting their conduct, gathering like fish scales and shining like stars; those two men were merely acting in accord with the opportunity of the moment, while the nobility of the scholars of Zhou remained just as it was.
