And the scholars of Qin were indeed base, yet Peach Blossom Spring (Taoyuan) and the ocean island were both in the territory of Qin: the recluses hid their tracks there and declined the fisherman's inquiries, while Tian Heng (田橫) took his own life and refused the summons of the Sovereign of Han. Forsaking glory and holding life lightly, how could they be deemed base? Yet one must realize that after the era of cunning deceit and the burning of books and burying of scholars, there were many men who boasted and peddled themselves for fame and profit; vulgar, crooked, and transgressing all bounds, they followed close upon one another's carriage wheels and spread like weeds. Those two examples were merely straight fleabane growing amidst hemp, while the baseness of the scholars of Qin remained as before. The Four Graybeards (Sihao) hid their tracks on Mount Shang, yet came forth to stabilize the fiery…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
劉之業孔明高枕南陽而起成鼎足之勳
是其操脩不苟而致用自宏也乃毛遂自
薦楚趙定從鄧禹投歸雲臺首烈而張齊
賢布衣獻策卒成賢相之功焉則異才亦
起於自售不專以養望得之者然不知暗
合道妙者不以膠柱而隳績是鄧禹諸賢
各有當也子厚締黨叔文卒投老於西粤
仲淹獻策十二乃托興於東征是其樹立
旣汙而蒙詬非過也乃樊英强起損譽漢
===
庭殷浩一出蒼生觖望而房琯素負時名
亦不免陳濤之辱焉則誤國多出於徵士
不專以干謁失之者然不知聲聞過情者
難以倖時而建功房琯諸賢固晝龍也之
數賢者就事功而論之則安劉定鼎鞏兩
主之基解紛定難皆有用之器視諸旅進
旅退貽譏黨友者相逕庭矣要心術而評
之則商山之謀出於呂氏布衣之策終爲
上援方諸抱膝長吟光明俊偉者隔霄壤
punctuated: 劉之業；孔明高枕南陽，而起成鼎足之勳：是其操脩不苟，而致用自宏也。乃毛遂自薦，楚、趙定從；鄧禹投歸，雲臺首烈；而張齊賢布衣獻策，卒成賢相之功焉。則異才亦起於自售，不專以養望得之者。然不知暗合道妙者，不以膠柱而隳績，是鄧禹諸賢各有當也。子厚締黨叔文，卒投老於西粤；仲淹獻策十二，乃托興於《東征》：是其樹立旣汙，而蒙詬非過也。乃樊英强起，損譽漢庭；殷浩一出，蒼生觖望；而房琯素負時名，亦不免陳濤之辱焉。則誤國多出於徵士，不專以干謁失之者。然不知聲聞過情者，難以倖時而建功，房琯諸賢固晝龍也。之數賢者，就事功而論之，則安劉定鼎，鞏兩主之基，解紛定難，皆有用之器，視諸旅進旅退、貽譏黨友者，相逕庭矣。要心術而評之，則商山之謀出於呂氏，布衣之策終爲上援，方諸抱膝長吟、光明俊偉者，隔霄壤
translation_en: … the enterprise of the Fiery Liu [the Han dynasty]; and Kongming [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] slept soundly on a high pillow at Nanyang before rising to achieve the merit of the tripartite balance of power. This is because their moral cultivation was not lax, and thus their practical application was naturally grand. Yet Mao Sui 毛遂 recommended himself, and the alliance between Chu and Zhao was settled; Deng Yu 鄧禹 cast his lot with his lord and ranked first in merit on the Cloud Terrace; and Zhang Qixian 張齊賢, while still a commoner in plain cloth, presented strategic plans and ultimately achieved the accomplishments of a worthy Grand Councilor. Thus extraordinary talents have also arisen by offering themselves for service, not exclusively attaining success by nurturing their reputations in retirement. Yet people fail to realize that those who tacitly accord with the subtleties of the Way do not ruin their achievements through rigid adherence to convention [gluing the tuning pegs]; thus Deng Yu and those other worthies each acted appropriately for their circumstances. Zihou [Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元] formed a faction with Shuwen [Wang Shuwen 王叔文] and ended up banished to grow old in Western Yue [Guangxi]; Zhongyan [Wang Tong 王通] presented twelve strategic plans, only to entrust his feelings to the "Eastern Expedition" (Dongzheng): because the way they established themselves was already sullied, the disgrace they suffered was not undeserved. Yet when Fan Ying 樊英 was compelled to take office, he damaged his reputation at the Han court; as soon as Yin Hao 殷浩 emerged from retirement, the common people were disappointed in their hopes; and although Fang Guan 房琯 had long enjoyed contemporary renown, even he could not escape the humiliation at Chentao. Thus those who fail the state have often come from among summoned scholars, not exclusively losing their way through self-seeking solicitation. Yet people fail to realize that those whose reputations exceed their actual substance can hardly rely on fortuitous timing to establish merit; Fang Guan and the others were truly like painted dragons [impressive in appearance only]. Regarding these several worthies, if we discuss them in terms of practical achievements, stabilizing the Liu clan and establishing the tripartite realm consolidated the foundations of two rulers, while resolving disputes and settling crises showed them all to be instruments of practical use—wildly different from those who merely advance and retreat with the crowd or leave behind ridicule on account of their factional associates. However, if we evaluate them by going to the root of their mental intentions, the scheme of the Four Hoaryheads of Mount Shang originated with Empress Lü, and the strategies presented by the commoner [Zhang Qixian] were ultimately a means of seeking advancement from above; compared with the bright, illustrious, and magnificent spirit of him who chanted long while clasping his knees [Zhuge Liang], they are as far apart as heaven and earth…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
矣蓋黃綺諸賢特衆人之尤而孔明則衆
尤之尤也若桃源海島業無可見而清風
凜凜尚有餘思樊英房琯寡謀輕試而迄
今猶潤牙頰者何哉蓋世變江河士習愈
下伏車泣血而不知哭途之鄙突梯滑稽
而不知升斗之汙懊不得意坐而書空者
視諸子之時猶瀾倒焉固宜其有述於後
世也故士之於世寧爲玉碎毋爲瓦全寧
爲雉經毋爲虺曲寧爲待聘之英强起之
===
琯而毋若平原河陽自鬻以成其身焉至
於開誠布公籍爲學古之梯而澹泊寧靜
毅然藩籬其身而不敢褻雖其成功在天
不可逆睹而後彫之栢特達之圭人固仰
之爲山斗矣而況節以志堅材以節立功
以材運世豈有厚自珍惜而不能建立於
世者乎噫可貴而不可賤可周而不可秦
士人之立身行已固如是也然聞周之待
士六德六行以爲稽尚其實也三詔五贄
punctuated: 矣。蓋黃綺諸賢，特衆人之尤，而孔明則衆尤之尤也。若桃源、海島，業無可見，而清風凜凜，尚有餘思；樊英、房琯，寡謀輕試，而迄今猶潤牙頰者，何哉？蓋世變江河，士習愈下：伏車泣血，而不知哭途之鄙；突梯滑稽，而不知升斗之汙；懊不得意，坐而書空者，視諸子之時，猶瀾倒焉，固宜其有述於後世也。故士之於世，寧爲玉碎，毋爲瓦全；寧爲雉經，毋爲虺曲；寧爲待聘之英、强起之琯，而毋若平原、河陽自鬻以成其身焉。至於開誠布公，籍爲學古之梯，而澹泊寧靜，毅然藩籬其身而不敢褻。雖其成功在天，不可逆睹，而後彫之栢、特達之圭，人固仰之爲山斗矣。而況節以志堅，材以節立，功以材運，世豈有厚自珍惜而不能建立於世者乎？噫！「可貴而不可賤，可周而不可秦」，士人之立身行已，固如是也。然聞周之待士，六德、六行以爲稽，尚其實也；三詔、五贄
translation_en: … Indeed, worthy men like Huang and Qi [of the Four Hoaryheads of Mount Shang] were merely outstanding among the multitude, whereas Kongming [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] was the most outstanding of the outstanding. As for those of Peach Blossom Spring (Taoyuan) and the Ocean Island (Haidao), their deeds left nothing visible to show, yet their pure wind blows briskly and still inspires lingering admiration; Fan Ying 樊英 and Fang Guan 房琯 were scant in strategy and rash in putting themselves to the test, yet why is it that down to the present day people still relish speaking of them? It is because as the world declines like rivers flowing ever downward, the customs of scholars sink ever lower: bowing before carriages and weeping blood, without knowing the baseness of wailing at the end of the road; being slick, compliant, and obsequious, without knowing the filth of [begging for] a peck or a pint of grain; or, vexed at failing to get their way, sitting and tracing characters in the empty air [like Yin Hao 殷浩]. Compared to the times of those earlier gentlemen, this is like a collapsing wave—so it is certainly fitting that those earlier men are still recounted in later ages. Therefore, for a scholar in the world, it is better to be shattered jade than intact tile; better to strangle oneself like a pheasant than to coil like a viper; better to be a Fan Ying awaiting an invitation or a Fang Guan forced from retirement than to be like those of Pingyuan [Lu Ji 陸機] and Heyang [Pan Yue 潘岳], peddling themselves only to bring ruin upon their own persons. As for displaying sincerity and fairness, taking that as the ladder for studying antiquity, and remaining tranquil and serene in few desires, resolutely fencing off one's person so that none dare profane it—even though success rests with Heaven and cannot be foreseen, like the cypress that is last to wither or the jade tablet that alone is presented directly at court, people will surely look up to such a man as Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper. How much more so when integrity is made firm by resolve, talent is established through integrity, and achievement is set in motion by talent—how could there be anyone in the world who deeply cherishes his own dignity and yet is unable to establish achievements in the world? Alas! "They can be honored, but cannot be debased; they would serve Zhou, but would not serve Qin"—such indeed is how scholars establish themselves and conduct their lives. Yet I have heard that in the way the Zhou treated scholars, the Six Virtues and Six Conducts were used to examine them, prizing their substance; three summonses and five ceremonial gifts …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而後見遠其耻也八法八柄以辨治省其
成也故士不得不貴而治不得不隆是化
導之權在上而不在下也方
今敦尚節行振勵士風選之以科目而戒其
浮蔓課之以久任而黜其競躁其貴士養
士之心不讓成周矣而猶有窳節之材如
執事所云者何哉大抵蓬戶甕牖之志不
過風雲月露之習文藝旣攻青紫立至其
於節行標致素所未嘗而旣仕之後又以
耀潤身家為念陟巍躋膴為期苟可得之
卽脂韋之行皆所不鄙而氣隳於積俗漸
於靡故需材愈急而應之者猶夫其初也
卽欲起敝維風豈無術乎今之選舉無遺
法矣然謂科目盡天下之材不可也枕流
漱石豈無瑰瑋卓犖出於制舉之外者乎
必舉辟薦之典責諸監司廣詢博訪有道
德隆重者有孝弟力田者有行誼脩潔者
據實陳薦不限其數而其揮霍勇毅機智
punctuated: 而後見，遠其耻也；八法八柄以辨治，省其成也。故士不得不貴，而治不得不隆，是化導之權在上而不在下也。方今敦尚節行，振勵士風，選之以科目而戒其浮蔓，課之以久任而黜其競躁，其貴士養士之心不讓成周矣。而猶有窳節之材如執事所云者，何哉？大抵蓬戶甕牖之志，不過風雲月露之習；文藝旣攻，青紫立至，其於節行標致素所未嘗。而旣仕之後，又以耀潤身家為念，陟巍躋膴為期，苟可得之，卽脂韋之行皆所不鄙，而氣隳於積，俗漸於靡，故需材愈急，而應之者猶夫其初也。卽欲起敝維風，豈無術乎？今之選舉無遺法矣，然謂科目盡天下之材，不可也。枕流漱石，豈無瑰瑋卓犖出於制舉之外者乎？必舉辟薦之典，責諸監司廣詢博訪，有道德隆重者，有孝弟力田者，有行誼脩潔者，據實陳薦，不限其數。而其揮霍勇毅、機智
translation_en:
…before granting an audience, so as to keep them far from shame; and they used the Eight Regulations and Eight Handles of Authority to differentiate governance, so as to inspect their accomplishments. Therefore, scholars could not fail to be valued, and governance could not fail to flourish. This shows that the power to transform and guide lies with those above and not with those below.

At present, His Majesty esteems integrity and conduct and rouses the ethos of the literati, selecting them through examination categories while warning against superficiality and floridity, and evaluating them through long tenures in office while dismissing those who are competitive and impatient. His commitment to valuing and nurturing scholars does not yield to that of the flourishing Zhou dynasty! Yet why are there still talents of flawed integrity such as Your Excellency has described?

Generally speaking, the ambitions of those living behind thatch doors and broken-jar windows go no further than the habit of composing verses on wind, clouds, moon, and dew. Once they master literary composition, high official robes and ribbons arrive immediately; as for integrity, conduct, and noble bearing, they have never experienced them. And after they enter office, their thoughts turn to glorifying and enriching themselves and their families, and their goal is to ascend to lofty and lucrative posts. So long as they can obtain these, they do not disdain even unctuous and pliant conduct. Thus morale collapses through long accumulation, and customs gradually sink into decadence; therefore, the more urgently talent is needed, the more those who respond remain just as they were before.

If one wishes to remedy this decline and uphold public mores, how could there be no method? Today's system of selection and promotion leaves out no regulation, yet one cannot say that the examination categories exhaust all the talents in the empire. Among those living in reclusion—"pillowing on streams and rinsing their mouths with stones"—how could there fail to be extraordinary and outstanding men who stand outside the regular civil service examinations? We must revive the institution of special summons and recommendation, charging the provincial surveillance officials to inquire widely and search broadly: whether there are men of lofty virtue, or men of filial piety, brotherly submission, and diligent farming, or men of cultivated and pure conduct and righteousness, they should recommend them on the basis of verified fact without limiting their numbers. And as for those who are bold, resolute, resourceful,…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
謀略可備一時緩急之需者將不病其為
屠釣為草野特設一科而羅之以弭天下
之變而待天下之用焉則埴之在冶惟陶
所範未有上作而下不應者也此不可以
廣選舉之所未盡乎今之考覈無遺法矣
然謂格例鼓天下之趨不可也循資躡級
豈無琦材異政限於資格之內者乎必酌
久任之法責諸銓部尚實均勞無以清華
為捷徑無以遠地為贅員無以流品為定
===
局以目正耳資望兼收而其奉職循雅植
節清脩足為一世人材之表者吾不疑其
為吏隱為市隱大破常調而庸之厚天下
之倡以養天下之鋒焉則一人善射百夫
拾决未有鋒在而劒不利者也此所以補
考覈之未盡者也若徒操舉業為彀率而
逸奇行於驪黃專停解於日月而滯賢庸
於鴈次則俊茂倜儻之士安肯鄙猥自衒
而曲學以覬聲利乎噫昔人所謂用法益
punctuated: 謀略可備一時緩急之需者，將不病其為屠釣、為草野，特設一科而羅之，以弭天下之變而待天下之用焉。則埴之在冶，惟陶所範，未有上作而下不應者也。此不可以廣選舉之所未盡乎？今之考覈無遺法矣，然謂格例鼓天下之趨不可也。循資躡級，豈無琦材異政限於資格之內者乎？必酌久任之法，責諸銓部，尚實均勞，無以清華為捷徑，無以遠地為贅員，無以流品為定局，以目正耳，資望兼收；而其奉職循雅、植節清脩，足為一世人材之表者，吾不疑其為吏隱、為市隱，大破常調而庸之，厚天下之倡以養天下之鋒焉。則一人善射，百夫拾决，未有鋒在而劒不利者也。此所以補考覈之未盡者也。若徒操舉業為彀率，而逸奇行於驪黃；專停解於日月，而滯賢庸於鴈次，則俊茂倜儻之士，安肯鄙猥自衒，而曲學以覬聲利乎？噫！昔人所謂用法益…
translation_en: …and strategic resourcefulness can meet the needs of sudden emergencies, we should not fault them for being butchers or fishermen, or men from the rustic wilds, but rather establish a special category to gather them in, so as to quell crises in the realm and await the realm's need for their service. Then, just as clay on the wheel is shaped solely by the potter's mold, never has there been a case where the ruler initiates above and those below do not respond. Could this not broaden what the selection system fails to exhaust? Today's system of performance evaluation leaves no method overlooked, yet one cannot say that fixed precedents and regulations suffice to rouse the ambitions of the realm. In following seniority and climbing the ranks step by step, how could there not be extraordinary talents and exceptional administrators confined within the bounds of seniority and qualifications? We must deliberate upon a system of long tenure and charge the Ministry of Personnel with prizing substance and equalizing toil—not treating prestigious posts as shortcuts, not treating remote regions as places for superfluous personnel, and not treating stream-of-entry status as a fixed destiny, while verifying what is heard with what is seen and taking into account both seniority and reputation. And for those who perform their duties with refined compliance, uphold integrity and pure self-cultivation, and suffice to stand as models of talent for their generation, we should not suspect them of being hermits hiding in minor clerkships or in the marketplace, but boldly break with routine appointments to employ them, strengthening leadership across the realm so as to nurture its sharp edge. Then, just as when one man excels at archery a hundred men pick up their thumb-rings and arm-guards, never has there been a sword that is not sharp when its point is intact. This is how to supplement what performance evaluation fails to exhaust. If instead we merely wield examination composition as the standard of the bow's draw, letting extraordinary conduct slip past while judging only by black or yellow coat; or focus exclusively on halting and forwarding credentials by counting days and months, stalling the worthy and the meritorious in rigid goose-file order—then how would outstanding and unconventional scholars deign to demean themselves by peddling their own wares and twisting their learning to covet fame and profit? Alas! What men of old meant by saying that the more…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
密而進人益難者其說固具在也上挽其
趨士勵其志而人材治道不古若焉愚固
未之信也
第五問
吳璨
同考試官教諭徐批積粟鑄錢裕民要務是作究
極利弊斟酌時宜皆鑿鑿可行優於用世者也
考試官教諭劉批興利當圖久遠子言有卓識矣
考試官教諭蔣批經畫周詳不特可行於一方者
===
聖王之致治也必導利以厚天下之生而
操權以制天下之用蓋食者民之資以生
也弗爲之殖則耗竭而不贍故導之而充
然有餘則無不厚之生矣利者人之所必
趨也弗爲之制則扤滯而弗通故制之而
民習於義則無不足之用矣生厚用足則
財裕而不爭天下之業安所爲而不成也
執事以積貯錢帛策諸生將謂其識時務
與非其人也然敢不拾所聞以對甞聞聖
punctuated:
密而進人益難者，其說固具在也。上挽其趨，士勵其志，而人材治道不古若焉，愚固未之信也。

第五問
吳璨
同考試官教諭徐批：積粟鑄錢，裕民要務。是作究極利弊，斟酌時宜，皆鑿鑿可行，優於用世者也。
考試官教諭劉批：興利當圖久遠，子言有卓識矣。
考試官教諭蔣批：經畫周詳，不特可行於一方者。

聖王之致治也，必導利以厚天下之生，而操權以制天下之用。蓋食者，民之資以生也，弗爲之殖，則耗竭而不贍；故導之而充然有餘，則無不厚之生矣。利者，人之所必趨也，弗爲之制，則扤滯而弗通；故制之而民習於義，則無不足之用矣。生厚用足，則財裕而不爭，天下之業安所爲而不成也？執事以積貯、錢帛策諸生，將謂其識時務與？非其人也，然敢不拾所聞以對？甞聞聖
translation_en:
… strict, the harder it is to advance men of talent"—that argument still stands intact. If those above redirect the prevailing trend and scholars rouse their aspirations, I certainly do not believe that human talent and the way of governance would fail to match antiquity.

Question Five
Wu Can 吳璨
Associate Examiner and Instructor Xu 徐 comments: Storing grain and casting coins are vital tasks for enriching the people. This essay thoroughly investigates the advantages and disadvantages and weighs what is appropriate to the times; everything in it is demonstrably practicable, showing someone well suited for service to the world.
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: In promoting what is beneficial, one ought to plan for the long term; your words show eminent insight.
Examiner and Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: The planning is comprehensive and detailed, and is practicable not merely in a single region.

When the sage kings brought about good order, they invariably guided material benefits so as to enrich the livelihood of all under heaven, and held the authority to regulate the expenditures of all under heaven. For food is what the people rely upon to live; if one does not foster its production, it becomes depleted and insufficient. Therefore, when one guides it so that there is an abundant surplus, there is no livelihood that is not enriched. Profit is what people inevitably pursue; if one does not regulate it, it becomes obstructed and fails to circulate. Therefore, when one regulates it so that the people become accustomed to righteousness, there is no expenditure that is not sufficient. When livelihood is enriched and expenditure is sufficient, wealth is abundant and there is no contention; what enterprise in the empire could then be undertaken and not succeed? In putting a policy question to us candidates concerning grain reserves and coin and silk, does Your Excellency suppose that we understand the affairs of the day? I am not such a man, yet how dare I not gather what I have heard in order to reply? I have heard that when the sages…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
人在上而民不凍饑者非能耕而食之織
而衣之也爲開其食貨之源也故辨土地
以藝植因水旱而鑄金使四民各勤其業
而遠近咸資其利一毫一縷事爲之制而
見於周官一書者尤備焉九穀之生責諸
三農國用之制以三十年爲通而九府圜
法復有以濟粟之所不及當其時民有餘
粟而國有餘財蓋因其利而利之非損下
也因其足而通之非奪民也鳧鷖既醉之
===
治有自來矣後之求理者亦常用之乃田
雖井而新自新官雖周而隋自隋者何哉
蓋古之人理其出而後之人理其入乃一
切苟且之術也豈古今異宜哉管仲九府
之制因貴賤以權輕重單穆公以錢輕爲
患則量資幣而權子母焉是雖未必盡合
周官之法度而操縱以時民胥便之固謂
之得策矣李悝平糴之法因歲入爲斂散
桑弘羊易以均輸則籠百貨而歸於官焉
punctuated: 人在上而民不凍饑者，非能耕而食之、織而衣之也，爲開其食貨之源也。故辨土地以藝植，因水旱而鑄金，使四民各勤其業，而遠近咸資其利，一毫一縷事爲之制，而見於《周官》一書者尤備焉。九穀之生責諸三農，國用之制以三十年爲通，而九府圜法復有以濟粟之所不及。當其時，民有餘粟而國有餘財，蓋因其利而利之，非損下也；因其足而通之，非奪民也。《鳧鷖》、《既醉》之治，有自來矣。後之求理者亦常用之，乃田雖井而新自新，官雖周而隋自隋者，何哉？蓋古之人理其出，而後之人理其入，乃一切苟且之術也，豈古今異宜哉？管仲九府之制，因貴賤以權輕重；單穆公以錢輕爲患，則量資幣而權子母焉。是雖未必盡合《周官》之法度，而操縱以時，民胥便之，固謂之得策矣。李悝平糴之法，因歲入爲斂散；桑弘羊易以均輸，則籠百貨而歸於官焉。
translation_en: …when a sage occupies the throne and the people suffer neither cold nor hunger, it is not because he personally plows to feed them or weaves to clothe them, but because he opens up the sources of their food and goods. Thus, by distinguishing types of soil for planting and cultivating, and by casting metal coins in response to floods and droughts, he ensured that the four classes of people each worked diligently at their occupations and that those near and far all relied on the benefits thereof. Regulations were made for every hair and thread of business, and what is seen in the book Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) is especially complete. The production of the nine grains was entrusted to the farmers of the three types of land; the regulation of state expenditures was calculated on a thirty-year cycle; and the round-coin system of the Nine Treasuries further served to supplement what grain alone could not achieve. At that time, the people had surplus grain and the state had surplus wealth. This was because the ruler benefited them based on what was already beneficial to them, without diminishing those below; he circulated goods based on their existing sufficiency, without robbing the people. The well-governed eras celebrated in the odes "Wild Ducks" (Fuyi) and "Already Drunk" (Jizui) indeed had their origins in this. Those in later times who sought good governance also frequently employed these measures. Yet why is it that even though the fields were divided according to the well-field system, the Xin dynasty remained the Xin, and even though the offices were modeled on those of the Zhou, the Sui dynasty remained the Sui? It is because the ancients managed fiscal administration on the basis of expenditures, whereas people of later times managed it on the basis of revenues—which is merely a makeshift, expedient art. How could it be that what is appropriate differs between antiquity and the present? Under Guan Zhong's system of the Nine Treasuries, the expensive and the cheap were used to balance the heavy and the light; Duke Mu of Shan, regarding light coinage as a problem, measured resources and currency to balance mother and child coins. Although these measures did not necessarily conform completely to the laws and standards of the Offices of Zhou, they expanded and contracted the money supply according to the times, and the people all found them convenient, so they may certainly be called successful policies. Li Kui's method of equitable grain purchasing regulated collection and distribution according to the annual harvest; when Sang Hongyang replaced this with equitable transport, he monopolized all manner of goods and brought them under government control…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
是雖均為心計之運量然平糴裕農而均
輸貿利悝固彼善於此者矣富民入粟實
邊順民心而三有所補此晁錯積儲計也
孝文賴以富庶可謂盛矣然積貲顯融則
累行者抑姦民蒙宥則犯科者多胥天下
離制而棄本冒禍而攘利焉其錯之作俑
乎摶銅盡歸公庾禁私鑄而致福有七此
賈誼治安策也文帝竟弛錢禁非不公矣
然利權旁落則倒持太阿法網太疎則姧
弛日衆至吳王鑄錢而富埒萬乘商賈滯
財而不佐公家焉其誼之先見乎是數子
者興一時之利便而為司計者所宗固能
臣也然財不可聚而獨厚於上權不可移
而反歸於下其得失異致而治亂常相反
者其所操者殊也我
祖宗軫念元元節以制度墾田科稅歲有常供
官俸軍需用有定額上不侈而下常餘宇
內蒸蒸富庶者餘二百年即滇南遠在徼
punctuated: 是雖均為心計之運量，然平糴裕農而均輸貿利，悝固彼善於此者矣。富民入粟實邊，順民心而三有所補，此晁錯積儲計也。孝文賴以富庶，可謂盛矣。然積貲顯融，則累行者抑；姦民蒙宥，則犯科者多。胥天下離制而棄本、冒禍而攘利焉，其錯之作俑乎！摶銅盡歸公庾，禁私鑄而致福有七，此賈誼《治安策》也。文帝竟弛錢禁，非不公矣。然利權旁落，則倒持太阿；法網太疎，則姧弛日衆。至吳王鑄錢而富埒萬乘，商賈滯財而不佐公家焉，其誼之先見乎！是數子者，興一時之利便而為司計者所宗，固能臣也。然財不可聚，而獨厚於上；權不可移，而反歸於下。其得失異致而治亂常相反者，其所操者殊也。我祖宗軫念元元，節以制度。墾田科稅，歲有常供；官俸軍需，用有定額。上不侈而下常餘，宇內蒸蒸富庶者餘二百年。即滇南遠在徼
translation_en: Although both of these were calculations of financial planning, grain-price stabilization (pingdi 平糴) enriched the farmers whereas equitable delivery (junshu 均輸) traded for profit; thus Li Kui 李悝 was certainly better than the latter in this regard. Having wealthy commoners deliver grain to supply the frontiers, thereby according with the people's wishes and bringing three benefits—this was Chao Cuo's 晁錯 plan for accumulating reserves. Emperor Xiaowen 孝文 relied on it to achieve wealth and populace, which may well be called flourishing. Yet when those who accumulated wealth attained prominence, men of cultivated conduct were suppressed; when wicked commoners received pardons, lawbreakers multiplied. Leading the entire realm to depart from regulations and abandon the fundamental occupation [agriculture], and to brave disaster in order to seize profit—was it not Cuo who started this evil practice? Gathering all copper into the public granaries and treasuries, prohibiting private minting, and thereby bringing about seven blessings—this was Jia Yi's 賈誼 Policy for Peace and Order (Zhi'an ce 治安策). Emperor Wen 文帝 ultimately relaxed the prohibition on minting coin, which was not ungenerous. Yet when control over financial profit fell into outside hands, it was like holding the Tai'e 太阿 sword by the blade; when the net of the law was too loose, the wicked and lax grew ever more numerous. Ultimately, the King of Wu 吳王 minted coin until his wealth rivaled that of the Son of Heaven, and merchants hoarded wealth without aiding the state—was this not Yi's foresight? These several men promoted the conveniences and benefits of a single era and were revered by those in charge of fiscal administration; they were indeed capable ministers. Yet wealth should not be amassed, and yet they concentrated it solely above; authority should not be transferred, and yet they let it revert below. That their successes and failures led to different outcomes, and order and disorder constantly ran counter to one another, was because what they held to was different. Our Imperial Ancestors felt deep compassion for the common people and regulated expenditures through institutional norms. In reclaiming land and levying taxes, there were regular annual quotas; for official salaries and military supplies, expenditures had fixed amounts. Those above were not extravagant and those below always had a surplus, so that within the realm all flourished in wealth and populace for over two hundred years. Even Diannan 滇南 [Yunnan], far out beyond the frontier…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
外亦沐膏澤稱富饒矣乃者生齒日繁歳
入漸寡稍旱暵而餓夫盈途是蓄積不如
古也貨物翔踴閭里瀟然緣轉徙而額餉
日逋是財用不如古也居常無事醫瘡剜
肉已不忍聞於慈父孝子之聲而卒然有
警則安知其計之所出哉
皇上睿德性生冲虛節愛積粟之課既
頒鑄錢之
令復下其視洪範之先食貨周官之阜民財
===
===
者
意尤渥也海內喁喁然思嚮
皇風而登殷阜而滇之急在燃眉者當事諸臣
將何以奉揚休美乎夫善爲治者莫不重
穀今滇民不勤本業而生寡食衆銍艾甫
停積蓄告匱粟之不足甚矣誠欲理之其
要有三屯地有定額而隱侵於豪右乾没
於武弁責餘丁以虛賠而質他室以負稅
夷民租種軍田輸稅十一額失而弊滋矣
punctuated:
外，亦沐膏澤，稱富饒矣。乃者生齒日繁，歳入漸寡，稍旱暵而餓夫盈途，是蓄積不如古也；貨物翔踴，閭里瀟然，緣轉徙而額餉日逋，是財用不如古也。居常無事，醫瘡剜肉，已不忍聞於慈父孝子之聲；而卒然有警，則安知其計之所出哉！
皇上睿德性生，冲虛節愛，積粟之課既頒，鑄錢之令復下，其視《洪範》之先食貨、《周官》之阜民財者，意尤渥也。海內喁喁然思嚮皇風而登殷阜，而滇之急在燃眉者，當事諸臣將何以奉揚休美乎？夫善爲治者莫不重穀，今滇民不勤本業，而生寡食衆，銍艾甫停，積蓄告匱，粟之不足甚矣。誠欲理之，其要有三：屯地有定額，而隱侵於豪右，乾没於武弁，責餘丁以虛賠，而質他室以負稅，夷民租種軍田，輸稅十一，額失而弊滋矣。
translation_en:
… beyond the frontiers, also bathed in imperial grace and was acclaimed for its wealth and abundance. Lately, however, the population has grown daily more numerous while annual revenues have gradually dwindled; at the slightest drought, starving people fill the roads—this shows that grain reserves do not match those of the past. Prices of goods soar, villages are desolate, and because of migration, the fixed quotas of military provisions fall further into arrears by the day—this shows that financial resources do not match those of the past. Even in ordinary times of peace, people must scoop out flesh to heal a sore, and one can already scarcely bear to hear the cries of compassionate fathers and filial sons; if a sudden alarm should arise, who knows what plan could be devised?

His Majesty, endowed by nature with sagely virtue, is modest, frugal, and benevolent. Assessments for accumulating grain have already been promulgated, and orders for casting coins have again been handed down; compared with the priority given to food and commodities in the Great Plan (Hongfan) and the enrichment of the people's wealth in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), his intentions are even more generous. Within the seas, all look up expectantly, longing to turn toward the imperial wind and ascend to prosperity and abundance. Yet with Yunnan's emergencies as pressing as singed eyebrows, how shall the officials in charge uphold and spread this splendid beneficence? Now, those who excel at governance never fail to value grain. Today, the people of Yunnan are not diligent in the fundamental occupation [agriculture]; producers are few and consumers many, so that no sooner have the sickles stopped harvesting than the reserves are reported exhausted. The shortage of grain is extreme! If we truly wish to put this in order, there are three essentials: Military colony lands have fixed quotas, yet they are secretly encroached upon by powerful families and embezzled by military officers. Supernumerary soldiers are held responsible for making up hollow deficits, and property is mortgaged to other households while still bearing the tax burden; native peoples rent and cultivate military fields, paying only a tenth in tax, so that the quotas are lost and abuses proliferate. …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
必按籍以稽履畝而覈番休老壯盜沽之
竇當塞也訪覈鱗圖乾没之姦當懲也則
田足贍軍而亦可以寬民此清屯田之爲
要也一夫不耕受以饑矣乃武定迷蒙荒
蕪未墾而遊食者日衆誠擇其長川廣野
可以開溝洫而畫經界者授可耕之人而
給之牛種薄征稅之入而時勸相焉則緣
南畝者多而積儲備矣此勸力作之爲要
也夫常平非李悝之法也三代之法也今
===
===
之春而貸秋而償善矣然栽桑紙上逋欠
日多放則利歸胥猾徵則迹涉誅求加以
潮濕浥爛又累司庾者之賠輸則孰與常
平之爲便哉必隨地而擇其亢爽立爲庾
司實以備賑之贖穀掌以茂實之耆民貴
出賤入無貲者量貸之惟其饑之上下而
不盡罄焉則貲本既有所出而浥腐亦不
爲病此立常平之爲要也夫民方艱食而
吾爲之開其源使三年九年之常蓄而凶
punctuated: 必按籍以稽，履畝而覈，番休老壯，盜沽之竇當塞也；訪覈鱗圖，乾没之姦當懲也。則田足贍軍，而亦可以寬民，此清屯田之爲要也。一夫不耕，受以饑矣。乃武定、迷蒙，荒蕪未墾，而遊食者日衆。誠擇其長川廣野，可以開溝洫而畫經界者，授可耕之人，而給之牛種，薄征稅之入，而時勸相焉。則緣南畝者多，而積儲備矣，此勸力作之爲要也。夫常平非李悝之法也，三代之法也。今之春而貸、秋而償，善矣。然栽桑紙上，逋欠日多；放則利歸胥猾，徵則迹涉誅求。加以潮濕浥爛，又累司庾者之賠輸，則孰與常平之爲便哉？必隨地而擇其亢爽，立爲庾司，實以備賑之贖穀，掌以茂實之耆民，貴出賤入，無貲者量貸之，惟其饑之上下而不盡罄焉。則貲本既有所出，而浥腐亦不爲病，此立常平之爲要也。夫民方艱食，而吾爲之開其源，使三年、九年之常蓄，而凶
translation_en: We must inspect them according to the registers and verify them by pacing the fields in person; we must rotate the elderly and the strong in service, and the loopholes for illicit sale must be plugged; we must investigate and verify the fish-scale land registers, and the villainy of embezzlement must be punished. Then the fields will be sufficient to support the military, and we can also give relief to the people. This is the essential point of clearing up the military state farms. If a single man does not plow, someone suffers hunger because of it. Yet in Wuding and Mimeng [Mi'le and Mengzi?], barren lands remain uncultivated while idle consumers grow more numerous by the day. If we truly select those areas with long rivers and broad plains where irrigation ditches can be opened and boundaries drawn, grant them to people capable of tilling, supply them with oxen and seed, lighten the collection of taxes, and seasonally encourage and assist them, then those working the southern acres will be many and stored reserves will be prepared. This is the essential point of encouraging diligent labor. Now, the Ever-Normal Granary is not the method of Li Kui; it is the method of the Three Dynasties. The present practice of lending in spring and repaying in autumn is good indeed. Yet it is like planting mulberries on paper, and arrears grow more numerous by the day; when grain is released, the profit goes to cunning clerks, and when it is collected, the practice borders on extortionate demands. Added to this, dampness and rotting further burden those in charge of the granaries with making restitution—so how can this compare to the convenience of the Ever-Normal Granary? We must choose high and dry ground in each locality to establish granary offices, fill them with redemption grain prepared for famine relief, and place them under the management of upright and substantial elders. Selling when prices are high and buying when prices are low, we should lend measured amounts to those without means, scaling it according to the severity of the famine without completely exhausting the stores. Then the capital will have a source from which to come, and dampness and rot will not be a problem. This is the essential point of establishing Ever-Normal Granaries. When the people are struggling for food, if we open up the source for them, ensuring regular reserves for three or nine years, so that in times of famine…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
荒水旱足以相恤如是而民生有不厚乎
善理財者以錢代貝蓋金銀細分則耗布
帛片折則廢惟錢為便也今銅產於滇充
溢闤闠市民捐軀命以浚求之況於錢之
利而不害乎茲欲行之其要亦有三念賈
誼召禍起姦之說而操之使不旁落藉其
贏餘以周困匱則利權在我而劉濞鄧通
之徒無自作矣此私鑄之當禁也錢議最
多而莫善於孔覬者不惜銅不愛工也試
===
倣開元之制而定以新名務使體厚而肉
好適均製工而輪郭周正則本多工費而
天下之觸禁者少此規式之當定也三幣
相準從古已然滇雲舊用海肥細微不混
故稱便焉惟令錢貝兼使二幣通融而一
準上幣以權之則俗不欺紿而賈無拆閱
矣此權宜之當酌也夫
朝有明令而吾為之通其變使民情土俗之
相安而公輸私費得以兼資如是而財用
punctuated:
荒水旱足以相恤，如是而民生有不厚乎？
善理財者，以錢代貝。蓋金銀細分則耗，布帛片折則廢，惟錢為便也。今銅產於滇，充溢闤闠，市民捐軀命以浚求之，況於錢之利而不害乎？茲欲行之，其要亦有三：念賈誼召禍起姦之說，而操之使不旁落，藉其贏餘以周困匱，則利權在我，而劉濞、鄧通之徒無自作矣，此私鑄之當禁也；錢議最多，而莫善於孔覬者，不惜銅、不愛工也，試倣開元之制而定以新名，務使體厚而肉好適均，製工而輪郭周正，則本多工費而天下之觸禁者少，此規式之當定也；三幣相準，從古已然，滇雲舊用海肥，細微不混，故稱便焉，惟令錢、貝兼使，二幣通融，而一準上幣以權之，則俗不欺紿而賈無拆閱矣，此權宜之當酌也。夫朝有明令，而吾為之通其變，使民情、土俗之相安，而公輸、私費得以兼資，如是而財用
translation_en:
…famine, flood, or drought, there will be enough to provide mutual relief. When it is like this, how could the people's livelihood fail to be enriched?

Those who are skilled at managing finances use bronze coins in place of cowrie shells. For when gold and silver are divided into tiny fractions, they suffer loss through wastage; when cloth and silk are cut into small pieces, they become ruined and useless; only bronze coins are convenient. Today, copper is produced in Dian (Yunnan) and fills the marketplaces; townspeople risk their very lives to mine and seek it out—how much more so when it comes to coins, which bring benefit without harm! If we now wish to put coinage into circulation, there are likewise three essentials:

First, bear in mind Jia Yi's 賈誼 argument that [private minting] invites disaster and gives rise to villainy, and hold tight to the authority over coinage so that it does not slip into other hands, using its surplus to relieve distress and scarcity. Then control over profit will rest with us, and men of the ilk of Liu Pi 劉濞 and Deng Tong 鄧通 will have no way to arise on their own. This is why private minting must be prohibited.

Second, discussions of coinage have been most numerous, yet none is better than that of Kong Ji 孔覬: "not begrudging copper and not sparing labor." Let us try imitating the system of the Kaiyuan 開元 era while establishing a new inscription, making sure that the body of the coin is thick and the rim (rou 肉) and center hole (hao 好) are properly proportioned, and that the workmanship is fine and the outer edge is square and regular. Then, because the capital required is large and the labor costly, few in the realm will violate the prohibitions [by counterfeiting]. This is why the standard specifications must be fixed.

Third, the mutual pegging of the three grades of currency has been practiced since antiquity. Yunnan has long used cowrie shells (haifei 海肥); even in minute transactions they are not confused, and so they are considered convenient. Only if we allow bronze coins and cowries to be used together so that the two currencies circulate interchangeably, while uniformly pegging them against the superior currency [silver] to weigh their value, will popular customs be free of deceit and merchants suffer no losses from selling below cost. This is why expedient adaptation must be carefully deliberated.

Now, the Court has issued clear decrees, and if we adapt them flexibly to changing circumstances—making sure that popular sentiment and local customs remain at ease with one another, and that both public tax payments and private expenditures can be jointly supported—when it is like this, [how could] financial resources…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
有不豐乎噫此富滇之術而推之富天下
可也雖然滇之可憂者豈止此乎租庸煩
苦則宜差恒産勾流寓以甦其困也隴畝
旱亢則當濬壩堰導桔槔以通其利也將
卒柔脆而無用夷玀剽掠而難捕則設武
舘以閑技略嚴保甲以訊知音者可不早
爲之防乎俗尚淫靡而惰農桑礦課虧額
而羈命吏則植棉麻以杜其澆易專官以
通其窮者可不曲爲之計乎若夫制防緬
===
甸分北沙儂又未然之憂出於積儲錢幣
之外者而要之莫非厚民計也顧豈無其
本哉彼谷永守鬱林而烏滸内附李靖撫
南粤而黎獞胥悅黃忠宣治安南而交人
不忍遽叛者得其人也今之仕者率戀中
原而厭邊徼除目一下索然無復向往之
心司銓者曲而通之遠方之吏非例廕則
遷謫不然則朴直寡援者也其視中土懸
異矣夫天下一體中原心腹也遠方四肢
punctuated: 有不豐乎？噫！此富滇之術，而推之富天下可也。雖然，滇之可憂者豈止此乎？租庸煩苦，則宜差恒産、勾流寓，以甦其困也；隴畝旱亢，則當濬壩堰、導桔槔，以通其利也；將卒柔脆而無用，夷玀剽掠而難捕，則設武舘以閑技略、嚴保甲以訊知音者，可不早爲之防乎？俗尚淫靡而惰農桑，礦課虧額而羈命吏，則植棉麻以杜其澆、易專官以通其窮者，可不曲爲之計乎？若夫制防緬甸，分北沙、儂，又未然之憂出於積儲、錢幣之外者，而要之莫非厚民計也。顧豈無其本哉？彼谷永守鬱林而烏滸内附，李靖撫南粤而黎、獞胥悅，黃忠宣治安南而交人不忍遽叛者，得其人也。今之仕者，率戀中原而厭邊徼，除目一下，索然無復向往之心。司銓者曲而通之，遠方之吏，非例廕則遷謫，不然則朴直寡援者也，其視中土懸異矣。夫天下一體，中原，心腹也；遠方，四肢…
translation_en:
… fail to be abundant? Alas! This is the art of enriching Yunnan, and it can be extended to enrich the entire realm. Even so, how could the matters of concern in Yunnan be limited merely to this? Taxes and corvée labor are burdensome and bitter, so we should grade levies according to permanent property and register floating migrants in order to relieve the people's distress. Fields and furrows suffer from severe drought, so we ought to dredge dams and weirs and introduce well-sweeps in order to open up benefits for them. Commanders and soldiers are soft, fragile, and useless, while the Yi and Luo tribes plunder and are hard to apprehend; should we not take early precautions by establishing military halls to train them in martial skills and strategy, and strictly enforcing the mutual-security (baojia) system to interrogate those who know their tongues [or: informants]? Local customs favor extravagance and neglect farming and sericulture, while mining taxes fall short of quotas and tie down commissioned officials; should we not devise careful plans by planting cotton and hemp to curb their frivolity, and replacing specialized officials to relieve this impasse? As for restraining and defending against Burma (Miandian) and dividing and isolating the Sha and Nong tribes, these are anxieties yet to materialize that lie beyond the issues of grain reserves and coinage—yet in essence, none of them is anything other than a plan for enriching the people's livelihood.

Yet how could this be without a fundamental root? In the past, when Gu Yong 谷永 served as Grand Protector of Yulin 鬱林, the Wuhu 烏滸 people submitted from within; when Li Jing 李靖 pacified Nanyue 南粤, the Li 黎 and Zhuang 獞 tribes all rejoiced together; and when Huang Zhongxuan 黃忠宣 (Huang Fu 黃福) governed Annam 安南, the people of Jiaozhi 交趾 could not bear to rebel hastily—all because the right men were found. Those who hold office today generally yearn for the Central Plains and detest the frontier marches; as soon as the appointment list is handed down, their spirits sink and they no longer have any heart to go forward. Those in charge of personnel selection bend the rules to accommodate this: officials sent to distant regions are either hereditary-privilege (yin) appointees by regulation or demoted exiles, and if not those, then simple, blunt men with few connections—a stark disparity from how the Central Lands are treated! Now, the realm is a single body: the Central Plains are the heart and belly, while the distant regions are the four limbs…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也四肢病而委諸庸醫善攝生者固如是
乎故吏茲土者非廉潔不足以震威非材
識不足以批蠹非久任不足以孚夷情練
土俗而非超遷又不足以繫士望而固久
任之心也則夫計材而陟擇人而使賢者
不以避嫌邀名不肖者不以貪墨敗事足
兵食之圖養和平之福則華尊夷遁
九重寬西顧之憂矣是又在
巖廊加之意耳愚生慨此已久惟執事轉
===
聞之焉
punctuated: 也。四肢病而委諸庸醫，善攝生者固如是乎？故吏茲土者，非廉潔不足以震威，非材識不足以批蠹，非久任不足以孚夷情、練土俗，而非超遷又不足以繫士望而固久任之心也。則夫計材而陟，擇人而使，賢者不以避嫌邀名，不肖者不以貪墨敗事，足兵食之圖，養和平之福，則華尊夷遁，九重寬西顧之憂矣。是又在巖廊加之意耳。愚生慨此已久，惟執事轉聞之焉。
translation_en: … [the four limbs]. When the four limbs are diseased and yet one entrusts them to quack physicians, would someone skilled at nourishing life really act like this? Therefore, for those who serve as officials in this land, without incorruptibility they cannot inspire awe; without talent and insight they cannot eradicate abuses; without long tenure they cannot win the trust of the native peoples and become well-versed in local customs; and yet without extraordinary promotion one cannot bind the aspirations of scholars and solidify their resolve for long tenure. Thus, to promote on the basis of measured talent and assign posts by selecting the right men—so that the worthy do not court reputation by avoiding suspicion, and the unworthy do not ruin affairs through greed and corruption—thereby fulfilling plans for sufficient troops and provisions and cultivating the blessings of peace and harmony, so that Chinese authority is revered and the border tribes submit [or: withdraw], relieving the Emperor in the Ninefold Palace of his anxieties looking westward: all this depends on the high ministers at court paying closer heed to it. This foolish student has long lamented these matters, and only prays that Your Excellency will relay them upward.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
萬曆丙子雲南鄉試事竣錄
旣成監察御史陳文燧謂朝
鳴祗役校文宜申忠告朝鳴
遂言曰二三子舉於鄉執事
者旣歌鹿鳴而賓興之矣予
何言哉無已則申鹿鳴之旨
爲諸士告可矣昔叔孫穆子
聘於晉晉公享之樂歌鹿鳴
者三而後拜使行人問焉穆
子對曰鹿鳴君之所以貺使
臣而來周行美德音者也敢
不拜嘉夫君之貺臣以周行
德音爲望則其禮遇延接之
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序
萬曆丙子，雲南鄉試事竣，錄旣成，監察御史陳文燧謂朝鳴祗役校文，宜申忠告。朝鳴遂言曰：二三子舉於鄉，執事者旣歌《鹿鳴》而賓興之矣，予何言哉？無已，則申《鹿鳴》之旨爲諸士告，可矣。昔叔孫穆子聘於晉，晉公享之，樂歌《鹿鳴》者三而後拜。使行人問焉，穆子對曰：「《鹿鳴》，君之所以貺使臣，而來周行、美德音者也，敢不拜嘉？」夫君之貺臣，以周行、德音爲望，則其禮遇延接之
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In the bingzi year of the Wanli era (1576), when the business of the Yunnan Provincial Examination had been concluded and the record was compiled, Inspecting Censor Chen Wensui 陳文燧 remarked that since I, Chaoming 朝鳴, had respectfully served to evaluate the examination papers, it was fitting that I should offer a word of earnest counsel. I, Chaoming, thereupon spoke as follows:

You gentlemen have been recommended at the provincial level, and the officiating authorities have already sung the ode "Criticism of the Deer" (Luming 鹿鳴) and sent you forth as honored guests. What more is there for me to say? If I must speak, then it will suffice to expound upon the meaning of "Criticism of the Deer" to advise you scholars.

In antiquity, when Shusun Muzi 叔孫穆子 went on a diplomatic mission to Jin 晉, the Duke of Jin feasted him. Only after the musicians had sung "Criticism of the Deer" three times did he bow in acknowledgment. When the Duke sent a Messenger to inquire the reason, Muzi replied: "'Criticism of the Deer' is the song with which my lord bestows favor upon an envoy, thereby inviting him to show the great way and praising his virtuous reputation—how could I dare not bow in gratitude for such kindness?" Now, when a ruler bestows favor upon his subject with the hope that he will show the great way and possess a virtuous reputation, then the… [sincerity of his courteous treatment and reception]

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
誠已溢於琴瑟筐篚之外而
臣之所以報稱
主德者顧在於言語文字之間乎
彼其屬望嘉賔者不曰德音
孔昭則曰視民不佻而以君
子是則是傚者終之蓋謂身
無逸行則陳之為周行昭之
為德音而臣民胥範焉是周
之人君所以禮其臣者誠渥
而責之者亦誠殷也今
主上嗜學勤政
執中建極遠邁成周而
夢寐賢哲即遐陬僻壤之士必
隆禮厚宴羅而致之惟恐其
punctuated: 誠，已溢於琴瑟筐篚之外，而臣之所以報稱主德者，顧在於言語文字之間乎？彼其屬望嘉賔者，不曰「德音孔昭」，則曰「視民不佻」，而以「君子是則是傚」者終之。蓋謂身無逸行，則陳之為周行，昭之為德音，而臣民胥範焉。是周之人君所以禮其臣者誠渥，而責之者亦誠殷也。今主上嗜學勤政，執中建極，遠邁成周，而夢寐賢哲，即遐陬僻壤之士，必隆禮厚宴，羅而致之，惟恐其
translation_en: … sincerity in treating and receiving them with courtesy had already overflowed beyond the lutes, zithers, and baskets of gifts; could the means by which a subject repays and matches the Sovereign’s virtue lie merely in spoken words and written texts? What the ode expects of the honored guests is expressed either as “their virtuous reputation is grandly manifest” or as “they show the people how not to be frivolous,” concluding with “the noble men take them as model and pattern.” This means that when one’s personal conduct is free of waywardness, setting it forth constitutes the “Great Way” (zhouhang) and manifesting it constitutes “virtuous reputation” (deyin), so that officials and commoners alike take it as their standard. Thus, the way the rulers of the Zhou treated their subjects with courtesy was truly generous, and what they demanded of them was also truly earnest. Today, His Majesty delights in learning and is diligent in governance, holding fast to the Mean and establishing the Supreme Standard, far surpassing the flourishing Zhou; he longs for worthy and wise men even in his dreams, so that even scholars from distant corners and remote regions arewithout fail gathered and brought forth through grand rites and lavish banquets, His only fear being that their …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
周行之說不亟聞於
上諸士生於朱提炎方去中原萬
餘里其初不過與齊民耦耳
一旦策名
天府光華燁然即且司民社臣鄰
之寄竒哉遘也乃可衒空名
於鉛槧隮盛美於聲華而不
===
思履德蹈道以求稱塞於萬
一乎夫熊蹯豹胎不若菽粟
之味錦文綺縠不若韋布之
温所謂不佻之德豈其踔厲
﨑崛而絕俗為異者哉惟篤
衷不欺表裏符契則其材固
君子之材文亦君子之文也
punctuated: 周行之說不亟聞於上。諸士生於朱提炎方，去中原萬餘里，其初不過與齊民耦耳。一旦策名天府，光華燁然，即且司民社臣鄰之寄，竒哉遘也！乃可衒空名於鉛槧，隮盛美於聲華，而不思履德蹈道，以求稱塞於萬一乎？夫熊蹯豹胎，不若菽粟之味；錦文綺縠，不若韋布之温。所謂不佻之德，豈其踔厲﨑崛而絕俗為異者哉？惟篤衷不欺，表裏符契，則其材固君子之材，文亦君子之文也。
translation_en: …doctrines of the Grand Way (zhouhang) may not swiftly reach the ears of the Sovereign. You scholars were born in the tropical southern region of Zhuti, more than ten thousand li distant from the Central Plains; at the outset, you were merely equals of the common people. Yet once your names are inscribed in the imperial registers, your glory shines brilliantly, and soon you will be entrusted with the charge of the people and the altars of the soil, serving as the Sovereign's ministers and close aides—what a marvelous encounter this is! How then could you merely parade empty fame through your writing tablets, or exalt splendid praise in superficial reputation, without thinking of treading the path of virtue and the Way so as to fulfill even one ten-thousandth of your charge? Indeed, bear's paws and leopard fetuses do not match the nourishment of beans and grain; patterned brocades and fine silks do not match the warmth of plain leather and homespun cloth. Could what is called "unfrivolous virtue" consist of being flamboyant, eccentric, and aloof from the world just to appear extraordinary? Only when your inner heart is sincere and without deceit, and your outer conduct and inner substance correspond like the halves of a tally, will your talent truly be the talent of a gentleman, and your writing likewise be the writing of a gentleman.

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
今方内之士握瑜懷瑾孰不
標表藝林希高慕大孰不抵
掌先哲居常奮嘆天下之事
若以爲言之無由行之無會
汲汲然不得以其身試之然
一肩重鉅輒相牾悮無論屬
厭溫飽巽懦鮮立即或建樹
===
===
卓犖焜耀耳目而玄覽未深
一涉於虛驕之念焉則視古
之立功立言者尚不免堂奧
之隔矣諸士脩詞績德蓋亦
有年自今謀之心揆之後其
能以周行之陳報
寵遇不佻之德視臣民乎鹿鳴之
punctuated: 今方内之士，握瑜懷瑾，孰不標表藝林？希高慕大，孰不抵掌先哲？居常奮嘆天下之事，若以爲言之無由、行之無會，汲汲然不得以其身試之。然一肩重鉅，輒相牾悮。無論屬厭溫飽、巽懦鮮立，即或建樹卓犖，焜耀耳目，而玄覽未深，一涉於虛驕之念焉，則視古之立功、立言者，尚不免堂奧之隔矣。諸士脩詞績德，蓋亦有年，自今謀之心、揆之後，其能以周行之陳報寵遇、不佻之德視臣民乎？《鹿鳴》之
translation_en: Today, among the scholars within the realm, holding fine jade in their hands and cherishing gems in their bosoms, who does not set himself up as a paragon in the forest of letters? Aspiring to the lofty and admiring the great, who does not clap his hands in animated discussion of the former sages? In ordinary life they indignantly sigh over the affairs of the world, as though thinking there is no avenue to speak of them and no opportunity to put them into practice, anxiously lamenting that they cannot test them in person. Yet once they shoulder heavy and great responsibilities, they immediately fall into contradiction and error. To say nothing of those who are sated with warmth and full bellies, timid and weak, scarcely establishing anything—even if someone achieves towering accomplishments that dazzle the eyes and ears, if his profound insight is not yet deep and he once indulges in empty and arrogant thoughts, then compared with the ancients who established merit and established words, he still cannot avoid being separated from the inner sanctum by the outer hall. You scholars have cultivated your words and accumulated virtue for some years now. From this day forward, as you ponder in your hearts and measure the future, will you be able to repay Imperial favor by setting forth the大道 (great way / Highway of Zhou), and display unfrivolous virtue to the officials and people? The [strains] of "Lu ming" (The Deer Cry)…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
音固在耳也奈之何其弗懋
哉昔人謂
君臣際會比諸雲龍而大雲五色
其下必有賢人兹省之得名
者固以彩雲自南方出也朝
鳴初歷龍華境方旱暵蒼碧
之巔雲峯硉兀咸欣欣然以
===
===
爲雨也少焉飄揭晴空日出
有曜眾且嗒然寂矣詰朝望
瀟湘木容之區雲猶是也已
而頹飆怒雹偃苗拔木人皆
咨睢又明日陟苴蘭廻視盤
龍太華諸峯烟霧四塞褰裳
疾避乃霖霡淋漓槁甦仆植
punctuated: 音，固在耳也，奈之何其弗懋哉！昔人謂君臣際會比諸雲龍，而大雲五色，其下必有賢人。兹省之得名者，固以彩雲自南方出也。朝鳴初歷龍華境，方旱暵，蒼碧之巔，雲峯硉兀，咸欣欣然以爲雨也；少焉，飄揭晴空，日出有曜，眾且嗒然寂矣。詰朝，望瀟湘、木容之區，雲猶是也；已而頹飆怒雹，偃苗拔木，人皆咨睢。又明日，陟苴蘭，廻視盤龍、太華諸峯，烟霧四塞，褰裳疾避；乃霖霡淋漓，槁甦仆植，
translation_en: … strains are surely still ringing in your ears; how could you fail to exert yourselves! Men of old compared the auspicious encounter of ruler and minister to clouds and dragons, and said that beneath great clouds of five colors there must be a worthy man. Indeed, this province derived its name from the multicolored clouds that appeared in the south. When I, Chaoming, first passed through the territory of Longhua, it was suffering from a parching drought. Atop the verdant peaks, towering banks of clouds rose ruggedly, and everyone rejoiced, thinking it would rain; yet in a short while they scattered into a clear sky and the sun came out shining brightly, leaving the crowd dejected and silent. The next morning, looking toward the regions of Xiaoxiang and Murong, the clouds were just the same; soon after, however, a fierce gale and raging hail flattened the sprouts and uprooted trees, making everyone sigh and stare in dismay. On the following day, ascending Julan and looking back at the peaks of Panlong and Taihua, mist and fog closed in on all sides, and we hitched up our garments to hurry for shelter; thereupon a soaking rain poured down in abundance, reviving the withered and raising up the fallen, …

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
三農籲天稱慶焉然則民何
心哉固雲之變態爾殊也今
諸士之文即祥光景雲不是
過日當服休服采雲附景從
其為浮雲乎無咎無譽矣為
暴雲乎眾且咨之矣惟輝煌
治理霖雨蒼生使臣鄰胥有
===
視傚則人將稱為慶雲如昔
賢臚第不負太史之奏即滇
省人物自兹科稱盛而彩雲
之號亦惟諸士當其實矣進
而馥稿書裳垂光萬禩充之
為虞周之傑焉又豈得以滇
雲之人物限之哉昔祁奚舉
punctuated: 三農籲天稱慶焉。然則民何心哉？固雲之變態爾殊也。今諸士之文，即祥光景雲不是過。日當服休服采，雲附景從。其為浮雲乎？無咎無譽矣。為暴雲乎？眾且咨之矣。惟輝煌治理，霖雨蒼生，使臣鄰胥有視傚，則人將稱為慶雲，如昔賢臚第，不負太史之奏。即滇省人物，自兹科稱盛，而彩雲之號，亦惟諸士當其實矣。進而馥稿書裳，垂光萬禩，充之為虞周之傑焉，又豈得以滇雲之人物限之哉！昔祁奚舉
translation_en: …and the farmers of all three terrains called out to Heaven in celebration. What, then, is in the hearts of the people? Surely it is because the shifting manifestations of the clouds differ so greatly! Now the writings of you gentlemen are surpassed not even by auspicious light and propitious clouds. One day, when you enter into the service of the state and undertake official duties, gathering like clouds and following like shadows: will you be like floating clouds? Then there will be neither blame nor praise. Will you be like violent storm clouds? Then the multitude will sigh and glare in resentment. Only if you bring resplendent governance and fall as timely rain upon the common people, giving your fellow ministers and colleagues a model to emulate, will people call you "auspicious clouds" (qingyun)—just as when worthy men of the past had their names announced in the examination lists and did not disappoint the Grand Astrologer's memorial. Then the men of talent of Yunnan province will be celebrated as flourishing from this examination onward, and the epithet "Colored Clouds" (Caiyun, i.e., Yunnan) will truly be lived up to by you gentlemen alone. Going further, if your fragrant drafts are inscribed upon robes and your radiance is handed down for ten thousand generations, expanding your achievements to become heroes of the caliber of the Yu and Zhou eras—how could you be limited merely to being talents of the clouds of Dian (Yunnan)! In ancient times, Qi Xi recommended…

title: 萬曆四年雲南鄉試錄
text:
善人謂惟善也故能舉其類
朝鳴非其人也追武前脩式
貽主司令名在二三子
河南汝州伊陽縣儒□□□
劉朝鳴謹序
punctuated:
善，人謂惟善也，故能舉其類。朝鳴非其人也，追武前脩，式貽主司令名，在二三子。
河南汝州伊陽縣儒□□□劉朝鳴謹序。
translation_en:
… the good, people said it was only because he was good himself that he was able to recommend those of his own kind. I, Zhaoming, am not such a man; yet to follow in the footsteps of former worthies and thereby bequeath an illustrious reputation to the examiners rests with you gentlemen.

Respectfully prefaced by Liu Zhaoming 劉朝鳴, Confucian [School Instructor? …] of Yiyang County, Ruzhou, Henan.
